```rust
//! A user's ceiling (spec "The ceiling"): the most a self-issued credential
//! may reach. It is the catalogs owned by the user's teams, at each one's
//! `member_access`, merged with the user's entitlements (`user_catalogs`);
//! the higher level wins. Every write here that changes a ceiling bumps
//! `admin_generation`, so running servers re-cap within one poll.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::auth::{Principal, Reach};
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::store::catalogs::{self, bump_admin_generation};
use crate::store::keys::Access;
use crate::store::users;

/// Catalog name to the highest level a user's self-issued credentials may
/// have there: `Read` or `Write`, never `Admin`.
pub type Ceiling = BTreeMap<String, Access>;

/// What members of a catalog's owning team may reach through self-issued
/// credentials.
// `clap::ValueEnum` parses `--access none|read|write`; `serde::Deserialize`
// with `rename_all = "lowercase"` reads `"none"`/`"read"`/`"write"` from REST
// bodies. A variant named `None` is fine: `Option`'s `None` is a different
// item, and this one is always written `MemberAccess::None`.
#[derive(
    Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, clap::ValueEnum, serde::Deserialize,
)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum MemberAccess {
    /// Team members get nothing through the team.
    None,
    /// Read only.
    Read,
    /// Read and write (the default).
    Write,
}

impl MemberAccess {
    /// The stored spelling.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `"none"`, `"read"` or `"write"`.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            MemberAccess::None => "none",
            MemberAccess::Read => "read",
            MemberAccess::Write => "write",
        }
    }

    /// Parses the stored spelling.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `text` - a `catalogs.member_access` value.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The value, or `None` for anything else.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match text {
            "none" => Some(MemberAccess::None),
            "read" => Some(MemberAccess::Read),
            "write" => Some(MemberAccess::Write),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The level it gives a member.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `Read` or `Write`, or `None` for [`MemberAccess::None`].
    pub fn level(self) -> Option<Access> {
        match self {
            MemberAccess::None => None,
            MemberAccess::Read => Some(Access::Read),
            MemberAccess::Write => Some(Access::Write),
        }
    }
}

/// One entitlement: a catalog given to a user beyond their teams' catalogs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Entitlement {
    /// The catalog's name.
    pub catalog: String,
    /// `Read` or `Write`.
    pub access: Access,
    /// When it was first given.
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

/// One catalog of one user's ceiling, as the query below returns it.
#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
struct CeilingRow {
    user_id: String,
    catalog: String,
    // `true` when any source gives write: the higher level wins.
    write: bool,
}

/// Every user's ceiling (or one user's, with `$1`), one row per user and
/// catalog. The union is the two sources; `bool_or` merges them.
const CEILING_ROWS: &str = "\
    SELECT s.user_id, c.name AS catalog, bool_or(s.access = 'write') AS write \
    FROM (SELECT m.user_id, c.id AS catalog_id, c.member_access AS access \
          FROM team_members m JOIN catalogs c ON c.owner_team_id = m.team_id \
          WHERE c.member_access <> 'none' \
          UNION ALL \
          SELECT e.user_id, e.catalog_id, e.access FROM user_catalogs e) s \
    JOIN catalogs c ON c.id = s.catalog_id \
    WHERE $1::text IS NULL OR s.user_id = $1 \
    GROUP BY s.user_id, c.name";

/// The ceiling rows of every user, or of the user with this id.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn ceiling_rows(pool: &PgPool, user_id: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<CeilingRow>, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query_as::<_, CeilingRow>(CEILING_ROWS)
        .bind(user_id)
        .fetch_all(pool)
        .await?)
}

/// The level a row stands for.
fn row_level(write: bool) -> Access {
    if write {
        Access::Write
    } else {
        Access::Read
    }
}

/// The id of the user called `name`, without locking it (a read).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`]; [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn user_id(pool: &PgPool, name: &str) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = $1")
        .bind(name)
        .fetch_optional(pool)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "user",
            name: name.to_string(),
        })
}

/// Every user's ceiling, for the key cache.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
///
/// # Returns
/// The ceilings by user id; a user with an empty ceiling is absent.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn ceilings(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<HashMap<String, Ceiling>, OkfError> {
    let mut by_user: HashMap<String, Ceiling> = HashMap::new();
    for row in ceiling_rows(pool, None).await? {
        // `entry(..).or_default()`: Python's `setdefault(key, {})`.
        by_user
            .entry(row.user_id)
            .or_default()
            .insert(row.catalog, row_level(row.write));
    }
    Ok(by_user)
}

/// One user's ceiling.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user` - the user's name.
///
/// # Returns
/// The ceiling (empty when the user reaches nothing).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn ceiling_of(pool: &PgPool, user: &str) -> Result<Ceiling, OkfError> {
    let user_id = user_id(pool, user).await?;
    Ok(ceiling_rows(pool, Some(&user_id))
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(|row| (row.catalog, row_level(row.write)))
        .collect())
}

/// Sets what members of a catalog's owning team may reach, and bumps
/// `admin_generation` when it changes.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `catalog` - the catalog's name.
/// * `access` - the new value.
///
/// # Returns
/// The value it had before.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::CatalogNotSelected`] for an unknown catalog;
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn set_member_access(
    pool: &PgPool,
    catalog: &str,
    access: MemberAccess,
) -> Result<MemberAccess, OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // As in `catalogs::set_owner`: the subquery reads the row as it was,
    // under its row lock, so this returns the value it replaced.
    let previous: Option<String> = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "UPDATE catalogs c SET member_access = $2 \
         FROM (SELECT id, member_access FROM catalogs WHERE name = $1 FOR UPDATE) old \
         WHERE c.id = old.id RETURNING old.member_access",
    )
    .bind(catalog)
    .bind(access.as_str())
    .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    let previous = previous.ok_or_else(|| OkfError::CatalogNotSelected {
        catalog: catalog.to_string(),
    })?;
    let previous =
        MemberAccess::parse(&previous).expect("the schema checks catalogs.member_access");
    if previous != access {
        bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    }
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(previous)
}

/// Gives a user a catalog at `access`, or changes the level of one already
/// given, and bumps `admin_generation` when anything changed.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user` - the user's name.
/// * `catalog` - the catalog's name.
/// * `access` - `Read` or `Write`.
/// * `now` - when it is given (server clock); kept when only the level changes.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] for `Admin`; [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an
/// unknown user; [`OkfError::CatalogNotSelected`] for an unknown catalog;
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn entitle(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user: &str,
    catalog: &str,
    access: Access,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    if access == Access::Admin {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "an entitlement is read or write; admin comes only from an admin key"
                .to_string(),
        });
    }
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // `FOR KEY SHARE` until commit: a concurrent `users::delete` waits.
    let user_id = users::id_of(&mut tx, user).await?;
    let catalog_id = catalogs::find(&mut *tx, catalog).await?.id;
    // The `WHERE` on the update makes an unchanged level write nothing, so
    // `rows_affected` is 0 and the generation stays.
    let written = sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO user_catalogs (user_id, catalog_id, access, created_at) \
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) \
         ON CONFLICT (user_id, catalog_id) DO UPDATE SET access = EXCLUDED.access \
         WHERE user_catalogs.access <> EXCLUDED.access",
    )
    .bind(&user_id)
    .bind(catalog_id)
    .bind(access.as_str())
    .bind(now)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    if written.rows_affected() != 0 {
        bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    }
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Takes a catalog entitlement from a user (not given is a no-op), and
/// bumps `admin_generation` when one was removed.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user` - the user's name.
/// * `catalog` - the catalog's name.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user;
/// [`OkfError::CatalogNotSelected`] for an unknown catalog;
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn unentitle(pool: &PgPool, user: &str, catalog: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    let user_id = users::id_of(&mut tx, user).await?;
    let catalog_id = catalogs::find(&mut *tx, catalog).await?.id;
    let removed = sqlx::query("DELETE FROM user_catalogs WHERE user_id = $1 AND catalog_id = $2")
        .bind(&user_id)
        .bind(catalog_id)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    if removed.rows_affected() != 0 {
        bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    }
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// A user's entitlements, by catalog name.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user` - the user's name.
///
/// # Returns
/// Each entitlement, sorted by catalog.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn entitlements(pool: &PgPool, user: &str) -> Result<Vec<Entitlement>, OkfError> {
    let user_id = user_id(pool, user).await?;
    let rows: Vec<(String, String, DateTime<Utc>)> = sqlx::query_as(
        "SELECT c.name, e.access, e.created_at FROM user_catalogs e \
         JOIN catalogs c ON c.id = e.catalog_id WHERE e.user_id = $1 ORDER BY c.name",
    )
    .bind(&user_id)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(catalog, access, created_at)| Entitlement {
            catalog,
            access: Access::parse(&access).expect("the schema checks user_catalogs.access"),
            created_at,
        })
        .collect())
}

/// May `principal` set `catalog`'s member access (or a user's
/// entitlement to it)? The one permission check the CLI, the REST routes
/// and the console use, so team owners can be allowed later here alone.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `principal` - the caller.
/// * `catalog` - the catalog.
///
/// # Returns
/// `true` for an admin that reaches every catalog (as M11's people routes
/// need), today.
pub fn may_set_member_access(principal: &Principal, catalog: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(principal.reach, Reach::All) && principal.level(catalog) == Some(Access::Admin)
}

/// Caps a credential's levels by a ceiling.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `grant` - the credential's catalogs and levels.
/// * `ceiling` - the user's ceiling.
///
/// # Returns
/// The catalogs in both, each at the lower of the two levels.
pub fn cap(grant: &BTreeMap<String, Access>, ceiling: &Ceiling) -> BTreeMap<String, Access> {
    grant
        .iter()
        // `filter_map` keeps the `Some`s: a catalog the ceiling lacks drops out.
        .filter_map(|(catalog, level)| {
            ceiling
                .get(catalog)
                .map(|limit| (catalog.clone(), (*level).min(*limit)))
        })
        .collect()
}
```

Add, above `impl KeyCache`:

```rust
/// The ceiling of a self-issued credential whose user has none.
// `BTreeMap::new` is a `const fn`, so an empty map can be a `static`.
static NO_CEILING: Ceiling = BTreeMap::new();

/// A record's principal: as stored for an admin-issued credential, capped by
/// its user's ceiling for a self-issued one (spec "Effective access").
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `record` - the row.
/// * `ceilings` - every user's ceiling, by user id.
///
/// # Returns
/// The principal.
fn principal_of(record: KeyRecord, ceilings: &HashMap<String, Ceiling>) -> Principal {
    // Looked up before `record` moves into the principal. `get` borrows
    // only `ceilings`, so the reference outlives the borrow of `record`.
    let ceiling = record.self_issued.then(|| {
        record
            .user_id
            .as_deref()
            .and_then(|user_id| ceilings.get(user_id))
            .unwrap_or(&NO_CEILING)
    });
    let mut principal = Principal::from(record);
    if let Some(ceiling) = ceiling {
        let levels = match &principal.reach {
            Reach::Catalogs(levels) => cap(levels, ceiling),
            // The schema refuses a self-issued all-catalogs row; one edited
            // by hand reaches nothing rather than everything.
            Reach::All => Ceiling::new(),
        };
        // Its highest level left, for display; `Read` when nothing is left
        // (it then reaches no catalog at all).
        principal.access = levels.values().copied().max().unwrap_or(Access::Read);
        principal.reach = Reach::Catalogs(levels);
    }
    principal
}
```

Change `from_records` to take the ceilings and use `principal_of`, and `read` to load both at once:

```rust
    /// Builds the cache from stored rows, leaving out revoked ones and
    /// those already expired, and capping self-issued ones.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `records` - the rows, as [`key_rows::list`] returns them.
    /// * `ceilings` - every user's ceiling by user id, as
    ///   [`ceiling::ceilings`] returns them (kept in the cache).
    /// * `now` - the server clock.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The cache.
    pub fn from_records(
        records: Vec<KeyRecord>,
        ceilings: HashMap<String, Ceiling>,
        now: DateTime<Utc>,
    ) -> Self {
        let mut cache = Self {
            by_user: ceilings,
            ..Self::default()
        };
        for record in records.into_iter().filter(|record| {
            record.revoked_at.is_none() && unexpired(record.expires_at, now)
        }) {
            let expires_at = record.expires_at;
            match record.kind {
                KeyKind::Key => {
                    // The schema checks `length(sha256) = 32`, so this fails
                    // only on a row edited by hand; such a key cannot
                    // authenticate. `let ... else` skips it.
                    let Some(hash) = record
                        .sha256
                        .as_deref()
                        .and_then(|sha256| <[u8; 32]>::try_from(sha256).ok())
                    else {
                        continue;
                    };
                    let principal = Arc::new(principal_of(record, &cache.by_user));
                    cache.by_hash.insert(hash, Cached { principal, expires_at });
                }
                KeyKind::OAuth => {
                    let id = record.id.clone();
                    let principal = Arc::new(principal_of(record, &cache.by_user));
                    cache.by_id.insert(id, Cached { principal, expires_at });
                }
            }
        }
        cache
    }

    /// Reads every key and every ceiling and builds the cache.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OkfError::Database`].
    async fn read(pool: &PgPool, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<Self, OkfError> {
        // Both at once, on two pooled connections (`try_join!` is
        // `asyncio.gather` that stops at the first error). A change committed
        // between the two reads also moved `admin_generation`, which every
        // caller reads first, so the next poll reloads again.
        let (records, ceilings) =
            tokio::try_join!(key_rows::list(pool), ceiling::ceilings(pool))?;
        Ok(Self::from_records(records, ceilings, now))
    }
```

```markdown
# M12 Task 3: the ceiling and capped self-issued credentials

## Added
- `store::ceiling`: `ceilings`, `ceiling_of`, `MemberAccess`,
  `set_member_access`, `entitle`, `unentitle`, `entitlements`,
  `may_set_member_access` and the pure `cap`.

## Changed

  self-issued key and grant at the lower of its own level and the ceiling.
  Admin-issued credentials are unchanged.
```

### Task 4: Users gain email, admin flag and password; passwords, emailed links and sign-in events

**Files:**

- Modify: `src/http/api/people.rs:41-75` (`UserView` and its `From<UserRecord>`, which destructures every field)
- Create: `src/store/passwords.rs`, `src/store/common_passwords.txt`, `src/store/email_tokens.rs`, `src/store/sign_in_events.rs`
- Modify: `src/store/mod.rs` (register the three modules, sorted)
- Modify: `src/clock.rs` (`after`, a checked "now plus a std duration")
- Modify: `src/app.rs` (`prune_oauth` also prunes sign-in events and emailed links)
- Modify: `Cargo.toml` (optimize `argon2` and `blake2` in the dev profile)
- Test: unit tests in each store module, `clock::tests`

This task relies on Task 1's migration for these columns and tables (spec "Data model", as corrected by Decision 8): `users.email citext UNIQUE`, `users.is_admin boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, `users.password_hash text`, `users.password_changed_at timestamptz`, `users.failed_sign_ins integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `users.locked_until timestamptz`, and the tables `email_tokens`, `sign_in_events` and `user_sessions` exactly as the spec writes them. It relies on Task 1's `OkfError::{Gone, LimitExceeded}`.

Rules this task enforces:

| Function | Refuses | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users::set_email` | `LimitExceeded { limit: "email" }` for a malformed address; `Refused` (409, "Another user has this email") for a duplicate, compared case-insensitively | `UnknownName` for the user. A changed address deletes the user's outstanding emailed links (a setup link must not keep working for an old address). No generation bump: email is not part of any credential. |
| `users::set_admin` | `Refused` (409) for clearing the last admin user unless `allow_last` | Returns the previous flag. A change bumps `admin_generation` and deletes the user's console sessions, so the next request signs in again with the new flag (spec "Rotation"). No change, no bump. |
| `passwords::check_policy` | `LimitExceeded { limit: "password" }` under 12 characters, over 1024, or in the bundled common list (case-insensitive) | No composition rules. |
| `passwords::verify` | never errors for a wrong password; returns `Failed` or `Locked` | Unknown email and a user without a password check the dummy hash, so every outcome costs one argon2 verification. 10 consecutive failures set `locked_until = now + 15 min` and reset the counter; a success resets both. A locked account answers `Locked` even for the right password. |
| `email_tokens::redeem` / `peek` | `Gone` (410) for an unknown, used, expired or wrong-purpose token | `redeem` marks the token used in the same statement that checks it, so a link works once. |
| `email_tokens::issue` | `UnknownName` for the user | Deletes the user's older tokens of the same purpose first. |

```rust
        let db = test_db().await;
        seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", None).await;
        set_admin(&db.pool, "alice", true, false).await.unwrap();

        let refused = set_admin(&db.pool, "alice", false, false).await;
        let allowed = set_admin(&db.pool, "alice", false, true).await;

        assert!(matches!(refused, Err(OkfError::Refused { .. })), "{refused:?}");
        assert!(allowed.unwrap());

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn two_admins_cleared_at_once_leave_one() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", None).await;
        seed_user(&db.pool, "bob", None).await;
        set_admin(&db.pool, "alice", true, false).await.unwrap();
        set_admin(&db.pool, "bob", true, false).await.unwrap();

        // Both run at once: the admin rows are locked in one order, so the
        // second sees the first's change and refuses.
        let (alice, bob) = tokio::join!(
            set_admin(&db.pool, "alice", false, false),
            set_admin(&db.pool, "bob", false, false),
        );

        assert_eq!([alice.is_ok(), bob.is_ok()].iter().filter(|ok| **ok).count(), 1);
        let admins: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE is_admin")
            .fetch_one(&db.pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(admins, 1);
```

```rust
/// A stored user.
// `sqlx::FromRow` maps a result row's columns onto the fields by name.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, sqlx::FromRow)]
pub struct UserRecord {
    /// Its name.
    pub name: String,
    /// Its display name (may be empty).
    pub display_name: String,
    /// When it was created (server clock).
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// How many keys, grants (live or revoked) and sign-in codes name it.
    pub credentials: i64,
    /// Its teams' names, sorted, its personal team included.
    pub teams: Vec<String>,
    /// Its email address, as entered (compared case-insensitively), if set.
    pub email: Option<String>,
    /// Whether a signed-in session of this user acts as an admin.
    pub is_admin: bool,
    /// Whether it has a local password (the hash itself never leaves SQL).
    pub has_password: bool,
}

/// What signing in needs to know about a user: who it is and whether its
/// session is an admin's. Returned by every sign-in path.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, sqlx::FromRow)]
pub struct UserAuth {
    /// `users.id` (a UUID as text), the user handle sessions and passkeys use.
    pub id: String,
    /// Its name.
    pub name: String,
    /// Its email address, if set.
    pub email: Option<String>,
    /// Whether its session acts as an admin.
    pub is_admin: bool,
}

// One SELECT shared by `list` and `find` (a macro so `concat!` can append
// each query's tail at compile time; see `select_codes!` in codes.rs).
// `email::text`: `citext` decodes as a string too, but the cast keeps the
// column's type plain for every reader.
macro_rules! select_users {
    () => {
        "SELECT u.name, u.display_name, u.created_at, \
                (SELECT count(*) FROM api_keys k WHERE k.user_id = u.id) \
              + (SELECT count(*) FROM sign_in_codes s WHERE s.user_id = u.id) AS credentials, \
                COALESCE((SELECT array_agg(t.name ORDER BY t.name) FROM team_members m \
                          JOIN teams t ON t.id = m.team_id WHERE m.user_id = u.id), \
                         '{}'::text[]) AS teams, \
                u.email::text AS email, u.is_admin, \
                u.password_hash IS NOT NULL AS has_password \
         FROM users u"
    };
}

/// The columns of a [`UserAuth`], for a query over `users u`.
// `pub(crate) use` below exports the macro to the other store modules
// (`email_tokens`, `passwords`), which splice it into their own `concat!`.
macro_rules! user_auth_columns {
    () => {
        "u.id, u.name, u.email::text AS email, u.is_admin"
    };
}
pub(crate) use user_auth_columns;
```

```rust
/// The longest email address accepted (RFC 5321's path limit).
const MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH: usize = 254;

/// Checks that `email` is one plain address, `local@domain`, with nothing a
/// mail header could read as a second recipient or a display name.
///
/// Deliberately loose: the only real test of an address is mail reaching
/// it. It refuses what would be dangerous in a `To` header (commas,
/// semicolons, angle brackets, quotes, whitespace, control characters).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `email` - the proposed address.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "email"`.
pub(crate) fn check_email(email: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let refuse = |reason: &str| OkfError::LimitExceeded {
        limit: "email",
        reason: format!("{email:?} is not an email address: {reason}"),
    };
    if email.len() > MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH {
        return Err(refuse("it is longer than 254 characters"));
    }
    // `split_once` splits at the first '@' only, like Python's
    // `str.partition`; `None` when there is no '@' at all.
    let Some((local, domain)) = email.split_once('@') else {
        return Err(refuse("it has no '@'"));
    };
    if local.is_empty() || domain.is_empty() || domain.contains('@') {
        return Err(refuse("it needs one '@' with text on both sides"));
    }
    let forbidden = |c: char| c.is_whitespace() || c.is_control() || "<>,;\"()[]\\".contains(c);
    if email.chars().any(forbidden) {
        return Err(refuse("it contains a space, a control character or one of <>,;\"()[]\\"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Sets or clears a user's email address. A changed address also deletes
/// the user's outstanding emailed links, so a link sent to the old address
/// stops working.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `name` - the user's name.
/// * `email` - the new address, or `None` to clear it.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] for a malformed address; [`OkfError::Refused`]
/// when another user has it (in any letter case); [`OkfError::UnknownName`];
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn set_email(pool: &PgPool, name: &str, email: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    // `Option::map(check_email)` runs the check only for `Some`;
    // `transpose` turns `Option<Result<..>>` into `Result<Option<..>>` for `?`.
    email.map(check_email).transpose()?;
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // The subquery reads (and locks) the old value, so `changed` compares it
    // with the new one in the same statement (the `set_owner` pattern).
    let updated = sqlx::query_as::<_, (String, bool)>(
        "UPDATE users u SET email = $2::citext \
         FROM (SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE name = $1 FOR UPDATE) old \
         WHERE u.id = old.id \
         RETURNING u.id, old.email IS DISTINCT FROM u.email",
    )
    .bind(name)
    .bind(email)
    .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
    .await;
    let (user_id, changed) = match updated {
        Ok(Some(row)) => row,
        Ok(None) => return Err(unknown(name)),
        // `users.email` is the only UNIQUE column this statement writes.
        Err(error) if is_unique_violation(&error) => {
            return Err(OkfError::Refused {
                reason: "Another user has this email".to_string(),
            })
        }
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    };
    if changed {
        sqlx::query("DELETE FROM email_tokens WHERE user_id = $1")
            .bind(&user_id)
            .execute(&mut *tx)
            .await?;
    }
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Turns a user's admin flag on or off. A change bumps the administrative
/// generation (a session's level depends on it) and ends the user's console
/// sessions, so its next request signs in again with the new flag.
///
/// Every admin row is locked first, in id order, then the user's row: two
/// concurrent "off" calls on the last two admins serialize, and the second
/// sees only one admin left. (A concurrent "on" for another user is not
/// counted until it commits, which only ever refuses more, never less.)
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `name` - the user's name.
/// * `on` - the new flag.
/// * `allow_last` - lets the last admin user be cleared (the CLI, which has
///   operator access; Decision 16). The API passes `false`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The flag before the call.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`]; [`OkfError::Refused`] when clearing the last
/// admin user without `allow_last`; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn set_admin(
    pool: &PgPool,
    name: &str,
    on: bool,
    allow_last: bool,
) -> Result<bool, OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    let admins: Vec<String> =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE is_admin ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE")
            .fetch_all(&mut *tx)
            .await?;
    let (user_id, previous): (String, bool) =
        sqlx::query_as("SELECT id, is_admin FROM users WHERE name = $1 FOR UPDATE")
            .bind(name)
            .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
            .await?
            .ok_or_else(|| unknown(name))?;
    if previous == on {
        // Nothing to write; dropping `tx` rolls back the locks.
        return Ok(previous);
    }
    if !on && !allow_last && admins.len() <= 1 {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: format!("{name:?} is the last admin user; make another user an admin first"),
        });
    }
    sqlx::query("UPDATE users SET is_admin = $2 WHERE id = $1")
        .bind(&user_id)
        .bind(on)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM user_sessions WHERE user_id = $1")
        .bind(&user_id)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(previous)
}

/// The user whose email is `email`, compared case-insensitively.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `email` - the address as typed.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user, or `None`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn find_by_email(pool: &PgPool, email: &str) -> Result<Option<UserAuth>, OkfError> {
    // `$1::citext`: without the cast, `citext = text` would compare as text,
    // case-sensitively.
    Ok(sqlx::query_as::<_, UserAuth>(concat!(
        "SELECT ",
        user_auth_columns!(),
        " FROM users u WHERE u.email = $1::citext"
    ))
    .bind(email)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?)
}

/// The user with id `user_id`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - a `users.id`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user, or `None`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn find_auth(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str) -> Result<Option<UserAuth>, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query_as::<_, UserAuth>(concat!(
        "SELECT ",
        user_auth_columns!(),
        " FROM users u WHERE u.id = $1"
    ))
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Add `clock::after` and its test.** In `src/clock.rs`, after `format_timestamp`:

```rust
/// `now` plus a configured duration, checked: a duration too long for a
/// timestamp is refused instead of panicking or wrapping.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `now` - the start (server clock).
/// * `duration` - how long after it (a std `Duration`, as config and
///   settings hold them).
///
/// # Returns
/// The instant `duration` after `now`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`crate::error::OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "duration"` when
/// the sum is past chrono's range.
pub fn after(
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    duration: std::time::Duration,
) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>, crate::error::OkfError> {
    // `from_std` fails for durations beyond chrono's range; `checked_add_signed`
    // for sums beyond the calendar's. `and_then` chains the two `Option`s.
    chrono::TimeDelta::from_std(duration)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|delta| now.checked_add_signed(delta))
        .ok_or_else(|| crate::error::OkfError::LimitExceeded {
            limit: "duration",
            reason: format!("{duration:?} is too long"),
        })
}
```

```rust
    fn after_adds_a_std_duration_and_refuses_an_absurd_one() {
        let start = Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2026, 11, 12, 12, 0, 0).unwrap();

        let later = after(start, std::time::Duration::from_secs(90)).unwrap();
        let absurd = after(start, std::time::Duration::from_secs(u64::MAX));

        assert_eq!(later, Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2026, 11, 12, 12, 1, 30).unwrap());
```

```rust
        let wrong = verify_user(&db.pool, &alice.id, "orbit staple violet", now()).await.unwrap();
        let unknown = verify_user(&db.pool, "no-such-id", GOOD, now()).await.unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(right, SignInOutcome::Ok(ref user) if user.id == alice.id));
        assert_eq!(wrong, SignInOutcome::Failed);
        assert_eq!(unknown, SignInOutcome::Failed);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn ten_failures_lock_for_fifteen_minutes_even_against_the_right_password() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", Some("alice@example.com")).await;
        set(&db.pool, &alice.id, GOOD, now()).await.unwrap();

        let mut outcomes = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..LOCK_AFTER {
            outcomes.push(verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", "wrong", now()).await.unwrap());
        }
        let while_locked = verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", GOOD, now()).await.unwrap();
        let just_before = now() + TimeDelta::minutes(LOCK_MINUTES) - TimeDelta::seconds(1);
        let still_locked = verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", GOOD, just_before).await.unwrap();
        let after = now() + TimeDelta::minutes(LOCK_MINUTES) + TimeDelta::seconds(1);
        let unlocked = verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", GOOD, after).await.unwrap();

        // `[..9]` is a slice of the first nine, like Python's `outcomes[:9]`.
        assert!(outcomes[..9].iter().all(|o| *o == SignInOutcome::Failed), "{outcomes:?}");
        assert_eq!(outcomes[9], SignInOutcome::Locked);
        assert_eq!(while_locked, SignInOutcome::Locked);
        assert_eq!(still_locked, SignInOutcome::Locked);
        assert_eq!(unlocked, SignInOutcome::Ok(alice));
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn a_success_resets_the_failure_count() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", Some("alice@example.com")).await;
        set(&db.pool, &alice.id, GOOD, now()).await.unwrap();
        for _ in 0..LOCK_AFTER - 1 {
            verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", "wrong", now()).await.unwrap();
        }

        verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", GOOD, now()).await.unwrap();
        let next = verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", "wrong", now()).await.unwrap();

        assert_eq!(next, SignInOutcome::Failed, "the count started again from zero");
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn setting_a_password_checks_the_policy_clears_a_lock_and_knows_the_user() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", Some("alice@example.com")).await;
        sqlx::query("UPDATE users SET failed_sign_ins = 4, locked_until = $2 WHERE id = $1")
            .bind(&alice.id)
            .bind(now() + TimeDelta::hours(1))
            .execute(&db.pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();

        let weak = set(&db.pool, &alice.id, "short", now()).await;
        set(&db.pool, &alice.id, GOOD, now()).await.unwrap();
        let unknown = set(&db.pool, "no-such-id", GOOD, now()).await;

        assert!(matches!(weak, Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded { limit: "password", .. })));
        assert!(matches!(unknown, Err(OkfError::UnknownName { noun: "user", .. })));
        assert_eq!(
            verify(&db.pool, "alice@example.com", GOOD, now()).await.unwrap(),
            SignInOutcome::Ok(alice)
        );
    }
}
```

> **Corrected (issue #312, 2026-11-12).** What shipped differs from the code below in three ways; read `src/store/passwords.rs`.
> - `DUMMY_HASH` is a `const &str`: a PHC string (argon2id, m=19456, t=2, p=1) of a random password that was thrown away. A `LazyLock` would compute argon2 on an async worker thread at the first unknown email, and that first answer would take twice as long. The test uses `DUMMY_HASH` (not `&DUMMY_HASH`) and also checks that it parses.
> - `check_candidate` hands off to `record_success` and `record_failure`. The row it read can be stale by the time argon2 finishes. So the success `UPDATE` only clears the counters `WHERE password_hash = <the hash it checked>` and while `locked_until` is not in the future. It answers `Locked` if a concurrent failure locked the account meanwhile, and `Failed` if the password changed or the user is gone. The failure `UPDATE` leaves the counter and lock alone while the account is already locked. Its CASEs first test `locked_until > now`, so a failure that read the row before the lock does not count during it. Both use `fetch_optional`, so a user deleted meanwhile is `Failed`, not a database error.
> - The candidate `SELECT` is the `candidate_columns!` macro shared by `verify`, `verify_user` and the tests. `matches_off_thread` and `set` map a `JoinError` with `map_err(hasher_error)` directly, with no `.to_string()`.
>
> Tests added: `concurrent_failures_all_count` (nine at once leave the counter at nine), `ten_concurrent_failures_lock_exactly_once`, `a_lock_set_while_the_right_password_is_checked_still_holds`, `a_failure_that_read_the_row_before_a_lock_does_not_count_during_it` and `the_old_password_checked_while_it_is_changed_fails`.

```rust
//! Local passwords (spec "Passwords"): the policy, argon2id hashing at
//! OWASP's parameters, and sign-in verification with a durable lockout
//! (Decision 8: `users.failed_sign_ins` and `users.locked_until`).
//!
//! Every verification costs one argon2 check, whatever the outcome: an
//! unknown email, or a user without a password, is checked against a dummy
//! hash, so the response time does not tell an attacker which emails exist.
//! Hashing is CPU-bound (19 MiB, two passes), so it runs on tokio's
//! blocking pool, never on an async worker thread.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::sync::LazyLock;

// The traits must be in scope for their methods (`hash_password`,
// `verify_password`) to be callable on `Argon2`, as with Python mixins.
use argon2::password_hash::{PasswordHasher, PasswordVerifier};
use argon2::{Argon2, PasswordHash};
use chrono::{DateTime, TimeDelta, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::store::users::{user_auth_columns, UserAuth};

/// The shortest password accepted, in characters (Unicode code points).
pub const MIN_LENGTH: usize = 12;

/// The longest password accepted, in characters: argon2 takes any length,
/// but a megabyte "password" is a cheap way to burn CPU.
pub const MAX_LENGTH: usize = 1024;

/// Consecutive failures that lock an account.
pub const LOCK_AFTER: i32 = 10;

/// How long a locked account stays locked.
pub const LOCK_MINUTES: i64 = 15;

/// The bundled common-password list, lowercase, one per line (`#` lines are
/// comments). Only entries of at least [`MIN_LENGTH`] characters matter,
/// since shorter ones fail the length rule first.
// `LazyLock` builds the set on first use and shares it after, like a
// module-level constant computed once in Python. `include_str!` embeds the
// file's text in the binary at compile time.
static COMMON: LazyLock<HashSet<&'static str>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    include_str!("common_passwords.txt")
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty() && !line.starts_with('#'))
        .collect()
});

/// A hash of a fixed password under the default parameters, checked when
/// there is no real hash to check, so that path costs the same time.
static DUMMY_HASH: LazyLock<String> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    // A fixed salt: this hash protects nothing, it only has to cost what a
    // real check costs. With fixed, valid inputs hashing cannot fail.
    let hashed: PasswordHash = Argon2::default()
        .hash_password_with_salt(b"okf dummy password", b"okf-dummy-salt-0")
        .expect("argon2 hashes a fixed password with a fixed 16-byte salt");
    hashed.to_string()
});

/// The outcome of a password sign-in. Every non-`Ok` outcome answers the
/// same 401 to the client; the difference is for the audit log.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SignInOutcome {
    /// The password matched an unlocked account.
    Ok(UserAuth),
    /// Unknown email, no password set, or a wrong password.
    Failed,
    /// The account is locked (or this failure locked it).
    Locked,
}

/// Checks a proposed password against the policy: 12 to 1024 characters,
/// not in the bundled common list (compared in lowercase). No composition
/// rules.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `password` - the proposed password.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "password"`, naming the rule.
pub fn check_policy(password: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let refuse = |reason: String| OkfError::LimitExceeded {
        limit: "password",
        reason,
    };
    let length = password.chars().count();
    if length < MIN_LENGTH {
        return Err(refuse(format!(
            "a password needs at least {MIN_LENGTH} characters"
        )));
    }
    if length > MAX_LENGTH {
        return Err(refuse(format!(
            "a password may have at most {MAX_LENGTH} characters"
        )));
    }
    if COMMON.contains(password.to_lowercase().as_str()) {
        return Err(refuse(
            "this password is on a list of common passwords; choose another".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Hashes a password with argon2id (m=19456 KiB, t=2, p=1) and a fresh
/// 16-byte salt from the OS. CPU-bound: call it from `spawn_blocking`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `password` - the password (already through [`check_policy`]).
///
/// # Returns
/// The PHC string (`$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$<salt>$<hash>`).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Io`] if the OS random source fails.
pub fn hash(password: &str) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    let hashed: PasswordHash = Argon2::default()
        .hash_password(password.as_bytes())
        .map_err(hasher_error)?;
    Ok(hashed.to_string())
}

/// Does `password` match the stored PHC string? The parameters come from
/// the string, and the comparison is constant-time. A malformed string
/// matches nothing.
fn matches(stored: &str, password: &str) -> bool {
    Argon2::default()
        .verify_password(password.as_bytes(), stored)
        .is_ok()
}

/// [`matches`] on tokio's blocking pool. Takes owned strings because the
/// closure outlives this call's borrows.
async fn matches_off_thread(stored: String, password: String) -> Result<bool, OkfError> {
    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || matches(&stored, &password))
        .await
        .map_err(|error| hasher_error(error.to_string()))
}

/// The error for a hasher that could not run (no OS randomness, or its
/// blocking task died).
fn hasher_error(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> OkfError {
    OkfError::Io {
        path: "<password hasher>".to_string(),
        source: std::io::Error::other(error.to_string()),
    }
}

/// One `users` row as sign-in reads it. No `Debug`: it holds the hash.
#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
struct Candidate {
    #[sqlx(flatten)]
    user: UserAuth,
    password_hash: Option<String>,
    locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
}

/// Checks an email and password, keeping the lockout counters.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `email` - as typed (compared case-insensitively).
/// * `password` - as typed.
/// * `now` - the attempt's time (server clock), for the lock.
///
/// # Returns
/// [`SignInOutcome::Ok`] with the user; [`SignInOutcome::Failed`] for an
/// unknown email, a user without a password or a wrong password;
/// [`SignInOutcome::Locked`] for a locked account, or for the failure that
/// locks it.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]; [`OkfError::Io`] if the hasher task fails.
pub async fn verify(
    pool: &PgPool,
    email: &str,
    password: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<SignInOutcome, OkfError> {
    let candidate = sqlx::query_as::<_, Candidate>(concat!(
        "SELECT ",
        user_auth_columns!(),
        ", u.password_hash, u.locked_until FROM users u WHERE u.email = $1::citext"
    ))
    .bind(email)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?;
    check_candidate(pool, candidate, password, now).await
}

/// Checks the password of the user with this id, with the same lockout
/// rules as [`verify`] (Task 10b's password change checks the current
/// password of a signed-in user, who may have no email).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user's `users.id`.
/// * `password` - as typed.
/// * `now` - the attempt's time (server clock), for the lock.
///
/// # Returns
/// As [`verify`]; an unknown id is [`SignInOutcome::Failed`].
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]; [`OkfError::Io`] if the hasher task fails.
pub async fn verify_user(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    password: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<SignInOutcome, OkfError> {
    let candidate = sqlx::query_as::<_, Candidate>(concat!(
        "SELECT ",
        user_auth_columns!(),
        ", u.password_hash, u.locked_until FROM users u WHERE u.id = $1"
    ))
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?;
    check_candidate(pool, candidate, password, now).await
}

/// The shared body of [`verify`] and [`verify_user`], once the user row
/// (if any) is read: the hash check, the lock, and the failure counter.
async fn check_candidate(
    pool: &PgPool,
    candidate: Option<Candidate>,
    password: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<SignInOutcome, OkfError> {
    // No user, or no password: spend the same time on the dummy hash.
    let Some((candidate, stored)) =
        candidate.and_then(|c| c.password_hash.clone().map(|stored| (c, stored)))
    else {
        matches_off_thread(DUMMY_HASH.clone(), password.to_string()).await?;
        return Ok(SignInOutcome::Failed);
    };
    let matched = matches_off_thread(stored, password.to_string()).await?;
    // Checked after the hash, so a locked account costs the same time too.
    if candidate.locked_until.is_some_and(|until| until > now) {
        return Ok(SignInOutcome::Locked);
    }
    if matched {
        sqlx::query("UPDATE users SET failed_sign_ins = 0, locked_until = NULL WHERE id = $1")
            .bind(&candidate.user.id)
            .execute(pool)
            .await?;
        return Ok(SignInOutcome::Ok(candidate.user));
    }
    // One atomic statement, so concurrent failures all count. The CASEs read
    // the old count; the failure that reaches LOCK_AFTER sets the lock and
    // starts the count again, so the next failure after the lock ends does
    // not lock at once.
    let locked: bool = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "UPDATE users SET \
             failed_sign_ins = CASE WHEN failed_sign_ins + 1 >= $2 THEN 0 \
                                    ELSE failed_sign_ins + 1 END, \
             locked_until = CASE WHEN failed_sign_ins + 1 >= $2 THEN $3 \
                                 ELSE locked_until END \
         WHERE id = $1 \
         RETURNING COALESCE(locked_until > $4, false)",
    )
    .bind(&candidate.user.id)
    .bind(LOCK_AFTER)
    .bind(now + TimeDelta::minutes(LOCK_MINUTES))
    .bind(now)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(if locked {
        SignInOutcome::Locked
    } else {
        SignInOutcome::Failed
    })
}

/// Sets a user's password (after the policy), records when, and clears the
/// lockout counters. Revoking other sessions is the caller's choice (spec
/// "Revocation").
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - a `users.id`.
/// * `password` - the new password.
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] from [`check_policy`]; [`OkfError::UnknownName`]
/// for an unknown id; [`OkfError::Io`] if hashing fails; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn set(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    password: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    check_policy(password)?;
    let owned = password.to_string();
    // The first `?` is the task's (did it run?), the second `hash`'s own.
    let hashed = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || hash(&owned))
        .await
        .map_err(|error| hasher_error(error.to_string()))??;
    let updated = sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE users SET password_hash = $2, password_changed_at = $3, \
                          failed_sign_ins = 0, locked_until = NULL \
         WHERE id = $1",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(&hashed)
    .bind(now)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?
    .rows_affected();
    if updated == 0 {
        return Err(OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "user",
            name: user_id.to_string(),
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

> **Corrected (issue #312, 2026-11-12).** `issue` locks the user row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, not `FOR KEY SHARE`. Two concurrent issues for one user could otherwise both delete the old token and both insert, leaving two live links. The stronger lock also makes `users::delete` and `set_email` wait for the insert. `two_concurrent_uses_give_one_user_and_one_gone` shipped as `concurrent_uses_give_one_user_and_the_rest_gone` (eight redeems on spawned tasks, multi-threaded runtime).
```rust
//! Single-use emailed links (spec "Emailed links"): setup and reset
//! tokens. A token is 256 random bits in base64url; only its SHA-256 is
//! stored. Issuing one deletes the user's older tokens of the same purpose,
//! and redeeming one marks it used in the statement that checks it.

use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::keys;
use crate::store::users::{user_auth_columns, UserAuth};

/// What a link is for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Purpose {
    /// The first password or passkey (`/account/setup`).
    Setup,
    /// A forgotten password (`/account/reset`).
    Reset,
}

impl Purpose {
    /// The `email_tokens.purpose` spelling.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `"setup"` or `"reset"`.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Purpose::Setup => "setup",
            Purpose::Reset => "reset",
        }
    }
}

/// The answer for every link that does not work, whatever the reason, so
/// the page never says whether a token ever existed.
fn gone() -> OkfError {
    OkfError::Gone {
        reason: "This link has expired. Ask for a new one.".to_string(),
    }
}

/// Issues a link token for a user, deleting its older tokens of the same
/// purpose.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - a `users.id`.
/// * `purpose` - setup or reset.
/// * `ttl` - how long it works (`setup_link_ttl` or `reset_link_ttl`).
/// * `now` - when it is issued (server clock).
///
/// # Returns
/// The raw token, to put in the link. Never stored or logged.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user; [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`]
/// for an absurd `ttl`; [`OkfError::Io`] if the OS random source fails;
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn issue(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    purpose: Purpose,
    ttl: Duration,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    let expires_at = crate::clock::after(now, ttl)?;
    let token = keys::generate_with("")?;
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // `FOR KEY SHARE`, as `users::id_of` does: a concurrent user delete
    // waits for this insert instead of failing it with a foreign-key error.
    let exists: Option<String> =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR KEY SHARE")
            .bind(user_id)
            .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
            .await?;
    if exists.is_none() {
        return Err(OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "user",
            name: user_id.to_string(),
        });
    }
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM email_tokens WHERE user_id = $1 AND purpose = $2")
        .bind(user_id)
        .bind(purpose.as_str())
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO email_tokens (hash, user_id, purpose, created_at, expires_at) \
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)",
    )
    .bind(keys::hash(&token).as_slice())
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(purpose.as_str())
    .bind(now)
    .bind(expires_at)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(token)
}

/// Uses a link token: marks it used and returns its user, in one statement,
/// so two concurrent uses cannot both succeed.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `token` - the raw token from the link.
/// * `purpose` - what the page expects.
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Returns
/// The token's user.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Gone`] for an unknown, used, expired or wrong-purpose token;
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn redeem(
    pool: &PgPool,
    token: &str,
    purpose: Purpose,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<UserAuth, OkfError> {
    sqlx::query_as::<_, UserAuth>(concat!(
        "WITH used AS (UPDATE email_tokens SET used_at = $3 \
                       WHERE hash = $1 AND purpose = $2 AND used_at IS NULL \
                         AND expires_at > $3 \
                       RETURNING user_id) \
         SELECT ",
        user_auth_columns!(),
        " FROM used JOIN users u ON u.id = used.user_id"
    ))
    .bind(keys::hash(token).as_slice())
    .bind(purpose.as_str())
    .bind(now)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?
    .ok_or_else(gone)
}

/// Checks a link token without using it (the page shown before the form is
/// submitted).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `token` - the raw token from the link.
/// * `purpose` - what the page expects.
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Returns
/// The token's user.
///
/// # Errors
/// As [`redeem`].
pub async fn peek(
    pool: &PgPool,
    token: &str,
    purpose: Purpose,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<UserAuth, OkfError> {
    sqlx::query_as::<_, UserAuth>(concat!(
        "SELECT ",
        user_auth_columns!(),
        " FROM email_tokens t JOIN users u ON u.id = t.user_id \
          WHERE t.hash = $1 AND t.purpose = $2 AND t.used_at IS NULL AND t.expires_at > $3"
    ))
    .bind(keys::hash(token).as_slice())
    .bind(purpose.as_str())
    .bind(now)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?
    .ok_or_else(gone)
}

/// Deletes tokens that expired before `before`, used or not (`App::poll`'s
/// hourly prune keeps a week for diagnosis).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `before` - the cutoff.
///
/// # Returns
/// How many were deleted.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn prune(pool: &PgPool, before: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<u64, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query("DELETE FROM email_tokens WHERE expires_at < $1")
        .bind(before)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?
        .rows_affected())
}

        let token = issue(&db.pool, &alice.id, Purpose::Setup, HOUR, now()).await.unwrap();
        let first = redeem(&db.pool, &token, Purpose::Setup, now()).await;

        assert_eq!(token.len(), 43);
        assert_eq!(first.unwrap(), alice);
        assert!(matches!(second, Err(OkfError::Gone { .. })), "{second:?}");

        let token = issue(&db.pool, &alice.id, Purpose::Reset, HOUR, now()).await.unwrap();

        let expired = redeem(&db.pool, &token, Purpose::Reset, now() + TimeDelta::hours(1)).await;
        let wrong_purpose = redeem(&db.pool, &token, Purpose::Setup, now()).await;
        let unknown = redeem(&db.pool, "not-a-token", Purpose::Reset, now()).await;

        for result in [expired, wrong_purpose, unknown] {

        let reset = issue(&db.pool, &alice.id, Purpose::Reset, HOUR, now()).await.unwrap();

        let new_setup = issue(&db.pool, &alice.id, Purpose::Setup, HOUR, now()).await.unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(

        assert_eq!(redeem(&db.pool, &new_setup, Purpose::Setup, now()).await.unwrap(), alice);

        let pruned = prune(&db.pool, now() + TimeDelta::hours(2)).await.unwrap();
```

```rust
//! The sign-in audit (spec "Logging and audit"): one row per attempt,
//! shown to the user and to admins, pruned after 90 days. Recording also
//! writes the `info` log line, so the two never disagree. Secrets are never
//! part of an event.

use std::net::IpAddr;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::error::OkfError;

/// How someone tried to sign in.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Method {
    /// Email and password.
    Password,
    /// A passkey (WebAuthn).
    Passkey,
    /// A linked OIDC identity.
    Oidc,
    /// A setup link (the first sign-in).
    Setup,
}

/// How the attempt ended.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Outcome {
    /// Signed in.
    Ok,
    /// Refused.
    Failed,
    /// Refused because the account is locked.
    Locked,
}

impl Method {
    /// The `sign_in_events.method` spelling.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `"password"`, `"passkey"`, `"oidc"` or `"setup"`.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Method::Password => "password",
            Method::Passkey => "passkey",
            Method::Oidc => "oidc",
            Method::Setup => "setup",
        }
    }

    /// Reads a stored spelling.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `text` - a `sign_in_events.method` value.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The method, or `None` for an unknown spelling.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match text {
            "password" => Some(Method::Password),
            "passkey" => Some(Method::Passkey),
            "oidc" => Some(Method::Oidc),
            "setup" => Some(Method::Setup),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

impl Outcome {
    /// The `sign_in_events.outcome` spelling.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `"ok"`, `"failed"` or `"locked"`.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Outcome::Ok => "ok",
            Outcome::Failed => "failed",
            Outcome::Locked => "locked",
        }
    }

    /// Reads a stored spelling.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `text` - a `sign_in_events.outcome` value.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The outcome, or `None` for an unknown spelling.
    pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match text {
            "ok" => Some(Outcome::Ok),
            "failed" => Some(Outcome::Failed),
            "locked" => Some(Outcome::Locked),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// One recorded attempt.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SignInEvent {
    /// How.
    pub method: Method,
    /// With what result.
    pub outcome: Outcome,
    /// From where, when known.
    pub ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// When (server clock).
    pub at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

/// Records an attempt and logs it at `info`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user, when the attempt named a known one (`None` for
///   an unknown email: the row is kept for counting, shown to nobody).
/// * `method` - how.
/// * `outcome` - with what result.
/// * `ip` - the client address, when known.
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn record(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: Option<&str>,
    method: Method,
    outcome: Outcome,
    ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    tracing::info!(
        user_id = user_id.unwrap_or("-"),
        method = method.as_str(),
        outcome = outcome.as_str(),
        ip = ip.map(|address| address.to_string()).as_deref().unwrap_or("-"),
        "sign-in attempt"
    );
    // The address goes in as text and is cast to `inet` by Postgres, so no
    // sqlx network-type feature is needed.
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO sign_in_events (user_id, method, outcome, ip, at) \
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::inet, $5)",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(method.as_str())
    .bind(outcome.as_str())
    .bind(ip.map(|address| address.to_string()))
    .bind(now)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// A user's most recent attempts, newest first.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user` - the user's name.
/// * `limit` - how many at most.
///
/// # Returns
/// The events.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`]; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn recent(pool: &PgPool, user: &str, limit: i64) -> Result<Vec<SignInEvent>, OkfError> {
    let user_id: String = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = $1")
        .bind(user)
        .fetch_optional(pool)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "user",
            name: user.to_string(),
        })?;
    // `host(ip)` is the address as text without a prefix length.
    let rows: Vec<(String, String, Option<String>, DateTime<Utc>)> = sqlx::query_as(
        "SELECT method, outcome, host(ip), at FROM sign_in_events \
         WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $2",
    )
    .bind(&user_id)
    .bind(limit)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(method, outcome, ip, at)| SignInEvent {
            // The table's CHECK constraints admit only these spellings.
            method: Method::parse(&method).expect("sign_in_events.method is checked"),
            outcome: Outcome::parse(&outcome).expect("sign_in_events.outcome is checked"),
            ip: ip.and_then(|text| text.parse().ok()),
            at,
        })
        .collect())
}

/// Deletes events from before `before` (the hourly prune passes 90 days ago).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `before` - the cutoff.
///
/// # Returns
/// How many were deleted.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn prune(pool: &PgPool, before: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<u64, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query("DELETE FROM sign_in_events WHERE at < $1")
        .bind(before)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?
        .rows_affected())
}

    use crate::db::test_db;
    use crate::store::users::tests::seed_user;
    use chrono::TimeDelta;

    fn now() -> DateTime<Utc> {
        DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339("2026-11-12T12:00:00Z")
            .unwrap()
            .with_timezone(&Utc)
    }

    #[test]
    fn spellings_round_trip() {
        for method in [Method::Password, Method::Passkey, Method::Oidc, Method::Setup] {
            assert_eq!(Method::parse(method.as_str()), Some(method));
        }
        for outcome in [Outcome::Ok, Outcome::Failed, Outcome::Locked] {
            assert_eq!(Outcome::parse(outcome.as_str()), Some(outcome));
        }
        assert_eq!(Method::parse("magic"), None);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn recent_is_newest_first_limited_and_keeps_the_address() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", None).await;
        let ip: IpAddr = "192.0.2.7".parse().unwrap();
        record(&db.pool, Some(&alice.id), Method::Password, Outcome::Failed, Some(ip), now())
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let later = now() + TimeDelta::minutes(1);
        record(&db.pool, Some(&alice.id), Method::Passkey, Outcome::Ok, None, later)
            .await
            .unwrap();
        record(&db.pool, None, Method::Password, Outcome::Failed, Some(ip), later)
            .await
            .unwrap();

        let one = recent(&db.pool, "alice", 1).await.unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            all,
            [
                SignInEvent { method: Method::Passkey, outcome: Outcome::Ok, ip: None, at: later },
                SignInEvent { method: Method::Password, outcome: Outcome::Failed, ip: Some(ip), at: now() },
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(one.len(), 1);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn an_unknown_user_is_unknown_name_and_prune_drops_old_events() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = seed_user(&db.pool, "alice", None).await;
        record(&db.pool, Some(&alice.id), Method::Setup, Outcome::Ok, None, now())
            .await
            .unwrap();

        let unknown = recent(&db.pool, "nobody", 10).await;
        let kept = prune(&db.pool, now()).await.unwrap();
        let pruned = prune(&db.pool, now() + TimeDelta::seconds(1)).await.unwrap();

        assert!(matches!(unknown, Err(OkfError::UnknownName { noun: "user", .. })));
        assert_eq!((kept, pruned), (0, 1));
    }
}
```

```markdown
# M12 Task 4: Users gain email, admin flag and password; emailed links and sign-in events

## Added
- `store::users::{set_email, set_admin, find_by_email, find_auth}` and `UserAuth`. `UserRecord` (and the API's user object) gains `email`, `is_admin` and `has_password`.

## Changed

- `argon2` and `blake2` build optimized in the dev profile, so the password tests run in seconds.

## Notes
- Clearing the last admin user is refused unless the caller passes `allow_last` (the CLI does; Decision 16).
- Every password outcome costs one argon2 verification, including a locked account and an unknown email.
```

### Task 5: `[auth]` config, `store::settings` and `store::user_sessions`

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/config.rs` (`AuthConfig`, its defaults and validation, `Config.auth`, `check_auth_duration`)
- Create: `src/store/settings.rs`, `src/store/user_sessions.rs`
- Modify: `src/store/mod.rs` (register both, sorted)
- Modify: `src/app.rs` (the effective settings live on `App`, reloaded with the key cache; sessions pruned hourly)
- Test: `config::tests`, `store::settings::tests`, `store::user_sessions::tests`, `app::tests`

**Where settings live at run time.** `App` holds `settings: RwLock<Arc<Settings>>`, loaded in `App::load` right after the key cache and reloaded in `App::reload_keys_if_changed` whenever `admin_generation` moves. `settings::set` and `settings::reset` bump `admin_generation` in their own transaction, so every running server sees a change within one poll interval (and at once on the server that made it, through `settle`). Readers call `app.settings()`, which clones the `Arc` (one atomic increment), and never query `server_settings` per request. The key cache is not the home: settings are not about credentials, and `Keys` has no `AuthConfig` to overlay.

Setting values are validated by one function, `settings::apply`, used both when a value is set (so a bad value is refused with 422) and when stored values are loaded (so a row a newer server wrote, or a hand edit, that this server can't read is logged at `warn` and the config default used, rather than stopping the server). Config defaults go through the same `config::check_auth_duration`.

| Key | Stored as (`server_settings.value`) | Accepts (`settings set KEY VALUE`) |
|---|---|---|
| `password_sign_in` | JSON boolean | `true`, `false`, `on`, `off` |
| `max_keys_per_user` | JSON number | `0` to `1000` |
| `max_key_lifetime` | JSON string (humantime) or `null` | a duration such as `90d`, or `none` |
| `console_session_idle`, `console_session_absolute`, `setup_link_ttl`, `reset_link_ttl` | JSON string (humantime) | a duration above zero |

Console sessions (spec "Sessions", Decision 9): the cookie value is 256 random bits (`keys::generate_with("")`, 43 base64url characters); only `keys::hash` of it is stored, as `user_sessions.id_hash`. `touch` returns `None` (and deletes the row) once `expires_at` passes or the session has been idle for `idle`; otherwise it writes `last_seen_at` only when the stored value is at least a minute old. A session's public handle is `id_prefix`, the first 12 hex characters of its hash: enough to tell sessions apart and revoke one, useless for signing in.

> **Corrected (issue #313, 2026-11-12).** What shipped differs from the code below in seven ways; `src/store/user_sessions.rs` is authoritative.
> - **The CSRF token is derived, not stored.** `csrf = base64url(SHA-256("okf-mcp console session csrf\0" + id))`, 43 characters, computed by `create` and again by `touch` from the raw id. `user_sessions.csrf_token` holds only the hex SHA-256 of the token, so the table holds no secret. `SessionRow` is no longer `sqlx::FromRow` (touch reads a private `Stored` and builds it). Callers see no change: `NewSession.csrf` and `SessionRow.csrf` are still the raw token.
> - **`touch` cannot extend an ended session under concurrency, and writes once per resolution.** Its first statement is the only write: `UPDATE ... SET last_seen_at = $now WHERE id_hash = $1 AND expires_at > $now AND ($idle_cutoff IS NULL OR last_seen_at > $idle_cutoff) AND last_seen_at <= $now - resolution RETURNING ...`. Postgres re-checks the `WHERE` under the row lock, so of concurrent touches one writes and the rest see a fresh row, and a session revoked or ended meanwhile matches nothing. When it writes nothing, a `SELECT` tells "live, no write needed" (the session) from "gone or ended" (`None`, with a delete that re-checks the same limits), so a concurrent writer never causes a false 401. The idle cutoff is `now - idle`, or none when that falls before 1970. (Review of PR #332.)
> - **The write resolution is `min(1 minute, idle / 4)`**, not a fixed minute, so an idle limit of a minute or less (`30s`) still keeps a session in use alive. Short limits are accepted, not refused.
> - **The idle limit has one write resolution of grace.** A use within a resolution of the last write is not recorded, so a session ends only once `last_seen_at + idle + resolution <= now`. That holds in `touch`'s `UPDATE`, its live-check `SELECT` and its conditional delete, which all share `idle_cutoff`. (`list` and `prune` have no idle predicate: `list` shows sessions until they are removed, and `prune` removes by absolute limit only.) The guarantee: a session is never ended sooner than `idle` after its last use, and always by `idle + resolution` after it. With the 12 h default that is 12 h 1 min; with `30s` it is 37.5 s. (Second review of PR #332.)
> - **`revoke_all` takes `impl PgExecutor<'_>`** (a `&PgPool` still works), and `users::set_admin` (Task 4, which wrote the `DELETE` itself) now calls `user_sessions::revoke_all(&mut *tx, &user_id, None)` inside its transaction, so `store::user_sessions` is the only owner of that SQL. Task 4's `seed_session` test helper uses `user_sessions::create`.
> - **`create` keeps the first 256 characters of `User-Agent`** (cut on a character boundary).
>
> - **`check_auth_duration` caps every lifetime at `config::MAX_AUTH_DURATION`, ten years** (humantime years, so `"10years"` is accepted), instead of only chrono's `TimeDelta` range. A value such as `"1000000years"` fits a `TimeDelta` but not a `DateTime` once added to `now`. It is refused ("must be at most 10 years") in the config file (`[auth]` and `[oauth]`), by `settings::set` (422, `limit: "setting"`) and on load: a stored row falls back to the default, so a session can always be created. OAuth token minting (`oauth/token.rs`) now uses `clock::after` (an error, never a panic, past the calendar) instead of `now + delta(..)`, and its private `delta` helper is gone. (Third review of PR #332.)
> Extra tests: `a_late_touch_never_revives_an_ended_session`, `a_revoked_session_is_not_revived_by_a_touch_waiting_on_its_lock`, `a_short_idle_limit_keeps_an_active_session_alive`, `touches_queued_on_the_row_lock_write_once_and_all_stay_signed_in`, `a_burst_of_concurrent_touches_writes_once`, `a_use_too_soon_to_be_written_still_counts_toward_the_idle_limit`, `an_unused_session_ends_once_idle_plus_the_resolution_has_passed`, `settings::tests::a_stored_lifetime_too_long_for_a_timestamp_falls_back_and_sessions_still_start`, `a_long_user_agent_is_cut_at_a_character_boundary`, and in `app::tests` `an_unreadable_stored_setting_never_stops_the_server` and `a_failed_settings_reload_keeps_the_old_settings_and_retries`. `Config::validate`'s `[oauth]` lifetimes now go through `check_auth_duration` too (same messages).

```rust
/// The policy keys can be overridden at run time by `server_settings`
/// (`store::settings`); `trusted_proxy_header` (and Task 9's `oidc`) are

    pub console_session_idle: Duration,
    /// How long a console session lasts at most (`"7d"`).
    #[serde(with = "humantime_serde")]
    pub console_session_absolute: Duration,
    /// How long a setup link works (`"24h"`).
    #[serde(with = "humantime_serde")]
    pub setup_link_ttl: Duration,
    /// How long a password-reset link works (`"1h"`).
    #[serde(with = "humantime_serde")]
    pub reset_link_ttl: Duration,
    /// The header whose last hop is the client's address behind a proxy
    /// (`"x-forwarded-for"`); unset means the peer address (Decision 7).
    pub trusted_proxy_header: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for AuthConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            password_sign_in: true,
            max_keys_per_user: DEFAULT_MAX_KEYS_PER_USER,
            max_key_lifetime: None,
            console_session_idle: DEFAULT_CONSOLE_SESSION_IDLE,
            console_session_absolute: DEFAULT_CONSOLE_SESSION_ABSOLUTE,
            setup_link_ttl: DEFAULT_SETUP_LINK_TTL,
            reset_link_ttl: DEFAULT_RESET_LINK_TTL,
            trusted_proxy_header: None,
        }
    }
}

impl AuthConfig {
    /// Checks the values serde cannot.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// A zero or out-of-range duration, `max_keys_per_user` above
    /// [`MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT`], or a `trusted_proxy_header` that is not
    /// an HTTP header name.
    fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        for (name, value) in [
            ("auth.console_session_idle", self.console_session_idle),
            ("auth.console_session_absolute", self.console_session_absolute),
            ("auth.setup_link_ttl", self.setup_link_ttl),
            ("auth.reset_link_ttl", self.reset_link_ttl),
        ] {
            check_auth_duration(name, value)?;
        }
        if let Some(lifetime) = self.max_key_lifetime {
            check_auth_duration("auth.max_key_lifetime", lifetime)?;
        }
        if self.max_keys_per_user > MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT {
            return Err(format!(
                "auth.max_keys_per_user must be at most {MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT}"
            ));
        }
        if let Some(header) = self.trusted_proxy_header.as_deref() {
            // The same parser axum uses for request headers.
            if axum::http::HeaderName::from_bytes(header.as_bytes()).is_err() {
                return Err(format!(
                    "auth.trusted_proxy_header {header:?} is not an HTTP header name"
                ));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Checks one sign-in policy duration: above zero, and small enough for a
/// timestamp. Shared by the config file and `store::settings`, so a value
/// is accepted or refused the same way in both.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `name` - the key, for the message.
/// * `value` - the duration.
///
/// # Errors
/// The problem in words.
pub(crate) fn check_auth_duration(name: &str, value: Duration) -> Result<(), String> {
    if value.is_zero() {
        return Err(format!("{name} must be more than zero"));
    }
    if chrono::Duration::from_std(value).is_err() {
        return Err(format!("{name} exceeds supported duration"));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
