- [ ] **Step 6: Implement `src/store/settings.rs`** (above the tests) and register it in `src/store/mod.rs` (`pub mod settings;` after `publish`, before `sign_in_events`):

```rust
//! Policy settings (spec "Settings"): the `[auth]` config supplies the
//! defaults, and `server_settings` rows override them. Every change bumps
//! `admin_generation`, so running servers reload the effective settings
//! with the key cache (`App::reload_keys_if_changed`).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
// humantime is the crate humantime_serde parses config durations with;
// `re` re-exports it, so the formats match without another dependency.
use humantime_serde::re::humantime;
use serde_json::Value;
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::config::{check_auth_duration, AuthConfig, MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT};
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::store::catalogs::bump_admin_generation;

/// The effective sign-in policy: config defaults with overrides applied.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Whether `/signin` offers email and password.
    pub password_sign_in: bool,
    /// Live self-issued keys a user may hold.
    pub max_keys_per_user: u32,
    /// The longest self-issued key expiry; `None` is no limit.
    pub max_key_lifetime: Option<Duration>,
    /// Console session idle timeout.
    pub console_session_idle: Duration,
    /// Console session absolute lifetime.
    pub console_session_absolute: Duration,
    /// Setup link lifetime.
    pub setup_link_ttl: Duration,
    /// Password-reset link lifetime.
    pub reset_link_ttl: Duration,
}

impl Settings {
    /// The settings with no overrides.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `config` - the `[auth]` section.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// Its policy values.
    pub fn from_config(config: &AuthConfig) -> Self {
        Self {
            password_sign_in: config.password_sign_in,
            max_keys_per_user: config.max_keys_per_user,
            max_key_lifetime: config.max_key_lifetime,
            console_session_idle: config.console_session_idle,
            console_session_absolute: config.console_session_absolute,
            setup_link_ttl: config.setup_link_ttl,
            reset_link_ttl: config.reset_link_ttl,
        }
    }
}

/// One setting's name. clap spells each exactly as stored
/// (`#[value(name = ...)]`; its default would be kebab-case).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, clap::ValueEnum)]
pub enum SettingKey {
    /// `password_sign_in`.
    #[value(name = "password_sign_in")]
    PasswordSignIn,
    /// `max_keys_per_user`.
    #[value(name = "max_keys_per_user")]
    MaxKeysPerUser,
    /// `max_key_lifetime`.
    #[value(name = "max_key_lifetime")]
    MaxKeyLifetime,
    /// `console_session_idle`.
    #[value(name = "console_session_idle")]
    ConsoleSessionIdle,
    /// `console_session_absolute`.
    #[value(name = "console_session_absolute")]
    ConsoleSessionAbsolute,
    /// `setup_link_ttl`.
    #[value(name = "setup_link_ttl")]
    SetupLinkTtl,
    /// `reset_link_ttl`.
    #[value(name = "reset_link_ttl")]
    ResetLinkTtl,
}

impl SettingKey {
    /// Every key, in the order `settings list` shows them.
    pub const ALL: [SettingKey; 7] = [
        SettingKey::PasswordSignIn,
        SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser,
        SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime,
        SettingKey::ConsoleSessionIdle,
        SettingKey::ConsoleSessionAbsolute,
        SettingKey::SetupLinkTtl,
        SettingKey::ResetLinkTtl,
    ];

    /// The stored name.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The `server_settings.key` value.
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            SettingKey::PasswordSignIn => "password_sign_in",
            SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser => "max_keys_per_user",
            SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime => "max_key_lifetime",
            SettingKey::ConsoleSessionIdle => "console_session_idle",
            SettingKey::ConsoleSessionAbsolute => "console_session_absolute",
            SettingKey::SetupLinkTtl => "setup_link_ttl",
            SettingKey::ResetLinkTtl => "reset_link_ttl",
        }
    }

    /// Reads a stored name.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `name` - a `server_settings.key` value.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The key, or `None` for a name this server does not know.
    pub fn parse(name: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        Self::ALL.into_iter().find(|key| key.as_str() == name)
    }
}

/// One row of `settings list`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SettingRow {
    /// Which setting.
    pub key: SettingKey,
    /// Its effective value, as `settings set` accepts it (`"true"`, `"20"`,
    /// `"12h"`, `"none"`).
    pub value: String,
    /// Whether a `server_settings` row overrides the config default.
    pub overridden: bool,
    /// When the override was written.
    pub updated_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    /// Who wrote it (an actor or user name).
    pub updated_by: Option<String>,
}

/// The refusal for a value a setting cannot take.
fn invalid(reason: String) -> OkfError {
    OkfError::LimitExceeded {
        limit: "setting",
        reason,
    }
}

/// Parses a duration in the config file's format.
fn duration(key: SettingKey, text: &str) -> Result<Duration, String> {
    let parsed = humantime::parse_duration(text)
        .map_err(|error| format!("{}: {text:?} is not a duration ({error})", key.as_str()))?;
    check_auth_duration(key.as_str(), parsed)?;
    Ok(parsed)
}

/// Turns the text `settings set` was given into the JSON to store.
fn parse_value(key: SettingKey, text: &str) -> Result<Value, String> {
    let text = text.trim();
    match key {
        SettingKey::PasswordSignIn => match text {
            "true" | "on" => Ok(Value::Bool(true)),
            "false" | "off" => Ok(Value::Bool(false)),
            _ => Err(format!("password_sign_in takes true or false, not {text:?}")),
        },
        SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser => text
            .parse::<u32>()
            .map(Value::from)
            .map_err(|_| {
                format!("max_keys_per_user takes a whole number from 0 to {MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT}")
            }),
        SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime if text == "none" => Ok(Value::Null),
        // Stored in humantime's own spelling, so `list` shows what `load` reads.
        SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime
        | SettingKey::ConsoleSessionIdle
        | SettingKey::ConsoleSessionAbsolute
        | SettingKey::SetupLinkTtl
        | SettingKey::ResetLinkTtl => duration(key, text)
            .map(|parsed| Value::String(humantime::format_duration(parsed).to_string())),
    }
}

/// Applies one stored value to `settings`, after checking it. Used when
/// setting a value (to refuse a bad one) and when loading (to skip one).
/// On an error `settings` is unchanged.
fn apply(settings: &mut Settings, key: SettingKey, value: &Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    let as_duration = |value: &Value| -> Result<Duration, String> {
        let text = value
            .as_str()
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{} must be a duration string", key.as_str()))?;
        duration(key, text)
    };
    match key {
        SettingKey::PasswordSignIn => {
            settings.password_sign_in = value
                .as_bool()
                .ok_or_else(|| "password_sign_in must be true or false".to_string())?;
        }
        SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser => {
            // `as_u64` is `None` for negatives, fractions and non-numbers;
            // `try_from` refuses what does not fit a `u32`.
            let count = value
                .as_u64()
                .and_then(|count| u32::try_from(count).ok())
                .filter(|count| *count <= MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT)
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    format!("max_keys_per_user must be from 0 to {MAX_KEYS_PER_USER_LIMIT}")
                })?;
            settings.max_keys_per_user = count;
        }
        SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime => {
            settings.max_key_lifetime = match value {
                Value::Null => None,
                other => Some(as_duration(other)?),
            };
        }
        SettingKey::ConsoleSessionIdle => settings.console_session_idle = as_duration(value)?,
        SettingKey::ConsoleSessionAbsolute => {
            settings.console_session_absolute = as_duration(value)?;
        }
        SettingKey::SetupLinkTtl => settings.setup_link_ttl = as_duration(value)?,
        SettingKey::ResetLinkTtl => settings.reset_link_ttl = as_duration(value)?,
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// A setting's effective value as `settings set` would accept it.
fn display(settings: &Settings, key: SettingKey) -> String {
    let format = |value: Duration| humantime::format_duration(value).to_string();
    match key {
        SettingKey::PasswordSignIn => settings.password_sign_in.to_string(),
        SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser => settings.max_keys_per_user.to_string(),
        SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime => settings
            .max_key_lifetime
            .map_or_else(|| "none".to_string(), format),
        SettingKey::ConsoleSessionIdle => format(settings.console_session_idle),
        SettingKey::ConsoleSessionAbsolute => format(settings.console_session_absolute),
        SettingKey::SetupLinkTtl => format(settings.setup_link_ttl),
        SettingKey::ResetLinkTtl => format(settings.reset_link_ttl),
    }
}

/// Overlays stored rows on the defaults, skipping (with a `warn`) rows this
/// server cannot read.
fn overlay<'a>(
    defaults: &AuthConfig,
    rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a Value)>,
) -> Settings {
    let mut settings = Settings::from_config(defaults);
    for (name, value) in rows {
        let Some(key) = SettingKey::parse(name) else {
            tracing::debug!(setting = name, "ignoring a setting this server does not know");
            continue;
        };
        if let Err(problem) = apply(&mut settings, key, value) {
            tracing::warn!(setting = name, %problem, "stored setting is invalid; using the default");
        }
    }
    settings
}

/// One stored override.
#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
struct StoredSetting {
    key: String,
    value: Value,
    updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    updated_by: String,
}

/// Every stored override.
async fn stored(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<Vec<StoredSetting>, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query_as::<_, StoredSetting>(
        "SELECT key, value, updated_at, updated_by FROM server_settings",
    )
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?)
}

/// The effective settings.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `defaults` - the `[auth]` section.
///
/// # Returns
/// The defaults with every readable override applied.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn load(pool: &PgPool, defaults: &AuthConfig) -> Result<Settings, OkfError> {
    let rows = stored(pool).await?;
    Ok(overlay(
        defaults,
        rows.iter().map(|row| (row.key.as_str(), &row.value)),
    ))
}

/// Overrides one setting, and bumps the administrative generation.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `key` - which setting.
/// * `value` - the new value, as text (see the module's table).
/// * `by` - who is setting it, for `settings list`.
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "setting"` for a value the
/// setting cannot take; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn set(
    pool: &PgPool,
    key: SettingKey,
    value: &str,
    by: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let json = parse_value(key, value).map_err(invalid)?;
    // Apply to a scratch copy only to run the same checks `load` will.
    apply(
        &mut Settings::from_config(&AuthConfig::default()),
        key,
        &json,
    )
    .map_err(invalid)?;
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO server_settings (key, value, updated_at, updated_by) \
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4) \
         ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value, \
             updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at, updated_by = EXCLUDED.updated_by",
    )
    .bind(key.as_str())
    .bind(&json)
    .bind(now)
    .bind(by)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Removes a setting's override, so the config default applies again.
/// Bumps the administrative generation when there was one.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `key` - which setting.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn reset(pool: &PgPool, key: SettingKey) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    let deleted = sqlx::query("DELETE FROM server_settings WHERE key = $1")
        .bind(key.as_str())
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?
        .rows_affected();
    if deleted > 0 {
        bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    }
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Every setting with its effective value and override, in
/// [`SettingKey::ALL`] order.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `defaults` - the `[auth]` section.
///
/// # Returns
/// One row per key.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn list(pool: &PgPool, defaults: &AuthConfig) -> Result<Vec<SettingRow>, OkfError> {
    let rows = stored(pool).await?;
    let settings = overlay(
        defaults,
        rows.iter().map(|row| (row.key.as_str(), &row.value)),
    );
    // Index the rows by name once instead of scanning them per key.
    let by_name: HashMap<&str, &StoredSetting> =
        rows.iter().map(|row| (row.key.as_str(), row)).collect();
    Ok(SettingKey::ALL
        .into_iter()
        .map(|key| {
            let row = by_name.get(key.as_str());
            SettingRow {
                key,
                value: display(&settings, key),
                overridden: row.is_some(),
                updated_at: row.map(|row| row.updated_at),
                updated_by: row.map(|row| row.updated_by.clone()),
            }
        })
        .collect())
}
```

```rust
//! Console sessions (spec "Sessions"; named apart from MCP sessions,
//! Decision 9). The `okf_session` cookie carries a 256-bit random id; only
//! its SHA-256 (`crate::keys::hash`, as for API keys) is stored. A session
//! ends when its absolute limit passes, when it sits idle too long, or when
//! it is revoked.

use std::net::IpAddr;
use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::{DateTime, TimeDelta, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::keys;

/// How stale `last_seen_at` may be before a request rewrites it, so an
/// active console writes at most once a minute per session.
const LAST_SEEN_RESOLUTION: TimeDelta = TimeDelta::minutes(1);

/// The length of [`SessionInfo::id_prefix`], in hex characters (6 bytes).
pub const ID_PREFIX_LENGTH: usize = 12;

/// A new session's secrets: the cookie value and the CSRF token. Its
/// `Debug` shows neither.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NewSession {
    /// The raw session id (the cookie's value).
    pub id: String,
    /// The raw CSRF token (sent back in `X-OKF-CSRF`).
    pub csrf: String,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for NewSession {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("NewSession")
            .field("id", &"<redacted>")
            .field("csrf", &"<redacted>")
            .finish()
    }
}

/// A live session, as a request sees it. Its `Debug` hides the CSRF token.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, sqlx::FromRow)]
pub struct SessionRow {
    /// Whose session.
    pub user_id: String,
    /// The CSRF token a cookie-authenticated write must carry.
    #[sqlx(rename = "csrf_token")]
    pub csrf: String,
    /// When it started.
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// When it ends at the latest.
    pub expires_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for SessionRow {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("SessionRow")
            .field("user_id", &self.user_id)
            .field("csrf", &"<redacted>")
            .field("created_at", &self.created_at)
            .field("expires_at", &self.expires_at)
            .finish()
    }
}

/// One session as the account page and `user sessions` list it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SessionInfo {
    /// The first [`ID_PREFIX_LENGTH`] hex characters of the stored hash:
    /// tells sessions apart, signs nobody in.
    pub id_prefix: String,
    /// When it started.
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// When it was last used (to the minute).
    pub last_seen_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// The address it started from, when known.
    pub ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// The browser it started in (`User-Agent`, possibly empty).
    pub user_agent: String,
    /// Whether this is the session asking.
    pub current: bool,
}

/// Starts a session.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - whose session.
/// * `ip` - the client address, when known.
/// * `user_agent` - the `User-Agent` header (empty when absent).
/// * `absolute` - `console_session_absolute`.
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Returns
/// The raw id and CSRF token. Neither is stored.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] for an absurd `absolute`; [`OkfError::Io`]
/// if the OS random source fails; [`OkfError::Database`] (a foreign-key
/// failure for an unknown user).
pub async fn create(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    user_agent: &str,
    absolute: Duration,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<NewSession, OkfError> {
    let expires_at = crate::clock::after(now, absolute)?;
    let session = NewSession {
        id: keys::generate_with("")?,
        csrf: keys::generate_with("")?,
    };
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO user_sessions \
             (id_hash, user_id, csrf_token, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at, ip, user_agent) \
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $4, $5, $6::inet, $7)",
    )
    .bind(keys::hash(&session.id).as_slice())
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(&session.csrf)
    .bind(now)
    .bind(expires_at)
    .bind(ip.map(|address| address.to_string()))
    .bind(user_agent)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(session)
}

/// A stored session with the column `touch` needs beyond [`SessionRow`].
#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
struct Stored {
    #[sqlx(flatten)]
    row: SessionRow,
    last_seen_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

/// Looks a session up for a request: ends it if it is past its absolute
/// limit or idle for `idle`, and otherwise records the activity (at most
/// once a minute).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `id` - the raw id from the cookie.
/// * `idle` - `console_session_idle`.
/// * `now` - the request's time (server clock).
///
/// # Returns
/// The session, or `None` when there is none or it just ended.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn touch(
    pool: &PgPool,
    id: &str,
    idle: Duration,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Option<SessionRow>, OkfError> {
    let hash = keys::hash(id);
    let Some(stored) = sqlx::query_as::<_, Stored>(
        "SELECT user_id, csrf_token, created_at, expires_at, last_seen_at \
         FROM user_sessions WHERE id_hash = $1",
    )
    .bind(hash.as_slice())
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?
    else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    // A configured idle beyond chrono's range never times out.
    let idle_until = TimeDelta::from_std(idle)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|idle| stored.last_seen_at.checked_add_signed(idle));
    let expired = now >= stored.row.expires_at || idle_until.is_some_and(|until| now >= until);
    if expired {
        revoke(pool, id).await?;
        return Ok(None);
    }
    if now - stored.last_seen_at >= LAST_SEEN_RESOLUTION {
        sqlx::query("UPDATE user_sessions SET last_seen_at = $2 WHERE id_hash = $1")
            .bind(hash.as_slice())
            .bind(now)
            .execute(pool)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(Some(stored.row))
}

/// Ends one session (sign-out).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `id` - the raw id from the cookie.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]. An unknown id is not an error.
pub async fn revoke(pool: &PgPool, id: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM user_sessions WHERE id_hash = $1")
        .bind(keys::hash(id).as_slice())
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Ends every session of a user, except perhaps the one asking.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - whose sessions.
/// * `except` - the raw id of a session to keep (the caller's own).
///
/// # Returns
/// How many ended.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn revoke_all(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    except: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<u64, OkfError> {
    // `[u8; 32]` lives in `kept`, so the slice bound below borrows it.
    let kept = except.map(keys::hash);
    Ok(sqlx::query(
        "DELETE FROM user_sessions WHERE user_id = $1 AND ($2::bytea IS NULL OR id_hash <> $2)",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(kept.as_ref().map(|hash| hash.as_slice()))
    .execute(pool)
    .await?
    .rows_affected())
}

/// One row of [`list`] as read.
#[derive(sqlx::FromRow)]
struct Listed {
    id_prefix: String,
    created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    last_seen_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    ip: Option<String>,
    user_agent: String,
    current: bool,
}

/// A user's sessions, most recently used first. Sessions past their limits
/// are included until [`touch`] or [`prune`] removes them.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - whose sessions.
/// * `current` - the raw id of the session asking, to mark it.
///
/// # Returns
/// The sessions.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn list(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    current: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>, OkfError> {
    let current = current.map(keys::hash);
    let rows = sqlx::query_as::<_, Listed>(
        "SELECT encode(substring(id_hash FROM 1 FOR 6), 'hex') AS id_prefix, \
                created_at, last_seen_at, host(ip) AS ip, user_agent, \
                COALESCE(id_hash = $2, false) AS current \
         FROM user_sessions WHERE user_id = $1 \
         ORDER BY last_seen_at DESC, created_at DESC",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(current.as_ref().map(|hash| hash.as_slice()))
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|row| SessionInfo {
            id_prefix: row.id_prefix,
            created_at: row.created_at,
            last_seen_at: row.last_seen_at,
            ip: row.ip.and_then(|text| text.parse().ok()),
            user_agent: row.user_agent,
            current: row.current,
        })
        .collect())
}

/// Ends one of a user's sessions by its [`SessionInfo::id_prefix`].
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - whose session (another user's prefix matches nothing).
/// * `id_prefix` - 12 lowercase hex characters.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] with `noun: "session"` for a malformed prefix
/// or one that matches none of the user's sessions; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn revoke_by_prefix(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    id_prefix: &str,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let unknown = || OkfError::UnknownName {
        noun: "session",
        name: id_prefix.to_string(),
    };
    let well_formed = id_prefix.len() == ID_PREFIX_LENGTH
        && id_prefix
            .bytes()
            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(&byte));
    if !well_formed {
        return Err(unknown());
    }
    let deleted = sqlx::query(
        "DELETE FROM user_sessions \
         WHERE user_id = $1 AND encode(substring(id_hash FROM 1 FOR 6), 'hex') = $2",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(id_prefix)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?
    .rows_affected();
    if deleted == 0 {
        return Err(unknown());
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Deletes sessions past their absolute limit (idle ones go at their next
/// [`touch`], or here once their absolute limit passes).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Returns
/// How many were deleted.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn prune(pool: &PgPool, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<u64, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query("DELETE FROM user_sessions WHERE expires_at <= $1")
        .bind(now)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?
        .rows_affected())
}
```

```markdown
# M12 Task 5: `[auth]` config, policy settings and console sessions

## Added
- `[auth]` in the config file: `password_sign_in`, `max_keys_per_user`, `max_key_lifetime`, `console_session_idle`, `console_session_absolute`, `setup_link_ttl`, `reset_link_ttl` (the policy defaults) and `trusted_proxy_header`.
```

### Task 6: Mail: `Mailer` (SMTP, Postmark, log), templates and the apalis `SendMail` job

**Files:**
- Create: `src/mail/mod.rs`, `src/mail/templates.rs`, `src/mail/smtp.rs`, `src/mail/postmark.rs`, `src/mail/log.rs`, `src/mail/queue.rs`
- Modify: `src/lib.rs` (`pub mod mail;`, and the crate doc's module list)
- Modify: `src/config.rs` (`MailConfig`, `MailProvider`, `SmtpConfig`, `PostmarkConfig`; `Config.mail`; validation)
- Modify: `src/app.rs` (the mailer on `App`, `clock_handle`, mail queue prune in the hourly prune)
- Modify: `src/http/mod.rs:265-292` (`serve` spawns the worker and awaits it on shutdown)
- Modify: `tests/support/pg.rs` `POOL_SIZE` (test pool 4 -> 8, Decision 19; corrected, issue #309: since #304 the size is the `POOL_SIZE` constant, not a literal at line 74), `tests/support/server.rs` (`serve_app` turns the worker off), `src/mcp/testing.rs` (`app_at` turns it off)
- Test: unit tests in each `mail` module, `config::tests`

This task relies on Task 1 for the `apalis`, `apalis-postgres`, `lettre` (features `tokio1-rustls`, `smtp-transport`, `builder`, `ring`, `webpki-roots`, `hostname`), `async-trait` and existing `reqwest` dependencies, for `db::migrate` running `PostgresStorage::setup` and the test template in `tests/support/pg.rs` running apalis' migrations (so every migrated test database, `test_db()` included, has the `apalis` schema; corrected, issue #309, 2026-11-12), and for `SQLX_OFFLINE=true` in the justfile. It relies on Task 4's `users::check_email`.

**How a mail is sent** (Decisions 10, 11 and 19, spec "Background jobs"):

1. A request (or the CLI) calls `queue::enqueue(pool, to, &template, now)` after its own transaction commits. `enqueue` renders the template and inserts one `apalis.jobs` row in queue `send_mail` through `apalis_postgres::queries::push_tasks`, with `max_attempts = 64`. The payload, `SendMail`, is the rendered `Mail`, the template's name, and `queued_at` (Unix seconds, server clock).
2. A worker in each `serve` process (`queue::spawn_worker`, started by `http::serve` unless `[mail] worker = false`) fetches it. The backend is `PostgresStorage::new(..).with_config(queue "send_mail").with_pubsub().poll_with_interval(30 s)`: pubsub wakes it for new jobs, and the interval picks up rescheduled and manually retried ones (apalis's NOTIFY fires only for inserts whose `run_at` has passed). Its name is `okf-mail-<host>-<pid>`, so replicas never share a heartbeat row.
3. The handler sends once through `Arc<dyn Mailer>`:
   - **Ok:** the job is `Done`.
   - **`MailError::Permanent`** (SMTP 5xx, Postmark 4xx other than 401 and 429, a malformed recipient): it returns `AbortError`, so apalis marks the job `Killed` and never fetches it again.
   - **`MailError::Retryable`**, with `queued_at` less than 24 hours ago: it sets the job's `run_at` to `now() + min(30 s * 2^attempts, 1 h)` in SQL and returns a plain error. apalis acks it `Failed` with `attempts + 1` and the error as `last_result`; `get_jobs` fetches it again once `run_at` passes, because `attempts < 64`.
   - **`MailError::Retryable`** after 24 hours: it returns `AbortError` ("gave up after 24 hours: ..."), so the job is `Killed` and keeps its last error.
4. `queue::list` shows pending, sending, retrying and failed jobs (recipient, template, attempts, last error, `run_at`; never the body). `queue::retry` puts a failed job back to `Pending` with `attempts = 0` and a fresh `queued_at`, so it gets a new 24-hour window; `queue::delete` removes one that is not being sent. `queue::prune` (from `App::poll`'s hourly prune) deletes `Done` jobs after 7 days and failed ones after 30.

64 attempts outlast 24 hours: the backoff reaches its 1-hour cap at the 8th retry, and 30 retries already take about 24 hours. A job that somehow reaches 64 (a database failure in every reschedule) is shown as failed, never retried without delay.

SQL over `apalis.jobs` (Task 1's facts: `id text`, `job_type text`, `status text`, `attempts integer`, `max_attempts integer`, `run_at timestamptz`, `last_result jsonb` as `{"Err": "..."}`, `done_at timestamptz` set by every ack, `job bytea` holding the JSON payload, `lock_by`, `lock_at`). Status values: `Pending`, `Queued`, `Running`, `Done`, `Failed`, `Killed`.

| `QueuedMail.status` | Rows |
|---|---|
| `pending` | `Pending` |
| `sending` | `Queued`, `Running` |
| `retrying` | `Failed` with `attempts < max_attempts` |
| `failed` | `Killed`, or `Failed` with `attempts >= max_attempts` |

Secrets: a setup or reset link is in `Mail.text` and `Mail.html` and so in the job payload (spec "Secrets in payloads"). `Mail`, `SendMail` and `Template` get hand-written `Debug` that omits the body and links, and no log line in this module prints a body, except the `log` provider's, whose purpose is exactly that (development and tests; it says so at start). SMTP passwords and Postmark tokens are read from the environment variables the config names when the server starts (`App::load` calls `mail::from_config`), so `serve` fails at once if one is missing; CLI commands that only enqueue never need them.

```rust
/// The default From address: a placeholder that is valid, so a server
/// without `[mail]` starts (with the log provider, it sends nothing).
pub const DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM: &str = "okf <okf@localhost>";

/// Which [`crate::mail::Mailer`] sends mail.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum MailProvider {
    /// An SMTP relay (`[mail.smtp]`).
    Smtp,
    /// Postmark's HTTP API (`[mail.postmark]`).
    Postmark,
    /// Writes each message, links included, to the log at `info`. For
    /// development and tests only.
    #[default]
    Log,
}

/// `[mail.smtp]`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
pub struct SmtpConfig {
    /// The relay's host name.
    pub host: String,
    /// Its port (587 for STARTTLS, 465 for implicit TLS).
    #[serde(default = "default_smtp_port")]
    pub port: u16,
    /// `true`: STARTTLS, required (the session never continues in clear).
    /// `false`: TLS from the first byte. There is no plaintext mode.
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub starttls: bool,
    /// The user to authenticate as, if the relay wants one.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub username: Option<String>,
    /// The environment variable holding the password (required with
    /// `username`).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub password_env: Option<String>,
}

/// `[mail.postmark]`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
pub struct PostmarkConfig {
    /// The environment variable holding the server token.
    pub token_env: String,
    /// The message stream (`"outbound"`, Postmark's default transactional stream).
    #[serde(default = "default_message_stream")]
    pub message_stream: String,
}

/// `serde(default = ...)` takes a function name, not a value.
fn default_smtp_port() -> u16 {
    587
}

fn default_true() -> bool {
    true
}

fn default_message_stream() -> String {
    "outbound".to_string()
}

/// The `[mail]` section. Secrets are not here: only the names of the
/// environment variables that hold them, read when the server starts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
#[serde(default)]
pub struct MailConfig {
    /// Which provider sends.
    pub provider: MailProvider,
    /// The From address (`"okf <okf@example.com>"`).
    pub from: String,
    /// Whether `serve` runs a mail worker. Off for a replica that should only
    /// enqueue, and in the test servers (Decision 19).
    pub worker: bool,
    /// The SMTP relay, for `provider = "smtp"`.
    pub smtp: Option<SmtpConfig>,
    /// Postmark, for `provider = "postmark"`.
    pub postmark: Option<PostmarkConfig>,
}

impl Default for MailConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            provider: MailProvider::Log,
            from: DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM.to_string(),
            worker: true,
            smtp: None,
            postmark: None,
        }
    }
}

impl MailConfig {
    /// Checks what serde cannot: that the chosen provider is configured,
    /// and that `from` is one address.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The problem in words.
    fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        self.from
            .parse::<Mailbox>()
            .map_err(|error| format!("mail.from {:?} is not an address: {error}", self.from))?;
        match self.provider {
            MailProvider::Log => Ok(()),
            MailProvider::Smtp => {
                let Some(smtp) = &self.smtp else {
                    return Err("mail.provider = \"smtp\" needs a [mail.smtp] table".to_string());
                };
                if smtp.host.trim().is_empty() {
                    return Err("mail.smtp.host is blank".to_string());
                }
                if smtp.port == 0 {
                    return Err("mail.smtp.port must be more than zero".to_string());
                }
                if smtp.username.is_some() != smtp.password_env.is_some() {
                    return Err(
                        "mail.smtp.username and mail.smtp.password_env go together".to_string()
                    );
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            MailProvider::Postmark => {
                let Some(postmark) = &self.postmark else {
                    return Err(
                        "mail.provider = \"postmark\" needs a [mail.postmark] table".to_string()
                    );
                };
                if postmark.token_env.trim().is_empty() {
                    return Err("mail.postmark.token_env is blank".to_string());
                }
                if postmark.message_stream.trim().is_empty() {
                    return Err("mail.postmark.message_stream is blank".to_string());
                }
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
            [setup.name(), Template::Reset { link: String::new() }.name(),
             Template::MethodAdded { method: String::new() }.name(), Template::Test.name()],
            ["setup", "reset", "method_added", "test"]
        );
        assert!(!format!("{setup:?}").contains("s3cr3t"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The mail templates (spec "Mail"): plain text with a minimal HTML twin.
//! No template engine: `format!` over fixed text, as the consent pages do,
//! with every interpolated value HTML-escaped in the twin.

use crate::oauth::consent::escape;

/// The setup page's path; the link adds `?token=...`.
pub const SETUP_PATH: &str = "/account/setup";

/// The set-password page a reset link opens.
pub const RESET_PATH: &str = "/account/reset";

/// A message to render. `link`s carry a single-use token, so `Debug` hides them.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Template {
    /// An admin's invitation: choose a password or register a passkey.
    Setup {
        /// The setup link ([`link`] with [`SETUP_PATH`]).
        link: String,
        /// The user's name, for the greeting.
        user: String,
    },
    /// A forgotten password.
    Reset {
        /// The reset link ([`link`] with [`RESET_PATH`]).
        link: String,
    },
    /// A notice after a password change, a new passkey or a linked identity.
    MethodAdded {
        /// What was added, in words ("a passkey", "a password", "Example ID").
        method: String,
    },
    /// The Settings page's test email.
    Test,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Template {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Template::Setup { user, .. } => formatter
                .debug_struct("Setup")
                .field("link", &"<redacted>")
                .field("user", user)
                .finish(),
            Template::Reset { .. } => formatter
                .debug_struct("Reset")
                .field("link", &"<redacted>")
                .finish(),
            Template::MethodAdded { method } => formatter
                .debug_struct("MethodAdded")
                .field("method", method)
                .finish(),
            Template::Test => formatter.write_str("Test"),
        }
    }
}

impl Template {
    /// The template's name, as the mail queue lists it.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `"setup"`, `"reset"`, `"method_added"` or `"test"`.
    pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Template::Setup { .. } => "setup",
            Template::Reset { .. } => "reset",
            Template::MethodAdded { .. } => "method_added",
            Template::Test => "test",
        }
    }
}

/// Builds an emailed link from `public_url` (already validated as an
/// origin) and a raw token (base64url, so it needs no escaping).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `public_url` - the configured origin, with or without a trailing `/`.
/// * `path` - [`SETUP_PATH`] or [`RESET_PATH`].
/// * `token` - the raw token from `store::email_tokens::issue`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The absolute URL.
pub fn link(public_url: &str, path: &str, token: &str) -> String {
    format!("{}{path}?token={token}", public_url.trim_end_matches('/'))
}

/// Wraps paragraphs of already-escaped HTML in a minimal document.
fn html_document(subject: &str, paragraphs: &[String]) -> String {
    let body: String = paragraphs
        .iter()
        .map(|paragraph| format!("<p>{paragraph}</p>\n"))
        .collect();
    format!(
        "<!doctype html>\n<html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\"><title>{}</title></head>\n\
         <body>\n{body}</body></html>\n",
        escape(subject)
    )
}

/// An escaped link, shown as its own text.
fn anchor(link: &str) -> String {
    let link = escape(link);
    format!("<a href=\"{link}\">{link}</a>")
}

/// Renders a template.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `template` - what to send.
///
/// # Returns
/// `(subject, plain text, HTML)`.
pub fn render(template: &Template) -> (String, String, String) {
    const IGNORE: &str = "If you did not expect this email, you can ignore it.";
    match template {
        Template::Setup { link, user } => {
            let subject = "Set up your okf account";
            let text = format!(
                "Hello {user},\n\n\
                 An administrator invited you to okf. Open this link to choose a password \
                 or register a passkey:\n\n{link}\n\n\
                 The link works once and expires soon. If it has expired, ask an \
                 administrator for a new one.\n\n{IGNORE}\n"
            );
            let html = html_document(
                subject,
                &[
                    format!("Hello {},", escape(user)),
                    "An administrator invited you to okf. Open this link to choose a \
                     password or register a passkey:"
                        .to_string(),
                    anchor(link),
                    "The link works once and expires soon. If it has expired, ask an \
                     administrator for a new one."
                        .to_string(),
                    IGNORE.to_string(),
                ],
            );
            (subject.to_string(), text, html)
        }
        Template::Reset { link } => {
            let subject = "Reset your password";
            let text = format!(
                "Someone asked to reset the password of your okf account. Open this link \
                 to choose a new one:\n\n{link}\n\n\
                 The link works once and expires soon. Using it signs you out everywhere.\n\n\
                 If you did not ask for this, ignore this email; your password is unchanged.\n"
            );
            let html = html_document(
                subject,
                &[
                    "Someone asked to reset the password of your okf account. Open this \
                     link to choose a new one:"
                        .to_string(),
                    anchor(link),
                    "The link works once and expires soon. Using it signs you out everywhere."
                        .to_string(),
                    "If you did not ask for this, ignore this email; your password is \
                     unchanged."
                        .to_string(),
                ],
            );
            (subject.to_string(), text, html)
        }
        Template::MethodAdded { method } => {
            let subject = "A sign-in method was added to your account";
            let notice = "If this was not you, reset your password and ask an administrator \
                          to check your account.";
            let text = format!("{method} was added to your okf account.\n\n{notice}\n");
            let html = html_document(
                subject,
                &[
                    format!("{} was added to your okf account.", escape(method)),
                    notice.to_string(),
                ],
            );
            (subject.to_string(), text, html)
        }
        Template::Test => {
            let subject = "okf test email";
            let line = "This is a test email from okf. Mail delivery works.";
            (
                subject.to_string(),
                format!("{line}\n"),
                html_document(subject, &[line.to_string()]),
            )
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Outgoing mail (spec "Mail", Decisions 10 and 11). A [`Mailer`] sends one
//! [`Mail`]; the provider (SMTP, Postmark or the log) is chosen at run time
//! from `[mail]`, so it is a trait object, `Arc<dyn Mailer>`. Requests never
//! send directly: they enqueue a `SendMail` job ([`queue::enqueue`]), and a
//! worker sends it with retries ([`queue::spawn_worker`]).

use std::sync::Arc;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::config::{MailConfig, MailProvider};
use crate::error::OkfError;

// `log` is the provider that writes to the log; it shares no name with a
// crate this project uses.
mod log;
mod postmark;
pub mod queue;
mod smtp;
pub mod templates;

// Re-exported so callers write `mail::render`, `mail::Template`.
pub use templates::{link, render, Template, RESET_PATH, SETUP_PATH};

/// One rendered message. It is the `SendMail` job's payload, so it is
/// serde; its `Debug` omits the bodies (they may hold a single-use link).
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Mail {
    /// One recipient address.
    pub to: String,
    /// The subject line.
    pub subject: String,
    /// The plain-text body.
    pub text: String,
    /// The HTML twin.
    pub html: String,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Mail {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("Mail")
            .field("to", &self.to)
            .field("subject", &self.subject)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// Why a send failed, and whether trying again could help. The text never
/// holds the message body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum MailError {
    /// A network problem, a timeout, a rate limit or a server error: retry.
    #[error("retryable: {0}")]
    Retryable(String),
    /// The provider refused this message for good (a bad address, a
    /// rejected sender): do not retry.
    #[error("permanent: {0}")]
    Permanent(String),
}

/// Sends mail. `#[async_trait]` rewrites `async fn` into a method returning
/// a boxed future, which is what lets the trait be used as `dyn Mailer`
/// (Rust's native `async fn` in traits cannot be called through `dyn`).
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait Mailer: Send + Sync {
    /// Sends one message, once.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `mail` - the message.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`MailError::Retryable`] or [`MailError::Permanent`].
    async fn send(&self, mail: &Mail) -> Result<(), MailError>;
}

/// Builds the configured mailer, reading its secrets from the environment.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `config` - `[mail]` (already validated).
///
/// # Returns
/// The mailer, shared.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Config`] when a named environment variable is unset or
/// empty, the From address does not parse, or the provider cannot be built
/// (an SMTP host lettre refuses).
pub fn from_config(config: &MailConfig) -> Result<Arc<dyn Mailer>, OkfError> {
    from_config_with(config, &|name| std::env::var(name).ok())
}

/// [`from_config`] with the environment as a function, so tests need not
/// set process-wide variables.
// `&dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>`: any callable taking a name, like a
// Python `Callable[[str], Optional[str]]`.
pub(crate) fn from_config_with(
    config: &MailConfig,
    env: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
) -> Result<Arc<dyn Mailer>, OkfError> {
    match config.provider {
        MailProvider::Log => {
            tracing::info!("mail provider is \"log\": messages, links included, go to the log");
            Ok(Arc::new(log::LogMailer))
        }
        MailProvider::Smtp => {
            let smtp = config
                .smtp
                .as_ref()
                .ok_or_else(|| config_error("provider = \"smtp\" needs [mail.smtp]".to_string()))?;
            let password = smtp
                .password_env
                .as_deref()
                .map(|name| secret(env, name, "mail.smtp.password_env"))
                .transpose()?;
            Ok(Arc::new(smtp::SmtpMailer::from_config(
                &config.from,
                smtp,
                password,
            )?))
        }
        MailProvider::Postmark => {
            let postmark = config.postmark.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {
                config_error("provider = \"postmark\" needs [mail.postmark]".to_string())
            })?;
            let token = secret(env, &postmark.token_env, "mail.postmark.token_env")?;
            Ok(Arc::new(postmark::PostmarkMailer::new(
                postmark::ENDPOINT,
                &token,
                &config.from,
                &postmark.message_stream,
            )?))
        }
    }
}

/// Reads a secret from the environment variable a config key names.
fn secret(
    env: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
    name: &str,
    key: &str,
) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    match env(name) {
        Some(value) if !value.trim().is_empty() => Ok(value),
        _ => Err(config_error(format!(
            "{key} names {name}, which is not set or is empty"
        ))),
    }
}

/// A `[mail]` problem found at start-up.
pub(crate) fn config_error(message: String) -> OkfError {
    OkfError::Config {
        path: "[mail]".to_string(),
        message,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::{PostmarkConfig, SmtpConfig};

    fn smtp_config() -> MailConfig {
        MailConfig {
            provider: MailProvider::Smtp,
            from: "okf <okf@example.com>".to_string(),
            smtp: Some(SmtpConfig {
                host: "smtp.example.com".to_string(),
                port: 587,
                starttls: true,
                username: Some("okf".to_string()),
                password_env: Some("OKF_TEST_SMTP_PASSWORD".to_string()),
            }),
            ..MailConfig::default()
        }
    }

    fn postmark_config() -> MailConfig {
        MailConfig {
            provider: MailProvider::Postmark,
            postmark: Some(PostmarkConfig {
                token_env: "OKF_TEST_POSTMARK_TOKEN".to_string(),
                message_stream: "outbound".to_string(),
            }),
            ..MailConfig::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_provider_builds_when_its_secret_is_set() {
        let env = |name: &str| name.starts_with("OKF_TEST_").then(|| "s3cr3t".to_string());

        assert!(from_config_with(&MailConfig::default(), &env).is_ok());
        assert!(from_config_with(&smtp_config(), &env).is_ok());

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_or_empty_secret_stops_start_up_and_names_the_variable() {

            (smtp_config(), "OKF_TEST_SMTP_PASSWORD"),
            (postmark_config(), "OKF_TEST_POSTMARK_TOKEN"),

                // `.err()` keeps the error and drops the `Ok` type (a

            text: "https://okf.example.com/account/reset?token=s3cr3t".to_string(),
            html: "<a href=\"https://okf.example.com/account/reset?token=s3cr3t\">".to_string(),
        };

        let shown = format!("{mail:?}");

        assert!(shown.contains("alice@example.com") && !shown.contains("s3cr3t"), "{shown}");
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The SMTP provider, over lettre's async transport (tokio, rustls with
//! ring and the webpki roots: no OpenSSL). Generic over the transport so
//! tests use lettre's `AsyncStubTransport`.

use std::time::Duration;

use lettre::message::{Mailbox, MultiPart};
use lettre::transport::smtp::authentication::Credentials;
use lettre::{AsyncSmtpTransport, AsyncTransport, Message, Tokio1Executor};

use super::{config_error, Mail, MailError, Mailer};
use crate::config::SmtpConfig;
use crate::error::OkfError;

/// How long one SMTP conversation may take.
const SMTP_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

/// Sends through an SMTP transport `T`.
pub(crate) struct SmtpMailer<T> {
    transport: T,
    from: Mailbox,
}

impl<T> SmtpMailer<T> {
    /// A mailer over any lettre async transport.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `transport` - the transport (the relay, or a stub in tests).
    /// * `from` - the From mailbox.
    pub(crate) fn new(transport: T, from: Mailbox) -> Self {
        Self { transport, from }
    }
}

impl SmtpMailer<AsyncSmtpTransport<Tokio1Executor>> {
    /// The relay `[mail.smtp]` describes. Builds the transport only; it
    /// connects when the first mail is sent.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `from` - `mail.from`.
    /// * `config` - `[mail.smtp]`.
    /// * `password` - the password read from `password_env`, if any.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OkfError::Config`] for a From address or host lettre refuses.
    pub(crate) fn from_config(
        from: &str,
        config: &SmtpConfig,
        password: Option<String>,
    ) -> Result<Self, OkfError> {
        // `starttls_relay` refuses to send unless the upgrade succeeds;
        // `relay` speaks TLS from the first byte.
        let builder = if config.starttls {
            AsyncSmtpTransport::<Tokio1Executor>::starttls_relay(&config.host)
        } else {
            AsyncSmtpTransport::<Tokio1Executor>::relay(&config.host)
        }
        .map_err(|error| config_error(format!("mail.smtp.host {:?}: {error}", config.host)))?;
        let mut builder = builder.port(config.port).timeout(Some(SMTP_TIMEOUT));
        // `if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (..)`: both present (validation makes
        // them go together).
        if let (Some(username), Some(password)) = (&config.username, password) {
            builder = builder.credentials(Credentials::new(username.clone(), password));
        }
        Ok(Self::new(builder.build(), parse_from(from)?))
    }
}

/// Parses `mail.from`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Config`].
pub(crate) fn parse_from(from: &str) -> Result<Mailbox, OkfError> {
    from.parse()
        .map_err(|error| config_error(format!("mail.from {from:?} is not an address: {error}")))
}

/// Builds the MIME message: one recipient, text and HTML alternatives.
fn message(from: &Mailbox, mail: &Mail) -> Result<Message, MailError> {
    let to: Mailbox = mail.to.parse().map_err(|error| {
        MailError::Permanent(format!("recipient {:?} is not an address: {error}", mail.to))
    })?;
    Message::builder()
        .from(from.clone())
        .to(to)
        .subject(mail.subject.clone())
        .multipart(MultiPart::alternative_plain_html(
            mail.text.clone(),
            mail.html.clone(),
        ))
        .map_err(|error| MailError::Permanent(format!("building the message: {error}")))
}

/// Sorts a transport error: an SMTP 5xx reply is permanent; anything else
/// (connection, TLS, timeout, 4xx, a stub's error) is worth retrying.
fn classify(error: &(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)) -> MailError {
    // `downcast_ref` is Python's `isinstance` check plus the cast: `Some`
    // only when the error really is lettre's SMTP error.
    match error.downcast_ref::<lettre::transport::smtp::Error>() {
        Some(smtp) if smtp.is_permanent() => MailError::Permanent(format!("smtp: {smtp}")),
        _ => MailError::Retryable(format!("smtp: {error}")),
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl<T> Mailer for SmtpMailer<T>
where
    T: AsyncTransport + Send + Sync,
    T::Ok: Send,
    T::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
{
    async fn send(&self, mail: &Mail) -> Result<(), MailError> {
        let message = message(&self.from, mail)?;
        self.transport
            .send(message)
            .await
            .map(|_| ())
            .map_err(|error| classify(&error))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use lettre::transport::stub::AsyncStubTransport;

    fn mail(to: &str) -> Mail {
        Mail {
            to: to.to_string(),
            subject: "Reset your password".to_string(),
            text: "the text".to_string(),
            html: "<p>the html</p>".to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn from() -> Mailbox {
        parse_from("okf <okf@example.com>").unwrap()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_message_goes_to_its_one_recipient_with_both_parts() {
        let transport = AsyncStubTransport::new_ok();
        // The stub's log is shared between clones, so the test keeps one.
        let mailer = SmtpMailer::new(transport.clone(), from());

        mailer.send(&mail("alice@example.com")).await.unwrap();

        let messages = transport.messages().await;
        assert_eq!(messages.len(), 1);
        let (envelope, raw) = &messages[0];
        assert_eq!(envelope.to().len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(envelope.to()[0].to_string(), "alice@example.com");
        assert!(raw.contains("Subject: Reset your password"), "{raw}");
        assert!(raw.contains("multipart/alternative"), "{raw}");
        assert!(raw.contains("the text") && raw.contains("the html"), "{raw}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_transport_failure_is_retryable_and_a_bad_recipient_is_permanent() {
        let failing = SmtpMailer::new(AsyncStubTransport::new_error(), from());
        let working = SmtpMailer::new(AsyncStubTransport::new_ok(), from());

        let failed = failing.send(&mail("alice@example.com")).await;
        let bad = working.send(&mail("alice@example.com, bob@example.com")).await;

        assert!(matches!(failed, Err(MailError::Retryable(_))), "{failed:?}");
        assert!(matches!(bad, Err(MailError::Permanent(_))), "{bad:?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_relay_is_built_without_connecting() {
        let config = SmtpConfig {
            host: "smtp.example.com".to_string(),
            port: 465,
            starttls: false,
            username: None,
            password_env: None,
        };

        assert!(SmtpMailer::from_config("okf <okf@example.com>", &config, None).is_ok());
        assert!(matches!(
            SmtpMailer::from_config("nobody", &config, None),
            Err(OkfError::Config { .. })
        ));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The Postmark provider: one `POST /email` per message over the crate's
//! reqwest (rustls). Retries 429, 5xx, 401 (a token an operator can fix
//! within the retry window) and network errors; every other refusal
//! (notably 422, an invalid request) is permanent.

use std::time::Duration;

use reqwest::header::{HeaderValue, ACCEPT};
use reqwest::StatusCode;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::{config_error, Mail, MailError, Mailer};
use crate::error::OkfError;

/// Postmark's single-message endpoint.
pub(crate) const ENDPOINT: &str = "https://api.postmarkapp.com/email";

/// How long one request may take.
const POSTMARK_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

/// The header carrying the server token.
const TOKEN_HEADER: &str = "X-Postmark-Server-Token";

/// Sends through Postmark. No `Debug`: it holds the token.
pub(crate) struct PostmarkMailer {
    client: reqwest::Client,
    endpoint: String,
    // Marked sensitive, so even reqwest's own debug output hides it.
    token: HeaderValue,
    from: String,
    message_stream: String,
}

/// The request body (Postmark's field names are PascalCase).
#[derive(Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")]
struct Body<'a> {
    from: &'a str,
    to: &'a str,
    subject: &'a str,
    text_body: &'a str,
    html_body: &'a str,
    message_stream: &'a str,
}

/// An error answer's body: `{"ErrorCode": 300, "Message": "..."}`.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase", default)]
struct Reply {
    error_code: i64,
    message: String,
}

impl PostmarkMailer {
    /// A Postmark mailer.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `endpoint` - [`ENDPOINT`] (tests pass a mock server's URL).
    /// * `token` - the server token from `token_env`.
    /// * `from` - `mail.from` (a confirmed sender signature).
    /// * `message_stream` - `mail.postmark.message_stream`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OkfError::Config`] for a token that cannot be a header value, or
    /// an HTTP client that cannot be built.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        endpoint: &str,
        token: &str,
        from: &str,
        message_stream: &str,
    ) -> Result<Self, OkfError> {
        let mut token = HeaderValue::from_str(token.trim()).map_err(|_| {
            config_error("mail.postmark.token_env holds characters a header cannot".to_string())
        })?;
        token.set_sensitive(true);
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .timeout(POSTMARK_TIMEOUT)
            .build()
            .map_err(|error| config_error(format!("building the Postmark client: {error}")))?;
        Ok(Self {
            client,
            endpoint: endpoint.to_string(),
            token,
            from: from.to_string(),
            message_stream: message_stream.to_string(),
        })
    }
}

/// Sorts a refusal by its HTTP status.
fn classify(status: StatusCode, reply: &Reply) -> MailError {
    let detail = format!(
        "postmark answered {status} (ErrorCode {}): {}",
        reply.error_code, reply.message
    );
    if status == StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
        || status == StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED
        || status.is_server_error()
    {
        MailError::Retryable(detail)
    } else {
        MailError::Permanent(detail)
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl Mailer for PostmarkMailer {
    async fn send(&self, mail: &Mail) -> Result<(), MailError> {
        let body = Body {
            from: &self.from,
            to: &mail.to,
            subject: &mail.subject,
            text_body: &mail.text,
            html_body: &mail.html,
            message_stream: &self.message_stream,
        };
        let response = self
            .client
            .post(&self.endpoint)
            .header(ACCEPT, "application/json")
            .header(TOKEN_HEADER, self.token.clone())
            .json(&body)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|error| MailError::Retryable(format!("postmark: {error}")))?;
        let status = response.status();
        if status.is_success() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // An unreadable error body still has a status to go by.
        let reply = response.json::<Reply>().await.unwrap_or_default();
        Err(classify(status, &reply))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

    use axum::extract::State;
    use axum::http::HeaderMap;
    use axum::routing::post;
    use axum::{Json, Router};
    use serde_json::{json, Value};

    /// What the mock saw, and what it answers.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct Mock {
        seen: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(HeaderMap, Value)>>>,
        status: axum::http::StatusCode,
        reply: Value,
    }

    async fn handle(
        State(mock): State<Mock>,
        headers: HeaderMap,
        Json(body): Json<Value>,
    ) -> (axum::http::StatusCode, Json<Value>) {
        mock.seen.lock().unwrap().push((headers, body));
        (mock.status, Json(mock.reply.clone()))
    }

    /// Serves a mock `/email` on a free port.
    async fn mock_postmark(status: u16, reply: Value) -> (String, Mock) {
        let mock = Mock {
            seen: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())),
            status: axum::http::StatusCode::from_u16(status).unwrap(),
            reply,
        };
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let endpoint = format!("http://{}/email", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
        let router = Router::new()
            .route("/email", post(handle))
            .with_state(mock.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move { axum::serve(listener, router).await });
        (endpoint, mock)
    }

    fn mail() -> Mail {
        Mail {
            to: "alice@example.com".to_string(),
            subject: "okf test email".to_string(),
            text: "the text".to_string(),
            html: "<p>the html</p>".to_string(),
        }
    }

    fn mailer(endpoint: &str) -> PostmarkMailer {
        PostmarkMailer::new(endpoint, "server-token", "okf <okf@example.com>", "outbound").unwrap()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_request_has_postmarks_shape() {
        let (endpoint, mock) = mock_postmark(
            200,
            json!({"To": "alice@example.com", "ErrorCode": 0, "Message": "OK", "MessageID": "m-1"}),
        )
        .await;

        mailer(&endpoint).send(&mail()).await.unwrap();

        let seen = mock.seen.lock().unwrap();
        let (headers, body) = &seen[0];
        assert_eq!(headers["x-postmark-server-token"], "server-token");
        assert_eq!(headers["accept"], "application/json");
        assert_eq!(headers["content-type"], "application/json");
        assert_eq!(
            body,
            &json!({
                "From": "okf <okf@example.com>",
                "To": "alice@example.com",
                "Subject": "okf test email",
                "TextBody": "the text",
                "HtmlBody": "<p>the html</p>",
                "MessageStream": "outbound",
            })
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn an_invalid_request_is_permanent_and_carries_postmarks_message() {
        let (endpoint, _mock) =
            mock_postmark(422, json!({"ErrorCode": 300, "Message": "Invalid 'To' address"})).await;

        let refused = mailer(&endpoint).send(&mail()).await;

        assert!(
            matches!(&refused, Err(MailError::Permanent(detail))
                if detail.contains("300") && detail.contains("Invalid 'To' address")),
            "{refused:?}"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn rate_limits_outages_bad_tokens_and_unreachable_servers_are_retryable() {
        for status in [429, 500, 503, 401] {
            let (endpoint, _mock) = mock_postmark(status, json!({})).await;
            let refused = mailer(&endpoint).send(&mail()).await;
            assert!(matches!(refused, Err(MailError::Retryable(_))), "{status}: {refused:?}");
        }
        // A port that was just free: nothing listens there now.
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let closed = format!("http://{}/email", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
        drop(listener);
        let unreachable = mailer(&closed).send(&mail()).await;
        assert!(matches!(unreachable, Err(MailError::Retryable(_))), "{unreachable:?}");
    }
}
```
