```rust
//! The `SendMail` job on apalis-postgres (spec "Background jobs";
//! Decision 11's durable retry). See the task's overview in the plan for
//! the life of a job; the SQL here reads and writes `apalis.jobs` directly
//! where apalis-postgres has no API (last error, reschedule, retry, delete,
//! prune).

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

// apalis's prelude: the worker builder, task builder and the extractors
// (`Data`, `TaskId`) a handler takes, as Python's `from x import *` would.
use apalis::prelude::{
    AbortError, BackendExt, BoxDynError, Data, TaskBuilder, TaskId, WorkerBuilder,
};
use apalis_postgres::queries::push_tasks;
use apalis_postgres::{Config as QueueConfig, PostgresStorage};
use chrono::{DateTime, TimeDelta, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sqlx::PgPool;
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use super::{render, Mail, MailError, Mailer, Template};
use crate::app::App;
use crate::clock::Clock;
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::store::users::check_email;

/// The apalis queue (`apalis.jobs.job_type`). Set explicitly: apalis's
/// default is the Rust type's path, which a rename would orphan.
pub const QUEUE: &str = "send_mail";

/// `max_attempts` for every job: more than the 24-hour window can use, so
/// the window, not the count, ends the retries (Decision 11).
pub const MAX_ATTEMPTS: usize = 64;

/// How long a mail keeps being retried after it was queued.
pub const RETRY_WINDOW_HOURS: i64 = 24;

/// The first retry's delay; each later one doubles, up to [`BACKOFF_MAX_SECS`].
const BACKOFF_FIRST_SECS: f64 = 30.0;

/// The longest delay between two tries.
const BACKOFF_MAX_SECS: f64 = 3600.0;

/// How often an idle worker looks for due jobs that no NOTIFY announced.
pub const POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

/// How long a worker that stopped on an error waits before starting again.
const RESTART_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

/// How long sent mail jobs are kept.
const DONE_RETENTION_DAYS: i64 = 7;

/// How long failed mail jobs are kept.
const FAILED_RETENTION_DAYS: i64 = 30;

/// The job's payload: the rendered mail, its template's name (for the
/// queue listing) and when it was queued (Unix seconds, server clock; the
/// start of its retry window). `Debug` omits the mail's bodies.
#[derive(Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct SendMail {
    mail: Mail,
    template: String,
    queued_at: i64,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for SendMail {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("SendMail")
            .field("mail", &self.mail)
            .field("template", &self.template)
            .field("queued_at", &self.queued_at)
            .finish()
    }
}

/// One mail job as `mail queue` and the Settings page show it: never the body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, sqlx::FromRow)]
pub struct QueuedMail {
    /// The job id (a ULID), for retry and delete.
    pub id: String,
    /// The recipient.
    pub to: String,
    /// The template's name.
    pub template: String,
    /// `pending`, `sending`, `retrying` or `failed`.
    pub status: String,
    /// Tries so far.
    pub attempts: i32,
    /// The last try's error, if it failed.
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
    /// When it is (or was) due.
    pub run_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

/// The error for a queue operation apalis refused (its own error type).
fn queue_error(error: impl std::fmt::Display) -> OkfError {
    OkfError::Io {
        path: "<mail queue>".to_string(),
        source: std::io::Error::other(error.to_string()),
    }
}

/// Renders a template and queues it for `to`. Call it after the request's
/// own transaction commits, so a rolled-back change sends nothing.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `to` - one recipient address.
/// * `template` - what to send.
/// * `now` - when (server clock): the start of the 24-hour retry window.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "email"` for a malformed
/// address; [`OkfError::Database`] or [`OkfError::Io`] if the insert fails.
pub async fn enqueue(
    pool: &PgPool,
    to: &str,
    template: &Template,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    check_email(to)?;
    let (subject, text, html) = render(template);
    let job = SendMail {
        mail: Mail {
            to: to.to_string(),
            subject,
            text,
            html,
        },
        template: template.name().to_string(),
        queued_at: now.timestamp(),
    };
    // apalis-postgres stores the payload as JSON bytes (its JsonCodec), so
    // encode it the same way the worker will decode it.
    let payload = serde_json::to_vec(&job).map_err(queue_error)?;
    let task = TaskBuilder::new(payload).max_attempts(MAX_ATTEMPTS).build();
    let mut conn = pool.acquire().await?;
    push_tasks(&mut *conn, QUEUE, vec![task])
        .await
        .map_err(queue_error)?;
    tracing::info!(template = template.name(), "mail queued");
    Ok(())
}

/// Every mail job that is not done, oldest due first.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
///
/// # Returns
/// The jobs (pending, sending, retrying and failed).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn list(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<Vec<QueuedMail>, OkfError> {
    // `job` is the JSON payload as bytes; `convert_from(..)::jsonb` reads
    // it. `"to"` is quoted: TO is an SQL keyword.
    Ok(sqlx::query_as::<_, QueuedMail>(
        "SELECT id, \
                convert_from(job, 'UTF8')::jsonb -> 'mail' ->> 'to' AS \"to\", \
                convert_from(job, 'UTF8')::jsonb ->> 'template' AS template, \
                CASE WHEN status = 'Killed' \
                       OR (status = 'Failed' AND attempts >= max_attempts) THEN 'failed' \
                     WHEN status = 'Failed' THEN 'retrying' \
                     WHEN status IN ('Queued', 'Running') THEN 'sending' \
                     ELSE 'pending' END AS status, \
                attempts, last_result ->> 'Err' AS last_error, run_at \
         FROM apalis.jobs WHERE job_type = $1 AND status <> 'Done' \
         ORDER BY run_at, id",
    )
    .bind(QUEUE)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?)
}

/// Explains why a job-id write matched no row: the job is unknown, or in a
/// state the operation does not take.
async fn refusal(pool: &PgPool, id: &str, why: &str) -> Result<OkfError, OkfError> {
    let exists: Option<String> =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT status FROM apalis.jobs WHERE id = $1 AND job_type = $2")
            .bind(id)
            .bind(QUEUE)
            .fetch_optional(pool)
            .await?;
    Ok(match exists {
        None => OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "mail job",
            name: id.to_string(),
        },
        Some(_) => OkfError::Refused {
            reason: format!("mail job {id} {why}"),
        },
    })
}

/// Puts a failed (or retrying) job back in the queue: due now, no attempts,
/// and a fresh 24-hour window from `now`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `id` - the job id from [`list`].
/// * `now` - when (server clock).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] (`noun: "mail job"`); [`OkfError::Refused`]
/// for a job that has not failed; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn retry(pool: &PgPool, id: &str, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    // `jsonb_set` rewrites `queued_at` inside the stored payload. No NOTIFY
    // fires for an UPDATE; the worker's interval poll finds the job.
    let updated = sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE apalis.jobs SET status = 'Pending', attempts = 0, run_at = now(), \
             lock_by = NULL, lock_at = NULL, done_at = NULL, last_result = NULL, \
             job = convert_to(jsonb_set(convert_from(job, 'UTF8')::jsonb, \
                                        '{queued_at}', to_jsonb($3::bigint))::text, 'UTF8') \
         WHERE id = $1 AND job_type = $2 AND status IN ('Failed', 'Killed')",
    )
    .bind(id)
    .bind(QUEUE)
    .bind(now.timestamp())
    .execute(pool)
    .await?
    .rows_affected();
    if updated == 0 {
        return Err(refusal(pool, id, "has not failed; only failed mail is retried").await?);
    }
    tracing::info!(job = id, "mail job queued again");
    Ok(())
}

/// Deletes a job that is not being sent right now.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `id` - the job id from [`list`].
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] (`noun: "mail job"`); [`OkfError::Refused`]
/// while a worker holds it; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn delete(pool: &PgPool, id: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let deleted = sqlx::query(
        "DELETE FROM apalis.jobs \
         WHERE id = $1 AND job_type = $2 AND status NOT IN ('Queued', 'Running')",
    )
    .bind(id)
    .bind(QUEUE)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?
    .rows_affected();
    if deleted == 0 {
        return Err(refusal(pool, id, "is being sent; try again in a moment").await?);
    }
    tracing::info!(job = id, "mail job deleted");
    Ok(())
}

/// Deletes sent jobs finished over 7 days before `now`, and failed ones
/// over 30 (spec "Secrets in payloads"). Called by `App::poll`'s hourly prune.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Returns
/// How many were deleted.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn prune(pool: &PgPool, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<u64, OkfError> {
    Ok(sqlx::query(
        "DELETE FROM apalis.jobs WHERE job_type = $1 AND ( \
             (status = 'Done' AND done_at < $2) \
          OR ((status = 'Killed' OR (status = 'Failed' AND attempts >= max_attempts)) \
              AND done_at < $3))",
    )
    .bind(QUEUE)
    .bind(now - TimeDelta::days(DONE_RETENTION_DAYS))
    .bind(now - TimeDelta::days(FAILED_RETENTION_DAYS))
    .execute(pool)
    .await?
    .rows_affected())
}

/// What the job handler needs, given to apalis as worker data (cloned per
/// job: every field is a cheap handle).
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct MailContext {
    /// The database (for rescheduling).
    pub pool: PgPool,
    /// The provider.
    pub mailer: Arc<dyn Mailer>,
    /// The server clock (for the retry window).
    pub clock: Arc<dyn Clock>,
}

/// Moves a job's `run_at` to now plus its backoff: 30 s doubling per
/// attempt so far, capped at an hour. In SQL, on the database's clock,
/// which is the one apalis compares `run_at` with.
async fn reschedule(pool: &PgPool, id: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE apalis.jobs SET run_at = now() + make_interval(secs => \
             LEAST($3, $4 * power(2.0::float8, LEAST(attempts, 16)))) \
         WHERE id = $1 AND job_type = $2",
    )
    .bind(id)
    .bind(QUEUE)
    .bind(BACKOFF_MAX_SECS)
    .bind(BACKOFF_FIRST_SECS)
    .execute(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// The job handler: one send, then Decision 11's outcome (see the module
/// doc). apalis fills each argument from the job: the payload, the worker
/// data and the job id.
async fn send_mail(
    job: SendMail,
    context: Data<MailContext>,
    id: TaskId,
) -> Result<(), BoxDynError> {
    let id = id.to_string();
    let error = match context.mailer.send(&job.mail).await {
        Ok(()) => {
            tracing::info!(job = %id, template = %job.template, "mail sent");
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(error) => error,
    };
    // `Box::new(...)` makes the boxed error trait object apalis expects;
    // `AbortError` tells it never to fetch the job again.
    match error {
        MailError::Permanent(_) => {
            tracing::warn!(job = %id, template = %job.template, %error, "mail refused for good");
            Err(Box::new(AbortError::new(error)))
        }
        MailError::Retryable(reason) => {
            let age = context.clock.now().timestamp() - job.queued_at;
            if age >= RETRY_WINDOW_HOURS * 60 * 60 {
                tracing::warn!(job = %id, template = %job.template, %reason, "mail given up");
                return Err(Box::new(AbortError::new(MailError::Retryable(format!(
                    "gave up after {RETRY_WINDOW_HOURS} hours: {reason}"
                )))));
            }
            if let Err(error) = reschedule(&context.pool, &id).await {
                // Still a plain error: apalis fetches it again, just sooner.
                tracing::error!(job = %id, %error, "rescheduling a mail job failed");
            }
            tracing::info!(job = %id, template = %job.template, %reason, "mail failed; will retry");
            Err(Box::new(MailError::Retryable(reason)))
        }
    }
}

/// This process's worker name: unique per host and process, so replicas
/// never share an `apalis.workers` row (Decision 11).
fn worker_name() -> String {
    // `$HOSTNAME`, else the kernel's name for the host, else a placeholder.
    let host = std::env::var("HOSTNAME")
        .ok()
        .or_else(|| std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/kernel/hostname").ok())
        .map(|host| host.trim().to_string())
        .filter(|host| !host.is_empty())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "host".to_string());
    format!("okf-mail-{host}-{}", std::process::id())
}

/// Starts the mail worker for a serving process (`http::serve` calls it,
/// unless `[mail] worker = false`).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state (its pool, mailer and clock).
/// * `shutdown` - cancelled when the server stops.
///
/// # Returns
/// The worker's task; it ends once `shutdown` is cancelled and the job in
/// hand (if any) is finished.
pub fn spawn_worker(app: Arc<App>, shutdown: CancellationToken) -> JoinHandle<()> {
    let context = MailContext {
        pool: worker_pool(app.pool()),
        mailer: Arc::clone(app.mailer()),
        clock: app.clock_handle(),
    };
    run_worker(context, worker_name(), WorkerTiming::SERVE, shutdown)
}

/// Runs one apalis worker on [`QUEUE`] until `shutdown`, restarting it
/// after [`RESTART_DELAY`] if it stops on an error (a lost database, say).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `context` - what the handler needs.
/// * `poll` - how often to look for due jobs no NOTIFY announced.
/// * `shutdown` - cancelled to stop.
///
/// # Returns
/// The worker's task.
pub(crate) fn run_worker(
    context: MailContext,
    name: String,
    poll: Duration,
    shutdown: CancellationToken,
) -> JoinHandle<()> {
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        for restarts in 0_u64.. {
            let backend = PostgresStorage::<SendMail>::new(&context.pool)
                .with_config(QueueConfig::default().queue(QUEUE))
                .with_pubsub()
                .poll_with_interval(poll);
            let registered = if restarts == 0 {
                name.clone()
            } else {
                format!("{name}-{restarts}")
            };
            let worker = WorkerBuilder::new(registered)
                .backend(backend)
                .data(context.clone())
                .build(send_mail);
            let stop = shutdown.clone();
            // The future apalis waits on: it resolves when we are cancelled.
            let signal = async move {
                stop.cancelled().await;
                Ok::<(), std::io::Error>(())
            };
            match worker.run_until(signal).await {
                Ok(()) => return,
                Err(error) => {
                    tracing::error!(%error, "the mail worker stopped; restarting it soon");
                }
            }
            tokio::select! {
                () = shutdown.cancelled() => return,
                () = tokio::time::sleep(RESTART_DELAY) => {}
            }
        }
    })
}
```

> The apalis paths are from apalis 1.0.0's prelude (`apalis::prelude::{AbortError, BoxDynError, Data, TaskBuilder, TaskId, WorkerBuilder, BackendExt}`) and `apalis_postgres::{Config, PostgresStorage, queries::push_tasks}`. If the handler's argument types do not satisfy apalis's `TaskFn` bounds as written, the fallback is `Data<Arc<MailContext>>` (Decision 10's `Arc` shape); correct the plan in the same PR.

> **Corrected (issue #314, 2026-11-12).** What shipped differs from the code above in these ways; `src/mail/queue.rs` is authoritative.

A restart after a backend error registers as `<name>-<restarts>`, a row of its own: apalis-postgres 1.1.0's `register.sql` updates an existing worker row only under a session-scoped `pg_try_advisory_lock`, which another pooled connection may still hold, and it then refuses with `WorkerAlreadyExists`.
> - The handler's arguments (`SendMail`, `Data<MailContext>`, `TaskId`) satisfy apalis's bounds as written; the `Data<Arc<MailContext>>` fallback was not needed.
> - The tests go further than Step 9's (all under real apalis on the test database). `a_provider_error_reschedules_with_doubling_backoff_then_the_retry_succeeds` fails twice: 30 s then 60 s, `attempts` 1 then 2, each last error in `list`, and the job is not taken again while `run_at` is ahead. `a_mail_still_failing_after_24_hours_gives_up_and_retry_gives_a_new_window` retries the given-up job and checks it is rescheduled (`retrying`), not given up again. `two_workers_never_send_the_same_mail_twice` starts two workers, waits until both are registered, queues 30 mails, and checks each is sent exactly once and both workers took some (apalis's `get_jobs` takes rows `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`). `shutdown_finishes_the_mail_in_hand` cancels while a send is in progress and checks the job ends `Done`. `retry_and_delete_refuse_unknown_and_unfinished_jobs` also checks that a `Running` job cannot be deleted. `debug_hides_the_payloads_bodies` covers `SendMail`'s `Debug`. `Scripted` gained a `delay` and a `sent()` count, and the tests stop workers with a `stop` helper that times out after 20 s.
> - `http::tests::serve_runs_the_mail_worker_on_its_own_connections_and_waits_for_it` checks that `serve` with the default `[mail]` on a one-connection request pool sends a queued mail, and returns after `shutdown` once the worker has stopped.
> - The worker never uses the request pool (review of PR #333). `spawn_worker` gives it `queue::worker_pool(app.pool())`: the same connect options, at most `WORKER_POOL_SIZE` (4) connections, `application_name` `WORKER_APPLICATION_NAME` (`okf-mail-worker`), connected lazily and closed when the worker ends. Otherwise apalis's LISTEN holds a request connection for good, and with `database_max_connections = 1` (still valid) nothing else is served. `run_worker(context, name, timing, shutdown)` takes a `WorkerTiming { poll, heartbeat, restart }` (`WorkerTiming::SERVE` is 30 s each), so tests can shorten the delays. Task 16's operations docs should say the worker's connections come on top of `database_max_connections`. The tests add `after_losing_the_database_the_worker_restarts_and_sends`, `smtp::tests::an_smtp_5xx_is_permanent_and_a_4xx_is_retryable` (a fake relay), and the `serve` test runs on a one-connection request pool (`serve_runs_the_mail_worker_on_its_own_connections_and_waits_for_it`).

```markdown
# M12 Task 6: Mail through a `Mailer` and the apalis `SendMail` job

## Added
- `mail::Mailer` (an `#[async_trait]` trait object) with three providers: SMTP (lettre over rustls), Postmark (`POST /email` over reqwest) and `log`. `[mail]` in the config file chooses one; SMTP passwords and Postmark tokens come from the environment variables it names, read when the server starts.
- `mail::templates`: `setup`, `reset`, `method_added` and `test`, each plain text with an HTML twin; `mail::link` builds emailed links from `public_url`.
- `mail::queue`: `enqueue` (renders, then queues a `SendMail` job in `apalis.jobs`), the worker (`spawn_worker`, run by `serve` unless `[mail] worker = false`), and `list`, `retry`, `delete` and `prune` over the queue.

## Changed
- `App` holds the mailer (`App::mailer`) and lends its clock as a handle (`App::clock_handle`).
- `http::serve` runs the mail worker and waits for it on shutdown.
- The hourly prune deletes sent mail jobs after 7 days and failed ones after 30.
- Test servers turn the mail worker off, and the test database pool has 8 connections.

## Notes
- Retries are durable: a retryable failure moves the job's `run_at` (30 s, doubling, capped at 1 h) and the job is fetched again once due, for 24 hours from when it was queued. A permanent failure (an SMTP 5xx, a Postmark 4xx other than 401 or 429, a malformed recipient) fails the job at once. A manual retry starts a new 24-hour window.
- The queue listing never shows a message body; job payloads hold the rendered mail, setup and reset links included, until they are pruned.
```

> **Corrected (issue #315, 2026-11-12).** What shipped differs from the code below in these ways; the files named are authoritative.
> - **The admin level comes from the key cache on every request** (`src/http/console_session.rs`, `session_principal`): `require_principal` builds the principal from `Keys::user_admin` and `Keys::ceiling_of`, and only for a user new to the cache from `users::find_auth` plus `ceiling::ceiling_of` (a user deleted between those two reads is a 401, not a 404). `start_session` uses only the user's id, so a `UserAuth` read at sign-in never sets the level. Test `a_demotion_between_the_password_check_and_the_session_is_honoured` lands `users::set_admin` between `passwords::verify` and `start_session`; `a_promotion_reaches_a_live_session_only_by_ending_it` checks Decision 20 with no poll.
> - **`GET /api/v1/session` reads `admin` and a non-admin's `ceiling` from the principal** the middleware built for the request (an admin's `ceiling` is `Keys::ceiling_of`, shown for information). `SessionView` and `ConsoleSession` have hand-written `Debug`s that redact the CSRF token and the session id; `Browser` (test helper) derives `Default` but not `Debug`.
> - **`users::set_email` bumps `admin_generation` when the address changes** (a case-only change is no change), because the key cache now holds every user's email (`users::auth_by_id`, which reuses `user_auth_columns!`). Test `an_email_change_bumps_the_generation_and_a_no_op_does_not`.
> - **`start_session` does not cut `User-Agent` itself**: `user_sessions::create` keeps 256 characters (issue #313), so `MAX_USER_AGENT_CHARS` is gone.
> - **`ip_key` keys an IPv6 address by its /64** (`2001:db8:1:2::/64`), so one host cannot get a bucket per address, and maps an IPv4-mapped address to its IPv4 form. Test `an_ipv6_host_gets_one_key_for_its_whole_64`.
> - **`KeyedLimiter::try_take` is one atomic step, and a bucket's lifetime slides** (two reviews of PR #334).
>   - The `update`-then-`insert` below let concurrent first requests each take from a fresh bucket, and let a late `insert` replace a drawn-down one. `ExpiringMap::update_or_insert_sliding(key, now, make, change)` finds or creates the live entry, renews it to `now + ttl` and applies `change`, all under one lock, and never replaces another caller's entry. `try_take` is that call with `TokenBucket::try_take`; `None` (a full map) refuses.
>   - The map's ttl is `per`, the time to refill from empty. A bucket is dropped only after `per` with no request, when it is full anyway, so expiry never grants tokens. A fixed expiry would have reset a just-drawn-down bucket: at capacity 3 per 900 s, 7 requests would get through in 899 s.
>   - The bound is a token bucket's: in any interval of length `t`, at most `capacity + t * capacity / per`. It is not "twice capacity per window".
>   - Tests: `concurrent_first_requests_share_one_bucket` and `an_expired_bucket_is_replaced_exactly_once` (16 threads behind a barrier, capacity 1: exactly one passes); `expiry_never_grants_more_than_the_burst_plus_the_refill` (the review's t=0/1/899/900 case); `an_idle_bucket_is_dropped_and_its_replacement_acts_like_a_refilled_one`; `update_or_insert_sliding_creates_once_changes_in_place_and_slides`.
>   - The OAuth maps only `insert` under fresh random keys and `update` existing ones, so they had no such race, and they keep fixed lifetimes. Later code that keys an `ExpiringMap` by something a client chooses (an address, an email) uses `update_or_insert_sliding`, not `update` then `insert`.
> - **`ExpiringMap` keeps a lower bound on its entries' expiries** (`src/oauth/expiring.rs`): a full map refuses a new key without its O(n) prune until the earliest entry can have expired, so a flood of new keys against a full limiter costs one lookup each. Test `a_full_map_tracks_its_earliest_expiry_through_removals_and_prunes`.
> - **Decision 5's guard lives in `open_changeset`** (`src/mcp/changesets.rs`), the only code that inserts a changeset: a session principal gets 403 there (test `a_console_session_cannot_open_a_changeset`). No `/api/v1` route opens one today. Every other `/api/v1` use of `principal.key_id` was checked: `whoami` (session arm), changeset list and discard (ownership compare only), maintenance dispositions and idempotency rows (`credential_id` is text with no foreign key; `maintenance_runs.key_id` is filled by a subselect), and log lines.
> - **The archive routes stay bearer-only; their `/api/v1` copies do not.** `/mcp` and `/catalogs/{name}/export|import` sit behind `require_key`, which never reads a cookie (test `a_cookie_never_reaches_mcp_or_the_archive_routes`, with an admin session). `/api/v1/catalogs/{catalog}/export|import` are under `require_principal` like every API route, at the session's levels (export read, import admin), because Task 14a's `upload.js` imports through them with the session's CSRF header.
> - **Future callers are marked.** `pages::safe_return_to`, `is_safe_return_to` and `DEFAULT_RETURN_TO` carry `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = ...))]` until Task 7b uses them, and `console_session::signed_in_user` until Task 11 does. Each of those tasks deletes the attribute (an `expect` that is met warns, which `just lint` refuses).
> - Extra tests: `a_policy_that_is_not_a_header_value_is_a_bare_500`, `only_get_head_and_options_skip_the_csrf_check`, `a_console_session_never_debug_prints_its_secrets`, `a_session_view_never_debug_prints_its_csrf_token`, `a_session_writes_only_where_its_ceiling_says_write`, `the_api_archive_routes_take_a_session_at_its_levels_and_with_csrf`, `a_revoked_session_is_refused_at_once`, `an_unknown_cookie_is_a_401_that_clears_it`, `each_sign_in_gets_a_new_session_and_a_full_cookie`, `a_user_new_to_the_cache_is_read_from_the_database`, `auth_by_id_holds_every_user_by_id`, `the_browser_posts_forms_follows_cookies_and_reads_redirects`.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    const WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(900);

    #[test]
    fn each_key_gets_its_own_capacity() {
        let limiter = KeyedLimiter::new(3, WINDOW, 100);
        let now = Instant::now();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            assert!(limiter.try_take("a", now));
        }
        assert!(!limiter.try_take("a", now));
        assert!(limiter.try_take("b", now), "another key is not limited by the first");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_key_refills_over_its_window() {
        let limiter = KeyedLimiter::new(3, WINDOW, 100);
        let now = Instant::now();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            limiter.try_take("a", now);
        }
        // One token comes back every 300 s (3 per 900 s).
        assert!(!limiter.try_take("a", now + Duration::from_secs(200)));
        assert!(limiter.try_take("a", now + Duration::from_secs(301)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_full_map_refuses_new_keys_rather_than_forgetting_old_ones() {
        let limiter = KeyedLimiter::new(1, WINDOW, 2);
        let now = Instant::now();
        assert!(limiter.try_take("a", now));
        assert!(limiter.try_take("b", now));
        assert!(!limiter.try_take("c", now));
        // Once the window passes, the expired keys make room.
        assert!(limiter.try_take("c", now + WINDOW + Duration::from_secs(1)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unknown_address_shares_one_key() {
        assert_eq!(ip_key(None), "unknown");
        assert_eq!(ip_key(Some("192.0.2.7".parse().expect("an address"))), "192.0.2.7");
    }
}
```

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::AuthConfig;

    fn parts(peer: Option<&str>, forwarded: &[&str]) -> Parts {
        // `axum::extract::Request` (imported above) is `Request<Body>`;
        // `builder()` lives on `http::Request<()>`.
        let mut builder = axum::http::Request::builder().uri("/signin");
        for value in forwarded {
            builder = builder.header("x-forwarded-for", *value);
        }
        let (mut parts, ()) = builder.body(()).expect("a request").into_parts();
        if let Some(peer) = peer {
            parts
                .extensions
                .insert(ConnectInfo(peer.parse::<SocketAddr>().expect("an address")));
        }
        parts
    }

    fn behind_proxy() -> AuthConfig {
        AuthConfig {
            trusted_proxy_header: Some("x-forwarded-for".to_string()),
            ..AuthConfig::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn without_a_trusted_header_the_peer_is_the_client() {
        let parts = parts(Some("192.0.2.1:5000"), &["198.51.100.9"]);
        assert_eq!(client_ip(&parts, &AuthConfig::default()), "192.0.2.1".parse().ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn behind_a_proxy_the_last_hop_of_the_last_header_is_the_client() {
        let parts = parts(
            Some("10.0.0.2:5000"),
            &["203.0.113.66, 198.51.100.1", "198.51.100.9, 192.0.2.44"],
        );
        assert_eq!(client_ip(&parts, &behind_proxy()), "192.0.2.44".parse().ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_or_garbled_forwarded_header_falls_back_to_the_peer() {
        assert_eq!(
            client_ip(&parts(Some("10.0.0.2:5000"), &[]), &behind_proxy()),
            "10.0.0.2".parse().ok()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            client_ip(&parts(Some("10.0.0.2:5000"), &["not-an-address"]), &behind_proxy()),
            "10.0.0.2".parse().ok()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_request_without_connect_info_has_no_address() {
        assert_eq!(client_ip(&parts(None, &[]), &AuthConfig::default()), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_session_cookie_is_found_among_others_and_in_any_cookie_header() {
        let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
        headers.append(header::COOKIE, HeaderValue::from_static("theme=dark; okf_passkey=p1"));
        headers.append(header::COOKIE, HeaderValue::from_static("okf_session=abc; x=y"));
        assert_eq!(cookie(&headers, COOKIE), Some("abc"));
        assert_eq!(cookie(&headers, "okf_passkey"), Some("p1"));
        assert_eq!(cookie(&headers, "missing"), None);
        let mut empty = HeaderMap::new();
        empty.insert(header::COOKIE, HeaderValue::from_static("okf_session="));
        assert_eq!(cookie(&empty, COOKIE), None, "an empty value is no cookie");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_set_cookie_line_carries_every_attribute() {
        let secure = set_cookie(COOKIE, "abc", Duration::from_secs(60), SameSite::Lax, true);
        assert_eq!(
            secure,
            "okf_session=abc; Max-Age=60; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure"
        );
        let plain = set_cookie("okf_passkey", "", Duration::ZERO, SameSite::Strict, false);
        assert_eq!(plain, "okf_passkey=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_csrf_header_must_equal_the_sessions_token() {
        let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
        assert!(!csrf_matches(&headers, "token"));
        headers.insert(CSRF_HEADER, HeaderValue::from_static("other"));
        assert!(!csrf_matches(&headers, "token"));
        headers.insert(CSRF_HEADER, HeaderValue::from_static("token"));
        assert!(csrf_matches(&headers, "token"));
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Server-rendered HTML shared by the OAuth consent pages and the sign-in
//! pages (plan Decision 14): one document shell, one escaper, one response
//! builder with the security headers, and the `return_to` check. There is
//! no template engine; every piece of text goes through [`escape`].

use axum::http::{header, HeaderValue, StatusCode};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};

/// Where a sign-in goes when it was given no usable `return_to`.
pub(crate) const DEFAULT_RETURN_TO: &str = "/ui/";

/// Escapes text for HTML element content and double- or single-quoted
/// attribute values.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `text` - untrusted text.
///
/// # Returns
/// The text with `& < > " '` as entities.
pub(crate) fn escape(text: &str) -> String {
    // Most text has nothing to escape; the capacity covers that case with
    // one allocation.
    let mut escaped = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    for character in text.chars() {
        match character {
            '&' => escaped.push_str("&amp;"),
            '<' => escaped.push_str("&lt;"),
            '>' => escaped.push_str("&gt;"),
            '"' => escaped.push_str("&quot;"),
            '\'' => escaped.push_str("&#39;"),
            other => escaped.push(other),
        }
    }
    escaped
}

/// The HTML document around a page body.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `title` - the page title (escaped here).
/// * `body` - the page body, already escaped where needed.
/// * `scripts` - paths of same-origin module scripts to load, in order;
///   empty for a page that runs no script (consent).
///
/// # Returns
/// The whole document.
pub(crate) fn document(title: &str, body: &str, scripts: &[&str]) -> String {
    // `map(...).collect::<String>()` concatenates one line per script.
    let scripts: String = scripts
        .iter()
        .map(|src| format!("    <script type=\"module\" src=\"{}\"></script>\n", escape(src)))
        .collect();
    format!(
        r#"<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
    <title>{title} - okf</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500&family=Space+Grotesk:wght@500;700&display=swap">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/ui/vendor/pico.min.css">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/ui/styles.css">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/ui/consent.css">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/ui/signin.css">
{scripts}</head>
<body>
    <main class="login-card consent-card">
        <p class="brand">okf</p>
{body}
    </main>
</body>
</html>
"#,
        title = escape(title),
    )
}

/// A page that runs no script: [`scripted_page`] with no scripts.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `status` - the HTTP status.
/// * `title` - the page title.
/// * `body` - the page body.
/// * `csp` - the Content-Security-Policy.
///
/// # Returns
/// The response.
pub(crate) fn page(status: StatusCode, title: &str, body: &str, csp: &str) -> Response {
    scripted_page(status, title, body, &[], csp)
}

/// A page with its security headers: `text/html`, `no-store`,
/// `no-referrer` (an emailed link's token must not leak to another site),
/// `nosniff` and `csp`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `status` - the HTTP status.
/// * `title` - the page title.
/// * `body` - the page body.
/// * `scripts` - same-origin module scripts (see [`document`]).
/// * `csp` - the Content-Security-Policy.
///
/// # Returns
/// The response, or a bare 500 (logged) if `csp` is not a header value,
/// which would be a bug: the policies are built from constants and parsed
/// URLs.
pub(crate) fn scripted_page(
    status: StatusCode,
    title: &str,
    body: &str,
    scripts: &[&str],
    csp: &str,
) -> Response {
    let Ok(csp) = HeaderValue::from_str(csp) else {
        tracing::error!("a page's CSP is not a header value");
        return StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.into_response();
    };
    (
        status,
        [
            (header::CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("text/html; charset=utf-8")),
            (header::CACHE_CONTROL, HeaderValue::from_static("no-store")),
            (header::REFERRER_POLICY, HeaderValue::from_static("no-referrer")),
            (header::X_CONTENT_TYPE_OPTIONS, HeaderValue::from_static("nosniff")),
            (header::CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY, csp),
        ],
        document(title, body, scripts),
    )
        .into_response()
}

/// Where a sign-in may send the browser next: a console path or an OAuth
/// authorize URL on this origin, or else [`DEFAULT_RETURN_TO`].
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `raw` - the `return_to` a page or form carried, if any.
///
/// # Returns
/// `raw` when it is safe, else `/ui/`.
pub(crate) fn safe_return_to(raw: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match raw {
        Some(path) if is_safe_return_to(path) => path.to_string(),
        // `Some(_)` that failed the guard, or `None`.
        _ => DEFAULT_RETURN_TO.to_string(),
    }
}

/// Whether `path` is a same-origin console or authorize path.
fn is_safe_return_to(path: &str) -> bool {
    // Visible ASCII only: no spaces, no control characters (a header
    // injection) and no `\`, which some browsers read as `/` (so `/\host`
    // would leave the origin). Both prefixes start with one `/` followed by
    // a path segment, so the result can never be `//host`.
    path.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_graphic() && byte != b'\\')
        && (path.starts_with("/ui/") || path.starts_with("/oauth/authorize?"))
}
```

```rust
//! Per-key rate limits for the sign-in routes (plan Decision 8): a token
//! bucket per client address or per email, held in an [`ExpiringMap`] so
//! idle keys are dropped. In memory and per process, like M10's global
//! buckets (multi-replica limits are a follow-up).

use std::net::IpAddr;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::oauth::expiring::ExpiringMap;
use crate::oauth::ratelimit::TokenBucket;

/// Password sign-in attempts per address per [`SIGN_IN_WINDOW`] (spec).
pub const SIGN_IN_PER_IP: u32 = 30;
/// The window of [`SIGN_IN_PER_IP`].
pub const SIGN_IN_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15 * 60);
/// Reset requests per email per [`FORGOT_WINDOW`] (spec).
pub const FORGOT_PER_EMAIL: u32 = 3;
/// Reset requests per address per [`FORGOT_WINDOW`] (spec).
pub const FORGOT_PER_IP: u32 = 20;
/// The window of the reset limits.
pub const FORGOT_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60 * 60);
/// The most keys one limiter tracks at once.
pub const MAX_LIMITED_KEYS: usize = 100_000;

/// A token bucket per key: `capacity` requests at once, refilled evenly
/// over `per` (see `src/http/limits.rs` for the shipped version: the
/// bucket's lifetime slides, so expiry never grants tokens).
pub struct KeyedLimiter {
    capacity: u32,
    refill_per_sec: f64,
    buckets: ExpiringMap<TokenBucket>,
}

impl KeyedLimiter {
    /// An empty limiter.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `capacity` - requests per key per `per`.
    /// * `per` - the window; more than zero.
    /// * `max_keys` - the most keys tracked at once.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The limiter.
    pub fn new(capacity: u32, per: Duration, max_keys: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            capacity,
            refill_per_sec: f64::from(capacity) / per.as_secs_f64(),
            buckets: ExpiringMap::new(per, max_keys),
        }
    }

    /// Takes one request for `key` if its bucket has one.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `key` - an address ([`ip_key`]) or a normalized email.
    /// * `now` - the current instant (passed in, so tests control time).
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `true` if the request may go ahead. A full map refuses a new key:
    /// spraying keys must not evict the buckets that are holding someone
    /// back.
    pub fn try_take(&self, key: &str, now: Instant) -> bool {
        // `update` runs the closure on a live entry under the map's lock and
        // returns its result, or `None` when the key has no live bucket.
        if let Some(taken) = self.buckets.update(key, now, |bucket| bucket.try_take(now)) {
            return taken;
        }
        let bucket = TokenBucket::new(self.capacity, self.refill_per_sec);
        let taken = bucket.try_take(now);
        // Two first requests racing for one key may each insert a bucket;
        // the second replaces the first, which costs at most one request.
        self.buckets.insert(key.to_string(), bucket, now) && taken
    }
}

/// The limits the sign-in routes share, held by `App`.
pub struct SignInLimits {
    /// Password and passkey sign-in attempts, by address.
    pub sign_in_per_ip: KeyedLimiter,
    /// `POST /signin/forgot`, by normalized email.
    pub forgot_per_email: KeyedLimiter,
    /// `POST /signin/forgot`, by address.
    pub forgot_per_ip: KeyedLimiter,
}

impl SignInLimits {
    /// Empty limiters at the spec's rates.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The limits.
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            sign_in_per_ip: KeyedLimiter::new(SIGN_IN_PER_IP, SIGN_IN_WINDOW, MAX_LIMITED_KEYS),
            forgot_per_email: KeyedLimiter::new(FORGOT_PER_EMAIL, FORGOT_WINDOW, MAX_LIMITED_KEYS),
            forgot_per_ip: KeyedLimiter::new(FORGOT_PER_IP, FORGOT_WINDOW, MAX_LIMITED_KEYS),
        }
    }
}

impl Default for SignInLimits {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// The limiter key of a client address.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `ip` - from `console_session::client_ip`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The address as text, or `"unknown"` (requests with no address, such as
/// in-process tests, share one bucket).
pub fn ip_key(ip: Option<IpAddr>) -> String {
    ip.map_or_else(|| "unknown".to_string(), |ip| ip.to_string())
}
```

```rust
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use axum::http::HeaderMap;

use crate::http::console_session::{start_session, COOKIE};
use crate::store::passwords;
use crate::store::users::{self, UserAuth};

/// A password every test user can be given: long enough and not common.
pub(crate) const PASSWORD: &str = "violet-lantern-orbit-42";

/// Settings with `public_url`, so the login routes exist (plan Decision 18).
/// The `https` origin also makes every cookie `Secure`.
pub(crate) fn login_config() -> Config {
    Config {
        public_url: Some("https://okf.example.com".to_string()),
        ..Config::default()
    }
}

/// [`app`], with [`login_config`].
pub(crate) async fn login_app() -> TestApp {
    app_with(
        &[("main", MAIN), ("other", &[("index.md", "# Other\n")])],
        login_config(),
    )
    .await
}

/// Creates a user with an email and, optionally, a password, then polls so
/// the key cache knows it.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user.
pub(crate) async fn user_with_password(
    test: &TestApp,
    name: &str,
    email: &str,
    password: Option<&str>,
) -> UserAuth {
    let pool = test.app.pool();
    users::create(pool, &users::NewUser { name, display_name: "" }, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("create the user");
    users::set_email(pool, name, Some(email)).await.expect("set the email");
    let user = users::find_by_email(pool, email)
        .await
        .expect("find the user")
        .expect("the user exists");
    if let Some(password) = password {
        passwords::set(pool, &user.id, password, Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("set the password");
    }
    test.app.poll().await.expect("poll the user in");
    user
}

/// A request body for [`Browser::send`].
pub(crate) enum Payload {
    /// No body.
    Empty,
    /// `application/json`.
    Json(serde_json::Value),
    /// `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, as an HTML form posts.
    Form(Vec<(&'static str, String)>),
}

/// One answer to [`Browser::send`].
pub(crate) struct Reply {
    /// The status.
    pub status: StatusCode,
    /// The headers (`Set-Cookie` and `Location` included).
    pub headers: HeaderMap,
    /// The body bytes.
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Reply {
    /// The body as JSON, or `Null` when it is not JSON.
    pub(crate) fn json(&self) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::from_slice(&self.body).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null)
    }

    /// The status and the body as JSON: the pair [`send`] answers, for
    /// tests written against it.
    pub(crate) fn parts(&self) -> (StatusCode, serde_json::Value) {
        (self.status, self.json())
    }

    /// The body as text.
    pub(crate) fn text(&self) -> String {
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.body).into_owned()
    }

    /// The `Location` header, or `""`.
    pub(crate) fn location(&self) -> &str {
        self.headers
            .get("location")
            .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
            .unwrap_or("")
    }

    /// The whole `Set-Cookie` line for `name`, if the reply set it.
    pub(crate) fn set_cookie(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        let prefix = format!("{name}=");
        self.headers
            .get_all("set-cookie")
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|value| value.to_str().ok())
            .find(|line| line.starts_with(&prefix))
            .map(str::to_string)
    }
}

/// What a browser keeps between requests: its cookies, the console's CSRF
/// token (sent as `x-okf-csrf` on every request but a GET), and optionally
/// a bearer key (sent on every request). Requests go through the whole
/// router with `oneshot`, so they carry no client address.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct Browser {
    cookies: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    /// The session's CSRF token.
    pub csrf: Option<String>,
    /// A bearer key.
    pub bearer: Option<String>,
}

impl Browser {
    /// A browser holding one cookie.
    pub(crate) fn with_cookie(name: &str, value: &str) -> Self {
        let mut browser = Self::default();
        browser.cookies.insert(name.to_string(), value.to_string());
        browser
    }

    /// A cookie's current value.
    pub(crate) fn cookie(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.cookies.get(name).map(String::as_str)
    }

    /// Sends one request and applies the reply's `Set-Cookie` lines.
    pub(crate) async fn send(
        &mut self,
        test: &TestApp,
        method: &str,
        uri: &str,
        payload: Payload,
    ) -> Reply {
        let mut request = Request::builder().method(method).uri(uri);
        if !self.cookies.is_empty() {
            let cookies: Vec<String> = self
                .cookies
                .iter()
                .map(|(name, value)| format!("{name}={value}"))
                .collect();
            request = request.header("cookie", cookies.join("; "));
        }
        if let Some(csrf) = self.csrf.as_deref().filter(|_| method != "GET") {
            request = request.header("x-okf-csrf", csrf);
        }
        if let Some(key) = &self.bearer {
            request = request.header("authorization", format!("Bearer {key}"));
        }
        let request = match payload {
            Payload::Empty => request.body(Body::empty()),
            Payload::Json(json) => request
                .header("content-type", "application/json")
                .body(Body::from(json.to_string())),
            Payload::Form(pairs) => {
                let encoded = form_urlencoded::Serializer::new(String::new())
                    .extend_pairs(pairs.iter().map(|(name, value)| (*name, value.as_str())))
                    .finish();
                request
                    .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
                    .body(Body::from(encoded))
            }
        }
        .expect("a valid request");
        let response = router(Arc::clone(&test.app), &CancellationToken::new())
            .oneshot(request)
            .await
            .expect("the router answers");
        let status = response.status();
        let headers = response.headers().clone();
        for line in headers.get_all("set-cookie").iter().filter_map(|v| v.to_str().ok()) {
            let pair = line.split(';').next().unwrap_or_default();
            if let Some((name, value)) = pair.split_once('=') {
                if value.is_empty() || line.contains("Max-Age=0;") {
                    self.cookies.remove(name);
                } else {
                    self.cookies.insert(name.to_string(), value.to_string());
                }
            }
        }
        let body = axum::body::to_bytes(response.into_body(), usize::MAX)
            .await
            .expect("read the body")
            .to_vec();
        Reply { status, headers, body }
    }

    /// Signs in with an email and password as `/signin` (Task 7b) does,
    /// without going through the page: the password is checked, then a
    /// session is started. The CSRF token is kept for writes, as the console
    /// keeps it from `GET /api/v1/session`.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    /// If the password is refused.
    pub(crate) async fn signed_in(test: &TestApp, email: &str, password: &str) -> Self {
        let outcome = passwords::verify(test.app.pool(), email, password, Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("check the password");
        let passwords::SignInOutcome::Ok(user) = outcome else {
            panic!("the password for {email} was refused");
        };
        Self::for_user(test, &user).await
    }

    /// A browser signed in as the existing user called `name`, with no
    /// password (tests of signed-in routes, Tasks 10a to 12). Polls first,
    /// so the key cache knows the user and its ceiling.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    /// If the user does not exist or the session cannot be stored.
    pub(crate) async fn session_for(test: &TestApp, name: &str) -> Self {
        test.app.poll().await.expect("poll the user in");
        let id: String = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = $1")
            .bind(name)
            .fetch_one(test.app.pool())
            .await
            .expect("the user exists");
        let user = users::find_auth(test.app.pool(), &id)
            .await
            .expect("read the user")
            .expect("the user exists");
        Self::for_user(test, &user).await
    }

    /// A browser holding a new console session for `user`.
    async fn for_user(test: &TestApp, user: &UserAuth) -> Self {
        let (_, session) = start_session(&test.app, user, None, "okf-test")
            .await
            .expect("start a console session");
        let mut browser = Self::with_cookie(COOKIE, &session.id);
        // `session.id` was only borrowed above, so the token can move out.
        browser.csrf = Some(session.csrf);
        browser
    }
}
```

The `Set-Cookie` lines Tasks 7a and 7b write put `Max-Age` before `Path`, so `"Max-Age=0;"` matches a cleared cookie exactly.

```rust
/// The `key_id` prefix of a console session's principal. Key ids match
```

`impl Principal` gains:

```rust
    /// The principal of a console session (plan Decision 5): an admin
    /// user acts as an admin on every catalog; anyone else reaches exactly
    /// their ceiling, at the ceiling's level for each catalog.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `user` - the signed-in user.
    /// * `ceiling` - the user's ceiling (unused for an admin).
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The principal; its `access` is the highest level it holds, for
    /// display and the admin checks (which a non-admin never passes).
    pub fn for_session(user: &UserAuth, ceiling: Ceiling) -> Self {
        let (access, reach) = if user.is_admin {
            (Access::Admin, Reach::All)
        } else {
            // `copied()` turns the `&Access` items into `Access` values;
            // `max()` is `None` for an empty ceiling.
            let highest = ceiling.values().copied().max().unwrap_or(Access::Read);
            (highest, Reach::Catalogs(ceiling))
        };
        Self {
            key_id: format!("{SESSION_KEY_PREFIX}{}", user.name),
            access,
            maintenance_report: false,
            reach,
            default_catalog: None,
            actor: user.name.clone(),
            kind: CredentialKind::Session {
                user_id: user.id.clone(),
            },
            user: Some(user.name.clone()),
        }
    }
```

```rust
    /// Reads every key, every ceiling and every user, and builds the cache.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OkfError::Database`].
    async fn read(pool: &PgPool, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<Self, OkfError> {
        // Three reads at once, on three pooled connections (`try_join!` is
        // `asyncio.gather` that stops at the first error).
        let (records, ceilings, users) = tokio::try_join!(
            key_rows::list(pool),
            ceiling::ceilings(pool),
            users::auth_by_id(pool)
        )?;
        Ok(Self::from_records(records, ceilings, now).with_users(users))
    }
```

```rust
pub async fn auth_by_id(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<HashMap<String, UserAuth>, OkfError> {
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Implement `src/http/console_session.rs`**

```rust
//! Console sessions over HTTP (spec "Sessions"): the `okf_session` cookie,
//! the CSRF rule, the client address, and `require_principal`, the
//! `/api/v1` middleware that admits a bearer credential or a session
//! cookie. MCP and the archive routes keep bearer-only `require_key`.

use std::net::{IpAddr, SocketAddr};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use axum::extract::{ConnectInfo, Request, State};
use axum::http::request::Parts;
use axum::http::{header, HeaderMap, HeaderValue, Method};
use axum::middleware::Next;
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;

use crate::app::App;
use crate::auth::{authenticate, bearer, unauthorized, Principal};
use crate::config::AuthConfig;
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::http::AppError;
use crate::store::ceiling;
use crate::store::user_sessions::{self, NewSession};
use crate::store::users::{self, UserAuth};

/// The session cookie (plan Decision 9).
pub const COOKIE: &str = "okf_session";

/// The header a cookie-authenticated write must carry, equal to the
/// session's CSRF token.
pub const CSRF_HEADER: &str = "x-okf-csrf";

/// The most `User-Agent` characters stored with a session.
const MAX_USER_AGENT_CHARS: usize = 256;

/// A cookie's `SameSite` attribute.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SameSite {
    /// Sent on top-level navigations from other sites (the session cookie,
    /// so a link to the console arrives signed in; and the OIDC flow cookie,
    /// which the provider's redirect must carry).
    Lax,
    /// Never sent from another site (the passkey ceremony cookie).
    Strict,
}

impl SameSite {
    /// The attribute's value.
    fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Lax => "Lax",
            Self::Strict => "Strict",
        }
    }
}

/// The console session a cookie-authenticated request came with, put in
/// the request's extensions next to its `Arc<Principal>`. Routes that act
/// on "the other sessions" (sign-out, passkeys, password change) read it.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ConsoleSession {
    /// The raw session id (the cookie's value).
    pub id: String,
    /// Its CSRF token.
    pub csrf: String,
    /// When it ends regardless of activity.
    pub expires_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

// Written by hand, not derived, so a stray `{:?}` never prints the id or
// the token.
impl std::fmt::Debug for ConsoleSession {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("ConsoleSession")
            .field("id", &"<redacted>")
            .field("csrf", &"<redacted>")
            .field("expires_at", &self.expires_at)
            .finish()
    }
}

/// The client's address (plan Decision 7).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `request_parts` - the request (its `ConnectInfo` extension and headers).
/// * `config` - `[auth]`, for `trusted_proxy_header`.
///
/// # Returns
/// With `trusted_proxy_header` set, the last address in the last such
/// header (the one the trusted proxy appended); otherwise, or when that
/// header is missing or unreadable, the peer address. `None` without
/// `ConnectInfo` (in-process `oneshot` tests).
pub fn client_ip(request_parts: &Parts, config: &AuthConfig) -> Option<IpAddr> {
    let peer = request_parts
        .extensions
        .get::<ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>>()
        .map(|ConnectInfo(address)| address.ip());
    // `let ... else`: without a trusted header, the peer is the client.
    let Some(name) = config.trusted_proxy_header.as_deref() else {
        return peer;
    };
    forwarded_ip(&request_parts.headers, name).or(peer)
}

/// The last hop of the last `name` header. Earlier entries were written by
/// the client (or proxies before ours) and prove nothing.
fn forwarded_ip(headers: &HeaderMap, name: &str) -> Option<IpAddr> {
    let value = headers.get_all(name).iter().last()?.to_str().ok()?;
    value.rsplit(',').next()?.trim().parse().ok()
}

/// A cookie's value from the request's `Cookie` headers.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `headers` - the request's headers.
/// * `name` - the cookie's name.
///
/// # Returns
/// The value, or `None` when absent or empty.
// `<'a>`: the returned `&str` borrows from `headers`, so it lives as long
// as they do (no copy is made).
pub(crate) fn cookie<'a>(headers: &'a HeaderMap, name: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    headers
        .get_all(header::COOKIE)
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|value| value.to_str().ok())
        .flat_map(|value| value.split(';'))
        .find_map(|pair| {
            let (key, value) = pair.trim().split_once('=')?;
            (key == name && !value.is_empty()).then_some(value)
        })
}

/// One `Set-Cookie` value: `HttpOnly`, `Path=/`, `Secure` when asked.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `name` - the cookie.
/// * `value` - its value (base64url from `keys::generate_with`, or empty to clear).
/// * `max_age` - its lifetime; zero clears it.
/// * `same_site` - its `SameSite`.
/// * `secure` - add `Secure` ([`secure_cookies`]).
///
/// # Returns
/// The header value.
///
/// # Panics
/// If `name` or `value` is not a valid header value: callers pass constants
/// and base64url, so that is a bug.
pub(crate) fn set_cookie(
    name: &str,
    value: &str,
    max_age: Duration,
    same_site: SameSite,
    secure: bool,
) -> HeaderValue {
    let secure = if secure { "; Secure" } else { "" };
    HeaderValue::from_str(&format!(
        "{name}={value}; Max-Age={}; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite={}{secure}",
        max_age.as_secs(),
        same_site.as_str(),
    ))
    .expect("cookie names and base64url values are valid header values")
}

/// Whether cookies get `Secure`: when `public_url` is `https` (plan
/// Decision 15; tests run on `http://127.0.0.1`).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
///
/// # Returns
/// `true` for an `https` `public_url`.
pub(crate) fn secure_cookies(app: &App) -> bool {
    app.config()
        .public_url
        .as_deref()
        .is_some_and(|url| url.starts_with("https://"))
}

/// Appends every header of `extra` to `target`, keeping repeated names
/// (`HeaderMap::extend` would replace an existing `Set-Cookie`).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `target` - the headers to add to.
/// * `extra` - the headers to add.
pub(crate) fn append_all(target: &mut HeaderMap, extra: &HeaderMap) {
    for (name, value) in extra {
        target.append(name.clone(), value.clone());
    }
}

/// Does the request carry the session's CSRF token? Compared in constant
/// time.
fn csrf_matches(headers: &HeaderMap, expected: &str) -> bool {
    headers
        .get(CSRF_HEADER)
        .is_some_and(|value| value.as_bytes().ct_eq(expected.as_bytes()).into())
}

/// Methods that change nothing, so need no CSRF header.
fn is_safe_method(method: &Method) -> bool {
    matches!(*method, Method::GET | Method::HEAD | Method::OPTIONS)
}

/// A user's sign-in identity: from the key cache, else (a user created
/// since the last reload) from the database.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
/// * `user_id` - the user's id.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user, or `None` once deleted.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub(crate) async fn session_user(app: &App, user_id: &str) -> Result<Option<UserAuth>, OkfError> {
    match app.keys().user_admin(user_id) {
        Some(user) => Ok(Some(user)),
        None => users::find_auth(app.pool(), user_id).await,
    }
}

/// The user of the console session this request's cookie names, for a
/// route outside `/api/v1` (Task 11's `/oauth/authorize`), which
/// [`require_principal`] does not cover. It touches the session as the
/// middleware does.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
/// * `headers` - the request's headers.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user, or `None` without a cookie, for an ended session, or once the
/// user is gone.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub(crate) async fn signed_in_user(
    app: &App,
    headers: &HeaderMap,
) -> Result<Option<UserAuth>, OkfError> {
    let Some(id) = cookie(headers, COOKIE) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let idle = app.settings().console_session_idle;
    match user_sessions::touch(app.pool(), id, idle, app.clock().now()).await? {
        Some(row) => session_user(app, &row.user_id).await,
        None => Ok(None),
    }
}

/// The principal of a live session's user.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn session_principal(app: &App, user_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Principal>, OkfError> {
    let Some(user) = session_user(app, user_id).await? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    // The cache's ceiling, unless the user is new to it; then one query.
    let ceiling = match app.keys().user_admin(user_id) {
        Some(_) => app.keys().ceiling_of(user_id),
        None => ceiling::ceiling_of(app.pool(), &user.name).await?,
    };
    Ok(Some(Principal::for_session(&user, ceiling)))
}

/// [`unauthorized`], also clearing a session cookie that no longer works.
fn unauthorized_clearing(app: &App) -> Response {
    let mut response = unauthorized(app);
    append_all(response.headers_mut(), &clear_cookie(app));
    response
}

/// axum middleware for `/api/v1`: a bearer credential, else a session
/// cookie (with [`CSRF_HEADER`] on anything but GET, HEAD and OPTIONS).
/// Inserts the `Arc<Principal>` and, for a cookie, the [`ConsoleSession`]
/// into the request's extensions.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state (the layer's state).
/// * `request` - the incoming request.
/// * `next` - the rest of the stack.
///
/// # Returns
/// The route's response; 401 with the challenge (clearing a dead cookie);
/// 403 for a cookie write without the CSRF token; 500 if a lookup fails.
pub async fn require_principal(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    mut request: Request,
    next: Next,
) -> Response {
    // A bearer credential wins and the cookie is not read at all (spec
    // "Bearer and cookie"); a bad bearer is a 401 even beside a good cookie.
    // The borrowed token ends with this expression, before `request` changes.
    let presented = match bearer(request.headers()) {
        Some(token) => Some(authenticate(&app, token).await),
        None => None,
    };
    match presented {
        Some(Ok(Some(principal))) => {
            tracing::debug!(key = %principal.key_id, "authenticated");
            request.extensions_mut().insert(principal);
            return next.run(request).await;
        }
        Some(Ok(None)) => return unauthorized(&app),
        Some(Err(error)) => return AppError(error).into_response(),
        None => {}
    }
    let Some(id) = cookie(request.headers(), COOKIE).map(str::to_string) else {
        return unauthorized(&app);
    };
    let settings = app.settings();
    let now = app.clock().now();
    let row = match user_sessions::touch(app.pool(), &id, settings.console_session_idle, now).await {
        Ok(Some(row)) => row,
        Ok(None) => return unauthorized_clearing(&app),
        Err(error) => return AppError(error).into_response(),
    };
    if !is_safe_method(request.method()) && !csrf_matches(request.headers(), &row.csrf) {
        return AppError(OkfError::Forbidden {
            reason: "a console write needs its session's X-OKF-CSRF header; reload the console"
                .to_string(),
        })
        .into_response();
    }
    let principal = match session_principal(&app, &row.user_id).await {
        Ok(Some(principal)) => principal,
        Ok(None) => return unauthorized_clearing(&app),
        Err(error) => return AppError(error).into_response(),
    };
    tracing::debug!(key = %principal.key_id, "authenticated by a console session");
    request.extensions_mut().insert(Arc::new(principal));
    request.extensions_mut().insert(ConsoleSession {
        id,
        csrf: row.csrf,
        expires_at: row.expires_at,
    });
    next.run(request).await
}

/// Starts a console session: a new random id (never the one the browser
/// had: rotation), stored as its hash, and the cookie.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
/// * `user` - the user who signed in.
/// * `ip` - their address, if known.
/// * `user_agent` - their `User-Agent` (cut to 256 characters).
///
/// # Returns
/// The `Set-Cookie` header and the new session (id and CSRF token).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]; [`OkfError::Io`] if the random source fails.
pub async fn start_session(
    app: &App,
    user: &UserAuth,
    ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    user_agent: &str,
) -> Result<(HeaderMap, NewSession), OkfError> {
    let settings = app.settings();
    let user_agent: String = user_agent.chars().take(MAX_USER_AGENT_CHARS).collect();
    let session = user_sessions::create(
        app.pool(),
        &user.id,
        ip,
        &user_agent,
        settings.console_session_absolute,
        app.clock().now(),
    )
    .await?;
    let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
    headers.insert(
        header::SET_COOKIE,
        set_cookie(COOKIE, &session.id, settings.console_session_absolute, SameSite::Lax, secure_cookies(app)),
    );
    tracing::info!(user = %user.id, "console session started");
    Ok((headers, session))
}

/// The `Set-Cookie` header that removes the session cookie.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state (for `Secure`).
///
/// # Returns
/// The header.
pub fn clear_cookie(app: &App) -> HeaderMap {
    let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
    headers.insert(
        header::SET_COOKIE,
        set_cookie(COOKIE, "", Duration::ZERO, SameSite::Lax, secure_cookies(app)),
    );
    headers
}
```

The handlers:

```rust
/// The calling session's user id and session, or 403 for a key or grant.
fn console(
    principal: &Principal,
    session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>,
) -> Result<(String, ConsoleSession), OkfError> {
    match (&principal.kind, session) {
        (CredentialKind::Session { user_id }, Some(Extension(session))) => {
            Ok((user_id.clone(), session))
        }
        // A key or a grant (or, impossibly, a session principal without its
        // session): there is no console session here.
        _ => Err(OkfError::Forbidden {
            reason: "this request is not a console session".to_string(),
        }),
    }
}

/// `GET /session`: the signed-in user, their ceiling and the CSRF token.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a key or grant; 401 once the user is gone; 500 on a lookup failure.
async fn session(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>,
) -> Result<Json<SessionView>, AppError> {
    let (user_id, session) = console(&principal, session)?;
    let user = console_session::session_user(&app, &user_id)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::Unauthenticated {
            reason: "this session's user no longer exists".to_string(),
        })?;
    let ceiling = app
        .keys()
        .ceiling_of(&user_id)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(catalog, access)| (catalog, access.as_str()))
        .collect();
    Ok(Json(SessionView {
        user: user.name,
        email: user.email,
        admin: user.is_admin,
        csrf: session.csrf,
        ceiling,
        expires_at: format_timestamp(session.expires_at),
    }))
}

/// `DELETE /session`: signs out (the session is deleted, the cookie cleared).
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a key or grant; 500 if the delete fails.
async fn sign_out(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let (user_id, session) = console(&principal, session)?;
    user_sessions::revoke(app.pool(), &session.id).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user_id, "console session signed out");
    Ok((StatusCode::NO_CONTENT, console_session::clear_cookie(&app)).into_response())
}
```

>   - `passwords::verify` and `verify_user` return `SignInOutcome::Ok(Verified { user, stamp })`. `stamp: PasswordStamp` is the stored PHC string the password matched, with a redacted `Debug`. A new password always has a new hash, because it gets a fresh salt.
>   - `user_sessions::start(pool, &SessionStart { user_id, ip, user_agent, absolute, now, password })` is one statement: `INSERT INTO user_sessions ... SELECT ... FROM users u WHERE u.id = $2 AND ($8::text IS NULL OR u.password_hash = $8) FOR SHARE`. If no row comes back, it returns `OkfError::Unauthenticated`, and `POST /signin` answers that with the uniform 401 (recorded as failed). `user_sessions::create` (no stamp) is unchanged for callers.
>   - `passwords::reset(pool, user_id, password, now) -> u64` updates the hash and runs `revoke_all` in one transaction. `reset_post` uses it.
>   - The two serialize on the user row. Either the insert commits first and the reset deletes its session, or the reset commits first and the insert re-checks the hash on the new row version and inserts nothing.
>   - `console_session::start_session_with(app, user, password, ip, user_agent)` is the stamped form of `start_session`. In `signin.rs`, `begin(app, parts, user, method, password)` is the stamped form of `sign_in`.
>   - Passkey, OIDC and setup sign-ins keep calling `sign_in` / `start_session` with no stamp.
>   - Tests: `a_sign_in_checked_before_a_reset_gets_no_session_after_it`, `a_sign_in_waiting_on_a_reset_in_progress_gets_no_session` (holds the user row so the reset and the insert queue behind it in that order) and `a_session_inserted_before_a_reset_is_ended_by_it`.
> - Console sign-out counts as done only on a 2xx or a 401 from `DELETE /api/v1/session`. Any other failure keeps the session state and the shell, and shows a "Sign-out failed ... Try again." toast. The setup journey fails the first `DELETE` with a fetch wrapper and checks this.
> - **Emailed links are issued and used atomically (third review of PR #337).**
>   - *Forgot.* `email_tokens::issue_for_email(pool, email, purpose, ttl, now) -> Option<IssuedLink { user, to, token }>` (redacted `Debug`) finds the user and issues the token in one transaction. One statement finds and locks the user's row by email (`... WHERE u.email = $1::citext FOR NO KEY UPDATE`); `users::set_email` takes the same row lock when it deletes a changed user's links. Either the issue commits first and the email change deletes the link, or the change commits first and the issue finds no user. The mail goes to `to`, the address read under the lock. `issue` and `issue_for_email` share a private `replace_token`. Tests: `a_reset_link_issued_before_an_email_change_dies_with_it` and `no_reset_link_is_issued_for_an_email_changed_meanwhile`. Each holds the row and queues the two in a chosen order.
>   - *Setup and reset.* The handlers' `use_link` hashes the new password first (`passwords::NewPassword::hash`, policy plus argon2, redacted `Debug`), outside any transaction. Then one transaction runs `email_tokens::redeem_in(&mut tx, token, purpose, now)` and either `passwords::set_in(&mut tx, user_id, &hashed, now)` (setup) or `passwords::reset_in(...) -> u64` (reset: the hash, then `revoke_all`). A failure anywhere rolls everything back: the old password, the sessions and the link stay as they were. `redeem`, `set` and `reset` are the pool wrappers. Tests: `a_reset_that_fails_changes_nothing_and_keeps_the_link` and `a_setup_that_fails_sets_nothing_and_keeps_the_link`. Each injects the failure with a trigger.
>   - Task 8's setup-link passkey path (`setup_finish`) must do the same: redeem the link with `redeem_in` and store the passkey in the same transaction. See the note there.
> - **Lock order: the user's row first, then that user's tokens or sessions (fourth review of PR #337).** The rule is stated once, in `src/store/email_tokens.rs`'s module docs.
>   - Every transaction that locks a `users` row and also writes `email_tokens` or `user_sessions` takes the user's row first. That covers `email_tokens::{issue, issue_for_email, redeem_in}`, `users::{set_email, set_admin, delete}`, `passwords::{set_in, reset_in}` (the `UPDATE users` comes before `revoke_all`) and `user_sessions::start` (the user row `FOR SHARE`, then the insert).
>   - Statements that touch only tokens or only sessions (`touch`, `revoke`, `revoke_by_prefix`, the prunes) take no user lock.
>   - `redeem_in` used to lock the token first, which could deadlock with an issue or an email change. It now reads the token's `user_id` with no lock, locks that user `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, and then marks the token used. The update re-checks the purpose, that the token is unused and unexpired, and that `user_id` still matches.
>   - Tests: `a_redemption_racing_a_new_link_completes_without_a_deadlock` and `a_redemption_racing_an_email_change_completes_without_a_deadlock`. Each holds the user row and queues the rival ahead of the redemption: the order that used to deadlock. With the old `redeem_in`, both fail.
>   - Later tasks (8, 9, 10b, 12) that write these tables in a transaction with a user row must keep this order.
> - **Every session insert in `signin.rs` is stamped (fifth review of PR #337).**
>   - `use_link` returns `LinkUsed { user, ended, stamp }`, where `stamp` is `NewPassword::stamp()`, the hash it just stored. Setup starts its session through the stamped `begin`, just as a password sign-in does. If a reset replaces the password between setup's commit and the session insert, setup creates no session and redirects to `/signin`.
>   - A reset signs nobody in.
>   - The unstamped `sign_in` is kept for Tasks 8 and 9 under `#[expect(dead_code)]`; delete that attribute when the first of them calls it.
>   - Test: `a_session_after_setup_is_refused_once_a_reset_replaced_the_password`.
> - **A console write with CSRF has a journey:** `an_admin_session_writes_through_the_console_with_its_csrf_token`. It signs in at `/signin`, reloads, checks that no key is stored, creates a user in the UI and reads it back through the API. Removing the `X-OKF-CSRF` line from `api.js` makes it fail.
> - **One place picks a request's credentials (sixth review of PR #337).** `core/api.js` exports `authHeaders(method, { key = store.key, csrf = store.csrf })`. With a key it returns `Authorization: Bearer`. Without one, a non-GET request gets `X-OKF-CSRF`, and the session cookie goes by itself.
>   - `request`, the import upload (`components/upload.js`'s XMLHttpRequest) and `main.js`'s cookie-only session calls (`key: null`) all use it.
>   - Task 14a's shared modules must not build an `Authorization` header anywhere else.
>   - Journey: `catalogs::an_admin_signed_in_with_a_password_imports_an_archive`.
> - **One credential at a time in the console (second review of PR #337).**
>   - At boot, `main.js` asks `GET /api/v1/session` first (a plain fetch, cookie only). A live session wins over a stored key, and the stored key is dropped. Otherwise a stored key is used; otherwise the login card is shown.
>   - Sign-out (`endCookieSession`) always asks the server, cookie-only, whether the browser has a session. If it does, it sends `DELETE /api/v1/session` with that session's CSRF token, and only then clears the key. The failure rule is unchanged.
>   - Journeys: `an_account_sign_in_replaces_a_stored_key_and_sign_out_ends_both` and `sign_out_ends_a_cookie_session_hidden_behind_a_stored_key`. Task 14a builds on this boot order.
> - Without `public_url`, `POST /signin` answers 404 (an explicit handler), not axum's 405.
> - `http::router`'s trace span (`request_span`) records the method and the path, not the URI: `DefaultMakeSpan` logged `?token=...` of every emailed link.
> - The console's 403 toast reads "Your account cannot do this." for a session (no stored key).
> - `Ui::sign_in_password` also waits for `#whoami` to show an identity (`" - "`), not only for `#app` to be visible. `tests/ui_e2e/signin.rs` has a `server()` helper and a second journey (a refused password, then a session that survives a reload, via `TestServer::user_with_password`).
> - Extra unit tests: hostile `return_to` values (`//evil.example`, `/\evil.example`, `javascript:`, encoded forms), the cross-site refusal, an expired setup and reset link, the per-address forgot limit, and the pages' CSP with no script.

```rust
    async fn post_sign_in(browser: &mut Browser, test: &TestApp, email: &str, password: &str) -> Reply {
        let form = vec![("email", email.to_string()), ("password", password.to_string())];
        browser.send(test, "POST", "/signin", Payload::Form(form)).await
    }

    async fn queued_mail(pool: &PgPool) -> i64 {
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT count(*) FROM apalis.jobs")
            .fetch_one(pool)
            .await
            .expect("count the queued mail")
    }

    /// Waits (up to 5 s) for `want` queued mails: `forgot` queues after it answers.
    async fn wait_for_mail(pool: &PgPool, want: i64) {
        for _ in 0..100 {
            if queued_mail(pool).await >= want {
                return;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
        }
        panic!("{want} mails never queued; {} did", queued_mail(pool).await);
    }

        };

        let html = sign_in_html(&view);

        assert!(html.contains(r#"id="signin-form""#));
        assert!(html.contains(r#"id="signin-passkey" class="secondary" data-return-to="/ui/#/keys""#));
        assert!(html.contains(r#"href="/auth/oidc/example/start?return_to=%2Fui%2F%23%2Fkeys""#));
        assert!(html.contains("Sign in with Example &lt;ID&gt;"));
        assert!(html.contains(SIGN_IN_FAILED));
        assert!(html.contains(r#"id="signin-api-key""#));
    }
}
```
