```rust
//! The server-rendered sign-in pages (spec "Signing in"): `/signin` with
//! the password form, `/signin/forgot`, and the emailed `/account/setup`
//! and `/account/reset` links. They use the console's CSP, so the passkey
//! script (Task 8) and provider links (Task 9) fit. Without `public_url`
//! only `GET /signin` exists, offering the API-key sign-in (Decision 18).

use std::net::IpAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;

use axum::extract::rejection::FormRejection;
use axum::extract::{Query, State};
use axum::http::request::Parts;
use axum::http::{header, HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Redirect, Response};
use axum::routing::get;
use axum::{Form, Router};
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::app::App;
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::http::console_session::{client_ip, cookie, start_session, COOKIE};
use crate::http::limits::ip_key;
use crate::http::pages::{self, escape, safe_return_to};
use crate::http::ui::CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY;
use crate::http::{timeout_layer, AppError};
use crate::mail::queue as mail_queue;
use crate::mail::{self, Template, RESET_PATH, SETUP_PATH};
use crate::store::email_tokens::{self, Purpose};
use crate::store::passwords::{self, SignInOutcome};
use crate::store::sign_in_events::{self, Method, Outcome};
use crate::store::user_sessions;
use crate::store::users::{self, UserAuth};

/// Every refused password sign-in says this, whatever the reason (spec).
pub const SIGN_IN_FAILED: &str = "Email or password is incorrect";
/// An expired, used or unknown emailed link (410).
pub const LINK_EXPIRED: &str = "This link has expired. Ask for a new one.";
/// `/signin/forgot`'s one answer.
pub const FORGOT_SENT: &str = "If an account exists, we sent a link.";
/// After a reset (`/signin?notice=reset`).
const PASSWORD_CHANGED: &str = "Your password was changed. Sign in with it.";
/// Over the per-address limit (429).
const TOO_MANY: &str = "Too many attempts from this address. Wait a few minutes and try again.";
/// The sign-in and setup pages' passkey script (Task 8).
pub(crate) const PASSKEY_SCRIPT: &str = "/ui/js/signin/passkey.js";

/// A configured OIDC provider's button on the sign-in page (Task 9).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ProviderButton {
    /// The provider's id (`[a-z0-9-]+`, checked at config load).
    pub id: String,
    /// Its button text.
    pub label: String,
}

/// What the sign-in page offers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub(crate) struct SignInView {
    /// The email and password form.
    pub password: bool,
    /// The passkey button (Task 8).
    pub passkey: bool,
    /// Where to go after signing in ([`safe_return_to`]).
    pub return_to: String,
    /// A refusal to show.
    pub error: Option<&'static str>,
    /// A notice to show.
    pub notice: Option<&'static str>,
    /// One button per OIDC provider (Task 9).
    pub providers: Vec<ProviderButton>,
}

/// What the setup page shows.
pub(crate) struct SetupView<'a> {
    /// The user's name.
    pub user: &'a str,
    /// The setup token (a hidden field; the page is `no-store`, `no-referrer`).
    pub token: &'a str,
    /// Where to go after setting up.
    pub return_to: &'a str,
    /// A problem with the last attempt.
    pub error: Option<&'a str>,
    /// The passkey option (Task 8).
    pub passkey: bool,
}

/// The login routes; without `public_url`, only the API-key sign-in page.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state (its `public_url`).
///
/// # Returns
/// The router, with the request timeout.
pub(crate) fn routes(app: &App) -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    let router = if app.config().public_url.is_some() {
        Router::new()
            .route("/signin", get(sign_in_page).post(sign_in_post))
            .route("/signin/forgot", get(forgot_page).post(forgot_post))
            // The paths the emailed links point at (`mail::link`, Task 6).
            .route(SETUP_PATH, get(setup_page).post(setup_post))
            .route(RESET_PATH, get(reset_page).post(reset_post))
    } else {
        Router::new().route("/signin", get(sign_in_page))
    };
    router.layer(timeout_layer())
}

/// Whether the pages offer a passkey (Task 8 makes this
/// `app.passkeys().is_some()`).
fn offers_passkeys(_app: &App) -> bool {
    false
}

/// The OIDC provider buttons (Task 9 fills this from the registry).
fn provider_buttons(_app: &App) -> Vec<ProviderButton> {
    Vec::new()
}

/// What `/signin` offers on this server.
fn sign_in_view(app: &App, return_to: String) -> SignInView {
    let login = app.config().public_url.is_some();
    SignInView {
        password: login && app.settings().password_sign_in,
        passkey: login && offers_passkeys(app),
        return_to,
        error: None,
        notice: None,
        providers: if login { provider_buttons(app) } else { Vec::new() },
    }
}

/// The sign-in page's body.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `view` - what to offer.
///
/// # Returns
/// The HTML, every value escaped.
pub(crate) fn sign_in_html(view: &SignInView) -> String {
    let return_to = escape(&view.return_to);
    let mut html = String::from("        <h1>Sign in</h1>\n");
    if let Some(notice) = view.notice {
        html.push_str(&format!(
            "        <p class=\"notice\" id=\"signin-notice\" role=\"status\">{}</p>\n",
            escape(notice)
        ));
    }
    if let Some(error) = view.error {
        html.push_str(&format!(
            "        <p class=\"error consent-error\" id=\"signin-error\" role=\"alert\">{}</p>\n",
            escape(error)
        ));
    }
    if view.password {
        html.push_str(&format!(
            r#"        <form method="post" action="/signin" id="signin-form">
            <input type="hidden" name="return_to" value="{return_to}">
            <label>Email
                <input type="email" name="email" id="signin-email" autocomplete="username" required>
            </label>
            <label>Password
                <input type="password" name="password" id="signin-password" autocomplete="current-password" required>
            </label>
            <button type="submit" id="signin-submit">Sign in</button>
        </form>
        <p class="small"><a href="/signin/forgot" id="signin-forgot">Forgot your password?</a></p>
"#
        ));
    }
    if view.passkey {
        html.push_str(&format!(
            r#"        <button type="button" id="signin-passkey" class="secondary" data-return-to="{return_to}">Sign in with a passkey</button>
        <p class="error" id="passkey-error" role="alert" hidden></p>
"#
        ));
    }
    if !view.providers.is_empty() {
        // The query value is URL-encoded, then the whole href HTML-escaped.
        let encoded: String = form_urlencoded::byte_serialize(view.return_to.as_bytes()).collect();
        html.push_str("        <div class=\"signin-providers\">\n");
        for provider in &view.providers {
            html.push_str(&format!(
                "            <a role=\"button\" class=\"secondary\" id=\"signin-oidc-{id}\" href=\"/auth/oidc/{id}/start?return_to={query}\">Sign in with {label}</a>\n",
                id = escape(&provider.id),
                query = escape(&encoded),
                label = escape(&provider.label),
            ));
        }
        html.push_str("        </div>\n");
    }
    html.push_str(
        "        <p class=\"muted signin-alt\"><a href=\"/ui/\" id=\"signin-api-key\">Use an API key instead</a></p>",
    );
    html
}

/// `/signin` with `status`; the passkey script only when offered.
fn sign_in_response(status: StatusCode, view: &SignInView) -> Response {
    let scripts: &[&str] = if view.passkey { &[PASSKEY_SCRIPT] } else { &[] };
    pages::scripted_page(status, "Sign in", &sign_in_html(view), scripts, CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY)
}

/// A page with a heading, one message and a link back to `/signin`.
fn message_page(status: StatusCode, title: &str, message: &str) -> Response {
    let body = format!(
        r#"        <h1>{title}</h1>
        <p class="consent-error" id="signin-message" role="alert">{message}</p>
        <p><a href="/signin">Back to sign in</a></p>"#,
        title = escape(title),
        message = escape(message),
    );
    pages::page(status, title, &body, CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY)
}

/// `GET /signin`'s query.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
struct SignInQuery {
    return_to: Option<String>,
    notice: Option<String>,
}

/// `GET /signin`.
async fn sign_in_page(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, Query(query): Query<SignInQuery>) -> Response {
    let mut view = sign_in_view(&app, safe_return_to(query.return_to.as_deref()));
    // Only a known notice is shown: the page never echoes text from its URL.
    view.notice = (query.notice.as_deref() == Some("reset")).then_some(PASSWORD_CHANGED);
    sign_in_response(StatusCode::OK, &view)
}

/// `POST /signin`'s form. No `Debug`: it holds a password.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct SignInForm {
    email: String,
    password: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    return_to: Option<String>,
}

/// `POST /signin`: 303 to `return_to` with the session cookie, or 401 with
/// the one message, or 429 past the per-address limit.
async fn sign_in_post(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    parts: Parts,
    form: Result<Form<SignInForm>, FormRejection>,
) -> Response {
    if !app.settings().password_sign_in {
        return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
    }
    let Ok(Form(form)) = form else {
        let mut view = sign_in_view(&app, safe_return_to(None));
        view.error = Some(SIGN_IN_FAILED);
        return sign_in_response(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, &view);
    };
    let return_to = safe_return_to(form.return_to.as_deref());
    let ip = client_ip(&parts, &app.config().auth);
    if !app.sign_in_limits().sign_in_per_ip.try_take(&ip_key(ip), Instant::now()) {
        let mut view = sign_in_view(&app, return_to);
        view.error = Some(TOO_MANY);
        return sign_in_response(StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, &view);
    }
    let email = form.email.trim();
    let verdict = passwords::verify(app.pool(), email, &form.password, app.clock().now()).await;
    let outcome = match verdict {
        Ok(SignInOutcome::Ok(user)) => {
            return match sign_in(&app, &parts, &user, Method::Password).await {
                Ok(headers) => (headers, Redirect::to(&return_to)).into_response(),
                Err(error) => AppError(error).into_response(),
            };
        }
        Ok(SignInOutcome::Failed) => Outcome::Failed,
        Ok(SignInOutcome::Locked) => Outcome::Locked,
        Err(error) => return AppError(error).into_response(),
    };
    // The same lookup runs for known and unknown emails, so its time says
    // nothing; it only lets the user see their failed attempts.
    let user_id = match users::find_by_email(app.pool(), email).await {
        Ok(found) => found.map(|user| user.id),
        Err(error) => return AppError(error).into_response(),
    };
    audit(&app, user_id.as_deref(), Method::Password, outcome, ip).await;
    let mut view = sign_in_view(&app, return_to);
    view.error = Some(SIGN_IN_FAILED);
    sign_in_response(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, &view)
}

/// Signs a verified user in: ends the session this browser held (rotation),
/// starts a new one and records the event.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
/// * `parts` - the request (cookie, address, `User-Agent`).
/// * `user` - the verified user.
/// * `method` - how they proved who they are.
///
/// # Returns
/// The `Set-Cookie` header to send.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]; [`OkfError::Io`] from the random source.
pub(crate) async fn sign_in(
    app: &App,
    parts: &Parts,
    user: &UserAuth,
    method: Method,
) -> Result<HeaderMap, OkfError> {
    if let Some(old) = cookie(&parts.headers, COOKIE) {
        user_sessions::revoke(app.pool(), old).await?;
    }
    let ip = client_ip(parts, &app.config().auth);
    let user_agent = parts
        .headers
        .get(header::USER_AGENT)
        .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let (headers, _session) = start_session(app, user, ip, user_agent).await?;
    audit(app, Some(&user.id), method, Outcome::Ok, ip).await;
    Ok(headers)
}

/// Records a sign-in attempt: an `info` line and a `sign_in_events` row.
/// A failure to record is logged; it never decides the sign-in.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
/// * `user_id` - the user, when known.
/// * `method` - how they tried.
/// * `outcome` - what happened.
/// * `ip` - their address, if known.
pub(crate) async fn audit(
    app: &App,
    user_id: Option<&str>,
    method: Method,
    outcome: Outcome,
    ip: Option<IpAddr>,
) {
    tracing::info!(
        user = user_id.unwrap_or("-"),
        method = ?method,
        outcome = ?outcome,
        ip = ?ip,
        "sign-in attempt"
    );
    let now = app.clock().now();
    if let Err(error) = sign_in_events::record(app.pool(), user_id, method, outcome, ip, now).await {
        tracing::error!(%error, "recording a sign-in event failed");
    }
}

/// Queues the "a sign-in method was added" notice to the user's email.
/// A user without an email, or a failure to queue (logged), sends nothing.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
/// * `user` - the user.
/// * `method` - what was added, in words ("a new password", "a passkey").
pub(crate) async fn notify_method_added(app: &App, user: &UserAuth, method: &str) {
    let Some(to) = user.email.as_deref() else {
        return;
    };
    let template = Template::MethodAdded { method: method.to_string() };
    if let Err(error) = mail_queue::enqueue(app.pool(), to, &template, app.clock().now()).await {
        tracing::error!(%error, user = %user.id, "queueing the sign-in method notice failed");
    }
}

/// The forgot page's body: the form, or the one answer.
fn forgot_html(sent: bool) -> String {
    if sent {
        return format!(
            r#"        <h1>Check your email</h1>
        <p id="forgot-sent" role="status">{}</p>
        <p><a href="/signin">Back to sign in</a></p>"#,
            escape(FORGOT_SENT)
        );
    }
    r#"        <h1>Forgot your password?</h1>
        <p class="muted">Enter your email address and we will send you a link to choose a new password.</p>
        <form method="post" action="/signin/forgot" id="forgot-form">
            <label>Email
                <input type="email" name="email" id="forgot-email" autocomplete="username" required>
            </label>
            <button type="submit" id="forgot-submit">Send the link</button>
        </form>
        <p><a href="/signin">Back to sign in</a></p>"#
        .to_string()
}

/// `GET /signin/forgot`.
async fn forgot_page() -> Response {
    pages::page(StatusCode::OK, "Forgot your password?", &forgot_html(false), CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY)
}

/// `POST /signin/forgot`'s form.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
struct ForgotForm {
    email: String,
}

/// `POST /signin/forgot`: always the same answer (spec), 429 only past the
/// per-address limit.
async fn forgot_post(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    parts: Parts,
    form: Result<Form<ForgotForm>, FormRejection>,
) -> Response {
    let now = Instant::now();
    let limits = app.sign_in_limits();
    let ip = client_ip(&parts, &app.config().auth);
    if !limits.forgot_per_ip.try_take(&ip_key(ip), now) {
        return message_page(StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, "Forgot your password?", TOO_MANY);
    }
    if let Ok(Form(form)) = form {
        let email = form.email.trim().to_lowercase();
        // Past the per-email limit the answer is the same, so it never says
        // whether the address is known. The work runs after the answer for
        // the same reason: its duration would.
        if !email.is_empty() && limits.forgot_per_email.try_take(&email, now) {
            let app = Arc::clone(&app);
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                if let Err(error) = send_reset(&app, &email).await {
                    tracing::error!(%error, "sending a password reset link failed");
                }
            });
        }
    }
    pages::page(StatusCode::OK, "Check your email", &forgot_html(true), CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY)
}

/// Issues a reset link and queues it, when `email` names a user.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]; [`OkfError::Io`] from the random source.
async fn send_reset(app: &App, email: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let Some(public_url) = app.config().public_url.as_deref() else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let Some(user) = users::find_by_email(app.pool(), email).await? else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let Some(to) = user.email.as_deref() else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let ttl = app.settings().reset_link_ttl;
    let token = email_tokens::issue(app.pool(), &user.id, Purpose::Reset, ttl, app.clock().now()).await?;
    let link = mail::link(public_url, RESET_PATH, &token);
    mail_queue::enqueue(app.pool(), to, &Template::Reset { link }, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user.id, "password reset link queued");
    Ok(())
}

/// A token in a link's query. No `Debug`: it holds the token.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct TokenQuery {
    #[serde(default)]
    token: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    return_to: Option<String>,
}

/// The answer to an emailed link that does not work: 410 for an expired,
/// used or unknown one, else the error.
fn link_error(error: OkfError) -> Response {
    match error {
        OkfError::Gone { .. } => message_page(StatusCode::GONE, "Link expired", LINK_EXPIRED),
        other => AppError(other).into_response(),
    }
}

/// A new password and its confirmation: equal, and within the policy.
///
/// # Returns
/// `Err` with what to tell the person.
fn check_new_password(password: &str, confirm: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if password != confirm {
        return Err("The two passwords do not match.".to_string());
    }
    match passwords::check_policy(password) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded { reason, .. }) => Err(reason),
        Err(other) => Err(other.to_string()),
    }
}

/// The error line of a form page.
fn error_line(error: Option<&str>) -> String {
    error.map_or_else(String::new, |message| {
        format!(
            "        <p class=\"error consent-error\" id=\"form-error\" role=\"alert\">{}</p>\n",
            escape(message)
        )
    })
}

/// The setup page's body.
pub(crate) fn setup_html(view: &SetupView<'_>) -> String {
    let return_to = escape(view.return_to);
    let passkey = if view.passkey {
        format!(
            r#"
        <section class="signin-passkey" id="setup-passkey-section">
            <h2>Or use a passkey</h2>
            <label>Passkey name
                <input type="text" id="setup-passkey-name" value="Passkey" maxlength="64">
            </label>
            <button type="button" id="setup-passkey" class="secondary" data-return-to="{return_to}">Register a passkey and sign in</button>
            <p class="error" id="passkey-error" role="alert" hidden></p>
        </section>"#
        )
    } else {
        String::new()
    };
    format!(
        r#"        <h1>Set up your account</h1>
        <p>Welcome, <strong>{user}</strong>. Choose a password to sign in with.</p>
{error}        <form method="post" action="/account/setup" id="setup-form">
            <input type="hidden" name="token" value="{token}">
            <input type="hidden" name="return_to" value="{return_to}">
            <label>Password (at least 12 characters)
                <input type="password" name="password" id="setup-password" autocomplete="new-password" minlength="12" required>
            </label>
            <label>Confirm the password
                <input type="password" name="confirm" id="setup-confirm" autocomplete="new-password" required>
            </label>
            <button type="submit" id="setup-submit">Set password and sign in</button>
        </form>{passkey}"#,
        user = escape(view.user),
        error = error_line(view.error),
        token = escape(view.token),
    )
}

/// The setup page with `status`.
fn setup_response(status: StatusCode, view: &SetupView<'_>) -> Response {
    let scripts: &[&str] = if view.passkey { &[PASSKEY_SCRIPT] } else { &[] };
    pages::scripted_page(status, "Set up your account", &setup_html(view), scripts, CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY)
}

/// `GET /account/setup?token=...`.
async fn setup_page(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, Query(query): Query<TokenQuery>) -> Response {
    let return_to = safe_return_to(query.return_to.as_deref());
    match email_tokens::peek(app.pool(), &query.token, Purpose::Setup, app.clock().now()).await {
        Ok(user) => setup_response(
            StatusCode::OK,
            &SetupView {
                user: &user.name,
                token: &query.token,
                return_to: &return_to,
                error: None,
                passkey: offers_passkeys(&app),
            },
        ),
        Err(error) => link_error(error),
    }
}

/// `POST /account/setup`'s form. No `Debug`: it holds the token and passwords.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct NewPasswordForm {
    token: String,
    password: String,
    confirm: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    return_to: Option<String>,
}

/// `POST /account/setup`: sets the password and signs in. The link is used
/// only once the password passes, so a weak one can be retried.
async fn setup_post(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    parts: Parts,
    form: Result<Form<NewPasswordForm>, FormRejection>,
) -> Response {
    let Ok(Form(form)) = form else {
        return message_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "Set up your account", "Open the link from your email again.");
    };
    let return_to = safe_return_to(form.return_to.as_deref());
    let now = app.clock().now();
    let user = match email_tokens::peek(app.pool(), &form.token, Purpose::Setup, now).await {
        Ok(user) => user,
        Err(error) => return link_error(error),
    };
    if let Err(problem) = check_new_password(&form.password, &form.confirm) {
        let view = SetupView {
            user: &user.name,
            token: &form.token,
            return_to: &return_to,
            error: Some(&problem),
            passkey: offers_passkeys(&app),
        };
        return setup_response(StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, &view);
    }
    let user = match email_tokens::redeem(app.pool(), &form.token, Purpose::Setup, now).await {
        Ok(user) => user,
        Err(error) => return link_error(error),
    };
    if let Err(error) = passwords::set(app.pool(), &user.id, &form.password, now).await {
        return AppError(error).into_response();
    }
    match sign_in(&app, &parts, &user, Method::Setup).await {
        Ok(headers) => (headers, Redirect::to(&return_to)).into_response(),
        Err(error) => AppError(error).into_response(),
    }
}

/// The reset page's body.
fn reset_html(token: &str, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
    format!(
        r#"        <h1>Choose a new password</h1>
        <p class="muted">Every session you have open will be signed out.</p>
{error}        <form method="post" action="/account/reset" id="reset-form">
            <input type="hidden" name="token" value="{token}">
            <label>New password (at least 12 characters)
                <input type="password" name="password" id="reset-password" autocomplete="new-password" minlength="12" required>
            </label>
            <label>Confirm the password
                <input type="password" name="confirm" id="reset-confirm" autocomplete="new-password" required>
            </label>
            <button type="submit" id="reset-submit">Change password</button>
        </form>"#,
        error = error_line(error),
        token = escape(token),
    )
}

/// `GET /account/reset?token=...`.
async fn reset_page(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, Query(query): Query<TokenQuery>) -> Response {
    match email_tokens::peek(app.pool(), &query.token, Purpose::Reset, app.clock().now()).await {
        Ok(_) => pages::page(StatusCode::OK, "Choose a new password", &reset_html(&query.token, None), CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY),
        Err(error) => link_error(error),
    }
}

/// `POST /account/reset`: sets the password, ends every session (spec),
/// sends the notice and returns to `/signin`.
async fn reset_post(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, form: Result<Form<NewPasswordForm>, FormRejection>) -> Response {
    let Ok(Form(form)) = form else {
        return message_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "Choose a new password", "Open the link from your email again.");
    };
    let now = app.clock().now();
    if let Err(error) = email_tokens::peek(app.pool(), &form.token, Purpose::Reset, now).await {
        return link_error(error);
    }
    if let Err(problem) = check_new_password(&form.password, &form.confirm) {
        let html = reset_html(&form.token, Some(&problem));
        return pages::page(StatusCode::UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY, "Choose a new password", &html, CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY);
    }
    let user = match email_tokens::redeem(app.pool(), &form.token, Purpose::Reset, now).await {
        Ok(user) => user,
        Err(error) => return link_error(error),
    };
    if let Err(error) = passwords::set(app.pool(), &user.id, &form.password, now).await {
        return AppError(error).into_response();
    }
    match user_sessions::revoke_all(app.pool(), &user.id, None).await {
        Ok(ended) => tracing::info!(user = %user.id, ended, "password reset; every session ended"),
        Err(error) => return AppError(error).into_response(),
    }
    notify_method_added(&app, &user, "a new password").await;
    Redirect::to("/signin?notice=reset").into_response()
}
```

`OkfError::LimitExceeded`'s `reason` is a `String`, and `Gone` is Task 1's 410 variant.

```js
async function request(method, path, { body, raw = false, quiet = false, key } = {}) {
    const headers = {};
    const bearer = key ?? store.key;
    // A pasted key goes as a bearer. Without one, the session cookie goes
    // by itself (same origin), and a write carries the session's CSRF token.
    if (bearer) headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${bearer}`;
    else if (method !== 'GET' && store.csrf) headers['X-OKF-CSRF'] = store.csrf;
```

```js
// Without a stored key, a console session (its cookie) may still be live:
// ask before showing the card. A plain fetch, so a 401 here is not "the key
// was refused".
async function resumeSession() {
    let response;
    try { response = await fetch('/api/v1/session'); } catch { showLogin(); return; }
    if (!response.ok) { showLogin(); return; }
    store.csrf = (await response.json()).csrf;
    await enterOrRecover();
}
```

```rust
//! Signing in as a person: an emailed setup link, a password, the console
//! showing the user, sign-out and sign-in again with the password.

use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::Utc;
use okf_mcp::config::Config;
use okf_mcp::mail::{link, SETUP_PATH};
use okf_mcp::mail::{queue as mail_queue, Template};
use okf_mcp::store::email_tokens::{self, Purpose};
use okf_mcp::store::keys::Access;
use okf_mcp::store::sign_in_events::{self, Method, Outcome};
use okf_mcp::store::{ceiling, users};
use rustwright::GotoOptions;

use crate::harness::drive;
use crate::support::server::{files, TestServer};

const PASSWORD: &str = "violet-lantern-orbit-42";

/// The link in a queued mail's payload, as the mailer would send it.
fn link_in(job: &str, path: &str) -> String {
    let at = job.find(path).expect("the mail carries the link");
    let start = job[..at].rfind("http").expect("an absolute link");
    let end = job[at..]
        .find(|c: char| !(c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || "/?=_-.:".contains(c)))
        .map_or(job.len(), |length| at + length);
    job[start..end].to_string()
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_setup_link_sets_a_password_and_the_console_shows_the_user() {
    let server = TestServer::start_with(vec![("main", files(&[("index.md", "# Main\n")]))], |base| Config {
        public_url: Some(base.to_string()),
        ..Config::default()
    })
    .await;
    let pool = &server.db.pool;
    users::create(pool, &users::NewUser { name: "alice", display_name: "Alice" }, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("create alice");
    users::set_email(pool, "alice", Some("alice@example.com")).await.expect("set the email");
    ceiling::entitle(pool, "alice", "main", Access::Read, Utc::now()).await.expect("entitle");
    server.app.poll().await.expect("poll");
    let alice = users::find_by_email(pool, "alice@example.com")
        .await
        .expect("find alice")
        .expect("alice exists");
    let token = email_tokens::issue(pool, &alice.id, Purpose::Setup, Duration::from_secs(3600), Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("issue a setup link");
    let template = Template::Setup {
        link: link(&server.base, SETUP_PATH, &token),
        user: "alice".to_string(),
    };
    mail_queue::enqueue(pool, "alice@example.com", &template, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("queue the mail");
    let job: String = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT convert_from(job, 'UTF8') FROM apalis.jobs")
        .fetch_one(pool)
        .await
        .expect("the queued mail");
    let link = link_in(&job, "/account/setup?token=");

    let ran = drive(server.base.clone(), move |ui| {
        ui.page.goto(&link, GotoOptions::default()).expect("open the setup link");
        ui.wait_visible("#setup-form");
        ui.fill("#setup-password", PASSWORD);
        ui.fill("#setup-confirm", PASSWORD);
        ui.click("#setup-submit");
        ui.wait_visible("#app");
        ui.wait_text("#whoami", "alice");
        assert!(!ui.page.is_visible("[data-need=admin]").expect("visible"));
        ui.click("#signout");
        ui.wait_visible("#login");
        ui.open("");
        ui.wait_visible("#login");
        ui.sign_in_password("alice@example.com", PASSWORD);
        ui.wait_text("#whoami", "alice");
    })
    .await;
    if !ran {
        return;
    }
    let events = sign_in_events::recent(pool, "alice", 10).await.expect("events");
    assert_eq!(events.len(), 2);
    assert!(matches!((&events[0].method, &events[0].outcome), (Method::Password, Outcome::Ok)));
    assert!(matches!((&events[1].method, &events[1].outcome), (Method::Setup, Outcome::Ok)));
    // `http::serve` gives requests their peer address (Decision 7).
    assert_eq!(events[0].ip, "127.0.0.1".parse().ok());
}
```

webauthn-rs facts this task relies on (verified in the probe, `crate-probe/tests/probe.rs`):
- `start_passkey_registration` asks for `residentKey: "discouraged"`, so the server sets `authenticator_selection.resident_key = Required` before sending the challenge (Decision 13). It never sets `require_resident_key`: the test authenticator refuses that.
- `start_discoverable_authentication` sets `mediation = Conditional` (autofill). The button flow clears it.
- `identify_discoverable_authentication` returns the user handle as a `Uuid` and the credential id. The library does not check that the handle is the credential's owner; the server does.
- `finish_discoverable_authentication_v2(&credential, state, &passkey)` refuses a counter that did not move (`CredentialPossibleCompromise`), and `Passkey::update_credential` raises the stored counter.
- `SoftPasskey::new(true)` (it fakes user verification) cannot discover credentials and sends no `userHandle`. HTTP tests therefore put the credential id in `allowCredentials` and the user's UUID bytes in `response.userHandle`; neither is covered by the signature.
- `WebauthnBuilder::new` needs a domain: an address origin fails. Passkeys are off for an address `public_url`.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod testing {
    //! A real registered passkey for store tests, made with the software
    //! authenticator (no HTTP).

    use webauthn_authenticator_rs::prelude::WebauthnAuthenticator;
    use webauthn_authenticator_rs::softpasskey::SoftPasskey;
    use webauthn_rs::prelude::{Passkey, Url, Uuid, WebauthnBuilder};

    /// Registers a new software passkey for `user_id` (a UUID).
    pub(crate) fn passkey_for(user_id: &str) -> Passkey {
        let origin = Url::parse("http://localhost:8080").expect("an origin");
        let webauthn = WebauthnBuilder::new("localhost", &origin)
            .expect("a builder")
            .build()
            .expect("webauthn");
        let handle = Uuid::parse_str(user_id).expect("user ids are UUIDs");
        let (challenge, state) = webauthn
            .start_passkey_registration(handle, "alice@example.com", "alice", None)
            .expect("a challenge");
        let credential = SoftPasskey::new(true)
            .do_registration(origin, challenge)
            .expect("the authenticator registers");
        webauthn
            .finish_passkey_registration(&credential, &state)
            .expect("a passkey")
    }
}
```

```rust
//! How many ways a user can sign in: the guard that keeps the last one
//! from being removed (spec "Self-service": 409).

use sqlx::PgConnection;

use crate::error::OkfError;

/// A user's sign-in methods: a password (0 or 1), plus passkeys, plus
/// linked identities. Locks the user's row `FOR UPDATE` first, so two
/// removals of different methods run one at a time and cannot both see a
/// count of two. Call it inside the transaction that removes a method.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `conn` - the caller's transaction (`&mut tx`).
/// * `user_id` - the user's id.
///
/// # Returns
/// The count.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] for an unknown user; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn count(conn: &mut PgConnection, user_id: &str) -> Result<i64, OkfError> {
    let has_password: Option<bool> =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT password_hash IS NOT NULL FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE")
            .bind(user_id)
            .fetch_optional(&mut *conn)
            .await?;
    let Some(has_password) = has_password else {
        return Err(OkfError::NotFound {
            path: format!("users/{user_id}"),
        });
    };
    let others: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM user_passkeys WHERE user_id = $1)
              + (SELECT count(*) FROM user_identities WHERE user_id = $1)",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_one(&mut *conn)
    .await?;
    Ok(others + i64::from(has_password))
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `src/store/passkeys.rs`**

```rust
//! Users' WebAuthn passkeys (`user_passkeys`): public keys only, stored as
//! webauthn-rs's serialized `Passkey` (its signature counter included).
//! Passkeys are not part of the key cache, so nothing here bumps
//! `admin_generation`.

use base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
use base64::Engine as _;
use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::types::Json;
use sqlx::PgPool;
use webauthn_rs::prelude::Passkey;

use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::store::catalogs::is_unique_violation;
use crate::store::sign_in_methods;

/// A passkey as the account page lists it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PasskeyInfo {
    /// Its credential id, unpadded base64url (the id the API takes).
    pub id: String,
    /// The name its owner gave it.
    pub name: String,
    /// When it was registered.
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// When it last signed in.
    pub last_used_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
}

/// Stores a newly registered passkey.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - its owner.
/// * `passkey` - from `finish_passkey_registration`.
/// * `name` - its name (checked by the caller).
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] if the credential is already registered;
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn add(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    passkey: &Passkey,
    name: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    // `Json(...)` binds the value as `jsonb` through serde.
    let inserted = sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO user_passkeys (credential_id, user_id, passkey, name, created_at)
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)",
    )
    .bind(passkey.cred_id().as_slice())
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(Json(passkey))
    .bind(name)
    .bind(now)
    .execute(pool)
    .await;
    match inserted {
        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
        Err(error) if is_unique_violation(&error) => Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "this passkey is already registered".to_string(),
        }),
        Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
    }
}

/// A user's passkeys, oldest first, for `exclude_credentials`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user.
///
/// # Returns
/// Each passkey's name and value.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn for_user(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<(String, Passkey)>, OkfError> {
    let rows: Vec<(String, Json<Passkey>)> = sqlx::query_as(
        "SELECT name, passkey FROM user_passkeys WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;
    // `Json(passkey)` destructures the wrapper.
    Ok(rows.into_iter().map(|(name, Json(passkey))| (name, passkey)).collect())
}

/// The passkey with this credential id.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `credential_id` - the raw id from the assertion.
///
/// # Returns
/// Its owner's id and the passkey, or `None`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn find(
    pool: &PgPool,
    credential_id: &[u8],
) -> Result<Option<(String, Passkey)>, OkfError> {
    let row: Option<(String, Json<Passkey>)> =
        sqlx::query_as("SELECT user_id, passkey FROM user_passkeys WHERE credential_id = $1")
            .bind(credential_id)
            .fetch_optional(pool)
            .await?;
    Ok(row.map(|(user_id, Json(passkey))| (user_id, passkey)))
}

/// Stores a passkey after a sign-in (its raised counter and backup flags)
/// and when it was used.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `credential_id` - its raw id.
/// * `passkey` - after `update_credential`.
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn update(
    pool: &PgPool,
    credential_id: &[u8],
    passkey: &Passkey,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    sqlx::query("UPDATE user_passkeys SET passkey = $2, last_used_at = $3 WHERE credential_id = $1")
        .bind(credential_id)
        .bind(Json(passkey))
        .bind(now)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// A user's passkeys, oldest first.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user.
///
/// # Returns
/// Their listing.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn list(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<PasskeyInfo>, OkfError> {
    let rows: Vec<(Vec<u8>, String, DateTime<Utc>, Option<DateTime<Utc>>)> = sqlx::query_as(
        "SELECT credential_id, name, created_at, last_used_at
         FROM user_passkeys WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(credential_id, name, created_at, last_used_at)| PasskeyInfo {
            id: URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(credential_id),
            name,
            created_at,
            last_used_at,
        })
        .collect())
}

/// The raw credential id of an API id; not found when it is not base64url.
fn credential_id(id: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, OkfError> {
    URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(id).map_err(|_| not_found(id))
}

fn not_found(id: &str) -> OkfError {
    OkfError::NotFound {
        path: format!("me/passkeys/{id}"),
    }
}

/// Renames one of the user's passkeys.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the owner.
/// * `id` - the passkey's base64url id.
/// * `name` - the new name (checked by the caller).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] unless the user owns it; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn rename(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str, id: &str, name: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let renamed = sqlx::query("UPDATE user_passkeys SET name = $3 WHERE credential_id = $1 AND user_id = $2")
        .bind(credential_id(id)?)
        .bind(user_id)
        .bind(name)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;
    if renamed.rows_affected() == 0 {
        return Err(not_found(id));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Removes one of the user's passkeys, unless it is their last sign-in
/// method.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the owner.
/// * `id` - the passkey's base64url id.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] unless the user owns it; [`OkfError::Refused`]
/// for the last sign-in method; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn remove(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let credential_id = credential_id(id)?;
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // Locks the user first, so concurrent removals see each other.
    let methods = sign_in_methods::count(&mut tx, user_id).await?;
    let owned: bool = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_passkeys WHERE credential_id = $1 AND user_id = $2)",
    )
    .bind(&credential_id)
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    if !owned {
        return Err(not_found(id));
    }
    if methods <= 1 {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "this is your last way to sign in; add a password or another passkey first"
                .to_string(),
        });
    }
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM user_passkeys WHERE credential_id = $1")
        .bind(&credential_id)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Register both in `src/store/mod.rs` (`pub mod passkeys;`, `pub mod sign_in_methods;`, sorted).

```rust
//! Passkeys (spec "Passkeys", plan Decision 13): WebAuthn registration from
//! an emailed setup link or a signed-in console session, and discoverable
//! ("usernameless") sign-in. The relying party id is `public_url`'s host
//! and the origin is `public_url`; webauthn-rs always requires user
//! verification.
//!
//! A ceremony's server-side state waits in memory for at most five
//! minutes, keyed by a random id in the `okf_passkey` cookie, and is used
//! once. Like pending consent pages, it is per process.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use axum::extract::State;
use axum::http::request::Parts;
use axum::http::{header, HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::middleware;
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
use axum::routing::post;
use axum::{Extension, Json, Router};
use base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
use base64::Engine as _;
use serde::Deserialize;
use webauthn_rs::prelude::{
    CredentialID, DiscoverableAuthentication, PasskeyRegistration, PublicKeyCredential,
    RegisterPublicKeyCredential, Url, Uuid, Webauthn, WebauthnBuilder, WebauthnError,
};
use webauthn_rs_proto::ResidentKeyRequirement;

use crate::app::App;
use crate::auth::{CredentialKind, Principal};
use crate::config::Config;

/// The ceremony cookie: `SameSite=Strict`, five minutes.
pub const CEREMONY_COOKIE: &str = "okf_passkey";
/// How long a ceremony may take (spec: a five-minute cookie).
pub const CEREMONY_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5 * 60);
/// The most ceremonies in progress at once (they start unauthenticated).
pub const MAX_CEREMONIES: usize = 10_000;
/// The longest passkey name.
pub const MAX_NAME_CHARS: usize = 64;

const SIGN_IN_FAILED: &str = "Passkey sign-in failed; try again";
const REGISTRATION_FAILED: &str = "The passkey could not be registered; try again";
const CEREMONY_EXPIRED: &str = "The passkey request expired; start again";

/// The WebAuthn relying party and the ceremonies in progress, held by `App`.
pub struct Passkeys {
    webauthn: Webauthn,
    ceremonies: ExpiringMap<Ceremony>,
}

impl Passkeys {
    /// The relying party for `public_url`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `config` - the server's settings.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `None` without `public_url`, or when its host is an address (WebAuthn
    /// needs a domain; logged at `info`).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OkfError::Config`] if `public_url` does not parse or webauthn-rs
    /// refuses it.
    pub fn new(config: &Config) -> Result<Option<Self>, OkfError> {
        let Some(public_url) = config.public_url.as_deref() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let error = |message: String| OkfError::Config {
            path: "public_url".to_string(),
            message,
        };
        let origin = Url::parse(public_url).map_err(|e| error(format!("{public_url:?}: {e}")))?;
        // `domain()` is `None` for an address host such as 127.0.0.1.
        let Some(rp_id) = origin.domain() else {
            tracing::info!("passkeys are off: public_url's host is an address, and WebAuthn needs a domain");
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let webauthn = WebauthnBuilder::new(rp_id, &origin)
            .and_then(|builder| builder.rp_name("okf").build())
            .map_err(|e| error(format!("WebAuthn refuses {public_url:?}: {e}")))?;
        Ok(Some(Self {
            webauthn,
            ceremonies: ExpiringMap::new(CEREMONY_TTL, MAX_CEREMONIES),
        }))
    }
}

/// A ceremony in progress.
enum Ceremony {
    /// Registering a passkey (boxed: much larger than a sign-in).
    Register(Box<Registration>),
    /// A discoverable sign-in.
    SignIn {
        state: DiscoverableAuthentication,
        return_to: String,
    },
}

/// A registration's state and what to do once it finishes.
struct Registration {
    state: PasskeyRegistration,
    user_id: String,
    pending: Pending,
}

/// What a registration was started with.
struct Pending {
    name: String,
    via: RegisterVia,
    return_to: String,
}

/// Who asked for a registration.
enum RegisterVia {
    /// The setup page, with the emailed token (redeemed at finish).
    Setup { token: String },
    /// A signed-in session, which other sessions are ended for unless kept.
    Session { session_id: String, keep_sessions: bool },
}

/// The open routes (no credential), merged only when passkeys are on.
///
/// # Returns
/// The router; every response is `no-store` and `nosniff`.
pub(crate) fn routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    Router::new()
        .route("/auth/passkey/setup/start", post(setup_start))
        .route("/auth/passkey/setup/finish", post(setup_finish))
        .route("/auth/passkey/signin/start", post(sign_in_start))
        .route("/auth/passkey/signin/finish", post(sign_in_finish))
        .layer(timeout_layer())
        .layer(middleware::map_response(api_headers))
}

/// The signed-in registration routes, merged into `/api/v1` (behind
/// `require_principal`); 404 while passkeys are off.
///
/// # Returns
/// The router.
pub(crate) fn api_routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    Router::new()
        .route("/me/passkeys/register/start", post(register_start))
        .route("/me/passkeys/register/finish", post(register_finish))
}

fn enabled(app: &App) -> Result<&Passkeys, OkfError> {
    app.passkeys().ok_or_else(|| OkfError::NotFound {
        path: "passkeys".to_string(),
    })
}

fn expired() -> OkfError {
    OkfError::Gone {
        reason: CEREMONY_EXPIRED.to_string(),
    }
}

/// Logs why webauthn-rs refused, and answers with one message.
fn refused(error: &WebauthnError, message: &str) -> OkfError {
    tracing::debug!(%error, "WebAuthn refused");
    OkfError::Unauthenticated {
        reason: message.to_string(),
    }
}

/// A passkey name: trimmed, 1 to 64 characters, no control characters.
fn passkey_name(raw: &str) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    let name = raw.trim();
    let length = name.chars().count();
    if length == 0 || length > MAX_NAME_CHARS || name.chars().any(char::is_control) {
        return Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded {
            limit: "passkey_name",
            reason: format!("a passkey name is 1 to {MAX_NAME_CHARS} characters"),
        });
    }
    Ok(name.to_string())
}

/// The WebAuthn user handle: the user's UUID (`users.id` is
/// `gen_random_uuid()::text`).
fn user_handle(user_id: &str) -> Result<Uuid, OkfError> {
    Uuid::parse_str(user_id).map_err(|_| OkfError::Refused {
        reason: "this user's id is not a UUID, which a passkey needs".to_string(),
    })
}

/// Stores a ceremony and returns the cookie that names it.
fn remember(app: &App, passkeys: &Passkeys, ceremony: Ceremony) -> Result<HeaderMap, OkfError> {
    let id = keys::generate_with("")?;
    if !passkeys.ceremonies.insert(id.clone(), ceremony, Instant::now()) {
        return Err(OkfError::Busy {
            reason: "too many passkey requests in progress; try again shortly".to_string(),
        });
    }
    let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
    headers.insert(
        header::SET_COOKIE,
        set_cookie(CEREMONY_COOKIE, &id, CEREMONY_TTL, SameSite::Strict, secure_cookies(app)),
    );
    Ok(headers)
}

/// Takes (single use) the ceremony the cookie names.
///
/// # Returns
/// The ceremony and the header that clears its cookie.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Gone`] without a cookie or a live ceremony.
fn take_ceremony(app: &App, passkeys: &Passkeys, headers: &HeaderMap) -> Result<(Ceremony, HeaderMap), OkfError> {
    let id = cookie(headers, CEREMONY_COOKIE).ok_or_else(expired)?;
    let ceremony = passkeys.ceremonies.take(id, Instant::now()).ok_or_else(expired)?;
    let mut clear = HeaderMap::new();
    clear.insert(
        header::SET_COOKIE,
        set_cookie(CEREMONY_COOKIE, "", Duration::ZERO, SameSite::Strict, secure_cookies(app)),
    );
    Ok((ceremony, clear))
}

/// Starts a registration for `user`: the challenge (asking for a
/// discoverable credential) and the ceremony cookie.
async fn begin_registration(
    app: &App,
    passkeys: &Passkeys,
    user: &UserAuth,
    pending: Pending,
) -> Result<Response, OkfError> {
    let handle = user_handle(&user.id)?;
    let existing: Vec<CredentialID> = passkey_rows::for_user(app.pool(), &user.id)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(_, passkey)| passkey.cred_id().clone())
        .collect();
    let account = user.email.as_deref().unwrap_or(&user.name);
    let (mut challenge, state) = passkeys
        .webauthn
        .start_passkey_registration(handle, account, &user.name, (!existing.is_empty()).then_some(existing))
        .map_err(|error| refused(&error, REGISTRATION_FAILED))?;
    // webauthn-rs asks for `residentKey: "discouraged"`; discoverable
    // sign-in needs the credential kept on the authenticator.
    if let Some(selection) = challenge.public_key.authenticator_selection.as_mut() {
        selection.resident_key = Some(ResidentKeyRequirement::Required);
    }
    let ceremony = Ceremony::Register(Box::new(Registration {
        state,
        user_id: user.id.clone(),
        pending,
    }));
    let headers = remember(app, passkeys, ceremony)?;
    Ok((headers, Json(challenge)).into_response())
}

/// Takes the registration the cookie names and verifies the credential.
///
/// # Returns
/// The new passkey, what the registration was started with, its owner and
/// the header that clears the ceremony cookie.
fn finish_registration(
    app: &App,
    passkeys: &Passkeys,
    headers: &HeaderMap,
    credential: &RegisterPublicKeyCredential,
) -> Result<(webauthn_rs::prelude::Passkey, Pending, String, HeaderMap), OkfError> {
    let (ceremony, clear) = take_ceremony(app, passkeys, headers)?;
    let Ceremony::Register(registration) = ceremony else {
        return Err(expired());
    };
    // `*registration` moves the struct out of its `Box`.
    let Registration { state, user_id, pending } = *registration;
    let passkey = passkeys
        .webauthn
        .finish_passkey_registration(credential, &state)
        .map_err(|error| refused(&error, REGISTRATION_FAILED))?;
    Ok((passkey, pending, user_id, clear))
}

/// `POST /auth/passkey/setup/start`'s body. No `Debug`: it holds the token.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct SetupStart {
    token: String,
    name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    return_to: Option<String>,
}

/// `POST /auth/passkey/setup/start`: a registration challenge for the
/// setup link's user. The link is checked, not used.
///
/// # Errors
/// 404 with passkeys off; 410 for a bad link; 422 for a bad name.
async fn setup_start(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, Json(body): Json<SetupStart>) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let passkeys = enabled(&app)?;
    let name = passkey_name(&body.name)?;
    let user = email_tokens::peek(app.pool(), &body.token, Purpose::Setup, app.clock().now()).await?;
    let pending = Pending {
        name,
        via: RegisterVia::Setup { token: body.token },
        return_to: safe_return_to(body.return_to.as_deref()),
    };
    Ok(begin_registration(&app, passkeys, &user, pending).await?)
}

/// `POST /auth/passkey/setup/finish`: stores the passkey, uses the link and
/// signs in. Answers `{"redirect": <return_to>}`.
///
/// # Errors
/// 410 for an expired ceremony or a used link; 401 for a credential that
/// does not verify.
async fn setup_finish(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    parts: Parts,
    Json(credential): Json<RegisterPublicKeyCredential>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let passkeys = enabled(&app)?;
    let (passkey, pending, user_id, mut headers) = finish_registration(&app, passkeys, &parts.headers, &credential)?;
    let RegisterVia::Setup { token } = pending.via else {
        return Err(expired().into());
    };
    let now = app.clock().now();
    // Corrected (issue #316): the link is used and the passkey stored in one
    // transaction, as the password setup does (`use_link` in signin.rs), so a
    // failure leaves the link usable. `passkey_rows::add` needs an `_in`
    // form taking `&mut PgConnection` for this.
    let mut tx = app.pool().begin().await?;
    let user = email_tokens::redeem_in(&mut tx, &token, Purpose::Setup, now).await?;
    if user.id != user_id {
        return Err(OkfError::Gone { reason: LINK_EXPIRED.to_string() }.into());
    }
    passkey_rows::add_in(&mut tx, &user.id, &passkey, &pending.name, now).await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    append_all(&mut headers, &sign_in(&app, &parts, &user, Method::Setup).await?);
    Ok((headers, Json(serde_json::json!({ "redirect": pending.return_to }))).into_response())
}

/// `POST /auth/passkey/signin/start`'s body.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct SignInStart {
    #[serde(default)]
    return_to: Option<String>,
}

/// `POST /auth/passkey/signin/start`: a discoverable challenge.
///
/// # Errors
/// 404 with passkeys off; 503 when too many ceremonies are in progress.
async fn sign_in_start(State(app): State<Arc<App>>, Json(body): Json<SignInStart>) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let passkeys = enabled(&app)?;
    let (mut challenge, state) = passkeys
        .webauthn
        .start_discoverable_authentication()
        .map_err(|error| refused(&error, SIGN_IN_FAILED))?;
    // A button press, not autofill: without conditional mediation the
    // browser shows its modal prompt.
    challenge.mediation = None;
    let return_to = safe_return_to(body.return_to.as_deref());
    let headers = remember(&app, passkeys, Ceremony::SignIn { state, return_to })?;
    Ok((headers, Json(challenge)).into_response())
}

/// What an assertion proved.
enum Verdict {
    SignedIn(UserAuth),
    Refused { user_id: Option<String> },
}

/// Checks an assertion against the stored passkey and, if it holds,
/// stores the raised counter.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn verify_assertion(
    app: &App,
    passkeys: &Passkeys,
    credential: &PublicKeyCredential,
    state: DiscoverableAuthentication,
) -> Result<Verdict, OkfError> {
    let Ok((handle, credential_id)) = passkeys.webauthn.identify_discoverable_authentication(credential) else {
        return Ok(Verdict::Refused { user_id: None });
    };
    let Some((user_id, mut passkey)) = passkey_rows::find(app.pool(), credential_id).await? else {
        return Ok(Verdict::Refused { user_id: None });
    };
    // webauthn-rs does not check that the user handle names the
    // credential's owner.
    if Uuid::parse_str(&user_id).ok() != Some(handle) {
        return Ok(Verdict::Refused { user_id: Some(user_id) });
    }
    let result = match passkeys.webauthn.finish_discoverable_authentication_v2(credential, state, &passkey) {
        Ok(result) => result,
        Err(error) => {
            // A counter that did not move lands here
            // (`CredentialPossibleCompromise`).
            tracing::debug!(%error, user = %user_id, "passkey assertion refused");
            return Ok(Verdict::Refused { user_id: Some(user_id) });
        }
    };
    // Raises the stored counter and syncs the backup flags; `None` only if
    // the result is for another credential, which `_v2` already refused.
    if passkey.update_credential(&result).is_none() {
        return Ok(Verdict::Refused { user_id: Some(user_id) });
    }
    passkey_rows::update(app.pool(), credential_id, &passkey, app.clock().now()).await?;
    Ok(match session_user(app, &user_id).await? {
        Some(user) => Verdict::SignedIn(user),
        None => Verdict::Refused { user_id: None },
    })
}

/// 429 for the per-address limit, as JSON.
fn too_many() -> Response {
    (
        StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
        Json(serde_json::json!({
            "error": "TooManyRequests",
            "message": "Too many attempts from this address; wait a few minutes.",
        })),
    )
        .into_response()
}

/// `POST /auth/passkey/signin/finish`: signs in. Answers
/// `{"redirect": <return_to>}` with the session cookie.
///
/// # Errors
/// 410 for an expired or used ceremony; 401 for an assertion that does not
/// verify; 429 past the per-address limit.
async fn sign_in_finish(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    parts: Parts,
    Json(credential): Json<PublicKeyCredential>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let passkeys = enabled(&app)?;
    let ip = client_ip(&parts, &app.config().auth);
    if !app.sign_in_limits().sign_in_per_ip.try_take(&ip_key(ip), Instant::now()) {
        return Ok(too_many());
    }
    let (ceremony, mut headers) = take_ceremony(&app, passkeys, &parts.headers)?;
    let Ceremony::SignIn { state, return_to } = ceremony else {
        return Err(expired().into());
    };
    match verify_assertion(&app, passkeys, &credential, state).await? {
        Verdict::SignedIn(user) => {
            append_all(&mut headers, &sign_in(&app, &parts, &user, Method::Passkey).await?);
            Ok((headers, Json(serde_json::json!({ "redirect": return_to }))).into_response())
        }
        Verdict::Refused { user_id } => {
            audit(&app, user_id.as_deref(), Method::Passkey, Outcome::Failed, ip).await;
            Err(OkfError::Unauthenticated { reason: SIGN_IN_FAILED.to_string() }.into())
        }
    }
}

/// The calling session's user id and session, or 403 for a key or grant.
fn signed_in(principal: &Principal, session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>) -> Result<(String, ConsoleSession), OkfError> {
    match (&principal.kind, session) {
        (CredentialKind::Session { user_id }, Some(Extension(session))) => Ok((user_id.clone(), session)),
        _ => Err(OkfError::Forbidden {
            reason: "adding a passkey needs a console session".to_string(),
        }),
    }
}

/// `POST /me/passkeys/register/start`'s body.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct RegisterStart {
    name: String,
    /// Keep the user's other sessions (the account page's checkbox).
    #[serde(default)]
    keep_sessions: bool,
}

/// `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/start`.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a key or grant; 404 with passkeys off; 422 for a bad name.
async fn register_start(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>,
    Json(body): Json<RegisterStart>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let (user_id, session) = signed_in(&principal, session)?;
    let passkeys = enabled(&app)?;
    let name = passkey_name(&body.name)?;
    let user = session_user(&app, &user_id)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::Unauthenticated { reason: "this session's user no longer exists".to_string() })?;
    let pending = Pending {
        name,
        via: RegisterVia::Session { session_id: session.id, keep_sessions: body.keep_sessions },
        return_to: "/ui/#/account".to_string(),
    };
    Ok(begin_registration(&app, passkeys, &user, pending).await?)
}

/// `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/finish`: stores the passkey, ends the
/// user's other sessions unless kept, and mails the notice. 201 with
/// `{"id", "name"}`.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a key, a grant or another user's ceremony; 410 for an expired
/// ceremony; 401 for a credential that does not verify.
async fn register_finish(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    Json(credential): Json<RegisterPublicKeyCredential>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let (user_id, _session) = signed_in(&principal, session)?;
    let passkeys = enabled(&app)?;
    let (passkey, pending, owner, clear) = finish_registration(&app, passkeys, &headers, &credential)?;
    let RegisterVia::Session { session_id, keep_sessions } = pending.via else {
        return Err(expired().into());
    };
    if owner != user_id {
        return Err(OkfError::Forbidden { reason: "this passkey request belongs to another session".to_string() }.into());
    }
    passkey_rows::add(app.pool(), &user_id, &passkey, &pending.name, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user_id, "passkey added");
    if !keep_sessions {
        let ended = user_sessions::revoke_all(app.pool(), &user_id, Some(&session_id)).await?;
        tracing::info!(user = %user_id, ended, "other sessions ended after a passkey was added");
    }
    if let Some(user) = session_user(&app, &user_id).await? {
        notify_method_added(&app, &user, "a passkey").await;
    }
    let body = serde_json::json!({
        "id": URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(passkey.cred_id().as_slice()),
        "name": pending.name,
    });
    Ok((StatusCode::CREATED, clear, Json(body)).into_response())
}
```

```js
// The browser's WebAuthn API takes and returns ArrayBuffers; the server's
// JSON (webauthn-rs) carries them as unpadded base64url. These convert both
// ways. Shared by the sign-in and setup pages (passkey.js) and the account
// page.

export function toBuffer(base64url) {
    const base64 = base64url.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
    const binary = atob(base64 + '='.repeat((4 - (base64.length % 4)) % 4));
    const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
    return bytes.buffer;
}

export function toBase64url(buffer) {
    let binary = '';
    for (const byte of new Uint8Array(buffer)) binary += String.fromCharCode(byte);
    return btoa(binary).replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');
}

// navigator.credentials.create() options from a registration challenge.
export function creationOptions(challenge) {
    const publicKey = structuredClone(challenge.publicKey);
    publicKey.challenge = toBuffer(publicKey.challenge);
    publicKey.user.id = toBuffer(publicKey.user.id);
    publicKey.excludeCredentials = (publicKey.excludeCredentials ?? [])
        .map(credential => ({ ...credential, id: toBuffer(credential.id) }));
    return { publicKey };
}

// navigator.credentials.get() options from a sign-in challenge (no
// mediation: the server asks for a modal prompt).
export function requestOptions(challenge) {
    const publicKey = structuredClone(challenge.publicKey);
    publicKey.challenge = toBuffer(publicKey.challenge);
    publicKey.allowCredentials = (publicKey.allowCredentials ?? [])
        .map(credential => ({ ...credential, id: toBuffer(credential.id) }));
    return { publicKey };
}

// A created credential as webauthn-rs's RegisterPublicKeyCredential. The
// transports and client extension results are left out: both are optional,
// and a browser may report values the server does not know.
export function registrationJson(credential) {
    return {
        id: credential.id,
        rawId: toBase64url(credential.rawId),
        type: credential.type,
        extensions: {},
        response: {
            attestationObject: toBase64url(credential.response.attestationObject),
            clientDataJSON: toBase64url(credential.response.clientDataJSON),
        },
    };
}

// The whole browser side of a registration, for the account page (Task
// 14b): the server's challenge in, the credential JSON out. Rejects with the
// browser's DOMException (NotAllowedError) when the prompt is cancelled.
export async function createCredential(challenge) {
    return registrationJson(await navigator.credentials.create(creationOptions(challenge)));
}

// An assertion as webauthn-rs's PublicKeyCredential.
export function assertionJson(credential) {
    const response = credential.response;
    return {
        id: credential.id,
        rawId: toBase64url(credential.rawId),
        type: credential.type,
        extensions: {},
        response: {
            authenticatorData: toBase64url(response.authenticatorData),
            clientDataJSON: toBase64url(response.clientDataJSON),
            signature: toBase64url(response.signature),
            userHandle: response.userHandle ? toBase64url(response.userHandle) : null,
        },
    };
}
```

`src/http/ui/js/signin/passkey.js`:

```js
// The passkey buttons of the sign-in and setup pages (src/http/signin.rs).
// Each page has at most one; its data-return-to says where to go after.
import { assertionJson, creationOptions, registrationJson, requestOptions } from './webauthn.js';

async function post(path, body) {
    const response = await fetch(path, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
    });
    let json = null;
    try { json = await response.json(); } catch { /* not JSON */ }
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(json?.message ?? `HTTP ${response.status}`);
    return json;
}

// Runs one ceremony from `button`, showing a failure under it.
function wire(button, ceremony) {
    const error = document.getElementById('passkey-error');
    if (!window.PublicKeyCredential) {
        button.disabled = true;
        error.textContent = 'This browser does not support passkeys.';
        error.hidden = false;
        return;
    }
    button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
        button.disabled = true;
        error.hidden = true;
        try {
            const done = await ceremony(button.dataset.returnTo);
            location.assign(done.redirect);
        } catch (failure) {
            // A dismissed prompt is a NotAllowedError; say so plainly.
            error.textContent = failure.name === 'NotAllowedError'
                ? 'The passkey prompt was closed. Try again.'
                : failure.message;
            error.hidden = false;
            button.disabled = false;
        }
    });
    button.dataset.ready = 'true';
}

const signIn = document.getElementById('signin-passkey');
if (signIn) {
    wire(signIn, async returnTo => {
        const challenge = await post('/auth/passkey/signin/start', { return_to: returnTo });
        const credential = await navigator.credentials.get(requestOptions(challenge));
        return post('/auth/passkey/signin/finish', assertionJson(credential));
    });
}

const setup = document.getElementById('setup-passkey');
if (setup) {
    wire(setup, async returnTo => {
        const token = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('token') ?? '';
        const name = document.getElementById('setup-passkey-name').value;
        const challenge = await post('/auth/passkey/setup/start', { token, name, return_to: returnTo });
        const credential = await navigator.credentials.create(creationOptions(challenge));
        return post('/auth/passkey/setup/finish', registrationJson(credential));
    });
}
```

```markdown
# M12 Task 8: passkeys

## Added
- Passkey registration from the setup link (`/auth/passkey/setup/*`) and from a signed-in session (`/api/v1/me/passkeys/register/*`), and discoverable sign-in (`/auth/passkey/signin/*`).
- `store::passkeys` (add, find, update, list, rename, remove) and `store::sign_in_methods::count`.
- The sign-in and setup pages' passkey buttons (`js/signin/passkey.js`, with `js/signin/webauthn.js` conversions).

## Changed
- `webauthn-rs-proto` is a direct dependency, for `ResidentKeyRequirement`.

## Notes
- Ceremony state is in memory, five minutes, single use, keyed by the `okf_passkey` cookie.
- Passkeys are off when `public_url`'s host is an address (WebAuthn needs a domain).
- Adding a passkey ends the user's other sessions unless `keep_sessions` is set.
```

### Task 9: OIDC sign-in and linking

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/config.rs` (`OidcProviderConfig`, `AuthConfig.oidc`, `Config::validate_oidc`)
- Create: `src/oidc.rs` (`OidcProviders`: secrets, cached discovery, the reqwest 0.13 adapter, the authorize URL, the code exchange; a mock provider for tests)
- Create: `src/store/identities.rs`
- Create: `src/http/oidc.rs` (`/auth/oidc/{provider}/start`, `/auth/oidc/{provider}/callback`, `POST /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}/link`, the sign-in page buttons)
- Modify: `src/lib.rs` (`pub mod oidc;`), `src/store/mod.rs`, `src/app.rs` (`OidcProviders` on `App`), `src/http/mod.rs` and `src/http/api/mod.rs` (merge the routes), `src/http/signin.rs` (`provider_buttons`; `message_page` becomes `pub(crate)`)
- Modify: `tests/ui_e2e/signin.rs` (the provider button)
- Test: `src/config.rs`, `src/oidc.rs`, `src/store/identities.rs`, `src/http/oidc.rs`

openidconnect 4.1.0 facts this task relies on (verified in `crate-probe/tests/oidc_flow.rs`):
- With `default-features = false` there is no HTTP client, and oauth2 5.0's built-in one is for reqwest 0.12. Any `Fn(HttpRequest) -> impl Future<Output = Result<HttpResponse, E>>` is an `AsyncHttpClient`, so a closure over the server's reqwest 0.13 client is one. `reqwest::Request: TryFrom<http::Request<Vec<u8>>>`, and both crates use http 1.x.
- Discovery requires the document's `issuer` to equal the configured issuer exactly, and fetches the JWKS.
- The discovered client's type is `CoreClient<EndpointSet, EndpointNotSet, EndpointNotSet, EndpointNotSet, EndpointMaybeSet, EndpointMaybeSet>`. `exchange_code` returns a `Result` (the token endpoint may be absent), and the `openid` scope is always added.
- The crate does not compare `state`; the app does, in constant time. `IdToken::claims(&verifier, &nonce)` checks the issuer, audience, expiry, signature and nonce.
- Test ID tokens are HS256 with `CoreHmacKey::new(client_secret)`, listed in `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`, with an empty JWKS.

```rust
const OIDC: &str = r#"

allowed_hosts = ["okf.example.com"]

id = "example"
label = "Example ID"

    config.validate().expect("valid");
    assert_eq!(config.auth.oidc.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(config.auth.oidc[0].id, "example");
    assert_eq!(config.auth.oidc[0].scopes, ["openid", "email", "profile"]);
}

#[test]
fn bad_oidc_providers_are_refused() {
    let base = Config::from_toml(OIDC).expect("parses");
    // Each case changes one thing and names a word the refusal must contain.
    let cases: [(&str, fn(&mut Config)); 7] = [
        ("public_url", |config| config.public_url = None),
        ("id", |config| config.auth.oidc[0].id = "Example".to_string()),
        ("twice", |config| {
            let again = config.auth.oidc[0].clone();
            config.auth.oidc.push(again);
        }),
        ("label", |config| config.auth.oidc[0].label = " ".to_string()),
        ("client_id", |config| config.auth.oidc[0].client_id = String::new()),
        ("client_secret_env", |config| config.auth.oidc[0].client_secret_env = String::new()),
        ("issuer", |config| config.auth.oidc[0].issuer = "http://id.example.com".to_string()),
    ];
    for (word, change) in cases {
        let mut config = base.clone();
        change(&mut config);
        let refused = config.validate().expect_err(word);
        assert!(refused.contains(word), "{word}: {refused}");
    }
}
```

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

    use super::testing::{self, SECRET};
    use super::*;
    use crate::config::AuthConfig;

    fn config(idp: &testing::MockIdp) -> Config {
        Config {
            public_url: Some("https://okf.example.com".to_string()),
            auth: AuthConfig {
                oidc: vec![testing::provider(idp, "UNUSED")],
                ..AuthConfig::default()
            },
            ..Config::default()
        }
    }

    fn providers(idp: &testing::MockIdp) -> OidcProviders {
        OidcProviders::new(&config(idp), |_| Some(SECRET.to_string()))
            .expect("built")
            .expect("on")
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn discovery_is_cached_for_an_hour_and_kept_when_a_refresh_fails() {
        let idp = testing::start().await;
        let providers = providers(&idp);
        let start = Instant::now();

        providers.client("example", start).await.expect("discovered");
        providers.client("example", start + Duration::from_secs(30 * 60)).await.expect("cached");
        assert_eq!(idp.discoveries(), 1);
        idp.discovery_down.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
        let later = start + Duration::from_secs(2 * 60 * 60);
        providers.client("example", later).await.expect("the cached document is kept");
        assert_eq!(idp.discoveries(), 2);
        // After a failed refresh it waits a minute before asking again.
        providers.client("example", later + Duration::from_secs(30)).await.expect("still kept");
        assert_eq!(idp.discoveries(), 2);
        let fresh = self::providers(&idp).client("example", start).await;
        assert!(matches!(fresh, Err(OidcError::Discovery { .. })), "nothing cached yet");
        let unknown = providers.client("nope", start).await;
        assert!(matches!(unknown, Err(OidcError::UnknownProvider(_))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_client_secret_fails_start_up() {
        let config = Config {
            public_url: Some("https://okf.example.com".to_string()),
            auth: AuthConfig {
                oidc: vec![OidcProviderConfig {
                    id: "example".to_string(),
                    label: "Example ID".to_string(),
                    issuer: "https://id.example.com".to_string(),
                    client_id: "okf-console".to_string(),
                    client_secret_env: "OKF_OIDC_EXAMPLE_SECRET".to_string(),
                    scopes: vec!["openid".to_string()],
                }],
                ..AuthConfig::default()
            },
            ..Config::default()
        };

        let refused = OidcProviders::new(&config, |_| None);

        assert!(matches!(refused, Err(OkfError::Config { .. })));
        assert!(OidcProviders::new(&Config::default(), |_| None).expect("no providers").is_none());
    }
}
```

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use chrono::{DateTime, TimeZone, Utc};
    use sqlx::PgPool;

    use super::*;
    use crate::db::test_db;
    use crate::store::{passwords, users};

    fn now() -> DateTime<Utc> {
        Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2026, 11, 12, 9, 0, 0).single().expect("a time")
    }

    async fn user(pool: &PgPool, name: &str) -> String {
        users::create(pool, &users::NewUser { name, display_name: "" }, now())
            .await
            .expect("create the user");
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = $1")
            .bind(name)
            .fetch_one(pool)
            .await
            .expect("the user's id")
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn a_linked_identity_finds_its_user_and_lists_with_its_email() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = user(&db.pool, "alice").await;

        link(&db.pool, &alice, "example", "sub-1", "alice@example.com", now()).await.expect("link");
        touch(&db.pool, "example", "sub-1", now()).await.expect("touch");

        let found = find(&db.pool, "example", "sub-1").await.expect("find").expect("linked");
        assert_eq!(found.id, alice);
        assert_eq!(found.name, "alice");
        assert!(find(&db.pool, "example", "sub-2").await.expect("find").is_none());
        let listed = list(&db.pool, &alice).await.expect("list");
        assert_eq!(listed.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(listed[0].provider, "example");
        assert_eq!(listed[0].email_at_link, "alice@example.com");
        assert_eq!(listed[0].last_used_at, Some(now()));
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn linking_again_is_a_no_op_but_another_users_subject_is_refused() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = user(&db.pool, "alice").await;
        let bob = user(&db.pool, "bob").await;
        link(&db.pool, &alice, "example", "sub-1", "alice@example.com", now()).await.expect("link");

        link(&db.pool, &alice, "example", "sub-1", "alice@example.com", now()).await.expect("again");
        let taken = link(&db.pool, &bob, "example", "sub-1", "bob@example.com", now()).await;
        let second = link(&db.pool, &alice, "example", "sub-2", "alice@example.com", now()).await;

        assert!(matches!(taken, Err(OkfError::Refused { .. })), "{taken:?}");
        assert!(matches!(second, Err(OkfError::Refused { .. })), "one account per provider: {second:?}");
        assert_eq!(list(&db.pool, &alice).await.expect("list").len(), 1);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn unlinking_refuses_the_last_sign_in_method_and_an_unlinked_provider() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let alice = user(&db.pool, "alice").await;
        link(&db.pool, &alice, "example", "sub-1", "alice@example.com", now()).await.expect("link");

        let last = unlink(&db.pool, &alice, "example").await;
        let missing = unlink(&db.pool, &alice, "other").await;
        passwords::set(&db.pool, &alice, "violet-lantern-orbit-42", now()).await.expect("password");
        unlink(&db.pool, &alice, "example").await.expect("unlinked once a password exists");

        assert!(matches!(last, Err(OkfError::Refused { .. })), "{last:?}");
        assert!(matches!(missing, Err(OkfError::NotFound { .. })), "{missing:?}");
        assert!(list(&db.pool, &alice).await.expect("list").is_empty());
    }
}
```
