```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    use axum::http::StatusCode;
    use serde_json::json;

    use super::{FLOW_COOKIE, LINKED_ELSEWHERE, NO_ACCOUNT};
    use crate::config::{AuthConfig, Config};
    use crate::http::api::testing::{
        keys, login_config, user_with_password, Browser, Payload, Reply, MAIN, PASSWORD,
    };
    use crate::http::console_session::COOKIE;
    use crate::mcp::testing::{app_with, TestApp};
    use crate::oidc::testing::{self as idp, MockIdp, CLIENT_ID, SECRET};
    use crate::store::identities;
    use crate::store::sign_in_events::{self, Method, Outcome};

    /// An app with the mock provider as `example`. The client secret comes
    /// from the environment, as in production; each test names its own
    /// variable, so tests running at once never share one.
    async fn oidc_app(idp: &MockIdp, secret_env: &str) -> TestApp {
        // Edition 2021: `set_var` is a safe call.
        std::env::set_var(secret_env, SECRET);
        let config = Config {
            auth: AuthConfig {
                oidc: vec![idp::provider(idp, secret_env)],
                ..AuthConfig::default()
            },
            ..login_config()
        };
        app_with(&[("main", MAIN)], config).await
    }

    fn query_of(url: &str) -> HashMap<String, String> {
        url::Url::parse(url)
            .expect("an absolute URL")
            .query_pairs()
            .into_owned()
            .collect()
    }

    /// Starts a sign-in and returns the authorize URL's query. The mock is
    /// told the nonce, as its authorize page would learn it.
    async fn start(test: &TestApp, idp: &MockIdp, browser: &mut Browser) -> HashMap<String, String> {
        let reply = browser
            .send(test, "GET", "/auth/oidc/example/start?return_to=%2Fui%2F%23%2Fkeys", Payload::Empty)
            .await;
        assert_eq!(reply.status, StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, "{}", reply.text());
        let cookie = reply.set_cookie(FLOW_COOKIE).expect("a flow cookie");
        assert!(cookie.contains("SameSite=Lax") && cookie.contains("Max-Age=600"), "{cookie}");
        let query = query_of(reply.location());
        idp.set_nonce(&query["nonce"]);
        query
    }

    async fn callback(test: &TestApp, browser: &mut Browser, state: &str) -> Reply {
        let uri = format!("/auth/oidc/example/callback?code=c&state={state}");
        browser.send(test, "GET", &uri, Payload::Empty).await
    }

    async fn queued_mail(test: &TestApp) -> i64 {
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT count(*) FROM apalis.jobs")
            .fetch_one(test.app.pool())
            .await
            .expect("count")
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn the_start_redirect_carries_pkce_state_nonce_and_the_redirect_uri() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_START").await;

        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut Browser::default()).await;

        assert_eq!(query["client_id"], CLIENT_ID);
        assert_eq!(query["response_type"], "code");
        assert_eq!(query["code_challenge_method"], "S256");
        assert_eq!(query["redirect_uri"], "https://okf.example.com/auth/oidc/example/callback");
        assert_eq!(query["scope"], "openid email");
        assert!(query["state"].len() >= 22 && query["nonce"].len() >= 22);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn a_verified_email_links_the_identity_and_signs_in() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_LINK").await;
        let alice = user_with_password(&test, "alice", "alice@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;
        idp.will_issue("sub-1", Some("Alice@Example.com"), Some(true));
        let mut browser = Browser::default();

        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut browser).await;
        let reply = callback(&test, &mut browser, &query["state"]).await;

        assert_eq!(reply.status, StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, "{}", reply.text());
        assert_eq!(reply.location(), "/ui/#/keys");
        assert!(browser.cookie(COOKIE).is_some());
        assert_eq!(browser.cookie(FLOW_COOKIE), None);
        let linked = identities::list(test.app.pool(), &alice.id).await.expect("list");
        assert_eq!(linked.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(linked[0].email_at_link, "Alice@Example.com");
        assert_eq!(queued_mail(&test).await, 1, "the method-added notice");
        let events = sign_in_events::recent(test.app.pool(), "alice", 5).await.expect("events");
        assert!(matches!((&events[0].method, &events[0].outcome), (Method::Oidc, Outcome::Ok)));
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn an_unverified_or_unknown_email_is_refused_with_403() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_REFUSE").await;
        let alice = user_with_password(&test, "alice", "alice@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;

        for (subject, email, verified) in [
            ("sub-2", "alice@example.com", false),
            ("sub-3", "nobody@example.com", true),
        ] {
            idp.will_issue(subject, Some(email), Some(verified));
            let mut browser = Browser::default();
            let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut browser).await;
            let reply = callback(&test, &mut browser, &query["state"]).await;
            assert_eq!(reply.status, StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, "{subject}");
            assert!(reply.text().contains(NO_ACCOUNT));
            assert_eq!(browser.cookie(COOKIE), None);
        }
        assert!(identities::list(test.app.pool(), &alice.id).await.expect("list").is_empty());
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn a_returning_subject_signs_in_after_its_email_changed() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_RETURN").await;
        user_with_password(&test, "alice", "alice@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;
        idp.will_issue("sub-1", Some("alice@example.com"), Some(true));
        let mut first = Browser::default();
        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut first).await;
        callback(&test, &mut first, &query["state"]).await;
        idp.will_issue("sub-1", Some("alice@elsewhere.example"), Some(false));
        let mut browser = Browser::default();

        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut browser).await;
        let reply = callback(&test, &mut browser, &query["state"]).await;

        assert_eq!(reply.status, StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, "{}", reply.text());
        let session = browser.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/session", Payload::Empty).await;
        assert_eq!(session.json()["user"], "alice");
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn a_wrong_state_a_wrong_nonce_a_provider_error_or_a_replay_is_400() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_BAD").await;
        user_with_password(&test, "alice", "alice@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;
        idp.will_issue("sub-1", Some("alice@example.com"), Some(true));

        let mut wrong_state = Browser::default();
        start(&test, &idp, &mut wrong_state).await;
        let wrong_state = callback(&test, &mut wrong_state, "not-the-state").await;

        let mut wrong_nonce = Browser::default();
        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut wrong_nonce).await;
        idp.set_nonce("not-the-nonce");
        let wrong_nonce = callback(&test, &mut wrong_nonce, &query["state"]).await;

        let mut denied = Browser::default();
        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut denied).await;
        let uri = format!("/auth/oidc/example/callback?error=access_denied&state={}", query["state"]);
        let denied = denied.send(&test, "GET", &uri, Payload::Empty).await;

        let mut replayed = Browser::default();
        let query = start(&test, &idp, &mut replayed).await;
        let flow = replayed.cookie(FLOW_COOKIE).expect("a flow").to_string();
        let first = callback(&test, &mut replayed, &query["state"]).await;
        let again = callback(&test, &mut Browser::with_cookie(FLOW_COOKIE, &flow), &query["state"]).await;

        for (what, reply) in [("state", &wrong_state), ("nonce", &wrong_nonce), ("error", &denied), ("replay", &again)] {
            assert_eq!(reply.status, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "{what}: {}", reply.text());
            assert!(reply.set_cookie(COOKIE).is_none(), "{what}");
        }
        assert_eq!(first.status, StatusCode::SEE_OTHER);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn a_signed_in_user_links_a_provider_whatever_its_email() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_ACCOUNT").await;
        let alice = user_with_password(&test, "alice", "alice@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;
        let mut here = Browser::signed_in(&test, "alice@example.com", PASSWORD).await;
        let mut elsewhere = Browser::signed_in(&test, "alice@example.com", PASSWORD).await;
        idp.will_issue("sub-9", Some("someone@elsewhere.example"), Some(false));

        let started = here
            .send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/identities/example/link", Payload::Json(json!({})))
            .await;
        assert_eq!(started.status, StatusCode::OK, "{}", started.text());
        let query = query_of(started.json()["url"].as_str().expect("a URL"));
        idp.set_nonce(&query["nonce"]);
        let done = callback(&test, &mut here, &query["state"]).await;

        assert_eq!(done.status, StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, "{}", done.text());
        assert_eq!(done.location(), "/ui/#/account");
        let linked = identities::list(test.app.pool(), &alice.id).await.expect("list");
        assert_eq!(linked[0].email_at_link, "someone@elsewhere.example");
        let kept = here.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/session", Payload::Empty).await;
        let ended = elsewhere.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/session", Payload::Empty).await;
        assert_eq!(kept.status, StatusCode::OK);
        assert_eq!(ended.status, StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn linking_a_subject_another_user_holds_is_409() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_TAKEN").await;
        user_with_password(&test, "alice", "alice@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;
        let bob = user_with_password(&test, "bob", "bob@example.com", Some(PASSWORD)).await;
        identities::link(test.app.pool(), &bob.id, "example", "sub-1", "bob@example.com", chrono::Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("bob holds sub-1");
        let mut alice = Browser::signed_in(&test, "alice@example.com", PASSWORD).await;
        idp.will_issue("sub-1", Some("bob@example.com"), Some(true));

        let started = alice
            .send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/identities/example/link", Payload::Json(json!({ "keep_sessions": true })))
            .await;
        let query = query_of(started.json()["url"].as_str().expect("a URL"));
        idp.set_nonce(&query["nonce"]);
        let done = callback(&test, &mut alice, &query["state"]).await;

        assert_eq!(done.status, StatusCode::CONFLICT);
        assert!(done.text().contains(LINKED_ELSEWHERE));
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn the_sign_in_page_shows_each_provider_and_unknown_ones_are_404() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_PAGE").await;
        let mut browser = Browser::default();

        let page = browser.send(&test, "GET", "/signin", Payload::Empty).await.text();
        let unknown = browser.send(&test, "GET", "/auth/oidc/nope/start", Payload::Empty).await;

        assert!(page.contains(r#"id="signin-oidc-example""#));
        assert!(page.contains("Sign in with Example ID"));
        assert_eq!(unknown.status, StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn linking_needs_a_console_session() {
        let idp = idp::start().await;
        let test = oidc_app(&idp, "OKF_TEST_OIDC_SECRET_KEY").await;
        let mut keyed = Browser::default();
        keyed.bearer = Some(keys(&test).await.write);

        let reply = keyed
            .send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/identities/example/link", Payload::Json(json!({})))
            .await;

        assert_eq!(reply.status, StatusCode::FORBIDDEN);
    }
}
```

```rust
/// from the environment variable `client_secret_env` at start-up, never

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
```

`AuthConfig` (Task 5) gains `pub oidc: Vec<OidcProviderConfig>,` documented as "The OIDC providers (`[[auth.oidc]]`); none by default", and `oidc: Vec::new(),` in its `Default`. `Config::validate` calls `self.validate_oidc()?;` before `self.validate_public_url()`:

```rust
    /// Checks `[[auth.oidc]]`: providers need `public_url` (the redirect
    /// URI's origin); each has a valid, unique id, a label, a client id and
    /// a secret variable, and an `https` issuer (`http` on loopback only)
    /// with no query or fragment.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The problem in words.
    fn validate_oidc(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self.auth.oidc.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if self.public_url.is_none() {
            return Err("auth.oidc needs public_url, the origin of its redirect URIs".to_string());
        }
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        for provider in &self.auth.oidc {
            let id = provider.id.as_str();
            let valid_id = (1..=32).contains(&id.len())
                && id.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_lowercase() || byte.is_ascii_digit() || byte == b'-');
            if !valid_id {
                return Err(format!("auth.oidc id {id:?} must be 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -"));
            }
            // `insert` returns `false` for a value already in the set.
            if !seen.insert(id) {
                return Err(format!("auth.oidc id {id:?} is listed twice"));
            }
            for (key, value) in [
                ("label", &provider.label),
                ("client_id", &provider.client_id),
                ("client_secret_env", &provider.client_secret_env),
            ] {
                if value.trim().is_empty() {
                    return Err(format!("auth.oidc.{id}: {key} is empty"));
                }
            }
            let issuer = url::Url::parse(&provider.issuer)
                .map_err(|_| format!("auth.oidc.{id}: issuer {:?} is not a URL", provider.issuer))?;
            let loopback = issuer
                .host_str()
                .is_some_and(|host| is_loopback(&normalize_host(host)));
            let secure = issuer.scheme() == "https" || (issuer.scheme() == "http" && loopback);
            if !secure || issuer.query().is_some() || issuer.fragment().is_some() {
                return Err(format!(
                    "auth.oidc.{id}: issuer {:?} must be an https URL (http only on a loopback host), \
                     with no query or fragment",
                    provider.issuer
                ));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `src/oidc.rs`**

```rust
//! OIDC providers from `[[auth.oidc]]` (spec "OIDC", plan Decision 12).
//! Each provider's discovery document is cached for an hour, and a failed
//! refresh keeps the cached one. The registry builds the authorize URL
//! (PKCE S256, `state`, `nonce`) and exchanges the code, verifying the ID
//! token. HTTP goes through the server's own reqwest 0.13 by a small
//! adapter, so no second reqwest is linked.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use openidconnect::core::{CoreAuthenticationFlow, CoreClient, CoreProviderMetadata};
use openidconnect::{
    AuthorizationCode, ClientId, ClientSecret, CsrfToken, EndpointMaybeSet, EndpointNotSet,
    EndpointSet, HttpRequest, HttpResponse, IssuerUrl, Nonce, PkceCodeChallenge,
    PkceCodeVerifier, RedirectUrl, Scope, TokenResponse,
};

use crate::config::{Config, OidcProviderConfig};
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::oauth::expiring::ExpiringMap;

/// A client configured from a discovery document: an authorization
/// endpoint, and maybe a token and a userinfo endpoint (the typestate the
/// crate gives `from_provider_metadata`).
pub type ConfiguredClient = CoreClient<
    EndpointSet,
    EndpointNotSet,
    EndpointNotSet,
    EndpointNotSet,
    EndpointMaybeSet,
    EndpointMaybeSet,
>;

/// How long a discovery document is used before it is fetched again.
pub const DISCOVERY_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60 * 60);
/// After a failed refresh, how long the cached document is used before
/// the next try.
pub const FAILED_REFRESH_RETRY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
/// How long a flow may take (spec: a ten-minute cookie).
pub const FLOW_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10 * 60);
/// The most flows in progress at once (they start unauthenticated).
pub const MAX_FLOWS: usize = 10_000;
/// The longest any provider request may take.
const HTTP_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

/// Why an OIDC step failed.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum OidcError {
    /// No provider has this id.
    #[error("unknown OIDC provider {0:?}")]
    UnknownProvider(String),
    /// Discovery failed and nothing is cached.
    #[error("OIDC discovery for {provider} failed: {message}")]
    Discovery {
        /// The provider's id.
        provider: String,
        /// What went wrong.
        message: String,
    },
    /// The code exchange failed.
    #[error("the OIDC code exchange failed: {0}")]
    Exchange(String),
    /// The ID token is missing or did not verify.
    #[error("the ID token was refused: {0}")]
    IdToken(String),
}

impl From<OidcError> for OkfError {
    fn from(error: OidcError) -> Self {
        let message = error.to_string();
        match error {
            OidcError::UnknownProvider(id) => OkfError::NotFound {
                path: format!("auth/oidc/{id}"),
            },
            OidcError::Discovery { .. } => OkfError::Busy { reason: message },
            OidcError::Exchange(_) | OidcError::IdToken(_) => {
                OkfError::Unauthenticated { reason: message }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A provider request that failed: the adapter's error type.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("{0}")]
pub struct HttpError(String);

/// The adapter: sends one openidconnect request with reqwest 0.13. A
/// closure calling it is an `AsyncHttpClient` (the crate's blanket impl).
async fn send(client: reqwest::Client, request: HttpRequest) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> {
    // The annotation names the conversion's error type for `map_err`.
    let request: reqwest::Request = request
        .try_into()
        .map_err(|error: reqwest::Error| HttpError(error.to_string()))?;
    let response = client
        .execute(request)
        .await
        .map_err(|error| HttpError(error.to_string()))?;
    let mut builder = openidconnect::http::Response::builder().status(response.status());
    for (name, value) in response.headers() {
        builder = builder.header(name, value);
    }
    let body = response
        .bytes()
        .await
        .map_err(|error| HttpError(error.to_string()))?
        .to_vec();
    builder.body(body).map_err(|error| HttpError(error.to_string()))
}

/// A flow's secrets: compared or sent back once, never logged.
pub struct FlowSecrets {
    /// The `state` sent to the provider.
    pub state: String,
    /// The `nonce` the ID token must carry.
    pub nonce: String,
    /// The PKCE verifier.
    pub verifier: String,
}

// Written by hand, not derived, so a stray `{:?}` prints no secret.
impl std::fmt::Debug for FlowSecrets {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter.write_str("FlowSecrets(<redacted>)")
    }
}

/// A signed-in user linking a provider from the account page.
pub struct LinkRequest {
    /// The user's id.
    pub user_id: String,
    /// The session that asked (kept when the others are ended).
    pub session_id: String,
    /// Keep the user's other sessions.
    pub keep_sessions: bool,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for LinkRequest {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("LinkRequest")
            .field("user_id", &self.user_id)
            .field("session_id", &"<redacted>")
            .field("keep_sessions", &self.keep_sessions)
            .finish()
    }
}

/// A flow in progress, keyed by the `okf_oidc` cookie's random id.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Flow {
    /// The provider it was started with.
    pub provider: String,
    /// Its secrets.
    pub secrets: FlowSecrets,
    /// Where to go after signing in.
    pub return_to: String,
    /// Set when a signed-in user is linking, not signing in.
    pub link: Option<LinkRequest>,
}

/// What a verified ID token says about the person.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Identity {
    /// The provider's `sub`.
    pub subject: String,
    /// Its `email`, if sent.
    pub email: Option<String>,
    /// Whether `email_verified` was `true`.
    pub email_verified: bool,
}

/// One configured provider.
struct Provider {
    config: OidcProviderConfig,
    secret: ClientSecret,
    redirect: RedirectUrl,
    // tokio's mutex, held across a discovery fetch: concurrent sign-ins
    // wait for one fetch instead of each making their own.
    cached: tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<Cached>>,
}

/// A configured client and when to refresh it.
struct Cached {
    client: ConfiguredClient,
    refresh_at: Instant,
}

/// The configured providers and the flows in progress, held by `App`.
pub struct OidcProviders {
    http: reqwest::Client,
    providers: BTreeMap<String, Provider>,
    /// Flows in progress (ten minutes, single use).
    pub flows: ExpiringMap<Flow>,
}

impl OidcProviders {
    /// The registry for `[[auth.oidc]]`.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `config` - the server's settings (validated).
    /// * `secret_of` - reads an environment variable (`std::env::var` in
    ///   production; a closure in tests).
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `None` without `public_url` or providers.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OkfError::Config`] when a provider's secret variable is unset or
    /// empty, or the HTTP client cannot be built.
    pub fn new(
        config: &Config,
        secret_of: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>,
    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, OkfError> {
        let Some(public_url) = config.public_url.as_deref() else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if config.auth.oidc.is_empty() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let config_error = |path: String, message: String| OkfError::Config { path, message };
        let http = reqwest::Client::builder()
            // Discovery and the token endpoint answer directly; following a
            // redirect could reach an internal address.
            .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
            .timeout(HTTP_TIMEOUT)
            .user_agent(concat!("okf-mcp/", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
            .build()
            .map_err(|error| config_error("auth.oidc".to_string(), format!("building its HTTP client: {error}")))?;
        let mut providers = BTreeMap::new();
        for provider in &config.auth.oidc {
            let path = format!("auth.oidc.{}", provider.id);
            let secret = secret_of(&provider.client_secret_env)
                .filter(|secret| !secret.is_empty())
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    config_error(
                        path.clone(),
                        format!("the environment variable {} is not set", provider.client_secret_env),
                    )
                })?;
            let redirect = RedirectUrl::new(format!(
                "{}/auth/oidc/{}/callback",
                public_url.trim_end_matches('/'),
                provider.id
            ))
            .map_err(|error| config_error(path.clone(), error.to_string()))?;
            providers.insert(
                provider.id.clone(),
                Provider {
                    config: provider.clone(),
                    secret: ClientSecret::new(secret),
                    redirect,
                    cached: tokio::sync::Mutex::new(None),
                },
            );
        }
        Ok(Some(Self {
            http,
            providers,
            flows: ExpiringMap::new(FLOW_TTL, MAX_FLOWS),
        }))
    }

    /// Every provider's id and label, by id.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// `(id, label)` pairs.
    // `+ '_`: the iterator borrows `self`.
    pub fn labels(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &str)> + '_ {
        self.providers
            .values()
            .map(|provider| (provider.config.id.as_str(), provider.config.label.as_str()))
    }

    /// A provider's label.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `id` - the provider's id.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// Its label, or `None` for an unknown id.
    pub fn label(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.providers.get(id).map(|provider| provider.config.label.as_str())
    }

    fn provider(&self, id: &str) -> Result<&Provider, OidcError> {
        self.providers
            .get(id)
            .ok_or_else(|| OidcError::UnknownProvider(id.to_string()))
    }

    /// Fetches the discovery document and configures a client from it.
    async fn discover(&self, provider: &Provider) -> Result<ConfiguredClient, OidcError> {
        let failed = |message: String| OidcError::Discovery {
            provider: provider.config.id.clone(),
            message,
        };
        let issuer = IssuerUrl::new(provider.config.issuer.clone()).map_err(|error| failed(error.to_string()))?;
        // The closure is the `AsyncHttpClient`; each call gets its own
        // handle to the pooled client.
        let http = |request: HttpRequest| send(self.http.clone(), request);
        let metadata = CoreProviderMetadata::discover_async(issuer, &http)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| failed(error.to_string()))?;
        Ok(CoreClient::from_provider_metadata(
            metadata,
            ClientId::new(provider.config.client_id.clone()),
            Some(provider.secret.clone()),
        )
        .set_redirect_uri(provider.redirect.clone()))
    }

    /// A provider's client, from the cache while it is fresh.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `id` - the provider's id.
    /// * `now` - the current instant (passed in, so tests control time).
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The client: freshly discovered, cached, or (after a failed refresh)
    /// the stale cached one, retried after [`FAILED_REFRESH_RETRY`].
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OidcError::UnknownProvider`]; [`OidcError::Discovery`] when
    /// nothing is cached and discovery fails.
    pub async fn client(&self, id: &str, now: Instant) -> Result<ConfiguredClient, OidcError> {
        let provider = self.provider(id)?;
        let mut cached = provider.cached.lock().await;
        if let Some(entry) = cached.as_ref().filter(|entry| now < entry.refresh_at) {
            return Ok(entry.client.clone());
        }
        match self.discover(provider).await {
            Ok(client) => {
                *cached = Some(Cached {
                    client: client.clone(),
                    refresh_at: now + DISCOVERY_TTL,
                });
                Ok(client)
            }
            Err(error) => match cached.as_mut() {
                Some(entry) => {
                    tracing::warn!(provider = id, %error, "OIDC discovery failed; keeping the cached document");
                    entry.refresh_at = now + FAILED_REFRESH_RETRY;
                    Ok(entry.client.clone())
                }
                None => Err(error),
            },
        }
    }

    /// The provider's authorize URL for a new flow.
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `id` - the provider's id.
    /// * `now` - the current instant.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// The URL and the flow's secrets (for the caller to keep).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// As [`Self::client`].
    pub async fn authorize_url(&self, id: &str, now: Instant) -> Result<(String, FlowSecrets), OidcError> {
        let client = self.client(id, now).await?;
        let provider = self.provider(id)?;
        let (challenge, verifier) = PkceCodeChallenge::new_random_sha256();
        let mut request = client
            .authorize_url(CoreAuthenticationFlow::AuthorizationCode, CsrfToken::new_random, Nonce::new_random)
            .set_pkce_challenge(challenge);
        // The crate always sends `openid`; adding it again would repeat it.
        for scope in provider.config.scopes.iter().filter(|scope| scope.as_str() != "openid") {
            request = request.add_scope(Scope::new(scope.clone()));
        }
        let (url, state, nonce) = request.url();
        let secrets = FlowSecrets {
            state: state.into_secret(),
            nonce: nonce.secret().clone(),
            verifier: verifier.into_secret(),
        };
        Ok((url.to_string(), secrets))
    }

    /// Exchanges the code and verifies the ID token (issuer, audience,
    /// expiry, signature and nonce).
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `id` - the provider's id.
    /// * `code` - the callback's `code`.
    /// * `secrets` - the flow's secrets (its `state` already checked).
    /// * `now` - the current instant.
    ///
    /// # Returns
    /// What the token says about the person.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`OidcError::Exchange`] or [`OidcError::IdToken`]; as [`Self::client`].
    pub async fn identify(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        code: String,
        secrets: FlowSecrets,
        now: Instant,
    ) -> Result<Identity, OidcError> {
        let client = self.client(id, now).await?;
        let http = |request: HttpRequest| send(self.http.clone(), request);
        let tokens = client
            .exchange_code(AuthorizationCode::new(code))
            .map_err(|error| OidcError::Exchange(error.to_string()))?
            .set_pkce_verifier(PkceCodeVerifier::new(secrets.verifier))
            .request_async(&http)
            .await
            .map_err(|error| OidcError::Exchange(error.to_string()))?;
        // `id_token` comes from the `TokenResponse` trait imported above.
        let id_token = tokens
            .id_token()
            .ok_or_else(|| OidcError::IdToken("the provider sent no ID token".to_string()))?;
        let nonce = Nonce::new(secrets.nonce);
        let claims = id_token
            .claims(&client.id_token_verifier(), &nonce)
            .map_err(|error| OidcError::IdToken(error.to_string()))?;
        Ok(Identity {
            subject: claims.subject().as_str().to_string(),
            email: claims.email().map(|email| email.as_str().to_string()),
            email_verified: claims.email_verified() == Some(true),
        })
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod testing {
    //! An in-process OIDC provider: discovery, an empty JWKS, an authorize
    //! page that signs the person in at once, and a token endpoint issuing
    //! HS256 ID tokens signed with the client secret.

    use std::collections::HashMap;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

    use axum::extract::{Query, State};
    use axum::http::{header, StatusCode};
    use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Redirect, Response};
    use axum::routing::{get, post};
    use axum::{Json, Router};
    use openidconnect::core::{CoreHmacKey, CoreIdToken, CoreIdTokenClaims, CoreJwsSigningAlgorithm};
    use openidconnect::{
        Audience, EmptyAdditionalClaims, EndUserEmail, IssuerUrl, Nonce, StandardClaims, SubjectIdentifier,
    };

    use crate::config::OidcProviderConfig;

    /// The client id the mock expects.
    pub(crate) const CLIENT_ID: &str = "okf-console";
    /// The client secret, also the HS256 key.
    pub(crate) const SECRET: &str = "test-secret-at-least-32-bytes-long!!";

    /// The claims the next ID token carries.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    pub(crate) struct NextToken {
        subject: String,
        email: Option<String>,
        email_verified: Option<bool>,
        nonce: Option<String>,
    }

    /// A running mock provider.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub(crate) struct MockIdp {
        /// `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`.
        pub issuer: String,
        next: Arc<Mutex<NextToken>>,
        discoveries: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
        /// Answer discovery with 503 while set.
        pub discovery_down: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    }

    impl MockIdp {
        /// Sets the subject and email claims of the next ID tokens.
        pub(crate) fn will_issue(&self, subject: &str, email: Option<&str>, email_verified: Option<bool>) {
            let mut next = self.next.lock().expect("mock lock");
            next.subject = subject.to_string();
            next.email = email.map(str::to_string);
            next.email_verified = email_verified;
        }

        /// Sets the nonce of the next ID tokens.
        pub(crate) fn set_nonce(&self, nonce: &str) {
            self.next.lock().expect("mock lock").nonce = Some(nonce.to_string());
        }

        /// How many discovery requests arrived.
        pub(crate) fn discoveries(&self) -> usize {
            self.discoveries.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
        }
    }

    /// The `[[auth.oidc]]` entry for the mock, as `example`.
    pub(crate) fn provider(idp: &MockIdp, secret_env: &str) -> OidcProviderConfig {
        OidcProviderConfig {
            id: "example".to_string(),
            label: "Example ID".to_string(),
            issuer: idp.issuer.clone(),
            client_id: CLIENT_ID.to_string(),
            client_secret_env: secret_env.to_string(),
            scopes: vec!["openid".to_string(), "email".to_string()],
        }
    }

    /// Starts a mock provider on a free port; it runs until the test ends.
    pub(crate) async fn start() -> MockIdp {
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.expect("bind");
        let port = listener.local_addr().expect("address").port();
        let idp = MockIdp {
            issuer: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
            next: Arc::new(Mutex::new(NextToken {
                subject: "sub-1".to_string(),
                email: None,
                email_verified: None,
                nonce: None,
            })),
            discoveries: Arc::default(),
            discovery_down: Arc::default(),
        };
        let router = Router::new()
            .route("/.well-known/openid-configuration", get(discovery))
            .route("/jwks", get(jwks))
            .route("/authorize", get(authorize))
            .route("/token", post(token))
            .with_state(idp.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move { axum::serve(listener, router).await });
        idp
    }

    async fn discovery(State(idp): State<MockIdp>) -> Response {
        idp.discoveries.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if idp.discovery_down.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.into_response();
        }
        let issuer = &idp.issuer;
        Json(serde_json::json!({
            "issuer": issuer,
            "authorization_endpoint": format!("{issuer}/authorize"),
            "token_endpoint": format!("{issuer}/token"),
            "jwks_uri": format!("{issuer}/jwks"),
            "response_types_supported": ["code"],
            "subject_types_supported": ["public"],
            "id_token_signing_alg_values_supported": ["HS256"],
        }))
        .into_response()
    }

    async fn jwks() -> Response {
        ([(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")], r#"{"keys":[]}"#).into_response()
    }

    /// Signs the person in at once: remembers the nonce and sends the
    /// browser back with a code.
    async fn authorize(State(idp): State<MockIdp>, Query(query): Query<HashMap<String, String>>) -> Response {
        if let Some(nonce) = query.get("nonce") {
            idp.set_nonce(nonce);
        }
        let back = format!(
            "{}?code=c&state={}",
            query.get("redirect_uri").map(String::as_str).unwrap_or_default(),
            query.get("state").map(String::as_str).unwrap_or_default(),
        );
        Redirect::to(&back).into_response()
    }

    async fn token(State(idp): State<MockIdp>, body: String) -> Response {
        if !body.contains("code_verifier=") {
            return (StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "no PKCE verifier").into_response();
        }
        let next = idp.next.lock().expect("mock lock").clone();
        let now = chrono::Utc::now();
        let claims = CoreIdTokenClaims::new(
            IssuerUrl::new(idp.issuer.clone()).expect("the issuer"),
            vec![Audience::new(CLIENT_ID.to_string())],
            now + chrono::Duration::minutes(5),
            now,
            StandardClaims::new(SubjectIdentifier::new(next.subject))
                .set_email(next.email.map(EndUserEmail::new))
                .set_email_verified(next.email_verified),
            EmptyAdditionalClaims {},
        )
        .set_nonce(next.nonce.map(Nonce::new));
        let id_token = CoreIdToken::new(
            claims,
            &CoreHmacKey::new(SECRET.as_bytes()),
            CoreJwsSigningAlgorithm::HmacSha256,
            None,
            None,
        )
        .expect("sign the ID token");
        Json(serde_json::json!({
            "access_token": "at",
            "token_type": "Bearer",
            "expires_in": 300,
            "id_token": id_token.to_string(),
        }))
        .into_response()
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Users' linked OIDC identities (`user_identities`), matched by
//! `(provider, subject)`. A user links at most one account per provider.
//! Identities are not part of the key cache, so nothing here bumps
//! `admin_generation`.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::store::catalogs::is_unique_violation;
use crate::store::sign_in_methods;
use crate::store::users::UserAuth;

/// A linked identity as the account page lists it (never the subject).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IdentityInfo {
    /// The provider's id.
    pub provider: String,
    /// The email the provider gave when it was linked.
    pub email_at_link: String,
    /// When it was linked.
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// When it last signed in.
    pub last_used_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
}

/// The user an identity is linked to.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `provider` - the provider's id.
/// * `subject` - the ID token's `sub`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user, or `None`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn find(pool: &PgPool, provider: &str, subject: &str) -> Result<Option<UserAuth>, OkfError> {
    let row: Option<(String, String, Option<String>, bool)> = sqlx::query_as(
        "SELECT u.id, u.name, u.email::text, u.is_admin
         FROM user_identities i JOIN users u ON u.id = i.user_id
         WHERE i.provider = $1 AND i.subject = $2",
    )
    .bind(provider)
    .bind(subject)
    .fetch_optional(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(row.map(|(id, name, email, is_admin)| UserAuth { id, name, email, is_admin }))
}

/// Links an identity to a user. Linking the same one again is a no-op.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user.
/// * `provider` - the provider's id.
/// * `subject` - the ID token's `sub`.
/// * `email` - its email, recorded as `email_at_link` (may be empty).
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] if another user holds the identity, or this user
/// already links another account at this provider; [`OkfError::NotFound`]
/// for an unknown user; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn link(
    pool: &PgPool,
    user_id: &str,
    provider: &str,
    subject: &str,
    email: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // The user's row first, as `sign_in_methods::count` takes it: a link
    // and an unlink of one user run one at a time.
    sqlx::query_scalar::<_, i32>("SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE")
        .bind(user_id)
        .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::NotFound { path: format!("users/{user_id}") })?;
    let holder: Option<String> =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT user_id FROM user_identities WHERE provider = $1 AND subject = $2")
            .bind(provider)
            .bind(subject)
            .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
            .await?;
    match holder.as_deref() {
        // Already linked here: nothing to change (the transaction rolls
        // back when dropped).
        Some(holder) if holder == user_id => return Ok(()),
        Some(_) => return Err(taken(provider)),
        None => {}
    }
    let another: bool = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_identities WHERE user_id = $1 AND provider = $2)",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(provider)
    .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    if another {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: format!("another {provider} account is already linked; unlink it first"),
        });
    }
    let inserted = sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO user_identities (provider, subject, user_id, email_at_link, created_at)
         VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)",
    )
    .bind(provider)
    .bind(subject)
    .bind(user_id)
    .bind(email)
    .bind(now)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await;
    match inserted {
        Ok(_) => {}
        // Another user linked it between the read and the insert.
        Err(error) if is_unique_violation(&error) => return Err(taken(provider)),
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    }
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}

fn taken(provider: &str) -> OkfError {
    OkfError::Refused {
        reason: format!("this {provider} account is already linked to another user"),
    }
}

/// Records that an identity signed in.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `provider` - the provider's id.
/// * `subject` - the `sub`.
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn touch(pool: &PgPool, provider: &str, subject: &str, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    sqlx::query("UPDATE user_identities SET last_used_at = $3 WHERE provider = $1 AND subject = $2")
        .bind(provider)
        .bind(subject)
        .bind(now)
        .execute(pool)
        .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// A user's linked identities, by provider.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user.
///
/// # Returns
/// The listing.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn list(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<IdentityInfo>, OkfError> {
    let rows: Vec<(String, String, DateTime<Utc>, Option<DateTime<Utc>>)> = sqlx::query_as(
        "SELECT provider, email_at_link::text, created_at, last_used_at
         FROM user_identities WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY provider",
    )
    .bind(user_id)
    .fetch_all(pool)
    .await?;
    Ok(rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(provider, email_at_link, created_at, last_used_at)| IdentityInfo {
            provider,
            email_at_link,
            created_at,
            last_used_at,
        })
        .collect())
}

/// Unlinks the user's account at `provider`, unless it is their last
/// sign-in method.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `user_id` - the user.
/// * `provider` - the provider's id.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] when nothing is linked there;
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] for the last sign-in method; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn unlink(pool: &PgPool, user_id: &str, provider: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    let methods = sign_in_methods::count(&mut tx, user_id).await?;
    let linked: i64 =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT count(*) FROM user_identities WHERE user_id = $1 AND provider = $2")
            .bind(user_id)
            .bind(provider)
            .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
            .await?;
    if linked == 0 {
        return Err(OkfError::NotFound {
            path: format!("me/identities/{provider}"),
        });
    }
    if methods - linked < 1 {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "this is your last way to sign in; add a password or a passkey first".to_string(),
        });
    }
    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM user_identities WHERE user_id = $1 AND provider = $2")
        .bind(user_id)
        .bind(provider)
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
//! OIDC sign-in and account linking (spec "OIDC", plan Decision 12): a GET
//! link starts the code flow; the provider sends the browser back to the
//! callback, which checks `state` itself, exchanges the code, verifies the
//! ID token and then finds the user by `(provider, sub)`, else by a
//! verified email (linking it), else refuses. Linking from the account
//! page starts through the API, so it needs a session and its CSRF token.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Instant;

use axum::extract::{Path, Query, State};
use axum::http::request::Parts;
use axum::http::{header, HeaderMap, StatusCode};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Redirect, Response};
use axum::routing::{get, post};
use axum::{Extension, Json, Router};
use serde::Deserialize;
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;

use crate::app::App;
use crate::auth::{CredentialKind, Principal};
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::http::console_session::{
    append_all, client_ip, cookie, secure_cookies, session_user, set_cookie, ConsoleSession,
    SameSite,
};
use crate::http::pages::safe_return_to;
use crate::http::signin::{audit, message_page, notify_method_added, sign_in, ProviderButton};
use crate::http::{timeout_layer, AppError};
use crate::keys;
use crate::oidc::{Flow, Identity, LinkRequest, OidcError, OidcProviders, FLOW_TTL};
use crate::store::sign_in_events::{Method, Outcome};
use crate::store::{identities, user_sessions, users};

/// The flow cookie: `SameSite=Lax`, so the provider's redirect carries it.
pub const FLOW_COOKIE: &str = "okf_oidc";
/// No user for this identity or verified email (403, spec).
pub const NO_ACCOUNT: &str = "No account for this email. Ask an admin to invite you.";
/// A bad state, nonce or token (400, spec).
const SIGN_IN_RETRY: &str = "Sign-in failed; try again";
/// Discovery failed with nothing cached (503).
const UNAVAILABLE: &str = "The sign-in provider cannot be reached right now; try again later.";
/// The identity belongs to another user (409).
pub const LINKED_ELSEWHERE: &str = "This account is already linked to another user.";
/// Where linking returns to.
const ACCOUNT_PAGE: &str = "/ui/#/account";

/// The open routes, merged only when providers are configured.
///
/// # Returns
/// The router, with the request timeout.
pub(crate) fn routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    Router::new()
        .route("/auth/oidc/{provider}/start", get(start))
        .route("/auth/oidc/{provider}/callback", get(callback))
        .layer(timeout_layer())
}

/// The linking route, merged into `/api/v1` (behind `require_principal`).
///
/// # Returns
/// The router.
pub(crate) fn api_routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    // `{provider}`: Task 10b's `/me/identities/{provider}` must use the same
    // parameter name at this position, or the router refuses to build.
    Router::new().route("/me/identities/{provider}/link", post(link))
}

/// The sign-in page's provider buttons.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the shared state.
///
/// # Returns
/// One button per configured provider, by id.
pub(crate) fn buttons(app: &App) -> Vec<ProviderButton> {
    app.oidc().map_or_else(Vec::new, |oidc| {
        oidc.labels()
            .map(|(id, label)| ProviderButton { id: id.to_string(), label: label.to_string() })
            .collect()
    })
}

/// The `Set-Cookie` header that clears the flow cookie.
fn clear_flow(app: &App) -> HeaderMap {
    let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
    headers.insert(
        header::SET_COOKIE,
        set_cookie(FLOW_COOKIE, "", std::time::Duration::ZERO, SameSite::Lax, secure_cookies(app)),
    );
    headers
}

/// Starts a flow: the provider's authorize URL and the flow cookie.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] for an unknown provider; [`OkfError::Busy`] when
/// discovery fails with nothing cached or too many flows are in progress.
async fn begin(
    app: &App,
    oidc: &OidcProviders,
    provider: &str,
    return_to: String,
    link: Option<LinkRequest>,
) -> Result<(String, HeaderMap), OkfError> {
    let (url, secrets) = oidc.authorize_url(provider, Instant::now()).await?;
    let id = keys::generate_with("")?;
    let flow = Flow {
        provider: provider.to_string(),
        secrets,
        return_to,
        link,
    };
    if !oidc.flows.insert(id.clone(), flow, Instant::now()) {
        return Err(OkfError::Busy {
            reason: "too many sign-ins in progress; try again shortly".to_string(),
        });
    }
    let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
    headers.insert(
        header::SET_COOKIE,
        set_cookie(FLOW_COOKIE, &id, FLOW_TTL, SameSite::Lax, secure_cookies(app)),
    );
    Ok((url, headers))
}

/// `GET /auth/oidc/{provider}/start`'s query.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
struct StartQuery {
    return_to: Option<String>,
}

/// `GET /auth/oidc/{provider}/start`: 303 to the provider.
async fn start(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Path(provider): Path<String>,
    Query(query): Query<StartQuery>,
) -> Response {
    let Some(oidc) = app.oidc() else {
        return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
    };
    let return_to = safe_return_to(query.return_to.as_deref());
    match begin(&app, oidc, &provider, return_to, None).await {
        Ok((url, headers)) => (headers, Redirect::to(&url)).into_response(),
        Err(OkfError::NotFound { .. }) => message_page(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "Sign in", "No such sign-in provider."),
        Err(OkfError::Busy { .. }) => message_page(StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, "Sign in", UNAVAILABLE),
        Err(error) => AppError(error).into_response(),
    }
}

/// The provider's redirect back. No `Debug`: it holds the code.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct CallbackQuery {
    #[serde(default)]
    code: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    state: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    error: Option<String>,
}

/// How a callback ends.
enum Done {
    /// Go to `to`, with the session cookie (empty when linking).
    Redirect { session_cookie: HeaderMap, to: String },
    /// A page with this status and message.
    Refused(StatusCode, &'static str),
}

/// `GET /auth/oidc/{provider}/callback`.
async fn callback(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Path(provider): Path<String>,
    parts: Parts,
    Query(query): Query<CallbackQuery>,
) -> Response {
    let Some(oidc) = app.oidc() else {
        return StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response();
    };
    // Every answer clears the flow cookie: the flow is single use.
    let mut headers = clear_flow(&app);
    let page = |headers: HeaderMap, status: StatusCode, message: &str| {
        let mut response = message_page(status, "Sign in", message);
        append_all(response.headers_mut(), &headers);
        response
    };
    let flow = cookie(&parts.headers, FLOW_COOKIE).and_then(|id| oidc.flows.take(id, Instant::now()));
    let Some(Flow { provider: started_with, secrets, return_to, link }) = flow else {
        return page(headers, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, SIGN_IN_RETRY);
    };
    // The `state` check is this redirect's CSRF guard; openidconnect leaves
    // it to the app. Constant time, like every other secret comparison.
    let state_ok = started_with == provider
        && query
            .state
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|state| bool::from(state.as_bytes().ct_eq(secrets.state.as_bytes())));
    // A tuple pattern: the state matched, the provider sent no error, and a code.
    let (true, None, Some(code)) = (state_ok, query.error.as_deref(), query.code) else {
        return page(headers, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, SIGN_IN_RETRY);
    };
    let ip = client_ip(&parts, &app.config().auth);
    let identity = match oidc.identify(&provider, code, secrets, Instant::now()).await {
        Ok(identity) => identity,
        Err(OidcError::Discovery { .. }) => return page(headers, StatusCode::SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, UNAVAILABLE),
        Err(error) => {
            tracing::info!(provider = %provider, %error, "OIDC sign-in refused");
            audit(&app, None, Method::Oidc, Outcome::Failed, ip).await;
            return page(headers, StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, SIGN_IN_RETRY);
        }
    };
    let done = match link {
        Some(link) => finish_link(&app, &provider, &identity, link).await,
        None => finish_sign_in(&app, &parts, &provider, &identity, return_to).await,
    };
    match done {
        Ok(Done::Redirect { session_cookie, to }) => {
            append_all(&mut headers, &session_cookie);
            (headers, Redirect::to(&to)).into_response()
        }
        Ok(Done::Refused(status, message)) => page(headers, status, message),
        Err(error) => AppError(error).into_response(),
    }
}

/// What to call a provider in the method-added notice.
fn method_text(app: &App, provider: &str) -> String {
    let label = app.oidc().and_then(|oidc| oidc.label(provider)).unwrap_or(provider);
    format!("your {label} account")
}

/// Signs in by `(provider, sub)`, else links by verified email and signs
/// in, else refuses with 403 (spec, in that order).
async fn finish_sign_in(
    app: &App,
    parts: &Parts,
    provider: &str,
    identity: &Identity,
    return_to: String,
) -> Result<Done, OkfError> {
    let pool = app.pool();
    let now = app.clock().now();
    let user = match identities::find(pool, provider, &identity.subject).await? {
        Some(user) => user,
        None => {
            // Only a verified email may claim an account.
            let verified = identity.email.as_deref().filter(|_| identity.email_verified);
            let found = match verified {
                Some(email) => users::find_by_email(pool, email).await?,
                None => None,
            };
            let (Some(user), Some(email)) = (found, verified) else {
                audit(app, None, Method::Oidc, Outcome::Failed, client_ip(parts, &app.config().auth)).await;
                return Ok(Done::Refused(StatusCode::FORBIDDEN, NO_ACCOUNT));
            };
            match identities::link(pool, &user.id, provider, &identity.subject, email, now).await {
                Ok(()) => {}
                Err(OkfError::Refused { .. }) => return Ok(Done::Refused(StatusCode::CONFLICT, LINKED_ELSEWHERE)),
                Err(error) => return Err(error),
            }
            tracing::info!(user = %user.id, provider, "OIDC identity linked by verified email");
            notify_method_added(app, &user, &method_text(app, provider)).await;
            user
        }
    };
    identities::touch(pool, provider, &identity.subject, now).await?;
    let session_cookie = sign_in(app, parts, &user, Method::Oidc).await?;
    Ok(Done::Redirect { session_cookie, to: return_to })
}

/// Links the identity to the signed-in user who started the flow,
/// whatever its email (spec), then ends their other sessions unless kept.
async fn finish_link(app: &App, provider: &str, identity: &Identity, link: LinkRequest) -> Result<Done, OkfError> {
    let email = identity.email.as_deref().unwrap_or_default();
    match identities::link(app.pool(), &link.user_id, provider, &identity.subject, email, app.clock().now()).await {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(OkfError::Refused { .. }) => return Ok(Done::Refused(StatusCode::CONFLICT, LINKED_ELSEWHERE)),
        Err(error) => return Err(error),
    }
    tracing::info!(user = %link.user_id, provider, "OIDC identity linked from the account page");
    if !link.keep_sessions {
        let ended = user_sessions::revoke_all(app.pool(), &link.user_id, Some(&link.session_id)).await?;
        tracing::info!(user = %link.user_id, ended, "other sessions ended after an identity was linked");
    }
    if let Some(user) = session_user(app, &link.user_id).await? {
        notify_method_added(app, &user, &method_text(app, provider)).await;
    }
    Ok(Done::Redirect { session_cookie: HeaderMap::new(), to: ACCOUNT_PAGE.to_string() })
}

/// `POST /me/identities/{provider}/link`'s body.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct LinkBody {
    /// Keep the user's other sessions (the account page's checkbox).
    #[serde(default)]
    keep_sessions: bool,
}

/// `POST /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}/link`: `{"url": <authorize URL>}`
/// and the flow cookie. The console navigates to the URL itself, so the
/// console CSP's `form-action 'self'` never meets the provider's origin.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a key or grant; 404 for an unknown provider or with OIDC off;
/// 503 when the provider cannot be reached.
async fn link(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Path(provider): Path<String>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    session: Option<Extension<ConsoleSession>>,
    Json(body): Json<LinkBody>,
) -> Result<Response, AppError> {
    let (user_id, session) = match (&principal.kind, session) {
        (CredentialKind::Session { user_id }, Some(Extension(session))) => (user_id.clone(), session),
        _ => {
            return Err(OkfError::Forbidden {
                reason: "linking an account needs a console session".to_string(),
            }
            .into())
        }
    };
    let oidc = app.oidc().ok_or_else(|| OkfError::NotFound {
        path: format!("me/identities/{provider}/link"),
    })?;
    let request = LinkRequest {
        user_id,
        session_id: session.id,
        keep_sessions: body.keep_sessions,
    };
    let (url, flow_cookie) = begin(&app, oidc, &provider, ACCOUNT_PAGE.to_string(), Some(request)).await?;
    Ok((flow_cookie, Json(serde_json::json!({ "url": url }))).into_response())
}
```

```markdown
# M12 Task 9: OIDC sign-in and linking

## Added
- `[[auth.oidc]]` providers (id, label, issuer, client_id, client_secret_env, scopes); the secret is read from the environment at start-up.
```

### Task 10a: Self-service API: account, keys and grants

**Files:**
- Create: `src/http/api/me.rs` (`GET /me`, `/me/keys`, `/me/grants`, their views and bodies, and their tests; Task 10b adds the account routes)
- Modify: `src/http/api/mod.rs` (`mod me;`, `.merge(me::routes())` beside `people::routes()`)
- Modify: `src/store/keys.rs` (`insert_key` factored out of `create_with_id`; new `create_self_issued` and `rename_by_id`, with tests)
- Test: `src/http/api/me.rs` (`mod tests`), `src/store/keys.rs` (`mod tests`)

Every route here acts for the signed-in user. The rules (spec "Self-service", Decisions 3 and 4):
- **Session principals only.** A bearer key or OAuth token gets 403 on every route except `GET /me`. `GET /me` also answers a key that belongs to a user, and a key without one gets 404.
- **Self-issued keys** are never admin and never maintenance reporters. They name their catalogs explicitly (a body with `all` is a 422 from `deny_unknown_fields`), and every level is within the user's ceiling. Above the ceiling is `422 LimitExceeded { limit: "ceiling" }`.
- **Live keys.** A user has at most `max_keys_per_user` live self-issued keys; past that is `422 { limit: "max_keys_per_user" }`. The count runs under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the user row, so two concurrent creates cannot both pass it.
- **Expiry.** It is at most `max_key_lifetime` from now; later is `422 { limit: "max_key_lifetime" }`. When the setting is set and the body gives no expiry, the key expires at the limit. Unset means no limit, and no expiry unless one is asked for.
- **Owner and flag.** The key's user is the signed-in user, its actor defaults to its name, and `self_issued = true`.
- **Admins too.** An admin user's session is capped like anyone's for its self-issued keys: the ceiling comes from teams and entitlements, never from the admin flag.

The ceiling check here gives a clear 422 at create time. It is not the only enforcement: the key cache caps every self-issued credential on each reload (Task 3), so a ceiling lowered between the check and the insert still wins.

> - **`create_self_issued` refuses a key not marked `self_issued`** (`Refused`), because its count covers only self-issued keys. Test `create_self_issued_refuses_a_key_not_marked_self_issued`.

```rust
async fn insert_key(

    new: &NewKey<'_>,

pub async fn create_with_id(
```

Keep `create_with_id`'s existing doc comment. Then add:

```rust
/// Creates a self-issued key (spec "Self-service") unless its user already
/// has `max_live` live ones, and bumps the administrative generation, in
/// one transaction. "Live" is a self-issued API key (not a grant) that is
/// neither revoked nor past its expiry.
///
/// The user row is locked `FOR UPDATE` before counting, so two concurrent
/// creates for one user run one after the other: the second counts the
/// first. `insert_key`'s own `FOR KEY SHARE` on that row is then a no-op,
/// since this transaction already holds a stronger lock.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `new` - the key; the caller sets `self_issued: true` and has checked
///   its levels against the ceiling.
/// * `max_live` - the `max_keys_per_user` setting.
/// * `now` - the creation time, also the expiry cut-off for the count.
///
/// # Returns
/// The key's id and the key itself (shown once).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "max_keys_per_user"` at the
/// limit; [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user; otherwise as
/// [`create`].
pub async fn create_self_issued(
    pool: &PgPool,
    new: &NewKey<'_>,
    max_live: u32,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<CreatedKey, OkfError> {
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    let user_id: String = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = $1 FOR UPDATE")
        .bind(new.user)
        .fetch_optional(&mut *tx)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "user",
            name: new.user.to_string(),
        })?;
    let live: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT count(*) FROM api_keys \
         WHERE user_id = $1 AND kind = 'key' AND self_issued AND revoked_at IS NULL \
           AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > $2)",
    )
    .bind(&user_id)
    .bind(now)
    .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    // `i64::from` widens the setting without a lossy `as` cast.
    if live >= i64::from(max_live) {
        return Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded {
            limit: "max_keys_per_user",
            reason: format!(
                "{} already has {live} live keys; the limit is {max_live}",
                new.user
            ),
        });
    }
    let created = insert_key(&mut tx, new, now).await?;
    bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(created)
}

/// Renames a live API key. The name is not part of the cached principal
/// (`whoami` reads it from the row), so nothing reloads and the
/// administrative generation is left alone.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `id` - the key's immutable id.
/// * `name` - the new name, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] for an invalid name, a name and actor another live
/// key already has, or no live API key with this id; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn rename_by_id(pool: &PgPool, id: &str, name: &str) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    if !is_valid_name(name) {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: format!("key name {name:?} must be letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'"),
        });
    }
    let renamed = sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE api_keys SET name = $2 WHERE id = $1 AND kind = 'key' AND revoked_at IS NULL",
    )
    .bind(id)
    .bind(name)
    .execute(pool)
    .await;
    let renamed = match renamed {
        Ok(done) => done,
        Err(error)
            if is_unique_violation(&error)
                && error
                    .as_database_error()
                    .and_then(|db_error| db_error.constraint())
                    == Some("api_keys_live_name_actor") =>
        {
            return Err(OkfError::Refused {
                reason: format!("another active key with this actor is named {name:?}"),
            })
        }
        Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
    };
    if renamed.rows_affected() == 0 {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: format!("no active key {id:?}"),
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
            .await
            .expect("create the user");
        for (catalog, access) in grants {
            ceiling::entitle(pool, name, catalog, *access, Utc::now())
                .await
                .expect("entitle");
        }
        test.app.poll().await.expect("poll the user in");
        Browser::session_for(test, name).await
    }

    /// A create body for one catalog at one level.
    fn one(name: &str, catalog: &str, access: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
        json!({"name": name, "catalogs": [{"catalog": catalog, "access": access}]})
    }

            ("GET", "/api/v1/me/keys", None),

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_session_creates_lists_renames_and_revokes_its_own_key() {
        let test = app().await;
        let mut alice = member(&test, "alice", &[("main", Access::Write)]).await;

        let (created, body) =
            alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(one("laptop", "main", "write"))).await.parts();
        let secret = body["secret"].as_str().expect("the secret, once").to_string();
        let id = body["key"]["id"].as_str().expect("an id").to_string();
        let (_, whoami) = send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/whoami", Some(&secret), None).await;
        let (_, listed) = alice.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (renamed, view) = alice
            .send(
                &test,
                "PATCH",
                &format!("/api/v1/me/keys/{id}"),
                Payload::Json(json!({"name": "desk"})),
            )
            .await.parts();
        let (revoked, gone) =
            alice.send(&test, "DELETE", &format!("/api/v1/me/keys/{id}"), Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (refused, _) = send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/whoami", Some(&secret), None).await;

        assert_eq!(created.as_u16(), 200, "{body}");
        assert_eq!(body["key"]["self_issued"], true);
        assert_eq!(body["key"]["access"], "write");
        assert_eq!(body["key"]["actor"], "laptop");
        assert_eq!(body["key"]["user"], "alice");
        assert_eq!(whoami["user"], "alice");
        assert_eq!(whoami["catalogs"], json!(["main"]));
        // Only alice's keys: the fixture user's are not listed.
        assert_eq!(listed["keys"].as_array().map(Vec::len), Some(1), "{listed}");
        assert_eq!(renamed.as_u16(), 200, "{view}");
        assert_eq!(view["name"], "desk");
        assert_eq!(revoked.as_u16(), 200);
        assert!(gone["revoked_at"].is_string());
        assert_eq!(refused.as_u16(), 401);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_key_above_the_ceiling_is_a_422_naming_the_limit() {
        let test = app().await;
        let mut alice = member(&test, "alice", &[("main", Access::Read)]).await;

        let (write, too_high) =
            alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(one("a", "main", "write"))).await.parts();
        let (other, outside) =
            alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(one("b", "other", "read"))).await.parts();
        let (admin, _) =
            alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(one("c", "main", "admin"))).await.parts();
        let (all, _) = alice
            .send(
                &test,
                "POST",
                "/api/v1/me/keys",
                Payload::Json(json!({"name": "d", "all": true, "catalogs": []})),
            )
            .await.parts();
        let (none, _) = alice
            .send(
                &test,
                "POST",
                "/api/v1/me/keys",
                Payload::Json(json!({"name": "e", "catalogs": []})),
            )
            .await.parts();

        assert_eq!(write.as_u16(), 422, "{too_high}");
        assert_eq!(too_high["error"], "LimitExceeded");
        assert_eq!(too_high["limit"], "ceiling");
        assert_eq!(other.as_u16(), 422, "{outside}");
        assert_eq!(outside["limit"], "ceiling");
        assert_eq!(admin.as_u16(), 422, "never an admin key");
        assert_eq!(all.as_u16(), 422, "no all-catalogs self-issued key");
        assert_eq!(none.as_u16(), 400, "a key names a catalog");
    }

        let id = body["key"]["id"].as_str().expect("an id").to_string();

        assert_eq!(first.as_u16(), 200, "{body}");

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_lifetime_limit_caps_and_defaults_the_expiry() {
        let test = app().await;
        let mut alice = member(&test, "alice", &[("main", Access::Read)]).await;
        settings::set(test.app.pool(), SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime, "24h", "test", Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("set the lifetime");
        let later = |hours: i64| {
            (Utc::now() + TimeDelta::hours(hours)).to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)
        };

        let (defaulted, body) =
            alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(one("a", "main", "read"))).await.parts();
        let mut long = one("b", "main", "read");
        long["expires_at"] = json!(later(48));
        let (too_long, refused) = alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(long)).await.parts();
        let mut short = one("c", "main", "read");
        short["expires_at"] = json!(later(2));
        let (within, kept) = alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(short)).await.parts();
        let mut past = one("d", "main", "read");
        past["expires_at"] = json!(later(-1));
        let (in_the_past, _) = alice.send(&test, "POST", "/api/v1/me/keys", Payload::Json(past)).await.parts();

        assert_eq!(defaulted.as_u16(), 200, "{body}");
        let expires: DateTime<Utc> = body["key"]["expires_at"]
            .as_str()
            .expect("an expiry")
            .parse()
            .expect("RFC 3339");
        let left = expires - Utc::now();
        assert!(left > TimeDelta::hours(23) && left <= TimeDelta::hours(24), "{left}");
        assert_eq!(too_long.as_u16(), 422);
        assert_eq!(refused["limit"], "max_key_lifetime");
        assert_eq!(within.as_u16(), 200, "{kept}");
        assert_eq!(in_the_past.as_u16(), 400);
    }

    #[test]
    fn requested_levels_refuse_an_empty_or_repeated_list() {
        let body = |entries: &[(&str, &str)]| -> Vec<CatalogLevelBody> {
            entries
                .iter()
                .map(|(catalog, access)| CatalogLevelBody {
                    catalog: catalog.to_string(),
                    access: access.to_string(),
                })
                .collect()
        };

        let empty = requested_levels(&body(&[]));
        let twice = requested_levels(&body(&[("main", "read"), ("main", "write")]));
        let bad = requested_levels(&body(&[("main", "owner")]));
        let good = requested_levels(&body(&[("main", "write"), ("other", "read")])).expect("valid");

        assert!(matches!(empty, Err(OkfError::InvalidPath { .. })), "{empty:?}");
        assert!(matches!(twice, Err(OkfError::InvalidPath { .. })), "{twice:?}");
        assert!(matches!(bad, Err(OkfError::InvalidPath { .. })), "{bad:?}");
        assert_eq!(good.get("main"), Some(&Access::Write));
        assert_eq!(good.get("other"), Some(&Access::Read));
    }

    #[test]
    fn within_ceiling_names_the_first_catalog_over_it() {
        let ceiling: Ceiling = [("main".to_string(), Access::Read)].into_iter().collect();
        let wanted = |catalog: &str, access| -> std::collections::BTreeMap<String, Access> {
            [(catalog.to_string(), access)].into_iter().collect()
        };

        assert!(within_ceiling(&wanted("main", Access::Read), &ceiling).is_ok());
        for refused in [
            wanted("main", Access::Write),
            wanted("main", Access::Admin),
            wanted("other", Access::Read),
        ] {
            let error = within_ceiling(&refused, &ceiling).expect_err("over the ceiling");
            assert!(
                matches!(error, OkfError::LimitExceeded { limit: "ceiling", .. }),
                "{error:?}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn key_expiry_defaults_to_and_is_capped_by_the_lifetime() {
        let now: DateTime<Utc> = "2026-11-12T12:00:00Z".parse().expect("time");
        let day = Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600));

        assert_eq!(key_expiry(None, None, now).expect("none"), None);
        assert_eq!(
            key_expiry(None, day, now).expect("defaulted"),
            Some(now + TimeDelta::hours(24))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            key_expiry(Some("2026-11-12T18:00:00Z"), day, now).expect("within"),
            Some(now + TimeDelta::hours(6))
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            key_expiry(Some("2026-11-14T12:00:00Z"), day, now),
            Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded { limit: "max_key_lifetime", .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            key_expiry(Some("2026-11-12T11:00:00Z"), None, now),
            Err(OkfError::InvalidPath { .. })
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            key_expiry(Some("tomorrow"), None, now),
            Err(OkfError::InvalidPath { .. })
        ));
        // An empty field is "no expiry asked for", as the console sends it.
        assert_eq!(key_expiry(Some(""), None, now).expect("empty"), None);
    }
}
```
