```rust
//! `/api/v1/me/...` (spec "Self-service"): what a signed-in person does for
//! themselves. They manage their own keys and OAuth grants, change their
//! password, manage their passkeys and linked identities, and see their
//! sessions, recent sign-ins, teams and ceiling.
//!
//! Access:
//! - every route but `GET /me` needs a console session
//!   ([`CredentialKind::Session`]); a bearer key or OAuth token is a 403,
//!   since a key must not mint keys for itself;
//! - `GET /me` also answers a key that belongs to a user;
//! - a route acts only on the session user's own rows: anyone else's key,
//!   grant, passkey, identity or session is a 404, like an unknown id.
//!
//! Self-issued keys (Decisions 3 and 4) are never admin or reporters, name
//! their catalogs, stay within the ceiling, the key limit and the lifetime
//! limit, and belong to the signed-in user. Each refusal is a 422
//! [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] naming the limit.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::Arc;

use axum::extract::{Path, State};
use axum::http::StatusCode;
use axum::routing::{delete, get, patch};
use axum::{Extension, Json, Router};
use chrono::{DateTime, TimeDelta, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::app::App;
use crate::auth::{CredentialKind, Principal};
use crate::clock::format_timestamp;
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::http::api::keys::{parse_access, CreatedKeyView, KeyView};
use crate::http::api::settle;
use crate::http::AppError;
use crate::store::ceiling::{self, Ceiling};
use crate::store::keys::{
    self as key_rows, Access, CatalogGrant, Grants, KeyKind, KeyRecord, NewKey,
};
use crate::store::users;

/// The signed-in user a self-service request acts for.
// `Copy`: two borrowed strings, cheap to pass by value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct SessionUser<'a> {
    /// `users.id`, which rows reference.
    id: &'a str,
    /// The user's name, which the store's by-name functions take.
    name: &'a str,
}

/// The session user behind `principal`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `principal` - the caller, from `require_principal`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The user's id and name.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Forbidden`] for a bearer key or OAuth token.
fn session_user(principal: &Principal) -> Result<SessionUser<'_>, OkfError> {
    // A tuple match checks both at once; every combination is listed, so a
    // new credential kind fails to compile here until someone decides.
    match (&principal.kind, principal.user.as_deref()) {
        (CredentialKind::Session { user_id }, Some(name)) => Ok(SessionUser { id: user_id, name }),
        (CredentialKind::ApiKey | CredentialKind::OAuth { .. } | CredentialKind::Session { .. }, _) => {
            Err(OkfError::Forbidden {
                reason: "this needs a console session: sign in at /signin \
                         (a key cannot manage keys for itself)"
                    .to_string(),
            })
        }
    }
}

/// One catalog of a ceiling.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct CeilingEntry {
    /// The catalog's name.
    pub catalog: String,
    /// `read` or `write`.
    pub access: &'static str,
}

/// A ceiling as the API shows it: one entry per catalog, by name.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `ceiling` - the user's ceiling.
///
/// # Returns
/// The entries, sorted by catalog (a `BTreeMap` iterates in key order).
pub(crate) fn ceiling_view(ceiling: Ceiling) -> Vec<CeilingEntry> {
    ceiling
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(catalog, access)| CeilingEntry {
            catalog,
            access: access.as_str(),
        })
        .collect()
}

/// `GET /me`'s answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct AccountView {
    /// The user's name.
    pub user: String,
    /// Free text, possibly empty.
    pub display_name: String,
    /// Where setup, reset and notice mail goes.
    pub email: Option<String>,
    /// An admin user (its console session acts as an admin).
    pub admin: bool,
    /// Whether a password is set.
    pub has_password: bool,
    /// The user's teams, sorted, its personal team included.
    pub teams: Vec<String>,
    /// What its self-issued credentials may reach.
    pub ceiling: Vec<CeilingEntry>,
    /// Whether the caller is a console session (`false` for a key).
    pub session: bool,
    /// Whether password sign-in is on (the `password_sign_in` setting), so
    /// the account page can say why a password does not sign in.
    pub password_sign_in: bool,
    /// The self-issued key limits, so My keys can offer only what the API
    /// accepts.
    pub limits: AccountLimits,
}

/// The self-issued key limits (the policy settings).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct AccountLimits {
    /// The most live self-issued keys (`max_keys_per_user`).
    pub max_keys_per_user: u32,
    /// The longest expiry in seconds (`max_key_lifetime`), or `None` for no
    /// limit. Seconds, so the console needs no duration parser.
    pub max_key_lifetime_secs: Option<u64>,
}

/// `GET /me/keys`' answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct OwnKeys {
    /// The user's API keys, revoked ones included.
    pub keys: Vec<KeyView>,
}

/// `GET /me/grants`' answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct OwnGrants {
    /// The user's OAuth grants, revoked ones included.
    pub grants: Vec<KeyView>,
}

/// One catalog and level in `POST /me/keys`' body.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(super) struct CatalogLevelBody {
    /// The catalog's name.
    pub catalog: String,
    /// `read` or `write` (`admin` is refused as over the ceiling).
    pub access: String,
}

/// `POST /me/keys`' body. There is no `all` and no `maintenance_report`:
/// `deny_unknown_fields` makes either a 422.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct CreateKeyBody {
    /// Grouping name, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`.
    name: String,
    /// The catalogs, each with its level.
    catalogs: Vec<CatalogLevelBody>,
    /// The default catalog (empty or absent: none); must be one of `catalogs`.
    default_catalog: Option<String>,
    /// The actor (empty or absent: the name).
    actor: Option<String>,
    /// RFC 3339 expiry (empty or absent: the lifetime limit, or none).
    expires_at: Option<String>,
}

/// The rename bodies of `PATCH /me/keys/{id}` and `PATCH /me/passkeys/{id}`.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct RenameBody {
    /// The new name.
    name: String,
}

/// This area's routes.
pub(crate) fn routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    Router::new()
        .route("/me", get(account))
        .route("/me/keys", get(list_keys).post(create_key))
        .route("/me/keys/{id}", patch(rename_key).delete(revoke_key))
        .route("/me/grants", get(list_grants))
        .route("/me/grants/{id}", delete(revoke_grant))
}

/// The levels a create body asks for, by catalog.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `entries` - the body's `catalogs`.
///
/// # Returns
/// Each catalog's level.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::InvalidPath`] (400) for no catalogs, a catalog given twice,
/// or an unknown level.
pub(super) fn requested_levels(
    entries: &[CatalogLevelBody],
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Access>, OkfError> {
    if entries.is_empty() {
        return Err(OkfError::InvalidPath {
            path: "catalogs".to_string(),
            reason: "name at least one catalog".to_string(),
        });
    }
    let mut levels = BTreeMap::new();
    for entry in entries {
        let access = parse_access(&entry.access)?;
        // `insert` returns the value it replaced, like `dict.setdefault`
        // inverted: `Some` means the catalog was already there.
        if levels.insert(entry.catalog.clone(), access).is_some() {
            return Err(OkfError::InvalidPath {
                path: "catalogs".to_string(),
                reason: format!("{:?} is given twice", entry.catalog),
            });
        }
    }
    Ok(levels)
}

/// Refuses levels above the ceiling (the ceiling never holds `admin`, so
/// an admin level is always refused).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `levels` - what the key asks for.
/// * `ceiling` - the user's ceiling.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "ceiling"`, naming the first
/// catalog that is outside it or above its level.
pub(super) fn within_ceiling(
    levels: &BTreeMap<String, Access>,
    ceiling: &Ceiling,
) -> Result<(), OkfError> {
    for (catalog, &wanted) in levels {
        match ceiling.get(catalog) {
            Some(&allowed) if wanted <= allowed => {}
            Some(&allowed) => {
                return Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded {
                    limit: "ceiling",
                    reason: format!("your access to {catalog} is at most {}", allowed.as_str()),
                })
            }
            None => {
                return Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded {
                    limit: "ceiling",
                    reason: format!("{catalog} is not among the catalogs you may use"),
                })
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// A new self-issued key's expiry.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `requested` - the body's `expires_at` (RFC 3339; empty means none).
/// * `max_lifetime` - the `max_key_lifetime` setting.
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Returns
/// The requested expiry; with none requested, `now + max_lifetime` when the
/// setting is set, else no expiry.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::InvalidPath`] (400) for a malformed or past time;
/// [`OkfError::LimitExceeded`] with `limit: "max_key_lifetime"` past the limit.
pub(super) fn key_expiry(
    requested: Option<&str>,
    max_lifetime: Option<std::time::Duration>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Option<DateTime<Utc>>, OkfError> {
    // `transpose` turns `Option<Result<T, E>>` into `Result<Option<T>, E>`,
    // so `?` can apply to the parse only when there was something to parse.
    let requested = requested
        .filter(|text| !text.is_empty())
        .map(|text| {
            DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(text)
                .map(|at| at.with_timezone(&Utc))
                .map_err(|_| OkfError::InvalidPath {
                    path: "expires_at".to_string(),
                    reason: format!("must be an RFC 3339 time, not {text:?}"),
                })
        })
        .transpose()?;
    if requested.is_some_and(|at| at <= now) {
        return Err(OkfError::InvalidPath {
            path: "expires_at".to_string(),
            reason: "must be in the future".to_string(),
        });
    }
    // `None` when the setting is unset, or too large to represent as a
    // date: either way there is no limit.
    let latest = max_lifetime
        .and_then(|max| TimeDelta::from_std(max).ok())
        .and_then(|max| now.checked_add_signed(max));
    match (requested, latest) {
        (Some(at), Some(latest)) if at > latest => Err(OkfError::LimitExceeded {
            limit: "max_key_lifetime",
            reason: format!("a new key may live until {} at the latest", format_timestamp(latest)),
        }),
        (Some(at), _) => Ok(Some(at)),
        (None, latest) => Ok(latest),
    }
}

/// The user's own credential of `kind` with this id.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the application.
/// * `user` - the session user.
/// * `kind` - an API key or an OAuth grant.
/// * `id` - the credential's id.
///
/// # Returns
/// Its record.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] for an unknown id or another user's credential
/// (worded alike); [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn own(
    app: &App,
    user: SessionUser<'_>,
    kind: KeyKind,
    id: &str,
) -> Result<KeyRecord, OkfError> {
    key_rows::list(app.pool())
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .find(|record| {
            record.id == id && record.kind == kind && record.user_id.as_deref() == Some(user.id)
        })
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::NotFound {
            path: format!("me/{}/{id}", if kind == KeyKind::Key { "keys" } else { "grants" }),
        })
}

/// Every credential of `kind` belonging to the user.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn owned(app: &App, user: SessionUser<'_>, kind: KeyKind) -> Result<Vec<KeyView>, OkfError> {
    Ok(key_rows::list(app.pool())
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|record| record.kind == kind && record.user_id.as_deref() == Some(user.id))
        .map(KeyView::from)
        .collect())
}

/// `GET /me`: the account behind the caller: a session's user, or the user
/// a key belongs to.
///
/// # Errors
/// 404 for a key that belongs to no user; 500 for a database failure.
async fn account(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<AccountView>, AppError> {
    let Some(name) = principal.user.as_deref() else {
        return Err(OkfError::NotFound {
            path: "me".to_string(),
        }
        .into());
    };
    let record = users::find(app.pool(), name).await?;
    let ceiling = ceiling::ceiling_of(app.pool(), name).await?;
    let policy = app.settings();
    Ok(Json(AccountView {
        user: record.name,
        display_name: record.display_name,
        email: record.email,
        admin: record.is_admin,
        has_password: record.has_password,
        teams: record.teams,
        ceiling: ceiling_view(ceiling),
        session: matches!(principal.kind, CredentialKind::Session { .. }),
        password_sign_in: policy.password_sign_in,
        limits: AccountLimits {
            max_keys_per_user: policy.max_keys_per_user,
            max_key_lifetime_secs: policy.max_key_lifetime.map(|lifetime| lifetime.as_secs()),
        },
    }))
}

/// `GET /me/keys`: the user's API keys.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_keys(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<OwnKeys>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    Ok(Json(OwnKeys {
        keys: owned(&app, user, KeyKind::Key).await?,
    }))
}

/// `POST /me/keys`: creates a self-issued key and returns its secret, once.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 400 for no catalogs, a repeated catalog, an
/// unknown level or a bad expiry; 409 for a bad or taken name or a default
/// catalog that is not granted; 422 above the ceiling, past the key limit
/// or the lifetime limit, or for an unknown body field such as `all`.
async fn create_key(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Json(body): Json<CreateKeyBody>,
) -> Result<Json<CreatedKeyView>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let levels = requested_levels(&body.catalogs)?;
    let ceiling = ceiling::ceiling_of(app.pool(), user.name).await?;
    within_ceiling(&levels, &ceiling)?;
    let now = app.clock().now();
    // The cached policy (Task 5), not a query per request.
    let policy = app.settings();
    let expires_at = key_expiry(body.expires_at.as_deref(), policy.max_key_lifetime, now)?;
    let default_catalog = body
        .default_catalog
        .as_deref()
        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty());
    let actor = body
        .actor
        .as_deref()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|actor| !actor.is_empty())
        .unwrap_or(&body.name);
    let names: Vec<String> = levels.keys().cloned().collect();
    let grants: Vec<CatalogGrant> = levels
        .iter()
        .map(|(catalog, &access)| CatalogGrant {
            catalog: catalog.clone(),
            access: Some(access),
        })
        .collect();
    // The key's own level is its highest catalog level (Decision 1);
    // `requested_levels` refused an empty list, so the fallback never shows.
    let access = levels.values().copied().max().unwrap_or(Access::Read);
    let new = NewKey {
        name: &body.name,
        access,
        maintenance_report: false,
        grants: Grants::Catalogs(&names),
        default_catalog,
        actor,
        user: user.name,
        self_issued: true,
        expires_at,
        levels: &grants,
    };
    let created = key_rows::create_self_issued(app.pool(), &new, policy.max_keys_per_user, now).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, key = %created.id, "self-issued key created");
    settle(&app).await;
    let key = own(&app, user, KeyKind::Key, &created.id).await?;
    Ok(Json(CreatedKeyView {
        key: key.into(),
        secret: created.key,
    }))
}

/// `PATCH /me/keys/{id}`: renames one of the user's live keys.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 404 for another user's key or an unknown id;
/// 409 for a bad or taken name or a revoked key; 422 without `name`.
async fn rename_key(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
    Json(body): Json<RenameBody>,
) -> Result<Json<KeyView>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let target = own(&app, user, KeyKind::Key, &id).await?;
    key_rows::rename_by_id(app.pool(), &target.id, &body.name).await?;
    Ok(Json(own(&app, user, KeyKind::Key, &target.id).await?.into()))
}

/// `DELETE /me/keys/{id}`: revokes one of the user's keys; it
/// authenticates nothing from the next request on.
///
/// # Returns
/// The key as it now is.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 404 for another user's key or an unknown id;
/// 409 if it is already revoked.
async fn revoke_key(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<KeyView>, AppError> {
    revoke_own(&app, &principal, KeyKind::Key, &id).await
}

/// `GET /me/grants`: the user's OAuth grants.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_grants(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<OwnGrants>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    Ok(Json(OwnGrants {
        grants: owned(&app, user, KeyKind::OAuth).await?,
    }))
}

/// `DELETE /me/grants/{id}`: revokes one of the user's grants, and with it
/// every token issued under it.
///
/// # Errors
/// As [`revoke_key`].
async fn revoke_grant(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<KeyView>, AppError> {
    revoke_own(&app, &principal, KeyKind::OAuth, &id).await
}

/// The body of [`revoke_key`] and [`revoke_grant`].
async fn revoke_own(
    app: &App,
    principal: &Principal,
    kind: KeyKind,
    id: &str,
) -> Result<Json<KeyView>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(principal)?;
    let target = own(app, user, kind, id).await?;
    key_rows::revoke_by_id(app.pool(), &target.id, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, credential = %target.id, "self-service revoke");
    settle(app).await;
    Ok(Json(own(app, user, kind, &target.id).await?.into()))
}
```

```markdown
## Added
```

### Task 10b: Self-service API: password, passkeys, identities, sessions and sign-ins

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/http/api/me.rs` (the account routes, their views and bodies, and their tests)
- Test: `src/http/api/me.rs` (`mod tests`)

The rules of Task 10a hold here too: session principals only (403 for a key), and a route acts only on the session user's own rows (another user's passkey, identity or session is a 404). Removing or unlinking the last sign-in method is a 409. A password change ends the user's other sessions unless `keep_sessions`, and a wrong current password is a 403, never a 401 (the console signs out on any 401). It checks the current password with Task 4's `passwords::verify_user`, and mails the notice through Task 7b's `signin::notify_method_added`.

```rust
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn every_account_route_refuses_a_bearer_key() {
        let test = app().await;
        let keys = keys(&test).await;
        let rows: [(&str, &str, Option<serde_json::Value>); 8] = [
            ("PUT", "/api/v1/me/password", Some(json!({"new_password": "a long new password"}))),
            ("GET", "/api/v1/me/passkeys", None),

            assert_eq!(status.as_u16(), 403, "{method} {uri}: {answer}");
        }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn changing_the_password_needs_the_current_one_and_revokes_other_sessions() {
        let test = app().await;
        let mut first = member(&test, "alice", &[]).await;
        let mut second = Browser::session_for(&test, "alice").await;
        let id = user_id(&test, "alice").await;
        users::set_email(test.app.pool(), "alice", Some("alice@example.com"))
            .await
            .expect("email");
        passwords::set(test.app.pool(), &id, "correct horse battery", Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("password");
        let change = |current: &str, new: &str| {
            json!({"current_password": current, "new_password": new})
        };

        let (wrong, _) = first
            .send(
                &test,
                "PUT",
                "/api/v1/me/password",
                Payload::Json(change("not it at all", "a long new password")),
            )
            .await.parts();
        let (weak, refused) = first
            .send(
                &test,
                "PUT",
                "/api/v1/me/password",
                Payload::Json(change("correct horse battery", "short")),
            )
            .await.parts();
        let (changed, _) = first
            .send(
                &test,
                "PUT",
                "/api/v1/me/password",
                Payload::Json(change("correct horse battery", "a long new password")),
            )
            .await.parts();
        let (kept, _) = first.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (ended, _) = second.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let queued = mail_queue::list(test.app.pool()).await.expect("the queue");

        assert_eq!(wrong.as_u16(), 403, "a wrong current password");
        assert_eq!(weak.as_u16(), 422);
        assert_eq!(refused["limit"], "password");
        assert_eq!(changed.as_u16(), 204);
        assert_eq!(kept.as_u16(), 200, "the session that changed it stays");
        assert_eq!(ended.as_u16(), 401, "every other session is revoked");
        assert!(
            queued
                .iter()
                .any(|mail| mail.to == "alice@example.com" && mail.template == "method_added"),
            "{queued:?}"
        );
    }

        let mut second = Browser::session_for(&test, "alice").await;

        let (_, listed) = first.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me/sessions", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let sessions = listed["sessions"].as_array().expect("a list").clone();
        let other = sessions
            .iter()

            .expect("the other session")["id_prefix"]
            .as_str()

            .to_string();
        let (revoked, _) =
            first.send(&test, "DELETE", &format!("/api/v1/me/sessions/{other}"), Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (ended, _) = second.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (_, after) = first.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me/sessions", Payload::Empty).await.parts();

        assert_eq!(sessions.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(sessions.iter().filter(|s| s["current"] == true).count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(revoked.as_u16(), 204);
        assert_eq!(ended.as_u16(), 401);
        assert_eq!(after["sessions"].as_array().map(Vec::len), Some(1));

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn identities_unlink_unless_last_and_passkey_routes_answer_404_for_unknown_ids() {
        let test = app().await;

            .await
            .expect("link");

        let (_, listed) = alice.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me/identities", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (last, _) =
            alice.send(&test, "DELETE", "/api/v1/me/identities/example", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        passwords::set(test.app.pool(), &id, "a long first password", Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("password");
        let (unlinked, _) =
            alice.send(&test, "DELETE", "/api/v1/me/identities/example", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (_, passkeys) = alice.send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/me/passkeys", Payload::Empty).await.parts();
        let (rename, _) = alice
            .send(
                &test,
                "PATCH",
                "/api/v1/me/passkeys/AAAA",
                Payload::Json(json!({"name": "phone"})),
            )
            .await.parts();
        let (remove, _) = alice.send(&test, "DELETE", "/api/v1/me/passkeys/AAAA", Payload::Empty).await.parts();

        assert_eq!(listed["identities"][0]["provider"], "example");
        assert_eq!(listed["identities"][0]["email_at_link"], "alice@example.com");
        assert_eq!(listed["providers"], json!([]), "this app configures no provider");
        assert_eq!(last.as_u16(), 409, "the last sign-in method stays");
        assert_eq!(unlinked.as_u16(), 204);
        assert_eq!(passkeys, json!({"passkeys": []}));
        assert_eq!(rename.as_u16(), 404);
        assert_eq!(remove.as_u16(), 404);
    }
```

```rust
/// How many recent sign-ins `GET /me/sign-ins` shows.
const RECENT_SIGN_INS: i64 = 50;

/// One passkey, never its public key.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct PasskeyView {
    /// Its credential id, base64url (the `{id}` of the other routes).
    pub id: String,
    /// The name its owner gave it.
    pub name: String,
    /// When it was registered.
    pub created_at: String,
    /// When it last signed in.
    pub last_used_at: Option<String>,
}

/// `GET /me/passkeys`' answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct PasskeyList {
    /// The user's passkeys.
    pub passkeys: Vec<PasskeyView>,
}

/// One linked OIDC identity.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct IdentityView {
    /// The configured provider id (the `{provider}` of the unlink route).
    pub provider: String,
    /// The provider's email when it was linked.
    pub email_at_link: String,
    /// When it was linked.
    pub created_at: String,
    /// When it last signed in.
    pub last_used_at: Option<String>,
}

/// `GET /me/identities`' answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct IdentityList {
    /// The user's identities.
    pub identities: Vec<IdentityView>,
    /// Every configured provider, for the account page's Link buttons.
    pub providers: Vec<ProviderView>,
}

/// A configured OIDC provider (Task 9), never its secret.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct ProviderView {
    /// The provider id (the `{provider}` of the link and unlink routes).
    pub id: String,
    /// Its button label.
    pub label: String,
}

/// One console session, never its id.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct SessionView {
    /// The first 12 hex characters of the stored hash: enough to revoke it.
    pub id_prefix: String,
    /// When it started.
    pub created_at: String,
    /// When it was last used (to the minute).
    pub last_seen_at: String,
    /// The address it signed in from, if known.
    pub ip: Option<String>,
    /// The browser it signed in with.
    pub user_agent: String,
    /// Whether it is the session making this request.
    pub current: bool,
}

impl From<user_sessions::SessionInfo> for SessionView {
    fn from(info: user_sessions::SessionInfo) -> Self {
        let user_sessions::SessionInfo {
            id_prefix,
            created_at,
            last_seen_at,
            ip,
            user_agent,
            current,
        } = info;
        Self {
            id_prefix,
            created_at: format_timestamp(created_at),
            last_seen_at: format_timestamp(last_seen_at),
            // `IpAddr` prints as `192.0.2.1` or an IPv6 literal.
            ip: ip.map(|address| address.to_string()),
            user_agent,
            current,
        }
    }
}

/// A list of sessions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct SessionList {
    /// The sessions, as the store orders them.
    pub sessions: Vec<SessionView>,
}

/// One sign-in attempt.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct SignInView {
    /// `password`, `passkey`, `oidc` or `setup`.
    pub method: &'static str,
    /// `ok`, `failed` or `locked`.
    pub outcome: &'static str,
    /// The address it came from, if known.
    pub ip: Option<String>,
    /// When it happened.
    pub at: String,
}

impl From<sign_in_events::SignInEvent> for SignInView {
    fn from(event: sign_in_events::SignInEvent) -> Self {
        let sign_in_events::SignInEvent {
            method,
            outcome,
            ip,
            at,
        } = event;
        Self {
            method: method.as_str(),
            outcome: outcome.as_str(),
            ip: ip.map(|address| address.to_string()),
            at: format_timestamp(at),
        }
    }
}

/// A list of sign-in attempts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct SignInList {
    /// Newest first.
    pub sign_ins: Vec<SignInView>,
}

/// `PUT /me/password`'s body.
// `Debug` by hand: neither password may reach a log line.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct PasswordBody {
    /// The password now set; required when there is one.
    current_password: Option<String>,
    /// The new password (at least 12 characters, not a common one).
    new_password: String,
    /// Keep the user's other sessions (default: revoke them).
    #[serde(default)]
    keep_sessions: bool,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for PasswordBody {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("PasswordBody")
            .field("current_password", &"<redacted>")
            .field("new_password", &"<redacted>")
            .field("keep_sessions", &self.keep_sessions)
            .finish()
    }
}

/// `PUT /me/password`: sets or changes the user's password. The current
/// password is required when one is set. Other sessions are revoked unless
/// `keep_sessions`, and a notice goes to the user's email.
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller, or a wrong current password (never 401, which
/// the console reads as "signed out"); 422 for a password the policy
/// refuses (`limit: "password"`) or a body without `new_password`.
async fn change_password(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    Json(body): Json<PasswordBody>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let now = app.clock().now();
    let record = users::find(app.pool(), user.name).await?;
    if record.has_password {
        let current = body.current_password.as_deref().unwrap_or_default();
        match passwords::verify_user(app.pool(), user.id, current, now).await? {
            SignInOutcome::Ok(_) => {}
            SignInOutcome::Failed | SignInOutcome::Locked => {
                return Err(OkfError::Forbidden {
                    reason: "the current password is incorrect".to_string(),
                }
                .into())
            }
        }
    }
    passwords::check_policy(&body.new_password)?;
    passwords::set(app.pool(), user.id, &body.new_password, now).await?;
    if !body.keep_sessions {
        let revoked =
            user_sessions::revoke_all(app.pool(), user.id, cookie(&headers, COOKIE)).await?;
        tracing::info!(user = %user.name, revoked, "other sessions revoked after a password change");
    }
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, "password changed");
    // Task 7b's notice; it needs the user's email, which `UserAuth` carries.
    if let Some(account) = users::find_auth(app.pool(), user.id).await? {
        notify_method_added(&app, &account, "a new password").await;
    }
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `GET /me/passkeys`: the user's passkeys.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_passkeys(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<PasskeyList>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let passkeys = passkeys::list(app.pool(), user.id)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(|info| PasskeyView {
            id: info.id,
            name: info.name,
            created_at: format_timestamp(info.created_at),
            last_used_at: info.last_used_at.map(format_timestamp),
        })
        .collect();
    Ok(Json(PasskeyList { passkeys }))
}

/// `PATCH /me/passkeys/{id}`: renames one of the user's passkeys.
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 400 for an empty name; 404 for an unknown id or
/// another user's passkey.
async fn rename_passkey(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
    Json(body): Json<RenameBody>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let name = body.name.trim();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return Err(OkfError::InvalidPath {
            path: "name".to_string(),
            reason: "a passkey needs a name".to_string(),
        }
        .into());
    }
    passkeys::rename(app.pool(), user.id, &id, name).await?;
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `DELETE /me/passkeys/{id}`: removes one of the user's passkeys.
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 404 for an unknown id or another user's
/// passkey; 409 when it is the user's last sign-in method.
async fn remove_passkey(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    passkeys::remove(app.pool(), user.id, &id).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, "passkey removed");
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `GET /me/identities`: the user's linked OIDC identities.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_identities(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<IdentityList>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let identities = identities::list(app.pool(), user.id)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(|info| IdentityView {
            provider: info.provider,
            email_at_link: info.email_at_link,
            created_at: format_timestamp(info.created_at),
            last_used_at: info.last_used_at.map(format_timestamp),
        })
        .collect();
    // `oidc()` is `None` without providers; `labels()` lists them by id.
    let providers = app.oidc().map_or_else(Vec::new, |oidc| {
        oidc.labels()
            .map(|(id, label)| ProviderView { id: id.to_string(), label: label.to_string() })
            .collect()
    });
    Ok(Json(IdentityList { identities, providers }))
}

/// `DELETE /me/identities/{provider}`: unlinks the user's identity at that
/// provider.
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 404 when none is linked; 409 when it is the
/// user's last sign-in method.
async fn unlink_identity(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(provider): Path<String>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    identities::unlink(app.pool(), user.id, &provider).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, %provider, "identity unlinked");
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `GET /me/sessions`: the user's console sessions, the current one marked.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_sessions(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    headers: HeaderMap,
) -> Result<Json<SessionList>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let sessions = user_sessions::list(app.pool(), user.id, cookie(&headers, COOKIE))
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(SessionView::from)
        .collect();
    Ok(Json(SessionList { sessions }))
}

/// `DELETE /me/sessions/{id_prefix}`: revokes one of the user's sessions
/// (the current one too: that signs this browser out).
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 404 when no session of the user has that prefix.
async fn revoke_session(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id_prefix): Path<String>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    user_sessions::revoke_by_prefix(app.pool(), user.id, &id_prefix).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, %id_prefix, "session revoked by its user");
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `GET /me/sign-ins`: the user's recent sign-in attempts, newest first.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a bearer caller; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_sign_ins(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<SignInList>, AppError> {
    let user = session_user(&principal)?;
    let sign_ins = sign_in_events::recent(app.pool(), user.name, RECENT_SIGN_INS)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(SignInView::from)
        .collect();
    Ok(Json(SignInList { sign_ins }))
}
```

```markdown
# M12 Task 10b: self-service account routes

## Added
- `PUT /api/v1/me/password`; `GET /me/passkeys`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /me/passkeys/{id}`; `GET /me/identities` (with the configured providers), `DELETE /me/identities/{provider}`; `GET /me/sessions`, `DELETE /me/sessions/{id_prefix}`; `GET /me/sign-ins`. Console sessions only.
```

### Task 11: OAuth consent as the signed-in user

**Files:**
- Create: `src/store/oauth/grants.rs` (`NewSelfIssuedGrant`, `create_self_issued`, the grant naming rule, tests); register `pub mod grants;` in `src/store/oauth/mod.rs`
- Modify: `src/store/oauth/codes.rs` (`client_host` becomes `pub(crate)`)
- Modify: `src/oauth/state.rs` (`UserConsent`; `PendingAuthorization.consent`; its `Debug`; the Debug test)
- Modify: `src/oauth/authorize.rs` (`signin` query parameter; the redirect to `/signin`; the user consent page; `action=consent`; `finish` factored out of `approve`; `code_path_href`)
- Modify: `src/oauth/consent.rs` (`UserPage`, `user_page_html`, `user_page`)
- Modify: `src/http/ui/consent.css` (the catalog rows)
- Modify: `src/http/signin.rs` (Task 7b's sign-in page shows "Use a sign-in code instead" when `return_to` is an authorize URL)
- Modify: `src/oauth/testing.rs` (`authorize_query()` gains `signin=code`; `user_authorize_query()`; `send_as`)
- Modify: `tests/support/oauth.rs` (`authorize` adds `signin=code`), `tests/ui_e2e/consent.rs` (the journey's authorize URL adds `signin=code`)
- Test: `src/oauth/authorize.rs`, `src/store/oauth/grants.rs`, `src/oauth/state.rs`

The flow (spec "OAuth consent as the user"):
1. `GET /oauth/authorize` validates the client, the redirect URI, the response type, PKCE and the resource, exactly as today. Errors keep going where they go now.
2. **No session cookie** (or an expired one), and no `signin=code`: a 303 to `/signin?return_to=<the authorize URL>`. Nothing enters `oauth.pending`.
3. **`signin=code`**: today's step 1, the sign-in code form, unchanged. That path's grants stay admin-issued and uncapped.
4. **Signed in**: a pending authorization bound to the user and to a fresh consent nonce. The page lists the client and the user's ceiling: a checkbox per catalog and a level select offering only the levels the ceiling allows, a default catalog select, Approve and Deny, and a "Use a sign-in code instead" link.
5. **The POST** (`action=consent`). It first checks the CSRF token, the consent nonce and that the cookie still belongs to the user the page was shown to. It then re-reads the ceiling, refuses any choice outside it (the page is never trusted), and creates a self-issued `oauth` grant. From there it continues the existing code-issuance path.

The sign-in code path keeps working for people who have no account: `/signin` shows the same "Use a sign-in code instead" link when its `return_to` is an authorize URL.

Register it with `pub mod grants;` in `src/store/oauth/mod.rs`, and change `fn client_host` in `src/store/oauth/codes.rs` to `pub(crate) fn client_host`. Update the module doc of `src/store/oauth/mod.rs` to name `grants` ("self-issued grants from consent as a signed-in user").

```rust
//! Self-issued OAuth grants (spec "OAuth consent as the user"): what a
//! signed-in person approves on the consent page. Each one is an `api_keys`
//! row of kind `oauth` with `self_issued = true`, the person's user id and
//! one level per catalog. The key cache caps it by the user's ceiling on
//! every reload (Task 3), so lowering the ceiling later lowers it.
//!
//! Grants redeemed from admin-minted sign-in codes stay in
//! `store::oauth::codes::redeem`: they are admin-issued and uncapped.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::maintenance::types::new_id;
use crate::store::catalogs::bump_admin_generation;
use crate::store::keys::{resolve_grants, Access, Grants};
use crate::store::oauth::clients::ClientRecord;
use crate::store::oauth::codes::client_host;
use crate::store::users;

/// The longest actor a client's name becomes (client names are untrusted
/// metadata and may be long).
const MAX_ACTOR_CHARS: usize = 100;

/// A grant to create from a signed-in person's consent.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NewSelfIssuedGrant<'a> {
    /// The signed-in user's name; the grant belongs to it.
    pub user: &'a str,
    /// The client being authorized (already stored).
    pub client: &'a ClientRecord,
    /// Each chosen catalog's level, `Read` or `Write`, already checked
    /// against the user's ceiling.
    pub levels: &'a BTreeMap<String, Access>,
    /// The default catalog; must be one of `levels`.
    pub default_catalog: Option<&'a str>,
}

/// A self-issued grant's name: `<user>.<client host>-<8 random hex>`. The
/// user leads, as a code's name does for a redeemed grant. The suffix tells
/// apart two consents of one user to one client.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `user` - the user's name (`[a-z0-9-]+`).
/// * `client` - the client.
///
/// # Returns
/// A name that passes the `api_keys` name check.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Io`] if the OS random source fails.
fn grant_name(user: &str, client: &ClientRecord) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    let id = new_id()?;
    // `new_id` is 32 hex characters; `get(..8)` cannot fail, but returns
    // `None` rather than panicking if it ever did.
    let suffix = id.get(..8).unwrap_or(&id);
    Ok(format!("{user}.{}-{suffix}", client_host(client)))
}

/// A self-issued grant's actor: the client's name, trimmed and cut to
/// [`MAX_ACTOR_CHARS`], or its host when it gave none.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `client` - the client.
///
/// # Returns
/// A non-empty actor.
fn actor_for(client: &ClientRecord) -> String {
    match client.client_name.as_deref().map(str::trim) {
        // `chars().take(n)` cuts on character boundaries, never inside a
        // multi-byte character as a byte slice could.
        Some(name) if !name.is_empty() => name.chars().take(MAX_ACTOR_CHARS).collect(),
        Some(_) | None => client_host(client),
    }
}

/// Creates a self-issued OAuth grant and its per-catalog levels, and bumps
/// the administrative generation so the key cache loads it, in one
/// transaction.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `new` - the user, client, levels and default catalog.
/// * `now` - the creation time (server clock).
///
/// # Returns
/// The grant's id (its `api_keys.id`).
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] for no catalog, an `Admin` level, or a default
/// that is not chosen; [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user;
/// [`OkfError::CatalogNotSelected`] for a catalog deleted meanwhile;
/// [`OkfError::Io`] if the OS random source fails; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn create_self_issued(
    pool: &PgPool,
    new: &NewSelfIssuedGrant<'_>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    // The schema also refuses an admin self-issued row; checking here gives a
    // 409 with a reason instead of a CHECK violation.
    if new.levels.values().any(|&access| access == Access::Admin) {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "a grant from consent is never admin".to_string(),
        });
    }
    // `max` is `None` only for no catalogs, which `resolve_grants` would
    // refuse too; refusing first keeps the message about consent.
    let Some(access) = new.levels.values().copied().max() else {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "a grant from consent needs at least one catalog".to_string(),
        });
    };
    let name = grant_name(new.user, new.client)?;
    let names: Vec<String> = new.levels.keys().cloned().collect();
    // The same order as `names`: both iterate the map in key order.
    let levels: Vec<&'static str> = new.levels.values().map(|access| access.as_str()).collect();
    let mut tx = pool.begin().await?;
    // `FOR KEY SHARE` until commit, as for keys: a concurrent user delete
    // waits and then counts this grant.
    let user_id = users::id_of(&mut tx, new.user).await?;
    let (catalog_ids, default_catalog_id) = resolve_grants(
        &mut tx,
        "grant",
        &name,
        Grants::Catalogs(&names),
        new.default_catalog,
    )
    .await?;
    let grant_id: String = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "INSERT INTO api_keys \
         (name, sha256, kind, client_id, access, maintenance_report, all_catalogs, \
          default_catalog_id, actor, created_at, user_id, self_issued) \
         VALUES ($1, NULL, 'oauth', $2, $3, false, false, $4, $5, $6, $7, true) RETURNING id",
    )
    .bind(&name)
    .bind(&new.client.client_id)
    .bind(access.as_str())
    .bind(default_catalog_id)
    .bind(actor_for(new.client))
    .bind(now)
    .bind(&user_id)
    .fetch_one(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    // Two arrays unnested side by side give one row per catalog with its
    // level, like `zip` in Python.
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO key_catalogs (key_id, catalog_id, access) \
         SELECT $1, chosen.id, chosen.access \
         FROM unnest($2::bigint[], $3::text[]) AS chosen (id, access)",
    )
    .bind(&grant_id)
    .bind(&catalog_ids)
    .bind(&levels)
    .execute(&mut *tx)
    .await?;
    bump_admin_generation(&mut tx).await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(grant_id)
}
```

```rust
/// A valid authorization request's query string for a signed-in person:
/// [`authorize_query`] without `signin=code`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The encoded query, without the `?`.
pub(crate) fn user_authorize_query() -> String {
    form(&[
        ("response_type", "code"),
        ("client_id", CLIENT_ID),
        ("redirect_uri", REDIRECT_URI),
        ("state", "xyz"),
        ("code_challenge", CHALLENGE),
        ("code_challenge_method", "S256"),
        ("resource", RESOURCE),
    ])
}

/// As [`send`], with a console session's cookie when `session` is given.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `test` - the app.
/// * `method` - `GET` or `POST`.
/// * `uri` - the path and query.
/// * `body` - a form body, if any.
/// * `session` - a signed-in browser (Task 7a's `Browser`) whose session cookie to send, if any.
///
/// # Returns
/// The status, the headers and the body as text.
///
/// # Panics
/// If the request cannot be built or the body cannot be read.
pub(crate) async fn send_as(
    test: &TestApp,
    method: &str,
    uri: &str,
    body: Option<String>,
    session: Option<&Browser>,
) -> (StatusCode, HeaderMap, String) {
    let mut request = Request::builder().method(method).uri(uri);
    if body.is_some() {
        request = request.header(header::CONTENT_TYPE, "application/x-www-form-urlencoded");
    }
    // Only the cookie: these are top-level navigations and form posts,
    // which carry no CSRF header (the consent form has its own token).
    if let Some(id) = session.and_then(|browser| browser.cookie(COOKIE)) {
        request = request.header(header::COOKIE, format!("{COOKIE}={id}"));
    }
    // ... the rest of today's `send` body, unchanged ...
}
```

```rust
                .into_iter()
                .collect();

        assert_eq!(

        assert_eq!(
            chosen_levels(&choices(&[("grant.main", "yes"), ("level.main", "read")]), &ceiling),
            Err(Choice::Tampered)

            Err(Choice::Tampered)
```

```rust
/// A signed-in person's consent page: who it was shown to, and the random
/// token its Approve must echo (the summary nonce of the code path, for
/// the user path).
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UserConsent {
    /// The `users.id` the page was rendered for; the POST's session must
    /// still be this user.
    pub user_id: String,
    /// A random token in the page's form, compared in constant time.
    pub nonce: String,
}

// Written by hand, not derived, so a stray `{:?}` never prints the nonce.
impl std::fmt::Debug for UserConsent {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("UserConsent")
            .field("user_id", &self.user_id)
            .field("nonce", &"<redacted>")
            .finish()
    }
}
```

```rust
/// What the signed-in consent page shows beyond [`PageView`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UserPage<'a> {
    /// The signed-in user's name.
    pub user: &'a str,
    /// The user's ceiling: the catalogs and levels it may grant.
    pub ceiling: &'a Ceiling,
    /// The page's consent nonce (the hidden `summary` input).
    pub nonce: &'a str,
    /// The "Use a sign-in code instead" link (same-origin, unescaped).
    pub code_href: &'a str,
}

/// The signed-in consent page's HTML: a checkbox and a level select per
/// ceiling catalog (only the levels the ceiling allows), a default catalog
/// select, Approve and Deny, and the sign-in code link. With an empty
/// ceiling there is nothing to approve: Deny and the link only.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `view` - the request.
/// * `user` - the user, ceiling, nonce and link.
/// * `error` - a message from a refused choice, if any.
///
/// # Returns
/// The page body.
pub(crate) fn user_page_html(view: &PageView, user: &UserPage<'_>, error: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let error = error.map_or_else(String::new, |message| {
        format!(
            r#"        <p class="error consent-error" id="consent-error" role="alert">{}</p>
"#,
            escape(message)
        )
    });
    let link = format!(
        r#"        <p class="muted"><a href="{}" id="consent-use-code">Use a sign-in code instead</a></p>"#,
        escape(user.code_href)
    );
    if user.ceiling.is_empty() {
        return format!(
            r#"        <h1>Allow access?</h1>
{client}
        <p class="error consent-error" id="consent-empty">You have no catalogs to share yet. Ask an admin for access, or use a sign-in code.</p>
        <form method="post" action="/oauth/authorize" id="consent-user-form">
            {hidden}
            <div class="consent-actions">
                <button type="submit" name="action" value="deny" id="consent-deny" class="secondary">Deny</button>
            </div>
        </form>
{link}"#,
            client = client_block(view),
            hidden = hidden_fields(view),
        );
    }
    // Catalog names are `[a-z0-9-]+` (a schema CHECK), so they are safe in
    // ids and names; they are escaped anyway, as everything is.
    let rows: String = user
        .ceiling
        .iter()
        .map(|(catalog, &allowed)| {
            let name = escape(catalog);
            let write = if allowed >= Access::Write {
                r#"
                        <option value="write">write</option>"#
            } else {
                ""
            };
            format!(
                r#"                <div class="consent-catalog">
                    <label><input type="checkbox" name="grant.{name}" value="on" id="consent-catalog-{name}"> {name}</label>
                    <select name="level.{name}" id="consent-level-{name}" aria-label="Access to {name}">
                        <option value="read">read</option>{write}
                    </select>
                </div>
"#
            )
        })
        .collect();
    let defaults: String = user
        .ceiling
        .keys()
        .map(|catalog| {
            let name = escape(catalog);
            format!(
                r#"                    <option value="{name}">{name}</option>
"#
            )
        })
        .collect();
    format!(
        r#"        <h1>Allow access?</h1>
{client}
        <p class="muted">Signed in as <strong id="consent-user">{user}</strong>. Choose what <strong>{name}</strong> may use. You can grant up to your own access.</p>
{error}        <form method="post" action="/oauth/authorize" id="consent-user-form">
            {hidden}
            <input type="hidden" name="summary" value="{nonce}">
            <fieldset id="consent-catalogs">
                <legend>Catalogs</legend>
{rows}            </fieldset>
            <label>Default catalog
                <select name="default_catalog" id="consent-default">
                    <option value="">None</option>
{defaults}                </select>
            </label>
            <div class="consent-actions">
                <button type="submit" name="action" value="consent" id="consent-approve">Approve</button>
                <button type="submit" name="action" value="deny" id="consent-deny" class="secondary" formnovalidate>Deny</button>
            </div>
        </form>
{link}"#,
        client = client_block(view),
        user = escape(user.user),
        name = escape(&view.client_name),
        hidden = hidden_fields(view),
        nonce = escape(user.nonce),
    )
}

/// The signed-in consent page.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `view` - the request.
/// * `user` - the user, ceiling, nonce and link.
/// * `error` - a message from a refused choice, if any.
///
/// # Returns
/// 200 with the page.
pub fn user_page(view: &PageView, user: &UserPage<'_>, error: Option<&str>) -> Response {
    page(
        StatusCode::OK,
        "Allow access?",
        &user_page_html(view, user, error),
        Some(&view.redirect_origin),
    )
}
```

```rust
/// The "Use a sign-in code instead" link for an authorize URL.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `return_to` - a same-origin URL, such as `/signin`'s sanitised
///   `return_to`.
///
/// # Returns
/// The URL with `signin=code` added, or `None` when it is not an authorize
/// URL (so `/signin` shows no link for console sign-ins).
pub(crate) fn code_path_href(return_to: &str) -> Option<String> {
    return_to
        .starts_with("/oauth/authorize?")
        .then(|| format!("{return_to}&signin=code"))
}

/// A 303 to `/signin`, which comes back to this authorize URL after
/// sign-in. Nothing is stored: the GET simply runs again.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `raw_query` - the request's query string, as received.
///
/// # Returns
/// The redirect.
fn to_sign_in(raw_query: &str) -> Response {
    let return_to = format!("/oauth/authorize?{raw_query}");
    // `byte_serialize` percent-encodes for a query value, like Python's
    // `urllib.parse.quote_plus`.
    let encoded: String = form_urlencoded::byte_serialize(return_to.as_bytes()).collect();
    Redirect::to(&format!("/signin?return_to={encoded}")).into_response()
}

/// Why a signed-in consent's choices were refused.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Choice {
    /// Nothing was ticked: show the form again.
    Empty,
    /// Something the page never offered: refuse the request.
    Tampered,
}

/// The catalogs and levels a signed-in consent chose, checked against the
/// ceiling read again at POST time (the page is never trusted).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `choices` - the form's `grant.<catalog>` and `level.<catalog>` fields.
/// * `ceiling` - the user's ceiling now.
///
/// # Returns
/// Each ticked catalog's level.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`Choice::Empty`] when nothing is ticked; [`Choice::Tampered`] for a
/// catalog outside the ceiling, a level above it or unknown, a ticked
/// catalog without a level, a checkbox value other than `on`, or any
/// other field.
pub(super) fn chosen_levels(
    choices: &BTreeMap<String, String>,
    ceiling: &Ceiling,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Access>, Choice> {
    let mut chosen = BTreeMap::new();
    for (field, value) in choices {
        // `strip_prefix` is Python's `removeprefix`, returning `None` when
        // the prefix is absent.
        if let Some(catalog) = field.strip_prefix("grant.") {
            let allowed = *ceiling.get(catalog).ok_or(Choice::Tampered)?;
            let level = choices
                .get(&format!("level.{catalog}"))
                .and_then(|level| Access::parse(level))
                .ok_or(Choice::Tampered)?;
            if value != "on" || level > allowed {
                return Err(Choice::Tampered);
            }
            chosen.insert(catalog.to_string(), level);
        } else if let Some(catalog) = field.strip_prefix("level.") {
            // Selects post even when unticked; they must still be offered ones.
            if !ceiling.contains_key(catalog) {
                return Err(Choice::Tampered);
            }
        } else {
            return Err(Choice::Tampered);
        }
    }
    if chosen.is_empty() {
        Err(Choice::Empty)
    } else {
        Ok(chosen)
    }
}

/// Renders the signed-in consent page for a pending authorization.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `app` - the application.
/// * `pending_id`, `pending` - the request; its `consent` is set.
/// * `user` - the signed-in user's name.
/// * `raw_query` - the authorize query, for the sign-in code link.
/// * `error` - a message, if the page is shown again.
///
/// # Returns
/// The page, or a 500 page if the ceiling cannot be read.
async fn user_consent_page(
    app: &App,
    pending_id: &str,
    pending: &PendingAuthorization,
    user: &str,
    raw_query: &str,
    error: Option<&str>,
) -> Response {
    let Some(consent) = pending.consent.as_ref() else {
        return consent::error_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, EXPIRED);
    };
    let ceiling = match ceiling::ceiling_of(app.pool(), user).await {
        Ok(ceiling) => ceiling,
        Err(error) => return server_error(&error),
    };
    let code_href = format!("/oauth/authorize?{raw_query}&signin=code");
    consent::user_page(
        &view(pending_id, pending),
        &UserPage {
            user,
            ceiling: &ceiling,
            nonce: &consent.nonce,
            code_href: &code_href,
        },
        error,
    )
}
```

  8. **The user path's POST:**

```rust
/// `action=consent`: a signed-in person's approval. It checks the nonce
/// and that the cookie is still that person's, re-reads the ceiling,
/// refuses any choice outside it, creates the self-issued grant, and
/// finishes as the code path does.
async fn consent_as_user(
    app: &App,
    oauth: &OAuth,
    form: &ConsentForm,
    pending: &PendingAuthorization,
    headers: &HeaderMap,
) -> Response {
    let Some(consent) = pending.consent.as_ref() else {
        return consent::error_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, EXPIRED);
    };
    let nonce_matches = form.summary.as_deref().is_some_and(|posted| {
        consent.nonce.as_bytes().ct_eq(posted.as_bytes()).into()
    });
    if !nonce_matches {
        return consent::error_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, EXPIRED);
    }
    let user = match signed_in_user(app, headers).await {
        Ok(Some(user)) if user.id == consent.user_id => user,
        Ok(_) => {
            oauth.pending.remove(&form.pending);
            return consent::error_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, SIGNED_OUT);
        }
        Err(error) => return server_error(&error),
    };
    let ceiling = match ceiling::ceiling_of(app.pool(), &user.name).await {
        Ok(ceiling) => ceiling,
        Err(error) => return server_error(&error),
    };
    let again = |message| {
        user_consent_page(app, &form.pending, pending, &user.name, &pending.query, Some(message))
    };
    let chosen = match chosen_levels(&form.choices, &ceiling) {
        Ok(chosen) => chosen,
        Err(Choice::Empty) => return again(NOTHING_CHOSEN).await,
        Err(Choice::Tampered) => {
            oauth.pending.remove(&form.pending);
            tracing::warn!(user = %user.name, client = %pending.client.client_id,
                           "refused a consent outside the offered choices");
            return consent::error_page(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, TAMPERED);
        }
    };
    let default_catalog = form
        .default_catalog
        .as_deref()
        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty());
    if default_catalog.is_some_and(|name| !chosen.contains_key(name)) {
        return again(DEFAULT_NOT_CHOSEN).await;
    }
    let new = NewSelfIssuedGrant {
        user: &user.name,
        client: &pending.client,
        levels: &chosen,
        default_catalog,
    };
    let grant_id = match grant_rows::create_self_issued(app.pool(), &new, app.clock().now()).await {
        Ok(grant_id) => grant_id,
        Err(error) => return server_error(&error),
    };
    tracing::info!(user = %user.name, client = %pending.client.client_id, grant = %grant_id,
                   "consent granted as the signed-in user");
    finish(app, oauth, &form.pending, pending, grant_id).await
}
```

  `again` is a closure that returns a future (each call builds one `user_consent_page(...)` future); `.await` runs it.

```markdown
# M12 Task 11: OAuth consent as the signed-in user

## Added
- `GET /oauth/authorize` without a session sends the person to `/signin?return_to=<the authorize URL>`; signed in, it shows the person's ceiling as checkboxes and level selects with a default catalog.
- Approving creates a self-issued `oauth` grant (`store::oauth::grants::create_self_issued`) named `<user>.<client host>-<8 hex>`, with the client's name as actor; the key cache caps it by the ceiling on every reload.
- "Use a sign-in code instead" (`signin=code`) on the consent page and on `/signin` when it returns to an authorize URL.

## Changed
- The sign-in code path is reached with `signin=code`; it is unchanged otherwise, and its grants stay admin-issued and uncapped.

## Notes
- The POST re-reads the ceiling, refuses anything the page did not offer, and checks the CSRF token, the consent nonce and that the cookie still belongs to the user the page was shown to.
```

This task lands before the CLI (Task 13), so `tests/admin_parity.rs` never breaks: the routes and their reference rows exist first, and Task 13 adds the commands together with their parity rows. The CLI column below names the command each route will match.

One REST route per admin action (Decision 17), with M11's permission rule: writes need an admin that reaches every catalog (`require_every_catalog`), and reads need any admin (`require_admin`). Member access goes through `ceiling::may_set_member_access`, the spec's single permission hook. Today it is the same rule as `require_every_catalog`.

The API refuses to clear the last admin user for every principal (Decision 16), so `set_admin` is called with `allow_last: false`.

| CLI | Route | Guard | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user set-admin` | `PUT /users/{name}/admin` `{admin}` | every-catalog admin | `{name, previous, admin}`; 409 for the last admin |
| `user set-email` | `PUT /users/{name}/email` `{email: string\|null}` | every-catalog admin | `UserView`; 409 duplicate |
| `user invite` | `POST /users/{name}/invite` | every-catalog admin | 202 `{name, email}`; 409 without email or `public_url` |
| `user entitle` | `PUT /users/{name}/entitlements/{catalog}` `{access}` | every-catalog admin | `{name, entitlements}` |
| `user unentitle` | `DELETE /users/{name}/entitlements/{catalog}` | every-catalog admin | `{name, entitlements}` |
| `user sessions` | `GET /users/{name}/sessions` | admin | `{sessions}` |
| `user revoke-sessions` | `DELETE /users/{name}/sessions` | every-catalog admin | `{name, revoked}` |
| (console: revoke one) | `DELETE /users/{name}/sessions/{id_prefix}` | every-catalog admin | 204 |
| `user sign-ins` | `GET /users/{name}/sign-ins` | admin | `{sign_ins}` |
| `catalog set-member-access` | `PUT /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access` `{access}` | `may_set_member_access` | `{name, previous, member_access}` |
| (console: current value) | `GET /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access` | admin on the catalog | `{name, member_access}` |
| `settings list` | `GET /settings` | admin | `{settings, oidc, mail}` |
| `settings set` | `PUT /settings/{key}` `{value}` | every-catalog admin | `SettingView` |
| `settings reset` | `DELETE /settings/{key}` | every-catalog admin | `SettingView` |
| `mail test` | `POST /mail/test` `{to}` | every-catalog admin | 202 `{to}` |
| `mail queue` | `GET /mail/queue` | admin | `{mail}` |
| `mail retry` | `POST /mail/queue/{id}/retry` | every-catalog admin | 204 |
| `mail delete` | `DELETE /mail/queue/{id}` | every-catalog admin | 204 |

Every write logs at `info` with `key = principal.key_id` and `actor = principal.actor`, as `catalogs.rs` does (spec "Logging and audit"), then calls `settle`.

```rust
/// The id of the user called `name`, without a lock: for callers that
/// pass it to functions keyed by user id (sessions, sign-in events, email
/// tokens) and need no consistency with a later write.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `executor` - the pool or a connection.
/// * `name` - the user's name.
///
/// # Returns
/// Its `users.id`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`]; [`OkfError::Database`].
// `impl PgExecutor<'e>` accepts `&PgPool` or `&mut PgConnection`, so one
// function serves both, like `catalogs::find`.
pub async fn id_by_name<'e>(
    executor: impl sqlx::PgExecutor<'e>,
    name: &str,
) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = $1")
        .bind(name)
        .fetch_optional(executor)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| unknown(name))
}
```

```rust
//! Setup emails (spec "Emailed links": Setup): an admin sends a user a
//! single-use link to choose a password or register a passkey. The CLI's
//! `user invite` and the API's `POST /users/{name}/invite` share this.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use crate::config::Config;
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::mail::{queue, Template};
use crate::store::email_tokens::{self, Purpose};
use crate::store::{settings, users};

/// Issues a setup link for `user` and queues the setup email. Any older
/// setup link of the user stops working (`email_tokens::issue`). The link
/// is never returned or logged: only the queued job holds it.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database (the job goes into apalis on it).
/// * `config` - for `public_url` (the link's origin) and the `[auth]`
///   defaults (`setup_link_ttl`).
/// * `user` - the user's name.
/// * `now` - the server clock.
///
/// # Returns
/// The address the email goes to.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Refused`] without `public_url` or without an email;
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`] for an unknown user; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn send_setup(
    pool: &PgPool,
    config: &Config,
    user: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<String, OkfError> {
    let Some(public_url) = config.public_url.as_deref() else {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: "setup links need public_url in the config (Decision 18)".to_string(),
        });
    };
    let user_id = users::id_by_name(pool, user).await?;
    let account = users::find_auth(pool, &user_id)
        .await?
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::UnknownName {
            noun: "user",
            name: user.to_string(),
        })?;
    let Some(email) = account.email else {
        return Err(OkfError::Refused {
            reason: format!("user {user} has no email; set one first (okf-mcp user set-email)"),
        });
    };
    let policy = settings::load(pool, &config.auth).await?;
    let token = email_tokens::issue(pool, &user_id, Purpose::Setup, policy.setup_link_ttl, now).await?;
    // The one link builder (Task 6), so the path matches Task 7b's page.
    let link = crate::mail::link(public_url, crate::mail::SETUP_PATH, &token);
    let template = Template::Setup {
        link,
        user: account.name,
    };
    queue::enqueue(pool, &email, &template, now).await?;
    tracing::info!(%user, "setup email queued");
    Ok(email)
}
```

```rust
        assert_eq!(unknown.as_u16(), 404);
```

```rust
        assert_eq!(back["value"], "20");
        assert_eq!(back["overridden"], false);
    }
```

```rust
        let keys = keys(&test).await;
        queue::enqueue(test.app.pool(), "ops@example.com", &crate::mail::Template::Test, Utc::now())
            .await
            .expect("queue one");
        let id = queue::list(test.app.pool()).await.expect("list")[0].id.clone();
        let write = |method: &'static str, uri: String, body: Option<serde_json::Value>| Row {
            method,
            uri,
            body,
            read: 403,
            write: 403,
            admin: 403,
            stranger: 403,
        };

        assert_matrix_with(
            &test,
            &keys,
            &[
                Row {
                    method: "GET",
                    uri: "/api/v1/mail/queue".to_string(),
                    body: None,
                    read: 403,
                    write: 403,
                    admin: 200,
                    stranger: 200,
                },
                write("POST", "/api/v1/mail/test".to_string(), Some(json!({"to": "ops@example.com"}))),
                write("POST", format!("/api/v1/mail/queue/{id}/retry"), None),
                write("DELETE", format!("/api/v1/mail/queue/{id}"), None),
            ],
        )
        .await;
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_test_mail_is_queued_retried_and_deleted() {
        let test = app().await;
        let root = every_catalog_admin(&test).await;

        let (queued, body) = send(
            &test,
            "POST",
            "/api/v1/mail/test",
            Some(&root),
            Some(json!({"to": "ops@example.com"})),
        )
        .await;
        let (_, listed) = send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/mail/queue", Some(&root), None).await;
        let id = listed["mail"][0]["id"].as_str().expect("an id").to_string();
        sqlx::query("UPDATE apalis.jobs SET status = 'Killed' WHERE id = $1")
            .bind(&id)
            .execute(test.app.pool())
            .await
            .expect("fail the job");
        let (_, failed) = send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/mail/queue", Some(&root), None).await;
        let (retried, _) =
            send(&test, "POST", &format!("/api/v1/mail/queue/{id}/retry"), Some(&root), None).await;
        let (_, pending) = send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/mail/queue", Some(&root), None).await;
        let (deleted, _) =
            send(&test, "DELETE", &format!("/api/v1/mail/queue/{id}"), Some(&root), None).await;
        let (_, empty) = send(&test, "GET", "/api/v1/mail/queue", Some(&root), None).await;

        assert_eq!(queued.as_u16(), 202, "{body}");
        assert_eq!(body, json!({"to": "ops@example.com"}));
        assert_eq!(listed["mail"][0]["to"], "ops@example.com");
        assert_eq!(listed["mail"][0]["template"], "test");
        assert!(listed["mail"][0].get("text").is_none(), "never the body");
        assert_eq!(failed["mail"][0]["status"], "failed");
        assert_eq!(retried.as_u16(), 204);
        assert_eq!(pending["mail"][0]["status"], "pending");
        assert_eq!(deleted.as_u16(), 204);
        assert_eq!(empty, json!({"mail": []}));
    }
}
```

```rust
/// A catalog's member access, for the console's catalog drawer.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the database.
/// * `catalog` - the catalog's name.
///
/// # Returns
/// Its `member_access`.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::CatalogNotSelected`] for an unknown catalog; [`OkfError::Database`].
pub async fn member_access(pool: &PgPool, catalog: &str) -> Result<MemberAccess, OkfError> {
    let stored: Option<String> =
        sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT member_access FROM catalogs WHERE name = $1")
            .bind(catalog)
            .fetch_optional(pool)
            .await?;
    let stored = stored.ok_or_else(|| OkfError::CatalogNotSelected {
        catalog: catalog.to_string(),
    })?;
    Ok(MemberAccess::parse(&stored).expect("the schema checks catalogs.member_access"))
}
```

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct UserView {
    /// Its name (`[a-z0-9-]+`), which its personal team shares.
    pub name: String,

}

impl From<UserRecord> for UserView {
    fn from(record: UserRecord) -> Self {

            display_name,
            created_at,

            teams,
            email,
            is_admin,
            has_password,

        Self {
            name,
            display_name,
            created_at: format_timestamp(created_at),
            credentials,
            teams,
            email,
            admin: is_admin,
            has_password,
        }
    }
```
