The handlers:

```rust
/// How many recent sign-ins `GET /users/{name}/sign-ins` shows.
const RECENT_SIGN_INS: i64 = 50;

/// The user's entitlements as the routes answer them.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::UnknownName`]; [`OkfError::Database`].
async fn entitlements_of(app: &App, name: &str) -> Result<Entitlements, OkfError> {
    Ok(Entitlements {
        name: name.to_string(),
        entitlements: ceiling::entitlements(app.pool(), name)
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(EntitlementView::from)
            .collect(),
    })
}

/// `PUT /users/{name}/admin`: turns the user's admin flag on or off. The
/// API never clears the last admin user (Decision 16).
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown user; 409 for clearing the last admin; 422 without `admin`.
async fn set_admin(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(name): Path<String>,
    Json(body): Json<AdminBody>,
) -> Result<Json<AdminChanged>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let previous = users::set_admin(app.pool(), &name, body.admin, false).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, admin = body.admin, key = %principal.key_id,
                   actor = %principal.actor, "admin flag changed");
    settle(&app).await;
    Ok(Json(AdminChanged {
        name,
        previous,
        admin: body.admin,
    }))
}

/// `PUT /users/{name}/email`: sets or (with `null`) clears the email.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown user; 409 for an email another user has; 422 without `email`.
async fn set_email(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(name): Path<String>,
    Json(body): Json<EmailBody>,
) -> Result<Json<UserView>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    users::set_email(app.pool(), &name, body.email.as_deref()).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, cleared = body.email.is_none(), key = %principal.key_id,
                   actor = %principal.actor, "email changed");
    Ok(Json(users::find(app.pool(), &name).await?.into()))
}

/// `POST /users/{name}/invite`: queues a setup email with a single-use link.
///
/// # Returns
/// 202 with the address: the mail is queued, not yet sent.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown user; 409 without an email or without `public_url`.
async fn invite(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(name): Path<String>,
) -> Result<(StatusCode, Json<Invited>), AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let email =
        mail_invite::send_setup(app.pool(), app.config(), &name, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor,
                   "setup email requested");
    Ok((StatusCode::ACCEPTED, Json(Invited { name, email })))
}

/// `PUT /users/{name}/entitlements/{catalog}`: lets the user reach the
/// catalog at `access`, beyond its teams' catalogs.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 400 for an
/// access other than `read` or `write`; 404 for an unknown user or catalog.
async fn entitle(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path((name, catalog)): Path<(String, String)>,
    Json(body): Json<EntitlementBody>,
) -> Result<Json<Entitlements>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let access = parse_access(&body.access)?;
    if access == Access::Admin {
        return Err(OkfError::InvalidPath {
            path: "access".to_string(),
            reason: "an entitlement is read or write".to_string(),
        }
        .into());
    }
    ceiling::entitle(app.pool(), &name, &catalog, access, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, %catalog, access = access.as_str(), key = %principal.key_id,
                   actor = %principal.actor, "entitlement granted");
    settle(&app).await;
    Ok(Json(entitlements_of(&app, &name).await?))
}

/// `DELETE /users/{name}/entitlements/{catalog}`: removes an entitlement
/// (none: no change).
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown user or catalog.
async fn unentitle(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path((name, catalog)): Path<(String, String)>,
) -> Result<Json<Entitlements>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    ceiling::unentitle(app.pool(), &name, &catalog).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, %catalog, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor,
                   "entitlement removed");
    settle(&app).await;
    Ok(Json(entitlements_of(&app, &name).await?))
}

/// `GET /users/{name}/sessions`: the user's console sessions (none is
/// marked current: the caller is not that browser).
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 below admin; 404 for an unknown user.
async fn list_sessions(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(name): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<SessionList>, AppError> {
    require_admin(&principal)?;
    let id = users::id_by_name(app.pool(), &name).await?;
    let sessions = user_sessions::list(app.pool(), &id, None)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(SessionView::from)
        .collect();
    Ok(Json(SessionList { sessions }))
}

/// `DELETE /users/{name}/sessions`: signs the user out everywhere.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown user.
async fn revoke_sessions(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(name): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<SessionsRevoked>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let id = users::id_by_name(app.pool(), &name).await?;
    let revoked = user_sessions::revoke_all(app.pool(), &id, None).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, revoked, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor,
                   "sessions revoked by an admin");
    Ok(Json(SessionsRevoked { name, revoked }))
}

/// `DELETE /users/{name}/sessions/{id_prefix}`: ends one of the user's
/// sessions (the console's per-row revoke).
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown user or prefix.
async fn revoke_session(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path((name, id_prefix)): Path<(String, String)>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let id = users::id_by_name(app.pool(), &name).await?;
    user_sessions::revoke_by_prefix(app.pool(), &id, &id_prefix).await?;
    tracing::info!(user = %name, %id_prefix, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor,
                   "session revoked by an admin");
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `GET /users/{name}/sign-ins`: the user's recent sign-in attempts.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 below admin; 404 for an unknown user.
async fn list_sign_ins(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(name): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<SignInList>, AppError> {
    require_admin(&principal)?;
    // Resolving the id first turns an unknown name into a 404, not an
    // empty list.
    users::id_by_name(app.pool(), &name).await?;
    let sign_ins = sign_in_events::recent(app.pool(), &name, RECENT_SIGN_INS)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .map(SignInView::from)
        .collect();
    Ok(Json(SignInList { sign_ins }))
}
```

```rust
/// `PUT /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access`'s body.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct MemberAccessBody {
    /// `none`, `read` or `write`.
    access: String,
}

/// `GET /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access`'s answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct MemberAccessView {
    /// The catalog.
    pub name: String,
    /// `none`, `read` or `write`.
    pub member_access: &'static str,
}

/// `PUT /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access`'s answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct MemberAccessChanged {
    /// The catalog.
    pub name: String,
    /// The level before.
    pub previous: &'static str,
    /// The level now.
    pub member_access: &'static str,
}

/// `GET /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access`: what the owning team's members
/// may reach through their self-issued credentials.
///
/// # Errors
/// 404 for a catalog the key does not reach or that does not exist; 403
/// below `admin`.
async fn member_access(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(catalog): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<MemberAccessView>, AppError> {
    principal.require(Access::Admin, &catalog)?;
    let access = ceiling::member_access(app.pool(), &catalog).await?;
    Ok(Json(MemberAccessView {
        name: catalog,
        member_access: access.as_str(),
    }))
}

/// `PUT /catalogs/{catalog}/member-access`: sets it, then polls so every
/// member's self-issued credentials are re-capped at once. The permission
/// is `ceiling::may_set_member_access`, the one hook team owners will
/// later share (spec "Admin surface").
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 for a caller `may_set_member_access` refuses; 400 for an unknown
/// level; 404 for an unknown catalog; 422 without `access`.
async fn set_member_access(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(catalog): Path<String>,
    Json(body): Json<MemberAccessBody>,
) -> Result<Json<MemberAccessChanged>, AppError> {
    if !ceiling::may_set_member_access(&principal, &catalog) {
        return Err(OkfError::Forbidden {
            reason: "this needs an admin key that reaches every catalog".to_string(),
        }
        .into());
    }
    let access = MemberAccess::parse(&body.access).ok_or_else(|| OkfError::InvalidPath {
        path: "access".to_string(),
        reason: format!("must be none, read or write, not {:?}", body.access),
    })?;
    let previous = ceiling::set_member_access(app.pool(), &catalog, access).await?;
    tracing::info!(%catalog, previous = previous.as_str(), access = access.as_str(),
                   key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor, "member access changed");
    settle(&app).await;
    Ok(Json(MemberAccessChanged {
        name: catalog,
        previous: previous.as_str(),
        member_access: access.as_str(),
    }))
}
```

```rust
//! `/api/v1/settings` (spec "Settings"): what `okf-mcp settings ...` does.
//! The listing also shows the configured OIDC providers and the mail
//! provider and From address, read-only, never a secret.
//!
//! Access: listing needs any admin; setting and resetting need an admin
//! that reaches every catalog (M11's rule for server-wide changes).

use std::sync::Arc;

use axum::extract::{Path, State};
use axum::routing::{get, put};
use axum::{Extension, Json, Router};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::app::App;
use crate::auth::Principal;
use crate::clock::format_timestamp;
use crate::error::OkfError;
use crate::http::api::{require_admin, require_every_catalog, settle};
use crate::http::AppError;
use crate::store::settings::{self, SettingKey, SettingRow};

/// One setting as the API shows it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct SettingView {
    /// Its snake_case key.
    pub key: &'static str,
    /// Its value now (the override, else the config default).
    pub value: String,
    /// Whether the database overrides the config file.
    pub overridden: bool,
    /// When it was last set, if it is overridden.
    pub updated_at: Option<String>,
    /// Who set it, if it is overridden.
    pub updated_by: Option<String>,
}

impl From<SettingRow> for SettingView {
    fn from(row: SettingRow) -> Self {
        let SettingRow {
            key,
            value,
            overridden,
            updated_at,
            updated_by,
        } = row;
        Self {
            key: key.as_str(),
            value,
            overridden,
            updated_at: updated_at.map(format_timestamp),
            updated_by,
        }
    }
}

/// One configured OIDC provider, without its secret.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct OidcProviderView {
    /// Its stable id.
    pub id: String,
    /// Its button text.
    pub label: String,
    /// Its issuer URL.
    pub issuer: String,
}

/// The mail provider, without any secret.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct MailView {
    /// `smtp`, `postmark` or `log`.
    pub provider: &'static str,
    /// The From address.
    pub from: String,
}

/// `GET /settings`' answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct SettingsView {
    /// Every setting, in the store's order.
    pub settings: Vec<SettingView>,
    /// The configured OIDC providers.
    pub oidc: Vec<OidcProviderView>,
    /// The mail provider.
    pub mail: MailView,
}

/// `PUT /settings/{key}`'s body.
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct SettingBody {
    /// The value, as the CLI takes it (`true`, `20`, `12h`, ...).
    value: String,
}

/// This area's routes.
pub(crate) fn routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    Router::new()
        .route("/settings", get(list_settings))
        .route("/settings/{key}", put(set_setting).delete(reset_setting))
}

/// The key named by a path segment.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::NotFound`] for an unknown key.
fn key_of(text: &str) -> Result<SettingKey, OkfError> {
    SettingKey::parse(text).ok_or_else(|| OkfError::NotFound {
        path: format!("settings/{text}"),
    })
}

/// One setting as it now is.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`OkfError::Database`]; [`OkfError::NotFound`] if the store has no row
/// for a key it defines (a bug).
async fn current(app: &App, key: SettingKey) -> Result<SettingView, OkfError> {
    settings::list(app.pool(), &app.config().auth)
        .await?
        .into_iter()
        .find(|row| row.key == key)
        .map(SettingView::from)
        .ok_or_else(|| OkfError::NotFound {
            path: format!("settings/{}", key.as_str()),
        })
}

/// `GET /settings`: every setting, the OIDC providers and the mail provider.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 below admin; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_settings(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<SettingsView>, AppError> {
    require_admin(&principal)?;
    let config = app.config();
    Ok(Json(SettingsView {
        settings: settings::list(app.pool(), &config.auth)
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(SettingView::from)
            .collect(),
        oidc: config
            .auth
            .oidc
            .iter()
            .map(|provider| OidcProviderView {
                id: provider.id.clone(),
                label: provider.label.clone(),
                issuer: provider.issuer.clone(),
            })
            .collect(),
        mail: MailView {
            provider: config.mail.provider.as_str(),
            from: config.mail.from.clone(),
        },
    }))
}

/// `PUT /settings/{key}`: overrides a setting.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown key; a 4xx for a value the setting refuses; 422 without `value`.
async fn set_setting(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(key): Path<String>,
    Json(body): Json<SettingBody>,
) -> Result<Json<SettingView>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let key = key_of(&key)?;
    settings::set(app.pool(), key, &body.value, &principal.actor, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(setting = key.as_str(), value = %body.value, key_id = %principal.key_id,
                   actor = %principal.actor, "setting changed");
    settle(&app).await;
    Ok(Json(current(&app, key).await?))
}

/// `DELETE /settings/{key}`: back to the config file's default.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 404 for an
/// unknown key.
async fn reset_setting(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(key): Path<String>,
) -> Result<Json<SettingView>, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    let key = key_of(&key)?;
    settings::reset(app.pool(), key).await?;
    tracing::info!(setting = key.as_str(), key_id = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor,
                   "setting reset");
    settle(&app).await;
    Ok(Json(current(&app, key).await?))
}
```

(`settings` writes log `key_id`, since the field `key` names the setting there.)

```rust
//! `/api/v1/mail` (spec "Background jobs: Visibility"): what `okf-mcp mail
//! ...` does. The queue shows recipients, templates, attempts and errors,
//! never a body (a setup or reset link is a secret).
//!
//! Access: listing needs any admin; queueing, retrying and deleting need
//! an admin that reaches every catalog.

use std::sync::Arc;

use axum::extract::{Path, State};
use axum::http::StatusCode;
use axum::routing::{delete, get, post};
use axum::{Extension, Json, Router};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::app::App;
use crate::auth::Principal;
use crate::clock::format_timestamp;
use crate::http::api::{require_admin, require_every_catalog};
use crate::http::AppError;
use crate::mail::queue::{self, QueuedMail};
use crate::mail::Template;

/// One queued mail, never its body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct QueuedMailView {
    /// The job's id (the `{id}` of the other routes).
    pub id: String,
    /// The recipient.
    pub to: String,
    /// `setup`, `reset`, `method_added` or `test`.
    pub template: String,
    /// `pending` or `failed`.
    pub status: String,
    /// Attempts so far.
    pub attempts: i32,
    /// The last provider error, if any.
    pub last_error: Option<String>,
    /// When it runs next (or ran last).
    pub run_at: String,
}

impl From<QueuedMail> for QueuedMailView {
    fn from(mail: QueuedMail) -> Self {
        let QueuedMail {
            id,
            to,
            template,
            status,
            attempts,
            last_error,
            run_at,
        } = mail;
        Self {
            id,
            to,
            template,
            status,
            attempts,
            last_error,
            run_at: format_timestamp(run_at),
        }
    }
}

/// `GET /mail/queue`'s answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub(crate) struct MailQueue {
    /// Pending and failed mail.
    pub mail: Vec<QueuedMailView>,
}

/// `POST /mail/test`'s body and answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub(crate) struct TestMail {
    /// The recipient.
    pub to: String,
}

/// This area's routes.
pub(crate) fn routes() -> Router<Arc<App>> {
    Router::new()
        .route("/mail/test", post(send_test))
        .route("/mail/queue", get(list_queue))
        .route("/mail/queue/{id}", delete(delete_mail))
        .route("/mail/queue/{id}/retry", post(retry_mail))
}

/// `POST /mail/test`: queues the test email.
///
/// # Returns
/// 202: the mail is queued, not yet sent.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; 422 without `to`.
async fn send_test(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Json(body): Json<TestMail>,
) -> Result<(StatusCode, Json<TestMail>), AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    queue::enqueue(app.pool(), &body.to, &Template::Test, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(to = %body.to, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor,
                   "test email queued");
    Ok((StatusCode::ACCEPTED, Json(body)))
}

/// `GET /mail/queue`: pending and failed mail.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 below admin; 500 for a database failure.
async fn list_queue(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
) -> Result<Json<MailQueue>, AppError> {
    require_admin(&principal)?;
    Ok(Json(MailQueue {
        mail: queue::list(app.pool())
            .await?
            .into_iter()
            .map(QueuedMailView::from)
            .collect(),
    }))
}

/// `POST /mail/queue/{id}/retry`: sends a failed mail again.
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; as
/// `mail::queue::retry` for an unknown or unretryable job.
async fn retry_mail(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    queue::retry(app.pool(), &id, app.clock().now()).await?;
    tracing::info!(mail = %id, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor, "mail retried");
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}

/// `DELETE /mail/queue/{id}`: deletes a queued mail.
///
/// # Returns
/// 204.
///
/// # Errors
/// 403 unless the caller is an admin reaching every catalog; as
/// `mail::queue::delete` for an unknown job.
async fn delete_mail(
    State(app): State<Arc<App>>,
    Extension(principal): Extension<Arc<Principal>>,
    Path(id): Path<String>,
) -> Result<StatusCode, AppError> {
    require_every_catalog(&principal)?;
    queue::delete(app.pool(), &id).await?;
    tracing::info!(mail = %id, key = %principal.key_id, actor = %principal.actor, "mail deleted");
    Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT)
}
```

Add a subsection after "Users and teams API":

```markdown
### Settings and mail API

The routes behind the Settings page, `okf-mcp settings ...` and `okf-mcp mail
...`. Reads need any admin; changes need an admin that reaches every catalog.

| Method and path | Key | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/settings` | admin | `{settings, oidc, mail}`: each setting's `key`, `value` (the effective value, as text), `overridden`, `updated_at`, `updated_by`; the OIDC providers' `id`, `label`, `issuer`; the mail `provider` and `from`. Never a secret |
| `PUT /api/v1/settings/{key}` | admin, every catalog | Body `{value}` (a string, as on the command line). Answers the setting. 404 for an unknown key, 4xx for an invalid value (the message names the key) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/settings/{key}` | admin, every catalog | Drops the override; answers the setting at its default |
| `POST /api/v1/mail/test` | admin, every catalog | Body `{to}`. Queues the test email; 202 `{to}` |
| `GET /api/v1/mail/queue` | admin | `{mail}`: pending and failed mail: `id`, `to`, `template`, `status` (`pending` or `failed`), `attempts`, `last_error`, `run_at`. Never a body |
| `POST /api/v1/mail/queue/{id}/retry` | admin, every catalog | Sends the mail again now, with a new 24-hour retry window; 204. 404 for an unknown id |
| `DELETE /api/v1/mail/queue/{id}` | admin, every catalog | Deletes pending or failed mail; 204 |
```

```rust
    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn set_admin_turns_the_flag_on_and_off_and_may_clear_the_last_admin() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        okf(&db, &["user", "create", "alice"]).await.unwrap();

        let on = okf(&db, &["user", "set-admin", "alice", "--on"]).await.unwrap();
        let again = okf(&db, &["user", "set-admin", "alice", "--on"]).await.unwrap();
        let listed = okf(&db, &["user", "list"]).await.unwrap();
        // alice is the only admin: the CLI may still clear it (Decision 16).
        let off = okf(&db, &["user", "set-admin", "alice", "--off"]).await.unwrap();
        let neither = okf(&db, &["user", "set-admin", "alice"]).await;
        let both = okf(&db, &["user", "set-admin", "alice", "--on", "--off"]).await;

        assert_eq!(off, "alice is no longer an admin\n");

        }
        sign_in_events::record(&db.pool, Some(&id), Method::Password, Outcome::Failed, None, Utc::now())
            .await
            .unwrap();

        let sessions = okf(&db, &["user", "sessions", "alice"]).await.unwrap();
        let sign_ins = okf(&db, &["user", "sign-ins", "alice"]).await.unwrap();
        let revoked = okf(&db, &["user", "revoke-sessions", "alice"]).await.unwrap();
        let none = okf(&db, &["user", "sessions", "alice"]).await.unwrap();

        assert_eq!(sessions.lines().count(), 2, "{sessions}");
        assert!(sessions.contains("\tip -\tBrowser One\n"), "{sessions}");
        assert!(sign_ins.contains("\tpassword\tfailed\tip -\n"), "{sign_ins}");
        assert_eq!(revoked, "revoked 2 sessions of alice\n");
        assert_eq!(none, "alice has no sessions\n");
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn set_member_access_reports_the_previous_level() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        okf(&db, &["catalog", "create", "notes", "--owner", TEST_USER]).await.unwrap();

        let read = okf(&db, &["catalog", "set-member-access", "notes", "--access", "read"])
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let none = okf(&db, &["catalog", "set-member-access", "notes", "--access", "none"])
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let unknown = okf(&db, &["catalog", "set-member-access", "nowhere", "--access", "read"]).await;

        assert_eq!(read, "catalog notes: member access write -> read\n");
        assert_eq!(none, "catalog notes: member access read -> none\n");
        assert!(unknown.is_err());
    }
```

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use chrono::Utc;
    use clap::Parser;

    use super::{mail, settings};
    use crate::cli::{Cli, Command, MailCommand, SettingsCommand};
    use crate::config::AuthConfig;
    use crate::db::test_db;
    use crate::store::settings::SettingKey;

    /// Parses `okf-mcp <args>` into its command.
    fn parse(args: &[&str]) -> Result<Command, clap::Error> {
        Cli::try_parse_from(std::iter::once(&"okf-mcp").chain(args))
            .map(|cli| cli.command.expect("a subcommand"))
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn settings_set_list_and_reset() {
        let db = test_db().await;
        let defaults = AuthConfig::default();

        let set = settings(
            &db.pool,
            &defaults,
            SettingsCommand::Set {
                key: SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser,
                value: "5".to_string(),
            },
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        let listed = settings(&db.pool, &defaults, SettingsCommand::List, Utc::now()).await.unwrap();
        let invalid = settings(
            &db.pool,
            &defaults,
            SettingsCommand::Set {
                key: SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser,
                value: "many".to_string(),
            },
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .await;
        let reset = settings(
            &db.pool,
            &defaults,
            SettingsCommand::Reset { key: SettingKey::MaxKeysPerUser },
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        let after = settings(&db.pool, &defaults, SettingsCommand::List, Utc::now()).await.unwrap();

        assert_eq!(set, "set max_keys_per_user to 5\n");
        assert!(listed.contains("max_keys_per_user\t5\tset by cli at "), "{listed}");
        assert!(listed.contains("password_sign_in\ttrue\tdefault\n"), "{listed}");
        assert!(invalid.is_err());
        assert_eq!(reset, "reset max_keys_per_user to its default\n");
        assert!(after.contains("max_keys_per_user\t20\tdefault\n"), "{after}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_setting_key_is_parsed_by_its_snake_case_name() {
        let parsed = parse(&["settings", "set", "max_key_lifetime", "30d"]);
        let unknown = parse(&["settings", "set", "max_keys", "5"]);

        assert!(matches!(
            parsed,
            Ok(Command::Settings(SettingsCommand::Set { key: SettingKey::MaxKeyLifetime, .. }))
        ));
        let message = unknown.expect_err("an unknown key").to_string();
        assert!(message.contains("max_keys_per_user"), "lists the keys: {message}");
    }

    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
    async fn mail_test_queue_retry_and_delete() {
        let db = test_db().await;

        let queued = mail(
            &db.pool,
            MailCommand::Test { address: "ops@example.com".to_string() },
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        let listed = mail(&db.pool, MailCommand::Queue, Utc::now()).await.unwrap();
        let id = crate::mail::queue::list(&db.pool).await.unwrap()[0].id.clone();
        // As a failed job looks once its retries are spent.
        sqlx::query("UPDATE apalis.jobs SET status = 'Killed' WHERE id = $1")
            .bind(&id)
            .execute(&db.pool)
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let retried = mail(&db.pool, MailCommand::Retry { id: id.clone() }, Utc::now()).await.unwrap();
        let deleted = mail(&db.pool, MailCommand::Delete { id: id.clone() }, Utc::now()).await.unwrap();
        let empty = mail(&db.pool, MailCommand::Queue, Utc::now()).await.unwrap();

        assert_eq!(queued, "queued a test email to ops@example.com\n");
        assert!(listed.contains("\tto ops@example.com\ttemplate test\t"), "{listed}");
        assert_eq!(retried, format!("requeued mail {id}\n"));
        assert_eq!(deleted, format!("deleted mail {id}\n"));
        assert_eq!(empty, "the mail queue is empty\n");
    }
}
```

```rust
/// `okf-mcp settings ...`.
#[derive(Debug, Subcommand)]
pub enum SettingsCommand {
    /// List every setting with its value and where it comes from.
    List,
    /// Override a setting (validated; a running server applies it within
    /// one poll interval).
    Set {
        /// The setting, by its snake_case name.
        #[arg(value_parser = parse_setting_key)]
        key: SettingKey,
        /// Its value (`true`, `20`, `12h`, `7d`, ...).
        value: String,
    },
    /// Remove an override, back to the config file's default.
    Reset {
        /// The setting.
        #[arg(value_parser = parse_setting_key)]
        key: SettingKey,
    },
}

/// `okf-mcp mail ...`.
#[derive(Debug, Subcommand)]
pub enum MailCommand {
    /// Queue the test email to an address.
    Test {
        /// The recipient.
        address: String,
    },
    /// List pending and failed mail (never the bodies).
    Queue,
    /// Send a failed mail again.
    Retry {
        /// Its id, from `mail queue`.
        id: String,
    },
    /// Delete a queued mail.
    Delete {
        /// Its id, from `mail queue`.
        id: String,
    },
}

/// Parses a setting key by its snake_case name, listing every key when the
/// name is unknown.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `text` - the argument.
///
/// # Returns
/// The key.
///
/// # Errors
/// A message naming the valid keys.
fn parse_setting_key(text: &str) -> Result<SettingKey, String> {
    SettingKey::parse(text).ok_or_else(|| {
        // `value_variants` is the ValueEnum list of every variant.
        let known: Vec<&str> = SettingKey::value_variants()
            .iter()
            .map(|key| key.as_str())
            .collect();
        format!("unknown setting {text:?}; one of {}", known.join(", "))
    })
}
```

```rust
/// Runs `okf-mcp catalog set-member-access`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the migrated database.
/// * `catalog` - the catalog's name.
/// * `access` - what the owning team's members may reach from now on.
///
/// # Returns
/// `catalog C: member access OLD -> NEW`.
///
/// # Errors
/// An unknown catalog, or a database error.
pub(super) async fn set_member_access(
    pool: &PgPool,
    catalog: &str,
    access: MemberAccess,
) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
    let previous = ceiling::set_member_access(pool, catalog, access).await?;
    Ok(format!(
        "catalog {catalog}: member access {} -> {}\n",
        previous.as_str(),
        access.as_str()
    ))
}

/// What `user set-admin` did, as one line.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `name` - the user.
/// * `previous` - the flag before.
/// * `on` - the flag asked for.
///
/// # Returns
/// The line, with its newline.
fn describe_admin_change(name: &str, previous: bool, on: bool) -> String {
    match (previous, on) {
        (false, true) => format!("{name} is now an admin\n"),
        (true, false) => format!("{name} is no longer an admin\n"),
        (true, true) => format!("{name} is already an admin\n"),
        (false, false) => format!("{name} is already not an admin\n"),
    }
}

/// One `user sessions` line, tab-separated: id prefix, `created T`,
/// `seen T`, `ip A` (`-` when unknown), then the free-text user agent last.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `session` - the session.
///
/// # Returns
/// The line, without a newline.
fn format_session(session: &SessionInfo) -> String {
    let ip = session.ip.map(|address| address.to_string());
    tab_row(&[
        &session.id_prefix,
        &format!("created {}", format_timestamp(session.created_at)),
        &format!("seen {}", format_timestamp(session.last_seen_at)),
        &labelled("ip", ip.as_deref()),
        &session.user_agent,
    ])
}

/// One `user sign-ins` line, tab-separated: time, method, outcome, `ip A`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `event` - the attempt.
///
/// # Returns
/// The line, without a newline.
fn format_sign_in(event: &SignInEvent) -> String {
    let ip = event.ip.map(|address| address.to_string());
    tab_row(&[
        &format_timestamp(event.at),
        event.method.as_str(),
        event.outcome.as_str(),
        &labelled("ip", ip.as_deref()),
    ])
}
```

```rust
//! `okf-mcp settings ...` and `okf-mcp mail ...`: the policy settings and
//! the mail queue (spec "Admin surface"). Like `people`, each handler
//! returns the text to print. Settings writes bump the administrative
//! generation (`store::settings`), so a running server applies them within
//! one poll interval. `mail test` only queues the job; a running server's
//! worker sends it.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use sqlx::PgPool;

use super::{labelled, tab_row, MailCommand, SettingsCommand};
use crate::clock::format_timestamp;
use crate::config::AuthConfig;
use crate::mail::queue::{self, QueuedMail};
use crate::mail::Template;
use crate::store::settings::{self, SettingRow};

/// Who the CLI records as having changed a setting: it has no principal.
const CLI_ACTOR: &str = "cli";

/// Runs `okf-mcp settings ...`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the migrated database.
/// * `defaults` - the config file's `[auth]` table.
/// * `command` - which settings subcommand.
/// * `now` - the time a `set` is recorded at.
///
/// # Returns
/// The text to print.
///
/// # Errors
/// A value the setting refuses, or a database error.
pub(super) async fn settings(
    pool: &PgPool,
    defaults: &AuthConfig,
    command: SettingsCommand,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
    Ok(match command {
        SettingsCommand::List => settings::list(pool, defaults)
            .await?
            .iter()
            .map(|row| format_setting(row) + "\n")
            .collect(),
        SettingsCommand::Set { key, value } => {
            settings::set(pool, key, &value, CLI_ACTOR, now).await?;
            format!("set {} to {value}\n", key.as_str())
        }
        SettingsCommand::Reset { key } => {
            settings::reset(pool, key).await?;
            format!("reset {} to its default\n", key.as_str())
        }
    })
}

/// Runs `okf-mcp mail ...`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `pool` - the migrated database (apalis's schema included).
/// * `command` - which mail subcommand.
/// * `now` - the server clock (a queued mail's start, Decision 11).
///
/// # Returns
/// The text to print.
///
/// # Errors
/// An unknown or unretryable job, or a database error.
pub(super) async fn mail(
    pool: &PgPool,
    command: MailCommand,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
    Ok(match command {
        MailCommand::Test { address } => {
            queue::enqueue(pool, &address, &Template::Test, now).await?;
            format!("queued a test email to {address}\n")
        }
        MailCommand::Queue => {
            let queued = queue::list(pool).await?;
            if queued.is_empty() {
                "the mail queue is empty\n".to_string()
            } else {
                queued.iter().map(|mail| format_mail(mail) + "\n").collect()
            }
        }
        MailCommand::Retry { id } => {
            queue::retry(pool, &id, now).await?;
            format!("requeued mail {id}\n")
        }
        MailCommand::Delete { id } => {
            queue::delete(pool, &id).await?;
            format!("deleted mail {id}\n")
        }
    })
}

/// One `settings list` line, tab-separated: key, value, then `default` or
/// `set by WHO at T`.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `row` - the setting.
///
/// # Returns
/// The line, without a newline.
fn format_setting(row: &SettingRow) -> String {
    let source = match (row.overridden, row.updated_by.as_deref(), row.updated_at) {
        (true, Some(by), Some(at)) => format!("set by {by} at {}", format_timestamp(at)),
        (true, _, _) => "set".to_string(),
        (false, _, _) => "default".to_string(),
    };
    let value = if row.value.is_empty() { "-" } else { row.value.as_str() };
    tab_row(&[row.key.as_str(), value, &source])
}

/// One `mail queue` line, tab-separated: id, `status S`, `attempts N`,
/// `to A`, `template T`, `run_at T`, then `error E` last (free text).
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `mail` - the queued job (never its body).
///
/// # Returns
/// The line, without a newline.
fn format_mail(mail: &QueuedMail) -> String {
    tab_row(&[
        &mail.id,
        &format!("status {}", mail.status),
        &format!("attempts {}", mail.attempts),
        &format!("to {}", mail.to),
        &format!("template {}", mail.template),
        &format!("run_at {}", format_timestamp(mail.run_at)),
        &labelled("error", mail.last_error.as_deref()),
    ])
}
```

```rust
//! Every admin subcommand for users, teams, assignment, sign-in, settings
//! and mail has a documented REST route and console control (users and
//! teams design, "Web console"; user login design, "Admin surface"): the
//! parity table in `docs/operations.md` lists each one, so the CLI, the API
//! and the console cannot drift apart unnoticed.
//!
//! The checks, all without a database or a server:
//! - every covered subcommand exists in the clap tree;
//! - every `user`, `team`, `settings` and `mail` subcommand is covered, so
//!   a new one fails until it is added to the table;
//! - each covered subcommand has a parity row whose REST cell names a route
//!   that `docs/operations.md`'s API reference documents, and whose console
//!   cell is not empty.
//!
//! (`tests/parity.rs` is a different test: the differential tests against
//! `okf.py`.)
```

```rust
/// The subcommands under parity, as `okf-mcp <path>`.
const COVERED: &[&str] = &[
    "user create",
    "user list",
    "user delete",
    "user set-admin",
    "user set-email",
    "user invite",
    "user entitle",
    "user unentitle",
    "user sessions",
    "user revoke-sessions",
    "user sign-ins",
    "team create",
    "team list",
    "team add-member",
    "team set-role",
    "team remove-member",
    "team delete",
    "catalog set-owner",
    "catalog set-member-access",
    "key assign",
    "oauth code assign",
    "unassigned",
    "settings list",
    "settings set",
    "settings reset",
    "mail test",
    "mail queue",
    "mail retry",
    "mail delete",
];

/// The command groups whose every subcommand must be covered.
const SCANNED_GROUPS: &[&str] = &["user", "team", "settings", "mail"];
```

```rust
#[test]
fn every_subcommand_of_the_scanned_groups_is_covered() {
    let cli = Cli::command();
    for group in SCANNED_GROUPS {
        let subcommands = cli
            .find_subcommand(group)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("`okf-mcp {group}` is not a subcommand"))
            .get_subcommands();
        for sub in subcommands {
            let path = format!("{group} {}", sub.get_name());
            assert!(
                COVERED.contains(&path.as_str()),
                "`okf-mcp {path}` is missing from COVERED (and the parity table)"
            );
        }
    }
```

### Task 14a: Console, user side: account sessions in the shell, and My keys

Task 7b already lets the console run on an account session: `api.js` sends a bearer only when a key is stored and otherwise `X-OKF-CSRF` (from `store.csrf`) on writes, `main.js` resumes a live cookie with `resumeSession()` and signs out over `DELETE /api/v1/session`, `#whoami` reads `alice - write` for a session, and the login card links to `/signin`. This task extends those files, it does not replace them: it keeps the whole session answer in `store.session` (beside 7b's `store.csrf`), makes `store.can` follow the ceiling's level on the selected catalog, factors 7b's header lines into an exported `authHeaders` (so uploads send the same credentials), turns 7b's link into the card's main "Sign in with your account" button with a `return_to`, and adds a "Your account" nav group with the My keys page. A pasted key still works and still wins. The Administer group stays hidden unless the person is an admin user. Task 14b adds My grants and Account.

Routes this task calls:

| Route | Defined in | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/session` (`{user, email, admin, csrf, ceiling: {catalog: level}, expires_at}`) | 7a | boot (7b's `resumeSession`), `refreshIdentity` |
| `DELETE /api/v1/session` | 7a | Sign out (7b's handler, unchanged) |
| `GET /api/v1/whoami` | existing (7a: `kind: "session"`) | the shell |
| `GET /api/v1/me` (`ceiling: [{catalog, access}]`, `limits: {max_keys_per_user, max_key_lifetime_secs}`) | 10a | My keys |
| `GET`/`POST /api/v1/me/keys`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/me/keys/{id}` | 10a | My keys |

- Modify: `src/http/ui/js/main.js` (7b's `resumeSession`, 401 handler, sign-out and key sign-in also keep `store.session`; `showLogin` sets the link's `return_to`)

```rust
    /// Waits until `selector`'s text no longer contains `gone` (an absent
    /// element has no text, so that counts too).
    ///
    /// # Arguments
    /// * `selector` - the element to watch.
    /// * `gone` - the text that must disappear.
    ///
    /// # Panics
    /// When the text is still there after [`WAIT`].
    pub fn wait_text_gone(&self, selector: &str, gone: &str) {
        self.poll(&format!("{selector} without {gone:?}"), || {
            !self.text(selector).contains(gone)
        });
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing self-service journeys.** Create `tests/ui_e2e/self_service.rs`:

```rust
//! The console signed in with an account (M12 Task 14a): password sign-in
//! from the login card's link, the "Your account" group and no Administer
//! group for a member, the full console for an admin user, sign-out ending
//! the server's session, and My keys: a key created within the ceiling
//! (its secret shown once), a key the ceiling no longer allows refused with
//! the reason, the key limit, rename and revoke. Task 14b adds My grants.
//!
//! The fixtures here (`login_server`, `console_base`, `member`, `PASSWORD`,
//! `EMAIL`) are shared with `account.rs` (Task 14b) and with `users.rs`,
//! `catalogs.rs` and `settings.rs` (Task 15).

use std::sync::Arc;

use chrono::Utc;
use okf_mcp::config::Config;
use okf_mcp::store::ceiling;
use okf_mcp::store::keys::{self as key_rows, Access, CatalogGrant, Grants, NewKey};
use okf_mcp::store::settings::{self, SettingKey};
use okf_mcp::store::users;
use serde_json::json;

use crate::catalogs::switcher;
use crate::harness::drive;
use crate::support::server::{files, TestServer};

/// alice's password in every journey: long enough, and not a common one.
pub(crate) const PASSWORD: &str = "correct horse battery staple";

/// alice's email in every journey.
pub(crate) const EMAIL: &str = "alice@example.com";

/// A server with login on, and two catalogs, `main` and `other`, both
/// owned by the fixture user's personal team (so alice reaches neither
/// through a team).
///
/// `public_url` names `localhost`, not `127.0.0.1`: a WebAuthn relying
/// party id must be a host name, and the session cookie belongs to the
/// host the browser used, so every journey that signs in opens the console
/// through [`console_base`].
///
/// # Returns
/// The running server.
pub(crate) async fn login_server() -> TestServer {
    TestServer::start_with(
        vec![
            ("main", files(&[("index.md", "# Main\n")])),
            ("other", files(&[("index.md", "# Other\n")])),
        ],
        |base| Config {
            public_url: Some(base.replace("127.0.0.1", "localhost")),
            ..Config::default()
        },
    )
    .await
}

/// The console's origin for journeys on a [`login_server`]: the server's
/// base with `localhost` for `127.0.0.1`. Chromium resolves `localhost`
/// to the loopback address itself.
///
/// # Returns
/// `http://localhost:<port>`.
pub(crate) fn console_base(server: &TestServer) -> String {
    server.base.replace("127.0.0.1", "localhost")
}

/// Makes alice, with [`EMAIL`] and [`PASSWORD`], entitled to `main` at
/// `access` (her whole ceiling), and reloads the key cache.
///
/// # Arguments
/// * `server` - a [`login_server`].
/// * `access` - her level on `main`: `Read` or `Write`.
///
/// # Panics
/// If a store call or the poll fails.
pub(crate) async fn member(server: &TestServer, access: Access) {
    server.user_with_password("alice", EMAIL, PASSWORD).await;
    ceiling::entitle(&server.db.pool, "alice", "main", access, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("entitle alice to main");
    server.app.poll().await.expect("poll");
}

/// Creates a self-issued key of alice's called `name`, with write on
/// `main`, as My keys would, and reloads the key cache.
async fn alices_key(server: &TestServer, name: &str) {
    let catalogs = ["main".to_string()];
    let levels = [CatalogGrant {
        catalog: "main".to_string(),
        access: Some(Access::Write),
    }];
    let new = NewKey {
        name,
        access: Access::Write,
        maintenance_report: false,
        grants: Grants::Catalogs(&catalogs),
        default_catalog: Some("main"),
        actor: name,
        user: "alice",
        self_issued: true,
        expires_at: None,
        levels: &levels,
    };
    key_rows::create(&server.db.pool, &new, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("create alice's key");
    server.app.poll().await.expect("poll");
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_member_signs_in_from_the_card_and_sees_only_their_pages() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    member(&server, Access::Write).await;
    drive(console_base(&server), |ui| {
        ui.open("");
        ui.wait_visible("#login");
        // The card's link comes back to this console.
        assert_eq!(
            ui.eval(
                "() => document.querySelector('#login-signin').getAttribute('href')",
                json!(null)
            ),
            json!("/signin?return_to=%2Fui%2F")
        );
        ui.sign_in_password(EMAIL, PASSWORD);
        ui.wait_text("#whoami", "alice");
        ui.wait_visible("a[data-nav=my-keys]");
        // (My grants and Account join the group in Task 14b: until their
        // pages exist, the manifest hides their links.)
        assert!(!ui.page.is_visible("[data-need=admin]").expect("visible"));
        // The switcher offers the ceiling's catalogs only.
        assert_eq!(switcher(ui), vec!["main".to_string()]);
        ui.click("#signout");
        ui.wait_visible("#login");
        // The server ended the session: a reload stays on the card.
        ui.open("");
        ui.wait_visible("#login");
        assert!(!ui.page.is_visible("#app").expect("visible"));
    })
    .await;
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn an_admin_user_signs_in_and_sees_the_full_console() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    member(&server, Access::Read).await;
    users::set_admin(&server.db.pool, "alice", true, false)
        .await
        .expect("make alice an admin");
    server.app.poll().await.expect("poll");
    drive(console_base(&server), |ui| {
        ui.sign_in_password(EMAIL, PASSWORD);
        ui.wait_text("#whoami", "admin");
        ui.wait_visible("[data-need=admin]");
        ui.wait_visible("a[data-nav=my-keys]");
        // An admin session reaches every catalog.
        assert_eq!(switcher(ui), vec!["main".to_string(), "other".to_string()]);
        ui.open("/users");
        ui.wait_text("[data-test=user-alice]", "you");
    })
    .await;
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_member_creates_a_key_within_the_ceiling_and_sees_its_secret_once() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    member(&server, Access::Write).await;
    let ran = drive(console_base(&server), |ui| {
        ui.sign_in_password(EMAIL, PASSWORD);
        ui.open("/my-keys");
        ui.wait_text("#my-keys-note", "0 of 20");
        ui.click("#my-key-new");
        ui.wait_visible("#my-key-form");
        // Only the ceiling's catalogs are offered.
        assert_eq!(
            ui.eval(
                "() => [...document.querySelectorAll('#my-key-form input[name=catalog]')] \
                 .map(input => input.value)",
                json!(null)
            ),
            json!(["main"])
        );
        ui.fill("#my-key-form input[name=name]", "laptop");
        ui.click("#my-key-form input[name=catalog][value=main]");
        ui.select("#my-key-form select[name=level-main]", "write");
        ui.select("#my-key-form select[name=expires_in]", "30d");
        ui.click("#my-key-form button[type=submit]");
        ui.wait_visible("#my-key-secret");
        assert!(ui.text("#my-key-secret").starts_with("okf_"));
        ui.click("#my-key-secret-done");
        ui.wait_hidden("#my-key-secret-dialog");
        ui.wait_text("[data-test=my-key-laptop]", "laptop");
        ui.wait_text("#my-keys-note", "1 of 20");
    })
    .await;
    if !ran {
        return;
    }
    let key = key_rows::list(&server.db.pool)
        .await
        .expect("list keys")
        .into_iter()
        .find(|record| record.name == "laptop")
        .expect("the key exists");
    assert!(key.self_issued);
    assert_eq!(key.user.as_deref(), Some("alice"));
    assert!(key.expires_at.is_some());
    assert_eq!(
        key.catalog_access.get("main").copied(),
        Some(Access::Write)
    );
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_key_the_ceiling_no_longer_allows_is_refused_and_names_the_limit() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    member(&server, Access::Write).await;
    let pool = server.db.pool.clone();
    let app = Arc::clone(&server.app);
    // The journey runs on a blocking thread; this handle lets it run the
    // admin's change on the test's runtime while the form is open.
    let runtime = tokio::runtime::Handle::current();
    drive(console_base(&server), move |ui| {
        ui.sign_in_password(EMAIL, PASSWORD);
        ui.open("/my-keys");
        ui.click("#my-key-new");
        ui.fill("#my-key-form input[name=name]", "too-much");
        ui.click("#my-key-form input[name=catalog][value=main]");
        ui.select("#my-key-form select[name=level-main]", "write");
        runtime.block_on(async {
            ceiling::unentitle(&pool, "alice", "main")
                .await
                .expect("take main away");
            app.poll().await.expect("poll");
        });
        ui.click("#my-key-form button[type=submit]");
        // Task 10a's 422 (`limit: "ceiling"`) says why.
        ui.wait_text("#toasts", "not among the catalogs you may use");
        // The form stays filled and no secret was shown.
        assert!(ui.page.is_visible("#my-key-form").expect("visible"));
        assert!(!ui.page.is_visible("#my-key-secret").expect("visible"));
    })
    .await;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Share the child filter, `fill` and `fact` in `core/dom.js`.** Replace the file:

```js
// DOM helpers. Data reaches the page only through h(), fill() and
// textContent, never innerHTML, so catalog text can never become markup.

export const $ = (selector, root = document) => root.querySelector(selector);

// Children as the DOM takes them: nested arrays flattened, null, undefined
// and false dropped, anything not a Node turned into text. The DOM's own
// append and replaceChildren print null as the text "null" (issue #302),
// so every conditional child goes through h() or fill(), never straight
// to the native methods.
function nodes(children) {
    return children
        .flat(Infinity)
        .filter(child => child !== null && child !== undefined && child !== false)
        .map(child => (child instanceof Node ? child : String(child)));
}

// h('a', { href: '#/x', class: 'nav', onclick: fn }, 'text', child, [more])
export function h(tag, attrs = {}, ...children) {
    const el = document.createElement(tag);
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(attrs ?? {})) {
        if (value === false || value === null || value === undefined) continue;
        if (name.startsWith('on') && typeof value === 'function') el.addEventListener(name.slice(2), value);
        else if (name === 'dataset') Object.assign(el.dataset, value);
        else el.setAttribute(name, value === true ? '' : String(value));
    }
    el.append(...nodes(children));
    return el;
}

// Replaces el's children, filtered as h() filters them. Returns el.
export function fill(el, ...children) {
    el.replaceChildren(...nodes(children));
    return el;
}

export function clear(el) {
    el.replaceChildren();
    return el;
}

// kind: ok | warn | error | info | muted
export function pill(text, kind = 'muted') {
    return h('span', { class: `pill pill-${kind}` }, text);
}

// One term and its value, for a <dl class="facts">.
export function fact(label, value) {
    return [h('dt', {}, label), h('dd', {}, value)];
}
```

```js
// The one time a secret is on screen: a modal that only the explicit
// button closes, after which the secret is removed from the page. Element
// ids start with `prefix` (`key-secret`, `code-secret-done`,
// `my-key-secret-dialog`, ...). The secret lives only in this dialog:
// never logged, never stored.
import { h } from '../core/dom.js';
import { toast } from '../core/toast.js';

export function showOnce({ prefix, title, warning, secret }) {
    let shown = secret; // dropped on close, so not even the copy handler keeps it
    const code = h('code', { id: `${prefix}-secret` }, shown);
    const copy = h('button', { type: 'button', id: `${prefix}-secret-copy`, class: 'secondary' }, 'Copy');
    const done = h('button', { type: 'button', id: `${prefix}-secret-done` }, 'I have stored it');
    const dialog = h('dialog', { id: `${prefix}-secret-dialog`, class: 'confirm' },
        h('article', {},
            h('h3', {}, title),
            h('p', { class: 'warn-text' }, warning),
            h('pre', { class: 'secret' }, code),
            h('footer', {}, copy, done)));
    copy.addEventListener('click', async () => {
        try {
            // navigator.clipboard exists only in secure contexts (https or localhost).
            await navigator.clipboard.writeText(shown);
            toast('Copied to the clipboard.', 'ok');
        } catch {
            toast('Copying failed: select the text and copy it by hand.', 'error');
        }
    });
    done.addEventListener('click', () => {
        shown = null;
        code.textContent = '';
        dialog.close();
        dialog.remove();
    });
    dialog.addEventListener('cancel', event => event.preventDefault()); // Escape does not close it
    document.body.append(dialog);
    dialog.showModal();
}
```

```js
// Access levels as the console shows them: the pill kinds, and a key's or
// grant's per-catalog levels.
import { h, pill } from '../core/dom.js';

export const ACCESS_KIND = { read: 'muted', write: 'info', admin: 'warn' };
const ORDER = ['read', 'write', 'admin'];

export function accessPill(access) {
    return pill(access, ACCESS_KIND[access]);
}

// A key's or grant's catalogs, from its `catalog_access` ({catalog: level},
// Task 2's KeyView). A self-issued one is capped at the account's
// `ceiling` ({catalog: level}, as GET /api/v1/session gives it): where the
// ceiling lowers a level, or no longer reaches the catalog, the cell says
// so (the server caps the credential at its next key reload). An
// admin-issued one keeps its levels.
export function levelsCell(credential, ceiling = {}) {
    const granted = Object.entries(credential.catalog_access ?? {});
    if (!granted.length) return '-';
    return h('ul', { class: 'level-list' }, granted.map(([catalog, access]) => {
        const allowed = credential.self_issued ? ceiling[catalog] : access;
        let note = null;
        if (!allowed) note = h('span', { class: 'muted small' }, ' (outside your ceiling now)');
        else if (ORDER.indexOf(allowed) < ORDER.indexOf(access)) note = h('span', { class: 'muted small' }, ` (capped to ${allowed})`);
        return h('li', { dataset: { catalog } }, h('span', { class: 'mono' }, catalog), ' ', accessPill(access), note);
    }));
}
```

```js
// Console sessions and sign-in history as tables: the Account page shows
// the signed-in person's (Task 14b), a user's drawer (Task 15) any user's.
import { h, pill } from '../core/dom.js';
import { ago, when } from '../core/format.js';
import { listTable } from './list-table.js';

const OUTCOME_KIND = { ok: 'ok', failed: 'warn', locked: 'error' };

// sessions: [{id_prefix, created_at, last_seen_at, ip, user_agent, current?}].
// Each row but the current one has a Sign out button calling revoke(row);
// `prefix` starts its data-test (`<prefix>-<id_prefix>`,
// `<prefix>-revoke-<id_prefix>`), and `allowed` false disables it.
export function sessionTable({ id, sessions, prefix, revoke, allowed = true }) {
    const table = listTable([
        { key: 'user_agent', label: 'Browser',
          render: row => h('span', { class: 'small', dataset: { test: `${prefix}-${row.id_prefix}` } },
              row.user_agent || 'unknown browser', row.current ? [' ', pill('this browser', 'info')] : null) },
        { key: 'ip', label: 'Address', class: 'mono', render: row => row.ip ?? '-' },
        { key: 'created_at', label: 'Signed in', sort: row => row.created_at, render: row => when(row.created_at) },
        { key: 'last_seen_at', label: 'Last seen', sort: row => row.last_seen_at, render: row => ago(row.last_seen_at) },
        { key: 'actions', label: '',
          render: row => row.current ? '-' : h('button', {
              type: 'button', class: 'text-btn', disabled: !allowed,
              dataset: { test: `${prefix}-revoke-${row.id_prefix}` }, onclick: () => revoke(row),
          }, 'Sign out') },
    ], sessions, { empty: 'No console sessions.' });
    table.id = id;
    return table;
}

// signIns: [{method, outcome, ip, at}], newest first.
export function signInTable({ id, signIns }) {
    const table = listTable([
        { key: 'at', label: 'When', sort: row => row.at, render: row => when(row.at) },
        { key: 'method', label: 'Method' },
        { key: 'outcome', label: 'Outcome', render: row => pill(row.outcome, OUTCOME_KIND[row.outcome]) },
        { key: 'ip', label: 'Address', class: 'mono', render: row => row.ip ?? '-' },
    ], signIns, { empty: 'No sign-ins yet.' });
    table.id = id;
    return table;
}
```

```js
export const CSRF_HEADER = 'X-OKF-CSRF';

// The credential headers for a `method` request, as Task 7b's `request`
// built them inline: the bearer `key` when there is one (a key wins over
// the cookie, on the server too); else, signed in by session, the CSRF
// token (`store.csrf`, Task 7b) on anything but a GET; else none. The
// session cookie goes by itself (same origin).
export function authHeaders(method, key = store.key) {
    if (key) return { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` };
    if (method !== 'GET' && store.csrf) return { [CSRF_HEADER]: store.csrf };
    return {};
}
```

```js
export async function refreshIdentity() {
    // Signed in with an account, the session (admin flag, ceiling, CSRF
    // token) is read again beside whoami: an admin may have changed it.
    const [session, me] = await Promise.all([
        store.session ? api.get('/session') : null,
        api.get('/whoami'),
    ]);
    if (session) {
        store.session = session;
        store.csrf = session.csrf;
    }
    store.whoami = me;
    // Task 7b's label: `alice - write` for a session, else
    // `alice / laptop - admin` (user / key - access).
    $('#whoami').textContent = me.kind === 'session'
        ? `${me.user} - ${me.access}`
        : `${me.user ? `${me.user} / ` : ''}${me.name ?? me.key_id} - ${me.access}`;
    document.querySelectorAll('[data-need]').forEach(el => { el.hidden = !shows(el.dataset.need); });
    if (!me.catalogs.includes(store.catalog)) {
        store.catalog = me.catalogs.includes(me.default_catalog) ? me.default_catalog : (me.catalogs[0] ?? null);
    }
    const select = $('#catalog-select');
    select.replaceChildren(...me.catalogs.map(name => h('option', { value: name }, name)));
    select.value = store.catalog ?? '';
}

// Whether an element marked data-need="<need>" shows: "session" for the
// account pages (signed in with an account, not a key), else an access
// level.
function shows(need) {
    return need === 'session' ? !!store.session : store.can(need);
}

// The account pages (My keys, My grants, Account) are for a person signed
// in with their account. Signed in by key, the page says so in a muted
// paragraph with this `id`. Returns whether the page may render.
export function requireSession(main, id) {
    if (store.session) return true;
    main.append(h('p', { class: 'muted', id },
        'This page is for people signed in with their account. Sign out, then sign in with your account to use it.'));
    return false;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Create `js/pages/my-keys.js`.** It uses Task 10a's routes as they are: `GET /api/v1/me` for the ceiling (`[{catalog, access}]`) and the limits, and `GET /api/v1/me/keys` for Task 2's `KeyView`s (`catalog_access`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`, `self_issued`). A key's state and its capped levels are worked out here from those fields.

```js
// My keys: the API keys that belong to the signed-in person. New key picks
// catalogs and read or write for each, all within the account's ceiling,
// and an expiry no longer than the longest allowed; the secret is shown
// once. Each key's drawer renames or revokes it. Keys an admin made for
// this user are listed too, uncapped. The server enforces the ceiling, the
// key limit and the lifetime limit (422, naming the limit); this page only
// offers what fits. Each drawer keeps the drawerTicket it was asked for, as
// on the API keys page.
import { h, pill, fact } from '../core/dom.js';
import { api, enc } from '../core/api.js';
import { store } from '../core/store.js';
import { toast } from '../core/toast.js';
import { drawerTicket } from '../core/drawer.js';
import { when } from '../core/format.js';
import { requireSession } from '../core/shell.js';
import { listTable } from '../components/list-table.js';
import { confirmDialog } from '../components/confirm.js';
import { showOnce } from '../components/secret.js';
import { levelsCell } from '../components/levels.js';

const LEVELS = ['read', 'write'];
const STATE_KIND = { active: 'ok', expired: 'muted', revoked: 'error' };
// Expiry choices: [the select's value, label, seconds].
const EXPIRIES = [
    ['7d', '7 days', 604800],
    ['30d', '30 days', 2592000],
    ['90d', '90 days', 7776000],
    ['365d', '1 year', 31536000],
];
// The select's value for "the longest allowed": sent as no expiry, which
// Task 10a turns into the `max_key_lifetime` limit itself.
const LONGEST = 'longest';

// A KeyView's state: revoked, expired (by its `expires_at`), or active.
function keyState(key) {
    if (key.revoked_at) return 'revoked';
    if (key.expires_at && Date.parse(key.expires_at) <= Date.now()) return 'expired';
    return 'active';
}

const COLUMNS = [
    { key: 'name', label: 'Name', sort: key => key.name,
      render: key => h('span', { class: 'key-name', dataset: { test: `my-key-${key.name}` } }, key.name) },
    { key: 'catalogs', label: 'Catalogs', render: key => levelsCell(key, store.session?.ceiling) },
    { key: 'default_catalog', label: 'Default', class: 'mono' },
    { key: 'created_at', label: 'Created', sort: key => key.created_at, render: key => when(key.created_at) },
    { key: 'expires_at', label: 'Expires', sort: key => key.expires_at ?? '9999',
      render: key => key.expires_at ? when(key.expires_at) : 'never' },
    { key: 'state', label: 'State', sort: keyState,
      render: key => h('span', { dataset: { test: `my-key-state-${key.name}` } }, pill(keyState(key), STATE_KIND[keyState(key)])) },
];

export async function render(main) {
    const head = h('header', { class: 'page-head' },
        h('div', {},
            h('h1', {}, 'My keys'),
            h('p', { class: 'muted' },
                'API keys that belong to you. Keys you create stay within your ceiling; a secret is shown once, when its key is created.')));
    main.append(head);
    if (!requireSession(main, 'my-keys-denied')) return;
    const create = h('button', { type: 'button', id: 'my-key-new', disabled: true }, 'New key');
    const note = h('p', { id: 'my-keys-note', class: 'muted small' });
    const showOld = h('input', { type: 'checkbox', id: 'my-keys-show-old' });
    const table = listTable(COLUMNS, [], { onRow: key => showKey(main, key, load), empty: 'You have no keys yet.' });
    table.id = 'my-keys-table';
    const applyFilter = () => table.setFilter(showOld.checked ? null : key => keyState(key) === 'active');
    showOld.addEventListener('change', applyFilter);
    applyFilter();
    head.append(h('div', { class: 'actions' }, create));
    main.append(note, h('label', { class: 'small muted' }, showOld, ' Show revoked and expired keys'), table);
    let account = null;
    create.addEventListener('click', () => newKey(main, account, load));

    async function load() {
        let keys;
        try {
            [account, { keys }] = await Promise.all([api.get('/me'), api.get('/me/keys')]);
        } catch { return; /* toasted */ }
        if (!main.isConnected) return;
        table.redraw(keys);
        // What `max_keys_per_user` counts: live self-issued keys.
        const live = keys.filter(key => key.self_issued && keyState(key) === 'active').length;
        const reason = createBlocker(account, live);
        create.disabled = !!reason;
        note.textContent = reason || `${live} of ${account.limits.max_keys_per_user} keys in use.`;
    }
    await load();
}

// Why New key is unavailable, or '' when it is not.
function createBlocker({ ceiling, limits }, live) {
    if (!ceiling.length) {
        return 'Your account reaches no catalog yet, so a key could reach nothing. Ask an admin for access.';
    }
    if (live >= limits.max_keys_per_user) {
        return `You have ${live} live keys, the most allowed. Revoke one first.`;
    }
    return '';
}

// The levels up to and including `access` (the ceiling's on a catalog).
function levelsUpTo(access) {
    return LEVELS.slice(0, LEVELS.indexOf(access) + 1);
}

// A lifetime in seconds, in words.
function lifetime(secs) {
    return secs % 86400 === 0 ? `${secs / 86400} days` : `${Math.round(secs / 3600)} hours`;
}

// The Expires options: "Never" and every choice when there is no limit;
// otherwise the choices within it, plus the limit itself (preselected),
// so the longest allowed is always on offer.
function expiryOptions({ max_key_lifetime_secs: longestSecs }) {
    if (longestSecs === null) {
        return [h('option', { value: '', selected: true }, 'Never'),
            ...EXPIRIES.map(([value, label]) => h('option', { value }, label))];
    }
    const fitting = EXPIRIES.filter(([, , secs]) => secs < longestSecs);
    return [...fitting.map(([value, label]) => h('option', { value }, label)),
        h('option', { value: LONGEST, selected: true }, `${lifetime(longestSecs)} (the longest allowed)`)];
}

// The body's `expires_at` (RFC 3339) for a choice, or null for "Never" and
// "the longest allowed" (Task 10a then applies the limit, if any).
function expiresAt(choice) {
    const entry = EXPIRIES.find(([value]) => value === choice);
    return entry ? new Date(Date.now() + entry[2] * 1000).toISOString() : null;
}

// The create form, in the drawer: one row per ceiling catalog, each a
// checkbox and a level select offering no more than the ceiling.
function newKey(main, account, reload) {
    if (!account) return;
    const ticket = drawerTicket(main);
    const rows = account.ceiling.map(({ catalog, access }) =>
        h('div', { class: 'inline-form', dataset: { test: `my-key-catalog-${catalog}` } },
            h('label', {},
                h('input', { type: 'checkbox', name: 'catalog', value: catalog }), ' ',
                h('span', { class: 'mono' }, catalog)),
            h('select', { name: `level-${catalog}`, 'aria-label': `Access to ${catalog}` },
                levelsUpTo(access).map(level => h('option', { value: level }, level)))));
    const form = h('form', { id: 'my-key-form' },
        h('label', {}, 'Name',
            h('input', { name: 'name', required: true, autocomplete: 'off', placeholder: 'letters, digits, . _ -' })),
        h('fieldset', {}, h('legend', {}, 'Catalogs, each read or write within your ceiling'), rows),
        h('label', {}, 'Default catalog',
            h('select', { name: 'default_catalog' },
                h('option', { value: '' }, 'None'),
                account.ceiling.map(({ catalog }) => h('option', { value: catalog }, catalog)))),
        h('label', {}, 'Expires', h('select', { name: 'expires_in' }, expiryOptions(account.limits))),
        h('button', { type: 'submit' }, 'Create key'));
    form.addEventListener('submit', async event => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const data = new FormData(form);
        const catalogs = data.getAll('catalog').map(String)
            .map(catalog => ({ catalog, access: String(data.get(`level-${catalog}`) ?? 'read') }));
        const defaultCatalog = String(data.get('default_catalog') ?? '') || null;
        if (!catalogs.length) {
            toast('Choose at least one catalog.', 'error');
            return;
        }
        if (defaultCatalog && !catalogs.some(entry => entry.catalog === defaultCatalog)) {
            toast('The default catalog must be one of the chosen catalogs.', 'error');
            return;
        }
        let created;
        try {
            // Task 10a's CreateKeyBody: {name, catalogs, default_catalog, actor, expires_at}.
            created = await api.post('/me/keys', {
                name: String(data.get('name') ?? '').trim(),
                catalogs,
                default_catalog: defaultCatalog,
                expires_at: expiresAt(String(data.get('expires_in') ?? '')),
            });
        } catch { return; /* toasted: the 422 says which limit; the form stays filled */ }
        // The secret is shown even after navigating away: it exists only now.
        ticket.close();
        showOnce({
            prefix: 'my-key',
            title: `Key ${created.key.name} created`,
            warning: 'Copy this key now. It is not stored anywhere and cannot be shown again.',
            secret: created.secret,
        });
        if (main.isConnected) await reload();
    });
    ticket.open('New key', 'The secret is shown once, right after creation.', form);
}

// One key's drawer: its facts, then Rename and Revoke while it is active.
// `ticket` is the drawer's claim; a re-render after a rename passes the one
// it was opened with.
function showKey(main, key, reload, ticket = drawerTicket(main)) {
    const base = `/me/keys/${enc(key.id)}`;
    const state = keyState(key);
    const facts = h('dl', { class: 'facts' },
        fact('Id', h('code', {}, key.id)),
        fact('Actor', h('code', {}, key.actor)),
        fact('Catalogs', levelsCell(key, store.session?.ceiling)),
        fact('Default', key.default_catalog ?? '-'),
        fact('Made by', key.self_issued ? 'you' : 'an admin (not capped by your ceiling)'),
        fact('Created', when(key.created_at)),
        fact('Expires', key.expires_at ? when(key.expires_at) : 'never'),
        fact('State', pill(state, STATE_KIND[state])),
        key.revoked_at ? fact('Revoked', when(key.revoked_at)) : null);
    if (state !== 'active') {
        ticket.open(key.name, `${state} key`, facts);
        return;
    }
    const name = h('input', { name: 'name', value: key.name, required: true, autocomplete: 'off', 'aria-label': 'New name' });
    const rename = h('form', { id: 'my-key-rename-form', class: 'inline-form' },
        name, h('button', { type: 'submit' }, 'Rename'));
    rename.addEventListener('submit', async event => {
        event.preventDefault();
        let updated;
        try { updated = await api.patch(base, { name: name.value.trim() }); } catch { return; /* toasted */ }
        toast(`Renamed ${key.name} to ${updated.name}.`, 'ok');
        if (main.isConnected) await reload();
        if (ticket.current()) showKey(main, updated, reload, ticket);
    });
    const revoke = h('button', {
        type: 'button', id: 'my-key-revoke', class: 'danger',
        onclick: async () => {
            const ok = await confirmDialog({
                title: `Revoke ${key.name}?`,
                message: 'Anything using this key is refused from its next request. This cannot be undone.',
                action: 'Revoke',
            });
            if (!ok) return;
            // Task 10a: DELETE /me/keys/{id} revokes (the row stays, revoked).
            try { await api.del(base); } catch { return; /* toasted */ }
            toast(`Revoked ${key.name}.`, 'ok');
            ticket.close();
            if (main.isConnected) await reload();
        },
    }, 'Revoke');
    ticket.open(key.name, 'Your key', facts,
        h('section', {}, h('h3', {}, 'Name'), rename),
        h('div', { class: 'drawer-actions' }, revoke));
}
```

### Task 14b: Console, user side: My grants and Account

The two remaining "Your account" pages, on top of Task 14a's session shell and shared components: **My grants** lists and revokes the signed-in person's OAuth grants, and **Account** shows the profile and the read-only ceiling, changes the password, adds (through Task 8's `createCredential`), renames and removes passkeys, links and unlinks OIDC identities, signs other console sessions out one at a time, and lists recent sign-ins. The server refuses removing the last sign-in method (409, toasted).

Routes this task calls:

| Route | Defined in | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/me` (`{user, display_name, email, admin, has_password, teams, ceiling: [{catalog, access}], session, password_sign_in, limits}`) | 10a | Account (profile, ceiling, password form) |
| `GET /api/v1/me/grants`, `DELETE /api/v1/me/grants/{id}` | 10a | My grants |
| `PUT /api/v1/me/password` (`{current_password, new_password, keep_sessions}`; 204, 403 for a wrong current password, 422 for the policy) | 10b | Account |
| `GET /api/v1/me/passkeys` (`{passkeys}`), `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys/{id}` | 10b | Account |
| `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/start` (`{name, keep_sessions}`), `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/finish` (the credential) | 8 | Account |
| `GET /api/v1/me/identities` (`{identities, providers}`), `DELETE /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}` | 10b | Account |
| `POST /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}/link` (`{keep_sessions}` -> `{url}`) | 9 | Account |
| `GET /api/v1/me/sessions` (`{sessions}`), `DELETE /api/v1/me/sessions/{id_prefix}` | 10b | Account |
| `GET /api/v1/me/sign-ins` (`{sign_ins}`) | 10b | Account |

```rust
//! The Account page (M12 Task 14b): changing the password (and signing in
//! with the new one), passkeys (rename, remove, and an add the browser
//! prompt cancels), signing out other sessions one at a time, unlinking an
//! identity, the read-only ceiling and recent sign-ins, and what a key sees.

use std::time::Duration;

use chrono::Utc;
use okf_mcp::store::keys::Access;
use okf_mcp::store::passwords::{self, SignInOutcome};
use okf_mcp::store::{identities, passkeys, user_sessions, users};
use serde_json::json;
use webauthn_authenticator_rs::prelude::WebauthnAuthenticator as _;
use webauthn_authenticator_rs::softpasskey::SoftPasskey;
use webauthn_rs::prelude::{Passkey, Url, Uuid, WebauthnBuilder};

use crate::harness::{drive, Ui};
use crate::self_service::{console_base, login_server, member, EMAIL, PASSWORD};

/// The password the first journey changes to.
const NEW_PASSWORD: &str = "a different long passphrase";

/// alice's user id, for the store calls that take one.
async fn alices_id(pool: &sqlx::PgPool) -> String {
    users::find_by_email(pool, EMAIL)
        .await
        .expect("find alice")
        .expect("alice exists")
        .id
}

/// A passkey for `user_id`, registered with `webauthn-rs`'s software
/// authenticator as the setup page would. Its relying party is
/// `localhost`; the Account page never checks a stored passkey's origin,
/// it only lists, renames and removes it.
fn soft_passkey(user_id: &str) -> Passkey {
    let origin = Url::parse("http://localhost").expect("origin");
    let webauthn = WebauthnBuilder::new("localhost", &origin)
        .expect("relying party")
        .rp_name("okf")
        .build()
        .expect("webauthn");
    let handle = Uuid::parse_str(user_id).expect("user ids are UUIDs");
    let (challenge, state) = webauthn
        .start_passkey_registration(handle, EMAIL, "alice", None)
        .expect("start registration");
    // `true`: report user verification, which passkeys require.
    let mut authenticator = SoftPasskey::new(true);
    let credential = authenticator
        .do_registration(origin, challenge)
        .expect("the authenticator registers");
    webauthn
        .finish_passkey_registration(&credential, &state)
        .expect("finish registration")
}

/// The `data-test` of the Sign out button on the session row whose text
/// contains `agent`, in `#session-table`.
fn revoke_button_of(ui: &Ui, agent: &str) -> String {
    let test = ui.eval(
        "(agent) => [...document.querySelectorAll('#session-table tbody tr')] \
         .find(row => row.textContent.includes(agent)) \
         ?.querySelector('button')?.dataset.test ?? null",
        json!(agent),
    );
    test.as_str()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("no session row for {agent:?}"))
        .to_string()
}

        // A cancelled browser prompt adds nothing and is not a script error.
```
