```rust
/// Inserts an OAuth grant of alice's, from consent signed in as her: read
/// on `main`, for a client called "Example Client". No store function
/// makes a grant without a consent round trip, so this writes the rows
/// itself and bumps the administrative generation so the poll sees it.
///
/// # Returns
/// The grant's id.
async fn alices_grant(server: &TestServer) -> String {
    let pool = &server.db.pool;
    let redirect_uris = ["https://client.example.com/callback".to_string()];
    let metadata = json!({ "redirect_uris": redirect_uris });
    let client = client_rows::insert_dcr(
        pool,
        &NewDcrClient {
            client_name: Some("Example Client"),
            redirect_uris: &redirect_uris,
            metadata: &metadata,
        },
        Utc::now(),
        MAX_UNBOUND_DCR,
    )
    .await
    .expect("register the client")
    .expect("under the cap");
    // `query_scalar` reads one column of one row, like `cursor.fetchone()[0]`.
    let id: String = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "INSERT INTO api_keys \
             (name, access, all_catalogs, actor, created_at, kind, client_id, user_id, self_issued) \
         SELECT 'example-client', 'read', false, 'Example Client', now(), 'oauth', $1, u.id, true \
         FROM users u WHERE u.name = 'alice' \
         RETURNING id",
    )
    .bind(&client.client_id)
    .fetch_one(pool)
    .await
    .expect("insert alice's grant");
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO key_catalogs (key_id, catalog_id, access) \
         SELECT $1, c.id, 'read' FROM catalogs c WHERE c.name = 'main'",
    )
    .bind(&id)
    .execute(pool)
    .await
    .expect("grant main");
    sqlx::query("UPDATE server_state SET admin_generation = admin_generation + 1")
        .execute(pool)
        .await
        .expect("bump the admin generation");
    server.app.poll().await.expect("poll");
    id
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `js/pages/my-grants.js`.** It lists Task 10a's `GET /api/v1/me/grants` (Task 2's `KeyView`s: `client_name`, `catalog_access`, `self_issued`, `revoked_at`) and revokes with `DELETE /api/v1/me/grants/{id}`.

```js
// My grants: the OAuth grants that let a client (a chat assistant, say)
// act as the signed-in person: those from consent signed in with the
// account, capped at the ceiling, and those from an admin's sign-in code.
// Each grant's drawer revokes it; the client is refused from its next
// request.
import { h, pill, fact } from '../core/dom.js';
import { api, enc } from '../core/api.js';
import { store } from '../core/store.js';
import { toast } from '../core/toast.js';
import { drawerTicket } from '../core/drawer.js';
import { when } from '../core/format.js';
import { requireSession } from '../core/shell.js';
import { listTable } from '../components/list-table.js';
import { confirmDialog } from '../components/confirm.js';
import { levelsCell } from '../components/levels.js';

// Where a grant came from.
const ORIGIN = grant => grant.self_issued ? 'your consent' : "an admin's sign-in code";

const COLUMNS = [
    { key: 'client_name', label: 'Client', sort: grant => grant.client_name ?? '',
      render: grant => h('span', { dataset: { test: `my-grant-${grant.name}` } }, grant.client_name ?? 'unknown client') },
    { key: 'catalogs', label: 'Catalogs', render: grant => levelsCell(grant, store.session?.ceiling) },
    { key: 'default_catalog', label: 'Default', class: 'mono' },
    { key: 'self_issued', label: 'From', render: ORIGIN },
    { key: 'created_at', label: 'Approved', sort: grant => grant.created_at, render: grant => when(grant.created_at) },
];

export async function render(main) {
    main.append(h('header', { class: 'page-head' },
        h('div', {},
            h('h1', {}, 'My grants'),
            h('p', { class: 'muted' }, 'OAuth clients you connected to your catalogs. Revoke one to disconnect it.'))));
    if (!requireSession(main, 'my-grants-denied')) return;
    const table = listTable(COLUMNS, [], { onRow: grant => showGrant(main, grant, load), empty: 'No OAuth grants.' });
    table.id = 'my-grants-table';
    // Revoked grants authenticate nothing; they stay in the admin's list.
    table.setFilter(grant => !grant.revoked_at);
    main.append(table);

    async function load() {
        try {
            const { grants } = await api.get('/me/grants');
            if (main.isConnected) table.redraw(grants);
        } catch { /* toasted */ }
    }
    await load();
}

function showGrant(main, grant, reload) {
    const ticket = drawerTicket(main);
    const revoke = h('button', {
        type: 'button', id: 'my-grant-revoke', class: 'danger',
        onclick: async () => {
            const ok = await confirmDialog({
                title: `Disconnect ${grant.client_name ?? 'this client'}?`,
                message: 'The client is refused from its next request, and its tokens stop working. This cannot be undone.',
                action: 'Revoke',
            });
            if (!ok) return;
            try { await api.del(`/me/grants/${enc(grant.id)}`); } catch { return; /* toasted */ }
            toast(`Revoked the grant for ${grant.client_name ?? 'that client'}.`, 'ok');
            ticket.close();
            if (main.isConnected) await reload();
        },
    }, 'Revoke');
    ticket.open(grant.client_name ?? 'unknown client', 'OAuth grant',
        h('dl', { class: 'facts' },
            fact('Id', h('code', {}, grant.id)),
            fact('Catalogs', levelsCell(grant, store.session?.ceiling)),
            fact('Default', grant.default_catalog ?? '-'),
            fact('From', ORIGIN(grant)),
            fact('Approved', when(grant.created_at)),
            fact('State', pill('active', 'ok'))),
        h('div', { class: 'drawer-actions' }, revoke));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `js/pages/account.js`.** Task 8 ships `src/http/ui/js/signin/webauthn.js`, whose `createCredential(challenge)` decodes the server's creation options, runs `navigator.credentials.create` and returns the credential encoded for JSON (it rejects with the browser's `DOMException` when the prompt is cancelled). The routes are Task 10a's `GET /api/v1/me`, Task 10b's password, passkey, identity, session and sign-in routes, Task 8's `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/start` and `/finish`, and Task 9's `POST /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}/link`.

```js
// Account: how the signed-in person signs in, and where. Profile and
// ceiling (read-only), password, passkeys (add, rename, remove), linked
// sign-in accounts (link, unlink), console sessions (sign another out)
// and recent sign-ins. Each section loads and redraws on its
// own, only while the page is shown. The server refuses removing the last
// sign-in method (409, toasted). Changing the password, adding a passkey
// or linking an account signs the other sessions out, unless "Keep me
// signed in elsewhere" is ticked.
import { h, fill, fact } from '../core/dom.js';
import { api, enc } from '../core/api.js';
import { toast } from '../core/toast.js';
import { ago, when } from '../core/format.js';
import { requireSession } from '../core/shell.js';
import { listTable } from '../components/list-table.js';
import { confirmDialog } from '../components/confirm.js';
import { accessPill } from '../components/levels.js';
import { sessionTable, signInTable } from '../components/activity.js';
import { createCredential } from '../signin/webauthn.js';

export async function render(main) {
    main.append(h('header', { class: 'page-head' },
        h('div', {},
            h('h1', {}, 'Account'),
            h('p', { class: 'muted' }, 'How you sign in, where you are signed in, and what your account may reach.'))));
    if (!requireSession(main, 'account-denied')) return;
    const profile = section('account-profile', 'Profile');
    const ceiling = section('account-ceiling', 'Your ceiling',
        'The most a key or OAuth grant you create can reach: the catalogs of your teams, at each catalog\'s '
        + 'member access, and the catalogs an admin entitled you to; where both apply, the higher level. '
        + 'An admin changes it.');
    const password = section('account-password', 'Password');
    const passkeys = section('account-passkeys', 'Passkeys', 'Sign in with your device instead of a password.');
    const identities = section('account-identities', 'Linked accounts', 'Sign in through another identity provider.');
    const sessions = section('account-sessions', 'Where you are signed in');
    const signIns = section('account-sign-ins', 'Recent sign-ins');
    main.append(profile.el, ceiling.el, password.el, passkeys.el, identities.el, sessions.el, signIns.el);

    async function drawAccount() {
        let account;
        try { account = await api.get('/me'); } catch { return; }
        if (!main.isConnected) return;
        fill(profile.body, h('dl', { class: 'facts', id: 'account-facts' },
            fact('Name', h('code', {}, account.user)),
            fact('Display name', account.display_name || '-'),
            fact('Email', account.email ?? 'none'),
            fact('Teams', account.teams.length ? account.teams.join(', ') : '-'),
            fact('Admin', account.admin ? 'yes: you sign in to the full console' : 'no')));
        const table = listTable([
            { key: 'catalog', label: 'Catalog', sort: row => row.catalog,
              render: row => h('code', { dataset: { test: `ceiling-${row.catalog}` } }, row.catalog) },
            { key: 'access', label: 'Access', render: row => accessPill(row.access) },
        ], account.ceiling, { empty: 'Your account reaches no catalog yet. Ask an admin.' });
        table.id = 'ceiling-table';
        fill(ceiling.body, table);
        fill(password.body, passwordForm(account));
    }

    function passwordForm(account) {
        const form = h('form', { id: 'password-form' },
            account.password_sign_in ? null : h('p', { class: 'muted small', id: 'password-sign-in-off' },
                'Password sign-in is turned off on this server: a password works once an admin turns it back on.'),
            account.has_password
                ? h('label', {}, 'Current password',
                    h('input', { type: 'password', name: 'current', required: true, autocomplete: 'current-password' }))
                : h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, 'You have no password yet. Set one to sign in with your email.'),
            h('label', {}, 'New password',
                h('input', { type: 'password', name: 'password', required: true, minlength: '12', autocomplete: 'new-password' })),
            h('label', {}, 'Repeat the new password',
                h('input', { type: 'password', name: 'confirm', required: true, minlength: '12', autocomplete: 'new-password' })),
            h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, 'At least 12 characters, and not a common password.'),
            keepSessionsBox('password-keep-sessions'),
            h('button', { type: 'submit' }, account.has_password ? 'Change password' : 'Set password'));
        form.addEventListener('submit', async event => {
            event.preventDefault();
            const data = new FormData(form);
            const next = String(data.get('password') ?? '');
            if (next !== String(data.get('confirm') ?? '')) {
                toast('The two new passwords differ.', 'error');
                return;
            }
            try {
                // Task 10b's PasswordBody; a wrong current password is 403.
                await api.put('/me/password', {
                    current_password: account.has_password ? String(data.get('current') ?? '') : null,
                    new_password: next,
                    keep_sessions: data.get('keep_sessions') === 'on',
                });
            } catch { return; /* toasted: a wrong current password (403) or the policy (422) */ }
            toast(account.has_password ? 'Password changed.' : 'Password set.', 'ok');
            await Promise.all([drawAccount(), drawSessions()]);
        });
        return form;
    }

    async function drawPasskeys() {
        let list;
        try { ({ passkeys: list } = await api.get('/me/passkeys')); } catch { return; }
        if (!main.isConnected) return;
        const name = h('input', { id: 'passkey-name', 'aria-label': 'A name for the new passkey',
                                  placeholder: 'a name, such as laptop', autocomplete: 'off' });
        const keep = keepSessionsBox('passkey-keep-sessions');
        const add = h('button', { type: 'button', id: 'passkey-add' }, 'Add a passkey');
        add.addEventListener('click', async () => {
            add.disabled = true;
            try {
                await addPasskey(name.value.trim() || 'passkey', keep.querySelector('input').checked);
            } finally {
                add.disabled = false;
            }
        });
        fill(passkeys.body,
            h('ul', { class: 'grant-list', id: 'passkey-list' },
                list.length ? list.map(passkeyRow) : h('li', { class: 'muted' }, 'No passkeys yet.')),
            h('div', { class: 'inline-form' }, name, add),
            keep);
    }

    function passkeyRow(passkey) {
        const base = `/me/passkeys/${enc(passkey.id)}`;
        const label = h('input', { value: passkey.name, autocomplete: 'off', 'aria-label': `New name for ${passkey.name}` });
        const rename = async () => {
            const next = label.value.trim();
            if (!next || next === passkey.name) return;
            try { await api.patch(base, { name: next }); } catch { return; }
            toast(`Renamed passkey ${passkey.name} to ${next}.`, 'ok');
            if (main.isConnected) await drawPasskeys();
        };
        const remove = async () => {
            const ok = await confirmDialog({
                title: `Remove passkey ${passkey.name}?`,
                message: 'You can no longer sign in with it. Remove it from the device too.',
                action: 'Remove',
            });
            if (!ok) return;
            try { await api.del(base); } catch { return; /* toasted: 409 for the last sign-in method */ }
            toast(`Removed passkey ${passkey.name}.`, 'ok');
            if (main.isConnected) await drawPasskeys();
        };
        return h('li', { dataset: { test: `passkey-${passkey.name}` } },
            label,
            h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'secondary', dataset: { test: `passkey-rename-${passkey.name}` }, onclick: rename }, 'Rename'),
            h('span', { class: 'muted small' },
                `added ${when(passkey.created_at)}, last used ${passkey.last_used_at ? ago(passkey.last_used_at) : 'never'}`),
            h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'text-btn', dataset: { test: `passkey-remove-${passkey.name}` }, onclick: remove }, 'Remove'));
    }

    // Registration (Task 8): the server's challenge (start takes the name
    // and the keep-sessions choice, and sets the ceremony cookie), the
    // browser's prompt, then the credential back to the server. A cancelled
    // or timed-out prompt is a toast, never a script error.
    async function addPasskey(name, keep) {
        let challenge;
        try {
            challenge = await api.post('/me/passkeys/register/start', { name, keep_sessions: keep });
        } catch { return; }
        let credential;
        try {
            credential = await createCredential(challenge);
        } catch (error) {
            toast(error?.name === 'NotAllowedError'
                ? 'No passkey was added: the browser prompt was cancelled or timed out.'
                : `No passkey was added: ${error?.message ?? error}`, 'error');
            return;
        }
        try { await api.post('/me/passkeys/register/finish', credential); } catch { return; }
        toast(`Added passkey ${name}.`, 'ok');
        if (main.isConnected) await Promise.all([drawPasskeys(), drawSessions()]);
    }

    async function drawIdentities() {
        let linked;
        let providers;
        try { ({ identities: linked, providers } = await api.get('/me/identities')); } catch { return; }
        if (!main.isConnected) return;
        const label = id => providers.find(provider => provider.id === id)?.label ?? id;
        const held = new Set(linked.map(identity => identity.provider));
        const keep = keepSessionsBox('identity-keep-sessions');
        fill(identities.body,
            h('ul', { class: 'grant-list', id: 'identity-list' }, linked.length
                ? linked.map(identity => h('li', { dataset: { test: `identity-${identity.provider}` } },
                    h('strong', {}, label(identity.provider)), ' ',
                    h('span', { class: 'mono small' }, identity.email_at_link),
                    h('span', { class: 'muted small' }, ` linked ${when(identity.created_at)}`),
                    h('button', {
                        type: 'button', class: 'text-btn', dataset: { test: `identity-unlink-${identity.provider}` },
                        onclick: () => unlink(identity.provider, label(identity.provider)),
                    }, 'Unlink')))
                : h('li', { class: 'muted' }, 'No linked accounts.')),
            providers.filter(provider => !held.has(provider.id)).map(provider => h('button', {
                type: 'button', class: 'secondary', dataset: { test: `identity-link-${provider.id}` },
                onclick: () => link(provider.id, keep.querySelector('input').checked),
            }, `Link ${provider.label}`)),
            providers.length ? keep : h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, 'This server has no sign-in providers configured.'));
    }

    // Linking leaves the console (Task 9): the server answers where to send
    // the browser (`{url}`, the provider's sign-in page, with the flow
    // cookie set), and its callback comes back to /ui/#/account.
    async function link(provider, keep) {
        let answer;
        try {
            answer = await api.post(`/me/identities/${enc(provider)}/link`, { keep_sessions: keep });
        } catch { return; }
        location.assign(answer.url);
    }

    async function unlink(provider, name) {
        const ok = await confirmDialog({
            title: `Unlink ${name}?`,
            message: `You can no longer sign in through ${name} until you link it again.`,
            action: 'Unlink',
        });
        if (!ok) return;
        try { await api.del(`/me/identities/${enc(provider)}`); } catch { return; /* toasted: 409 for the last method */ }
        toast(`Unlinked ${name}.`, 'ok');
        if (main.isConnected) await drawIdentities();
    }

    async function drawSessions() {
        let list;
        try { ({ sessions: list } = await api.get('/me/sessions')); } catch { return; }
        if (!main.isConnected) return;
        // One Sign out per other session (Task 10b has no "all others" route;
        // the current session signs out with the shell's Sign out).
        fill(sessions.body,
            sessionTable({
                id: 'session-table', prefix: 'session', sessions: list,
                revoke: async entry => {
                    try { await api.del(`/me/sessions/${enc(entry.id_prefix)}`); } catch { return; }
                    toast('Signed that session out.', 'ok');
                    if (main.isConnected) await drawSessions();
                },
            }));
    }

    async function drawSignIns() {
        let list;
        try { ({ sign_ins: list } = await api.get('/me/sign-ins')); } catch { return; }
        if (main.isConnected) fill(signIns.body, signInTable({ id: 'sign-in-table', signIns: list }));
    }

    await Promise.all([drawAccount(), drawPasskeys(), drawIdentities(), drawSessions(), drawSignIns()]);
}

// A titled section of the page and the body its draw function fills.
function section(id, title, intro = null) {
    const body = h('div', { class: 'account-body' });
    const el = h('section', { id, class: 'account-section' },
        h('h2', {}, title), intro ? h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, intro) : null, body);
    return { el, body };
}

// The "keep my other sessions" box: unticked, a new sign-in method signs
// every other session out.
function keepSessionsBox(id) {
    return h('label', { class: 'small' },
        h('input', { type: 'checkbox', id, name: 'keep_sessions' }), ' Keep me signed in elsewhere');
}
```

### Task 15: Console, admin side: user sign-in controls, member access, Settings

The admin controls for everything Task 12's REST routes and Task 13's CLI do: in a user's drawer the admin flag, the email, Send setup email, entitlements, the user's console sessions and recent sign-ins; in a catalog's drawer the team member access; and a new Settings page with the policy settings, the read-only OIDC providers and mail provider, Send test email and the mail queue. As in M11, any admin reads these; changing them needs an admin that reaches every catalog (`canAdministerPeople()`), and for any other admin the controls render disabled with the reason.

Routes this task calls (all defined in Task 12, with the shapes Task 12 documents in `docs/operations.md`):

| Route | Control |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/users`, `GET /api/v1/users/{name}` (users gain `email`, `admin`, `has_password`; the detail gains `entitlements: [{catalog, access, created_at}]`) | Users list and drawer |
| `PUT /api/v1/users/{name}/admin` (`{admin}` -> `{name, previous, admin}`) | Admin toggle |
| `PUT /api/v1/users/{name}/email` | Email field, Clear |
| `POST /api/v1/users/{name}/invite` (202 `{name, email}`) | Send setup email |
| `PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/users/{name}/entitlements/{catalog}` (`{access}` -> `{name, entitlements}`) | Entitlements |
| `GET /api/v1/users/{name}/sessions`, `DELETE /api/v1/users/{name}/sessions`, `DELETE /api/v1/users/{name}/sessions/{id_prefix}` | Sessions |
| `GET /api/v1/users/{name}/sign-ins` | Recent sign-ins |
| `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/catalogs/{catalog}/member-access` (`{name, member_access}`; `PUT` `{access}` -> `{name, previous, member_access}`) | Team member access, in the catalog's drawer |
| `GET /api/v1/settings` (`{settings: [{key, value, overridden, updated_at, updated_by}], oidc, mail: {provider, from}}`), `PUT`/`DELETE /api/v1/settings/{key}` | Settings → Policy |
| `POST /api/v1/mail/test` (`{to}`, 202) | Settings → Send test email |
| `GET /api/v1/mail/queue` (`{mail}`), `POST /api/v1/mail/queue/{id}/retry`, `DELETE /api/v1/mail/queue/{id}` (both 204) | Settings → Mail queue |

```rust
use std::time::Duration;
```

```rust
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn an_admin_sets_an_email_and_the_admin_flag_and_sends_a_setup_email() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    let admin = server.key("console-admin", Access::Admin, &[], None).await;
    let user = NewUser {
        name: "alice",
        display_name: "",
    };
    users::create(&server.db.pool, &user, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("create alice");
    server.app.poll().await.expect("poll");
    let ran = drive(console_base(&server), move |ui| {
        ui.login(&admin);
        ui.open("/users");
        ui.click("[data-test=user-alice]");
        // No email yet: no setup email either, and the reason is given.
        ui.wait_visible("#user-invite[disabled]");
        ui.wait_text("#user-invite-reason", "Set an email first");
        ui.fill("#user-email-form input[name=email]", EMAIL);
        ui.click("#user-email-form button[type=submit]");
        ui.wait_visible("#user-invite:not([disabled])");
        ui.wait_text("[data-test=user-alice-email]", EMAIL);
        ui.click("#user-invite");
        ui.wait_text("#toasts", "Queued a setup email");
        ui.click("#user-admin-toggle");
        ui.wait_text("#toasts", "alice is now an admin");
        ui.wait_visible("#user-admin-toggle:checked");
        ui.wait_text("[data-test=user-alice]", "admin");
        // A full admin key gets no "needs every catalog" note, and the
        // drawer carries no stray "null" (issue #302's pattern).
        assert!(!ui.text("#user-detail").contains("null"));
    })
    .await;
    if !ran {
        return;
    }
    let alice = users::find_by_email(&server.db.pool, EMAIL)
        .await
        .expect("find")
        .expect("alice has the email");
    assert!(alice.is_admin);
    // The setup mail was queued (or already sent: finished jobs stay for a
    // week), addressed to alice.
    let queued: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT count(*) FROM apalis.jobs \
         WHERE convert_from(job, 'UTF8')::jsonb->>'to' = $1",
    )
    .bind(EMAIL)
    .fetch_one(&server.db.pool)
    .await
    .expect("count mail jobs");
    assert_eq!(queued, 1);
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn an_admin_entitles_catalogs_and_the_member_sees_them() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    // alice exists with a password, but reaches nothing yet.
    server.user_with_password("alice", EMAIL, PASSWORD).await;
    let admin = server.key("console-admin", Access::Admin, &[], None).await;
    let ran = drive(console_base(&server), move |ui| {
        ui.login(&admin);
        ui.open("/users");
        ui.click("[data-test=user-alice]");
        ui.wait_text("#entitlement-list", "No entitlements");
        ui.select("#entitlement-form select[name=catalog]", "main");
        ui.select("#entitlement-form select[name=access]", "read");
        ui.click("#entitlement-form button[type=submit]");
        ui.wait_visible("[data-test=entitlement-main]");
        ui.select("#entitlement-form select[name=catalog]", "other");
        ui.select("#entitlement-form select[name=access]", "read");
        ui.click("#entitlement-form button[type=submit]");
        ui.wait_visible("[data-test=entitlement-other]");
        // Change a level in place, then remove the other entitlement.
        ui.select("[data-test=entitlement-level-other]", "write");
        ui.wait_text("#toasts", "write on other");
        ui.click("[data-test=entitlement-remove-main]");
        ui.wait_hidden("[data-test=entitlement-main]");
        ui.click("#drawer-close");
        ui.click("#signout");
        ui.wait_visible("#login");
        // alice sees exactly what she was entitled to.
        ui.sign_in_password(EMAIL, PASSWORD);
        ui.wait_text("#whoami", "alice");
        assert_eq!(switcher(ui), vec!["other".to_string()]);
        // My keys (Task 14a) offers exactly the ceiling, at its levels.
        ui.open("/my-keys");
        ui.click("#my-key-new");
        ui.wait_visible("#my-key-form");
        assert_eq!(
            ui.eval(
                "() => [...document.querySelectorAll('#my-key-form select[name=level-other] option')] \
                 .map(option => option.value)",
                serde_json::json!(null)
            ),
            serde_json::json!(["read", "write"])
        );
    })
    .await;
    if !ran {
        return;
    }
    let entitlements = ceiling::entitlements(&server.db.pool, "alice")
        .await
        .expect("entitlements");
    assert_eq!(entitlements.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(entitlements[0].catalog, "other");
    assert_eq!(entitlements[0].access, Access::Write);
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn an_admin_signs_a_user_out_and_sees_their_sign_ins() {
    let server = login_server().await;
    member(&server, Access::Write).await;
    let admin = server.key("console-admin", Access::Admin, &[], None).await;
    let pool = &server.db.pool;
    let alice = users::find_by_email(pool, EMAIL)
        .await
        .expect("find")
        .expect("alice");
    for agent in ["phone browser", "tablet browser"] {
        user_sessions::create(
            pool,
            &alice.id,
            None,
            agent,
            Duration::from_secs(7 * 86_400),
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .await
        .expect("a session of alice's");
    }
    sign_in_events::record(
        pool,
        Some(&alice.id),
        Method::Password,
        Outcome::Failed,
        None,
        Utc::now(),
    )
    .await
    .expect("record a failed sign-in");
    let ran = drive(console_base(&server), move |ui| {
        ui.login(&admin);
        ui.open("/users");
        ui.click("[data-test=user-alice]");
        ui.wait_text("#user-session-table", "phone browser");
        ui.wait_text("#user-sign-in-table", "failed");
        // One session, by its own button.
        let phone = ui.eval(
            "() => [...document.querySelectorAll('#user-session-table tbody tr')] \
             .find(row => row.textContent.includes('phone browser')) \
             ?.querySelector('button')?.dataset.test ?? null",
            serde_json::json!(null),
        );
        let phone = phone.as_str().expect("a revoke button").to_string();
        ui.click(&format!("[data-test={phone}]"));
        ui.wait_text_gone("#user-session-table", "phone browser");
        // Then the rest.
        ui.click("#user-sessions-revoke-all");
        ui.click("#confirm-ok");
        ui.wait_text("#user-session-table", "No console sessions");
    })
    .await;
    if !ran {
        return;
    }
    let left = user_sessions::list(pool, &alice.id, None)
        .await
        .expect("list");
    assert!(left.is_empty());
}
```

```rust
//! The Settings page (M12 Task 15): a policy override and its reset, a
//! refused value, the read-only mail provider, Send test email, and the
//! mail queue's Retry and Delete; what a scoped admin and a member see.

use chrono::Utc;
use okf_mcp::config::AuthConfig;
use okf_mcp::mail::queue;
use okf_mcp::mail::Template;
use okf_mcp::store::keys::Access;
use okf_mcp::store::settings::{self, SettingKey};
use serde_json::json;

use crate::harness::{drive, Ui};
use crate::self_service::{console_base, login_server, member, EMAIL, PASSWORD};
use crate::support::server::TestServer;

/// Queues a test mail to `to`, then marks it failed for good (apalis's
/// `Killed`, which no worker fetches again) with an SMTP error, as a
/// permanent provider refusal would.
///
/// # Returns
/// The job's id, as the queue lists it.
async fn failed_mail(server: &TestServer, to: &str) -> String {
    let pool = &server.db.pool;
    queue::enqueue(pool, to, &Template::Test, Utc::now())
        .await
        .expect("queue a mail");
    sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE apalis.jobs \
         SET status = 'Killed', attempts = 1, done_at = now(), \
             last_result = '{\"Err\": \"550 mailbox unavailable\"}'::jsonb \
         WHERE convert_from(job, 'UTF8')::jsonb->>'to' = $1",
    )
    .bind(to)
    .execute(pool)
    .await
    .expect("fail the mail");
    queue::list(pool)
        .await
        .expect("list the queue")
        .into_iter()
        .find(|mail| mail.to == to)
        .expect("the failed mail is listed")
        .id
}

/// Waits until the queue row's status cell no longer reads "failed" (the
/// retried job is pending, or already sent and gone).
fn wait_not_failed(ui: &Ui, id: &str) {
    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(10);
    loop {
        let status = ui.eval(
            "(id) => document.querySelector(`[data-test=mail-status-${id}]`)?.textContent ?? 'gone'",
            json!(id),
        );
        if status != json!("failed") {
            return;
        }
        assert!(std::time::Instant::now() < deadline, "the mail stayed failed");
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));
    }
}

    let server = login_server().await;

        ui.wait_text(&format!("[data-test=mail-error-{retried}]"), "550");
        ui.click(&format!("[data-test=mail-retry-{retried}]"));
        ui.wait_text("#toasts", "bob@example.com");

        ui.click(&format!("[data-test=mail-delete-{deleted}]"));
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create `js/components/user-account.js`.**

```js
// The account parts of a user's drawer (M12): sign-in (email, admin flag,
// Send setup email), entitlements (catalogs beyond the user's teams'), the
// user's console sessions, and recent sign-ins. Any admin reads them; every change needs an admin that
// reaches every catalog (`manager`), and for any other admin the controls
// render disabled. Each action toasts the server's answer and then calls
// `changed()`, which reloads the users table and re-renders the drawer
// while its ticket is current, so every control shows the server's state
// again (a refused admin toggle springs back).
import { h, fact } from '../core/dom.js';
import { api, enc } from '../core/api.js';
import { toast } from '../core/toast.js';
import { count } from '../core/format.js';
import { confirmDialog } from './confirm.js';
import { picker } from './picker.js';
import { sessionTable, signInTable } from './activity.js';

const LEVELS = ['read', 'write'];

// What the account sections show beyond GET /users/{name}: the sessions,
// the sign-ins and the catalog names an entitlement may name. Throws the
// toasted ApiError on failure.
export async function loadAccount(name) {
    const base = `/users/${enc(name)}`;
    const [{ sessions }, { sign_ins: signIns }, { catalogs }] = await Promise.all([
        api.get(`${base}/sessions`), api.get(`${base}/sign-ins`), api.get('/catalogs')]);
    return { sessions, signIns, catalogs: catalogs.map(row => row.name) };
}

// The sections, in drawer order. `detail` is GET /users/{name}'s answer,
// `account` loadAccount's.
export function accountSections({ detail, account, manager, changed }) {
    const act = async (request, message) => {
        try {
            await request();
            toast(message, 'ok');
        } catch { /* toasted */ }
        await changed();
    };
    const { user, entitlements } = detail;
    return [
        signInSection(user, manager, act),
        entitlementSection(user.name, entitlements, account.catalogs, manager, act),
        h('section', { id: 'user-sessions' },
            h('h3', {}, 'Console sessions'),
            sessionTable({
                id: 'user-session-table', prefix: 'user-session', sessions: account.sessions, allowed: manager,
                revoke: row => act(() => api.del(`/users/${enc(user.name)}/sessions/${enc(row.id_prefix)}`),
                    `Signed ${user.name} out of that session.`),
            }),
            account.sessions.length ? h('button', {
                type: 'button', id: 'user-sessions-revoke-all', class: 'secondary', disabled: !manager,
                onclick: async () => {
                    const ok = await confirmDialog({
                        title: `Sign ${user.name} out everywhere?`,
                        message: `Ends ${count(account.sessions.length, 'console session')}. Keys and OAuth grants keep working.`,
                        action: 'Sign out everywhere',
                    });
                    if (ok) await act(() => api.del(`/users/${enc(user.name)}/sessions`), `Signed ${user.name} out everywhere.`);
                },
            }, 'Sign out everywhere') : null),
        h('section', { id: 'user-sign-ins' },
            h('h3', {}, 'Recent sign-ins'),
            signInTable({ id: 'user-sign-in-table', signIns: account.signIns })),
    ];
}

function signInSection(user, manager, act) {
    const base = `/users/${enc(user.name)}`;
    const email = h('input', { type: 'email', name: 'email', value: user.email ?? '', autocomplete: 'off',
                               placeholder: 'name@example.com', 'aria-label': 'Email', disabled: !manager });
    const form = h('form', { id: 'user-email-form', class: 'inline-form' },
        email,
        h('button', { type: 'submit', disabled: !manager }, 'Save email'),
        user.email ? h('button', {
            type: 'button', id: 'user-email-clear', class: 'text-btn', disabled: !manager,
            onclick: () => act(() => api.put(`${base}/email`, { email: null }), `Cleared ${user.name}'s email.`),
        }, 'Clear') : null);
    form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const next = email.value.trim();
        act(() => api.put(`${base}/email`, { email: next || null }),
            next ? `${user.name}'s email is now ${next}.` : `Cleared ${user.name}'s email.`);
    });
    const admin = h('input', { type: 'checkbox', role: 'switch', id: 'user-admin-toggle',
                               checked: user.admin, disabled: !manager });
    admin.addEventListener('change', () => act(() => api.put(`${base}/admin`, { admin: admin.checked }),
        admin.checked ? `${user.name} is now an admin.` : `${user.name} is no longer an admin.`));
    const invite = h('button', {
        type: 'button', id: 'user-invite', class: 'secondary', disabled: !manager || !user.email,
        onclick: () => act(() => api.post(`${base}/invite`), `Queued a setup email to ${user.email}.`),
    }, 'Send setup email');
    return h('section', { id: 'user-account' },
        h('h3', {}, 'Sign-in'),
        h('dl', { class: 'facts' },
            fact('Email', h('span', { dataset: { test: `user-${user.name}-email` } }, user.email ?? 'none')),
            fact('Password', h('span', { id: 'user-password' }, user.has_password ? 'set' : 'not set'))),
        form,
        h('label', {}, admin, ' Admin: signs in to the full console'),
        h('div', { class: 'drawer-actions' }, invite),
        user.email ? null : h('p', { id: 'user-invite-reason', class: 'muted small' },
            'Set an email first: the setup link is sent there.'));
}

function entitlementSection(name, entitlements, catalogs, manager, act) {
    const base = `/users/${enc(name)}/entitlements`;
    const held = new Set(entitlements.map(entry => entry.catalog));
    const rows = entitlements.map(entry => {
        const level = h('select', { 'aria-label': `Access to ${entry.catalog}`, disabled: !manager,
                                    dataset: { test: `entitlement-level-${entry.catalog}` } },
            LEVELS.map(value => h('option', { value, selected: value === entry.access }, value)));
        level.addEventListener('change', () => act(
            () => api.put(`${base}/${enc(entry.catalog)}`, { access: level.value }),
            `${name} now has ${level.value} on ${entry.catalog}.`));
        return h('li', { dataset: { test: `entitlement-${entry.catalog}` } },
            h('span', { class: 'mono' }, entry.catalog), level,
            h('button', {
                type: 'button', class: 'text-btn', disabled: !manager,
                dataset: { test: `entitlement-remove-${entry.catalog}` },
                onclick: () => act(() => api.del(`${base}/${enc(entry.catalog)}`),
                    `Removed ${entry.catalog} from ${name}'s entitlements.`),
            }, 'Remove'));
    });
    const addable = catalogs.filter(catalog => !held.has(catalog));
    const catalog = picker({ name: 'catalog', required: true, 'aria-label': 'Catalog to entitle', disabled: !manager }, addable);
    const level = h('select', { name: 'access', 'aria-label': 'Access', disabled: !manager },
        LEVELS.map(value => h('option', { value }, value)));
    const form = h('form', { id: 'entitlement-form', class: 'inline-form' },
        catalog, level, h('button', { type: 'submit', disabled: !manager }, 'Entitle'));
    form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
        event.preventDefault();
        act(() => api.put(`${base}/${enc(catalog.value)}`, { access: level.value }),
            `${name} now has ${level.value} on ${catalog.value}.`);
    });
    return h('section', { id: 'user-entitlements' },
        h('h3', {}, 'Entitlements'),
        h('p', { class: 'muted small' },
            'Catalogs beyond those of the user\'s teams. Keys and grants the user creates are capped at the '
            + 'ceiling: these, plus the team catalogs at each catalog\'s member access, the higher level winning.'),
        h('ul', { class: 'grant-list', id: 'entitlement-list' },
            rows.length ? rows : h('li', { class: 'muted' }, 'No entitlements.')),
        addable.length ? form : null);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Create `js/pages/settings.js`.**

```js
// Settings (admin): the policy settings (each its effective value, and
// whether the database overrides the config file's default; Save and Reset), the
// configured OIDC providers and the mail provider (read-only: they live in
// the config file, and secrets are never shown), Send test email, and the
// mail queue: mail that is pending or failed, with Retry and Delete (never
// a body). Any admin reads it; changing anything needs an admin that
// reaches every catalog, as users and teams do.
import { h, pill, fact, fill } from '../core/dom.js';
import { api, enc } from '../core/api.js';
import { store } from '../core/store.js';
import { toast } from '../core/toast.js';
import { ago, when } from '../core/format.js';
import { canAdministerPeople } from '../core/shell.js';
import { listTable } from '../components/list-table.js';
import { confirmDialog } from '../components/confirm.js';

// What each setting does, under its key.
const MEANING = {
    password_sign_in: 'Offer email and password sign-in',
    max_keys_per_user: 'Live self-issued keys per user',
    max_key_lifetime: 'Longest self-issued key expiry ("none": no limit)',
    console_session_idle: 'Console session idle timeout',
    console_session_absolute: 'Console session absolute timeout',
    setup_link_ttl: 'Setup link lifetime',
    reset_link_ttl: 'Password reset link lifetime',
};
const MAIL_STATE_KIND = { pending: 'info', failed: 'error' };

export async function render(main) {
    main.append(h('header', { class: 'page-head' },
        h('div', {},
            h('h1', {}, 'Settings'),
            h('p', { class: 'muted' }, 'Sign-in and self-service policy, the sign-in providers and mail, and the mail queue.'))));
    if (!store.can('admin')) {
        main.append(h('p', { class: 'muted', id: 'settings-denied' }, 'Settings need an admin.'));
        return;
    }
    const manager = canAdministerPeople();
    if (!manager) {
        main.append(h('p', { class: 'muted small', id: 'settings-readonly' },
            'Changing settings or the mail queue needs an admin key that reaches every catalog.'));
    }

    // A change, then the settings again; the server's refusal is toasted.
    const change = async (request, message) => {
        try {
            await request();
            toast(message, 'ok');
        } catch { /* toasted: an invalid value names the setting */ }
        await loadSettings();
    };

    const valueControl = row => {
        const attrs = { class: 'settings-input', 'aria-label': row.key, disabled: !manager,
                        dataset: { test: `setting-input-${row.key}` } };
        const input = row.key === 'password_sign_in'
            ? h('select', attrs, ['true', 'false'].map(value => h('option', { value, selected: value === row.value }, value)))
            : h('input', { ...attrs, value: row.value ?? 'none', autocomplete: 'off' });
        return h('div', { class: 'inline-form' },
            input,
            h('button', {
                type: 'button', class: 'secondary', disabled: !manager, dataset: { test: `setting-save-${row.key}` },
                onclick: () => change(() => api.put(`/settings/${enc(row.key)}`, { value: input.value.trim() }),
                    `Saved ${row.key}.`),
            }, 'Save'),
            h('button', {
                type: 'button', class: 'text-btn', disabled: !manager || !row.overridden,
                dataset: { test: `setting-reset-${row.key}` },
                onclick: () => change(() => api.del(`/settings/${enc(row.key)}`), `${row.key} is back to its default.`),
            }, 'Reset'));
    };
    const settings = listTable([
        { key: 'key', label: 'Setting', sort: row => row.key,
          render: row => [h('code', { dataset: { test: `setting-${row.key}` } }, row.key),
              h('div', { class: 'muted small' }, MEANING[row.key] ?? '')] },
        { key: 'value', label: 'Value', render: valueControl },
        { key: 'overridden', label: 'Source',
          render: row => h('span', { dataset: { test: `setting-source-${row.key}` } },
              row.overridden ? pill('override', 'info') : pill('default', 'muted'),
              row.overridden && row.updated_by
                  ? h('span', { class: 'muted small' }, ` by ${row.updated_by}, ${ago(row.updated_at)}`)
                  : null) },
    ], [], { empty: 'No settings.' });
    settings.id = 'settings-table';

    const providers = h('div', { id: 'settings-oidc' });
    const mail = h('div', { id: 'settings-mail' });
    const to = h('input', { type: 'email', name: 'to', required: true, autocomplete: 'off',
                            placeholder: 'name@example.com', 'aria-label': 'Send a test email to', disabled: !manager });
    const testForm = h('form', { id: 'mail-test-form', class: 'inline-form' },
        to, h('button', { type: 'submit', disabled: !manager }, 'Send test email'));
    testForm.addEventListener('submit', async event => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const address = to.value.trim();
        try { await api.post('/mail/test', { to: address }); } catch { return; /* toasted */ }
        toast(`Queued a test email to ${address}.`, 'ok');
        testForm.reset();
        await loadQueue();
    });

    const queue = listTable([
        { key: 'to', label: 'To', class: 'mono', sort: row => row.to },
        { key: 'template', label: 'Template', sort: row => row.template },
        { key: 'status', label: 'Status', sort: row => row.status,
          render: row => h('span', { dataset: { test: `mail-status-${row.id}` } }, pill(row.status, MAIL_STATE_KIND[row.status])) },
        { key: 'attempts', label: 'Attempts', class: 'num', sort: row => row.attempts },
        { key: 'run_at', label: 'Next try', sort: row => row.run_at,
          render: row => row.status === 'pending' ? when(row.run_at) : '-' },
        { key: 'last_error', label: 'Last error',
          render: row => h('span', { class: 'small', dataset: { test: `mail-error-${row.id}` } }, row.last_error ?? '-') },
        { key: 'actions', label: '', render: row => h('div', { class: 'inline-form' },
            row.status === 'failed' ? h('button', {
                type: 'button', class: 'secondary', disabled: !manager, dataset: { test: `mail-retry-${row.id}` },
                onclick: () => queueChange(() => api.post(`/mail/queue/${enc(row.id)}/retry`), `Retrying the mail to ${row.to}.`),
            }, 'Retry') : null,
            h('button', {
                type: 'button', class: 'text-btn', disabled: !manager, dataset: { test: `mail-delete-${row.id}` },
                onclick: async () => {
                    const ok = await confirmDialog({
                        title: `Delete the mail to ${row.to}?`,
                        message: 'It is not sent. A setup or reset link in it stays valid until it expires.',
                        action: 'Delete',
                    });
                    if (ok) await queueChange(() => api.del(`/mail/queue/${enc(row.id)}`), `Deleted the mail to ${row.to}.`);
                },
            }, 'Delete')) },
    ], [], { empty: 'No pending or failed mail.' });
    queue.id = 'mail-queue-table';

    const queueChange = async (request, message) => {
        try {
            await request();
            toast(message, 'ok');
        } catch { /* toasted */ }
        await loadQueue();
    };

    main.append(
        h('section', { class: 'account-section', id: 'settings-policy' }, h('h2', {}, 'Policy'),
            h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, 'The config file\'s [auth] table gives the defaults; a value saved here overrides it until Reset.'),
            settings),
        h('section', { class: 'account-section' }, h('h2', {}, 'Sign-in providers'), providers),
        h('section', { class: 'account-section' }, h('h2', {}, 'Mail'), mail, testForm),
        h('section', { class: 'account-section' },
            h('div', { class: 'page-head' },
                h('h2', {}, 'Mail queue'),
                h('div', { class: 'actions' }, h('button', { type: 'button', id: 'mail-queue-refresh', class: 'secondary', onclick: () => loadQueue() }, 'Refresh'))),
            h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, 'Mail waiting to be sent, and mail that failed after its retries (24 hours) or at once.'),
            queue));

    async function loadSettings() {
        let answer;
        try { answer = await api.get('/settings'); } catch { return; }
        if (!main.isConnected) return;
        settings.redraw(answer.settings);
        fill(providers, answer.oidc.length
            ? h('ul', { class: 'grant-list' }, answer.oidc.map(provider =>
                h('li', { dataset: { test: `oidc-${provider.id}` } },
                    h('strong', {}, provider.label), ' ', h('code', {}, provider.id), ' ',
                    h('span', { class: 'mono small muted' }, provider.issuer))))
            : h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, 'No OIDC providers are configured: add [[auth.oidc]] tables to the config file.'));
        fill(mail, h('dl', { class: 'facts' },
            fact('Provider', h('code', {}, answer.mail.provider)),
            fact('From', answer.mail.from ?? 'none')));
    }

    async function loadQueue() {
        try {
            const { mail: rows } = await api.get('/mail/queue');
            if (main.isConnected) queue.redraw(rows);
        } catch { /* toasted */ }
    }

    await Promise.all([loadSettings(), loadQueue()]);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: The configuration table (section 3).** Add these rows to the table under "The configuration file", after the `oauth.*` rows:

```markdown
| `auth.password_sign_in` | `true` | Offer email and password sign-in on `/signin`. The default for the `password_sign_in` setting ("Signing in and self-service") |
| `auth.max_keys_per_user` | `20` | The most live self-issued keys a user may hold (`max_keys_per_user` setting) |
| `auth.max_key_lifetime` | none | The longest expiry a self-issued key may have, such as `"90d"`; unset means no limit (`max_key_lifetime` setting) |
| `auth.console_session_idle` | `"12h"` | A console session unused this long ends (`console_session_idle` setting). Not `session_idle_timeout`, which is MCP's |
| `auth.console_session_absolute` | `"7d"` | A console session ends this long after sign-in, used or not (`console_session_absolute` setting) |
| `auth.setup_link_ttl` | `"24h"` | How long a setup link works (`setup_link_ttl` setting) |
| `auth.reset_link_ttl` | `"1h"` | How long a password reset link works (`reset_link_ttl` setting) |
| `auth.trusted_proxy_header` | none | The header whose last hop is the client's address, such as `"x-forwarded-for"`, behind an ingress. Unset: the TCP peer's address. Sign-in limits and the sign-in history use it |
| `[[auth.oidc]]` | none | One table per OIDC provider: `id` (stable; stored with each linked identity), `label` (the button text), `issuer`, `client_id`, `client_secret_env` (the environment variable holding the secret) and `scopes` (default `["openid", "email", "profile"]`). Needs `public_url` |
| `mail.provider` | `"log"` | `"smtp"`, `"postmark"` or `"log"` (writes each message, links included, to the log at `info`: for development and tests only) |
| `mail.from` | none | The From address, such as `"okf <okf@example.com>"`. Required for `smtp` and `postmark` |
| `mail.smtp.host`, `mail.smtp.port`, `mail.smtp.starttls`, `mail.smtp.username`, `mail.smtp.password_env` | none, `587`, `true`, none, none | The SMTP relay; `password_env` names the environment variable holding the password |
| `mail.postmark.token_env`, `mail.postmark.message_stream` | none, `"outbound"` | Postmark's server token (by environment variable) and message stream |
```

- [ ] **Step 2: The new section `## Signing in and self-service`**, after "Users and teams" (before "Report-only maintenance"):

````markdown
## Signing in and self-service

People sign in to the console as themselves, with any of three methods: a
password, a passkey, or a linked account at an OIDC provider. Signed in,
they manage their own API keys and OAuth grants within a **ceiling** an admin
sets, and approve OAuth consent as themselves. Pasting an API key into the
console still works, for automation and for admins without a user.

Signing in needs `public_url` (section 3): it gives the cookie's origin, the
passkey relying party (its host) and the OIDC redirect URI. Without it,
`/signin` offers only "Use an API key", and the sign-in routes answer 404.

### Signing in

`GET /signin` offers:

- **Email and password**, while the `password_sign_in` setting is on.
- **Sign in with a passkey**: the browser offers the passkeys it holds for
  this server, so no email is typed first.
- **One button per `[[auth.oidc]]` provider.**
- **Use an API key instead**: the console's pasted-key card.

It takes `return_to`, a same-origin path (`/ui/...` or
`/oauth/authorize?...`); anything else becomes `/ui/`. The console's card
links to it with "Sign in with your account".

Every failed password sign-in (a wrong password, an unknown email, a locked
account) answers 401 "Email or password is incorrect", in the same time: an
unknown email is checked against a dummy hash. After 10 consecutive failures
an account locks for 15 minutes (stored, so a restart does not unlock it).
Each address may try 30 times per 15 minutes; that limit is in memory, per
process. Behind an ingress, set `auth.trusted_proxy_header`, or every request
seems to come from the ingress and shares one limit.

Passwords are hashed with argon2id (19 MiB, 2 passes). A password has at
least 12 characters and is not in the bundled list of common passwords;
there are no composition rules.

Every attempt writes a sign-in event (method, outcome, address) that the user
sees on their Account page and an admin in the user's drawer
(`okf-mcp user sign-ins NAME`), and an `info` log line with the user id,
method, outcome and address. Events older than 90 days are pruned.

### Sessions

A sign-in starts a **console session**: the `okf_session` cookie holds 256
random bits (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`, and `Secure` when
`public_url` is `https`); the server stores only its SHA-256.

- A session ends after `console_session_idle` unused (default 12 hours) or
  `console_session_absolute` after sign-in (default 7 days), whichever comes
  first.
- Every write the cookie authenticates must carry `X-OKF-CSRF` with the
  session's token (`GET /api/v1/session` gives it); otherwise it gets 403.
  The console does this itself.
- A request with a bearer key is the key's, whatever cookie it carries. `/mcp`
  and the archive routes take only bearer credentials.
- Sign-out (the console's Sign out, `DELETE /api/v1/session`) deletes the
  session. Changing a user's admin flag signs them out of every session
  (they sign in again with the new flag). Changing a password,
  adding a passkey or linking an account signs the user's other sessions
  out, unless the form's "Keep me signed in elsewhere" is ticked. A password
  reset signs every session out. An admin signs a user out with
  `okf-mcp user revoke-sessions NAME` or the user's drawer.
- An admin user's session is an admin that reaches every catalog, as an
  every-catalog admin key is. A member's session reaches exactly its ceiling,
  at the ceiling's levels.
- A session never owns a changeset, so MCP writes still need a key or a
  grant.

### Setting up an account, and resetting a password

No admin ever sees a password. An admin gives the user an email and sends a
setup link:

```sh
okf-mcp user set-email alice alice@example.com
okf-mcp user invite alice
```

The link opens `/account/setup`, where the person chooses a password,
registers a passkey, or both, and is signed in. It works once, for
`setup_link_ttl` (24 hours by default), and a newer setup link replaces it.

On `/signin/forgot` anyone may ask for a reset link. The answer is always "If
an account exists, we sent a link"; each email gets at most 3 requests per
hour, and each address 20. A reset link works once for `reset_link_ttl` (1
hour by default), opens a set-password page, and signs every session of the
user out. An expired, used or unknown link answers 410 "This link has
expired. Ask for a new one."

### Passkeys

Passkeys are registered on the setup page or the Account page, and need user
verification (a PIN or biometric). The relying party is `public_url`'s host,
so a passkey works only at that host: changing `public_url`'s host strands
every registered passkey (people then sign in another way and add a new
one). Sign-in uses discoverable credentials. The server stores public keys
only, and checks and advances each passkey's signature counter.

### OIDC providers

A provider is an `[[auth.oidc]]` table in the config file, with its client
secret in an environment variable:

```toml
[[auth.oidc]]
id = "example"                          # stable: stored with each linked identity
label = "Example ID"                    # the button text
issuer = "https://id.example.com"
client_id = "okf-console"
client_secret_env = "OKF_OIDC_EXAMPLE_SECRET"
scopes = ["openid", "email", "profile"]
```

Register the client at the provider as a confidential web client with the
redirect URI `{public_url}/auth/oidc/<id>/callback` (here
`https://okf-mcp.example.com/auth/oidc/example/callback`). The flow is the
authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), `state` and `nonce`. The provider's
discovery document is cached for an hour; a failed refresh keeps the cached
one.

After the ID token checks out (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry):

1. an identity already linked (by provider and subject) signs its user in;
2. otherwise, if the token's email is verified and matches a user's email
   (case-insensitively), the identity is linked, the user signs in, and gets
   a "sign-in method added" email;
3. otherwise sign-in is refused (403) with "No account for this email. Ask
   an admin to invite you." There is no self-signup.

A signed-in person can also link a provider from the Account page, whatever
its email, and unlink one unless it is their last sign-in method (409). The
Settings page lists the providers (id, label, issuer), never a secret.
Changing a provider's `id` orphans its linked identities.

### Mail

Mail goes through `[mail]`'s provider: `smtp` (any relay, with STARTTLS),
`postmark` (its HTTP API) or `log` (the message, link included, written to
the log at `info`; never in production). The templates are a setup link, a
reset link, "a sign-in method was added to your account", and the Settings
page's test email.

A request never sends mail itself: it queues a `SendMail` job in the server's
own Postgres database (the `apalis` schema, which `migrate` creates beside
okf's tables; it needs the `pgcrypto` and `hstore` extensions, and okf needs
`citext`, all three trusted, so the database owner creates them). A worker in
every server process sends it. A provider error that may pass (a network
error, Postmark 429 or 5xx, an SMTP 4xx) is retried after 30 seconds,
doubling to at most an hour, for 24 hours; a refusal (Postmark 422, an SMTP
5xx) fails at once. Failed mail keeps its last error. Sent mail is deleted
after 7 days and failed mail after 30.

The queue holds pending and failed mail; neither listing shows a body:

```sh
okf-mcp mail test alice@example.com    # queues the test email
okf-mcp mail queue                     # id, to, template, status, attempts, last error
okf-mcp mail retry ID                  # failed mail: send again now
okf-mcp mail delete ID
```

The Settings page shows the same queue with Retry and Delete. A setup or
reset link in a deleted mail stays valid until it expires; send a new one to
replace it.

### Settings

Policy settings live in the database, so the Settings page can change them
without a restart; the config file's `[auth]` table gives each one's default.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `password_sign_in` | `true` | Offer email and password sign-in |
| `max_keys_per_user` | `20` | Live self-issued keys per user |
| `max_key_lifetime` | `none` | Longest self-issued key expiry; `none` means no limit |
| `console_session_idle` | `12h` | Console session idle timeout |
| `console_session_absolute` | `7d` | Console session absolute timeout |
| `setup_link_ttl` | `24h` | Setup link lifetime |
| `reset_link_ttl` | `1h` | Password reset link lifetime |

```sh
okf-mcp settings list                      # key, value, default or override (by whom, when)
okf-mcp settings set max_key_lifetime 90d
okf-mcp settings reset max_key_lifetime    # back to the config file's default
```

A value is checked as its config key is (a duration like `12h`, a positive
number, `true`/`false`); a bad one is refused with the key named. Each change
is logged with the acting principal and reaches every server within
`poll_interval`.

### Self-service keys and grants

A signed-in person's **My keys** page lists, creates, renames and revokes the
keys they made themselves. A self-issued key:

- names its catalogs, each `read` or `write`, all within the ceiling; never
  "all catalogs", never `admin`, never a maintenance reporter;
- counts against `max_keys_per_user` while it is live;
- expires no later than `max_key_lifetime` allows, or never if that is
  `none`;
- belongs to the user, with the user's name as its default actor.

Creating one above the ceiling, past the key limit or beyond the lifetime
limit answers 422 naming the limit (`ceiling`, `max_keys_per_user` or
`max_key_lifetime`). Expired keys stop working at once. **My grants** lists
and revokes the user's OAuth grants. My keys also lists the keys an admin
made for the user: those are admin-issued, so not capped by the ceiling, and
an admin manages them on the API keys page too.

### The ceiling and member access

A user's **ceiling** is what their self-issued keys and grants may reach:

- the catalogs owned by every team the user belongs to, at each catalog's
  **member access** (`none`, `read` or `write`; `write` by default);
- plus the user's **entitlements**, catalogs an admin adds one at a time;
- where both give a catalog, the higher level.

A self-issued key or grant reaches, on each catalog, the lower of its own
level and the ceiling's; a catalog outside the ceiling is unreachable. Every
change that can move a ceiling (team membership, a catalog's owner or member
access, entitlements, the admin flag) reaches running servers within
`poll_interval`, so lowering a ceiling lowers live keys and grants. An admin
user's session is uncapped, but their self-issued keys are capped like
anyone's.

```sh
okf-mcp catalog set-member-access recipes --access read   # members read only
okf-mcp user entitle bob notes --access read             # one more catalog for bob
okf-mcp user unentitle bob notes
```

Only admins change member access and entitlements; team owners may later
(the server's one check is `may_set_member_access`).

### Rollout

Migration `0010` only adds. Until an admin acts nothing changes: every key,
grant, sign-in code and catalog works as before, every existing key is
admin-issued (uncapped), and pasting a key into the console still works.
After deploying:

1. Give yourself an email and the admin flag, and a setup link:

   ```sh
   okf-mcp user set-email alice alice@example.com
   okf-mcp user set-admin alice --on
   okf-mcp user invite alice
   ```

2. Configure `[mail]` (until then, `log` writes the setup link to the server
   log, which is fine on a test server only) and, if wanted, `[[auth.oidc]]`.
3. Open the link, choose a password or register a passkey, and sign in.
4. Team catalogs default to `member_access = write`: as members start
   creating their own keys, review shared catalogs and set `read` where
   intended.
5. Invite the others (`user set-email`, then `user invite`, or the user
   drawer's Send setup email).
````

```markdown
### Your account API

The routes behind My keys, My grants and Account, for a person signed in with
an account (a console session); a key gets 403 from every one but `GET
/api/v1/me`. Each acts only on the signed-in user's own keys, grants,
passkeys, identities and sessions; another user's id answers 404. Limits are
in "Signing in and self-service".

| Method and path | Key | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/me` | console session, or a key that belongs to a user | `{user, display_name, email, admin, has_password, teams, ceiling, session, password_sign_in, limits}`; `ceiling` is `[{catalog, access}]`, `session` says whether a console session asked, and `limits` is `{max_keys_per_user, max_key_lifetime_secs}` (`null` for no lifetime limit). 404 for a key without a user |
| `GET /api/v1/me/keys` | console session | `{keys}`: the user's keys, revoked and expired ones included, as `GET /api/v1/keys` shows them (with `catalog_access`, `expires_at`, `self_issued`) |
| `POST /api/v1/me/keys` | console session | Body `{name, catalogs: [{catalog, access}], default_catalog, actor, expires_at}` (`expires_at` RFC 3339 or absent; with `max_key_lifetime` set, absent means the limit). Answers `{key, secret}`, the secret once. 400 for a malformed or past expiry; 409 for a bad or taken name; 422 for `admin`, no catalogs, or a limit (`limit` is `ceiling`, `max_keys_per_user` or `max_key_lifetime`) |
| `PATCH /api/v1/me/keys/{id}` | console session | Body `{name}`. Renames the key; answers its view |
| `DELETE /api/v1/me/keys/{id}` | console session | Revokes it (the row stays, revoked); answers its view |
| `GET /api/v1/me/grants` | console session | `{grants}`: the user's OAuth grants, as key views (`client_name`, `catalog_access`, `self_issued`, `revoked_at`, ...) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/me/grants/{id}` | console session | Revokes the grant; its client is refused from its next request. Answers its view |
| `PUT /api/v1/me/password` | console session | Body `{current_password, new_password, keep_sessions}` (`current_password` is required while the user has a password). 204. 403 for a wrong current password (never 401); 422 for the policy (`limit: "password"`). Signs the other sessions out unless `keep_sessions` |
| `GET /api/v1/me/passkeys` | console session | `{passkeys}`: `id` (base64url), `name`, `created_at`, `last_used_at` |
| `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/start` | console session | Body `{name, keep_sessions}`. Starts registering a passkey: the WebAuthn creation options, with the ceremony bound to a 5-minute cookie. 404 while passkeys are off |
| `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/finish` | console session | Body: the browser's credential. Stores the passkey; 201 `{id, name}`. Signs the other sessions out unless the start said `keep_sessions`. 401 for a credential that does not verify, 410 for an expired ceremony |
| `PATCH /api/v1/me/passkeys/{id}` | console session | Body `{name}`. Renames it; 204 |
| `DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys/{id}` | console session | Removes it; 204. 409 for the last sign-in method |
| `GET /api/v1/me/identities` | console session | `{identities, providers}`: the linked identities (`provider`, `email_at_link`, `created_at`, `last_used_at`) and the configured providers (`id`, `label`) |
| `POST /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}/link` | console session | Body `{keep_sessions}`. Starts linking: answers `{url}`, the provider's sign-in URL (the flow cookie is set); the callback links the identity and returns to `/ui/#/account`. 404 for an unknown provider |
| `DELETE /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}` | console session | Unlinks it; 204. 409 for the last sign-in method |
| `GET /api/v1/me/sessions` | console session | `{sessions}`: `id_prefix`, `created_at`, `last_seen_at`, `ip`, `user_agent`, `current` (this browser's) |
| `DELETE /api/v1/me/sessions/{id_prefix}` | console session | Signs one session out; 204 |
| `GET /api/v1/me/sign-ins` | console session | `{sign_ins}`, newest first (at most 50): `method`, `outcome`, `ip`, `at` |
```

Append to the spec:

```markdown
## What shipped differently

Read the plan's "Decisions taken while planning" and its `Corrected (issue
#N)` notes for the detail; the per-task changelogs (`changelog/*-m12-task-*`)
give the reasons.

- **Per-catalog levels on keys** (plan Decision 1). `key_catalogs` gained a
  nullable `access` (NULL: the key's own level), and `Principal`'s reach
  became a level per catalog, so a self-issued key holds read on one catalog
  and write on another, and capping lowers each catalog separately.
- **`user_catalogs.catalog_id` is `bigint`** (Decision 2), as `catalogs.id`
  is; the data model above wrote `text`.
- **Self-issued keys name their catalogs** (Decision 3): "all catalogs" is
  refused (422), and a CHECK keeps self-issued keys from `admin`,
  maintenance reporting and all catalogs.
- **Key expiry is a column** (Decision 4): `api_keys.expires_at`, checked at
  lookup as well as on cache load. Only self-issued keys get one.
- **A console session is a principal** (Decision 5): `CredentialKind::Session`
  with `key_id = "session:<user>"`, which can never be a key id. A session
  owns no changesets. `whoami` answers for it with `kind: "session"`.
- **Three error variants** (Decision 6): `Unauthenticated` (401), `Gone`
  (410) and `LimitExceeded` (422, naming the limit).
- **Client addresses behind a proxy** (Decision 7): a new
  `[auth] trusted_proxy_header`; without it the peer address is used.
- **Limits** (Decision 8): per-address and per-email limits are in memory,
  per process, as M10's are; account lockout is durable
  (`users.failed_sign_ins`, `users.locked_until`).
- **Setting names** (Decision 9): `console_session_idle` and
  `console_session_absolute`, not `session_idle` and `session_absolute`,
  which would read as MCP's `session_idle_timeout`.
- **Mail retry** (Decision 11): 30 s doubling to 1 h for 24 hours; a
  permanent refusal fails at once; the worker polls every 30 s as well as
  listening, so manual retries are picked up.
- **OIDC over the existing HTTP client** (Decision 12): `openidconnect`
  without default features, through an adapter over the crate's `reqwest`
  0.13, so no second `reqwest` is linked.
- **Passkey ceremony state is in memory** (Decision 13), for 5 minutes and
  single use, keyed by a cookie, not a database row.
- **Sign-in pages may run script** (Decision 14): they share `http::pages`
  with consent, but use the console's CSP (`script-src 'self'`), since the
  passkey button needs WebAuthn; consent keeps its no-script CSP.
- **The last admin user** (Decision 16): the API refuses clearing it for any
  principal, admin keys included; the CLI may, as operator access.
- **One route per admin action** (Decision 17): entitle and unentitle,
  retry and delete, set and reset each have their own route, so the parity
  test keeps one route per row.
- **Linking an account from the console** goes through
  `POST /api/v1/me/identities/{provider}/link`, which answers the
  provider's URL, so the start of the link flow carries the CSRF token.
- **The console reads `GET /api/v1/session` beside `whoami`**: the session
  gives the CSRF token, admin flag and ceiling (`{catalog: level}`),
  `whoami` the catalogs, as for keys. Sign-out is `DELETE /api/v1/session`,
  behind the CSRF check, not a separate sign-out page.
- **An admin flag change signs the user out everywhere** (`users::set_admin`,
  Task 4; see the plan's decisions): instead of rotating the session id, every session of
  the user is deleted, so the next request signs in again with the new flag.
- **Passkey registration from the Account page** is
  `POST /api/v1/me/passkeys/register/start` and `/finish` (Task 8), beside
  the setup page's `POST /auth/passkey/setup/start` and `/finish`.
- **No "sign out everywhere else" for oneself**: the Account page signs other
  sessions out one at a time (`DELETE /api/v1/me/sessions/{id_prefix}`);
  admins still sign a user out everywhere.
```

Then add one bullet per `Corrected (issue #N)` note the `grep` found, saying in a sentence what shipped instead and naming the issue.

- [ ] **Step 6: File the follow-up issues** (the plan's deferred table), one each, labelled `enhancement`:

```bash
gh issue create --label enhancement \
  --title "Team owners manage member access and entitlements" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
Today only admins set a catalog's team member access and a user's entitlements (user login design, "Non-goals"; M12 plan, deferred table).

Let a team's owners set `member_access` on the catalogs their team owns, and entitle users to those catalogs. The permission check is one function, `store::ceiling::may_set_member_access(principal, catalog)`, which allows admins today: extend it to team owners, and add the console control to the team's drawer. No schema change is needed.
EOF
gh issue create --label enhancement \
  --title "OIDC providers configured in the database" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
OIDC providers are `[[auth.oidc]]` tables in the config file, with client secrets in environment variables, and the Settings page shows them read-only (user login design, "Non-goals" and "Future work" 2).

Store providers in the database instead, edited on the Settings page and by `okf-mcp settings`, with client secrets encrypted at rest under a key from the environment. Keep the config-file providers working, and keep provider ids stable, since linked identities store them.
EOF
gh issue create --label enhancement \
  --title "Multi-factor authentication for password sign-in" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
Password sign-in is a single factor today; passkeys are the only stronger method (user login design, "Non-goals" and "Future work" 3).

Add a second factor for password sign-in: TOTP, or a registered passkey as the second step. Include recovery codes, a setting to require it, and admin reset of a user's second factor.
EOF
gh issue create --label enhancement \
  --title "Self-service account deletion" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
A signed-in user cannot delete their own account (user login design, "Non-goals" and "Future work" 4). `user delete` is refused while any credential, revoked ones included, names the user (M11's deletion rules).

Once credential history no longer blocks deletion (#297), add "Delete my account" to the Account page: it revokes the user's keys, grants and sessions, removes their sign-in methods, and deletes the user and their personal team where the deletion rules allow.
EOF
gh issue create --label enhancement \
  --title "Move the background loops onto apalis" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
M12 runs mail through apalis on Postgres, but the existing loops stay as they were: the poll loop, OAuth token and code cleanup, and the new session, sign-in event, email token and mail-job pruning (user login design, "Background jobs" and "Future work" 5).

Move the cleanup tasks onto apalis as scheduled jobs, so they run once across replicas rather than in every process, and are visible in one queue.
EOF
gh issue create --label enhancement \
  --title "Rate limits shared across replicas" \
  --body-file - <<'EOF'
The per-address and per-email sign-in limits (and M10's OAuth limits) are in memory, per process (M12 plan Decision 8). With several replicas behind a load balancer, each replica allows the full budget.

Keep the limits in Postgres (or another shared store) so they hold across replicas, keeping the per-process limiter as a cheap first check.
EOF
```

```bash
# Milestone 12: user login (epic #<epic>)

People sign in to the web console as themselves, with a password, a passkey
or a linked OIDC account. They manage their own API keys and OAuth grants
within a ceiling an admin sets (team member access plus per-user
entitlements), and approve OAuth consent as themselves. Mail (setup and
reset links, notices) goes through a job queue in Postgres. Admins manage
all of it from the CLI, the REST API and the console, at parity. Closes #298
and #299. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-okf-user-login-design.md`;
plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-okf-mcp-m12-user-login.md`.

## Added

- **Task 1, schema (#<n>, PR #<n>):** migration `0010_user_login.sql`, apalis's schema set up by `db::migrate`, `OkfError::{Unauthenticated, Gone, LimitExceeded}`, the new dependencies.
- **Task 2, per-catalog levels (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `Reach::Catalogs` with a level per catalog, `Principal::level`, `key_catalogs.access`, `api_keys.expires_at` and `self_issued`, expiry at lookup.
- **Task 3, ceiling (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `store::ceiling` (team member access, entitlements, `cap`), capping self-issued credentials in the key cache.
- **Task 4, users (#<n>, PR #<n>):** email, admin flag and argon2id password; `store::passwords`, `store::email_tokens`, `store::sign_in_events`; durable lockout.
- **Task 5, settings and sessions (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `store::settings` over `[auth]` defaults; `store::user_sessions`.
- **Task 6, mail (#<n>, PR #<n>):** the `Mailer` trait (SMTP, Postmark, log), templates, the apalis `SendMail` job with durable retry, the queue.
- **Task 7a, console sessions (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `http::pages`, the keyed limiter and client addresses, `require_principal` (bearer or cookie plus CSRF), `CredentialKind::Session`, `GET` and `DELETE /api/v1/session` (sign-out).
- **Task 7b, sign-in pages (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `/signin` with password, setup, forgot and reset pages, sign-in events, the console's minimal session support and the first browser journey.
- **Task 8, passkeys (#<n>, PR #<n>):** WebAuthn registration and discoverable sign-in.
- **Task 9, OIDC (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `[[auth.oidc]]`, the provider registry, linking by verified email.
- **Task 10a, self-service keys and grants (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `GET /api/v1/me`, `/api/v1/me/keys` and `/api/v1/me/grants`, with every limit enforced.
- **Task 10b, self-service account (#<n>, PR #<n>):** password, passkeys, identities, sessions and sign-ins under `/api/v1/me`.
- **Task 11, consent as the user (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `/oauth/authorize` sends people to `/signin`; consent within the ceiling; self-issued grants.
- **Task 12, admin REST (#<n>, PR #<n>):** a route for every admin action (users, member access, settings, mail) and their API reference rows.
- **Task 13, CLI (#<n>, PR #<n>):** `user set-admin|set-email|invite|entitle|unentitle|sessions|revoke-sessions|sign-ins`, `catalog set-member-access`, `settings ...`, `mail ...`, with their parity rows and test.
- **Task 14a, console (user side) (#<n>, PR #<n>):** account sessions in the shell, My keys.
- **Task 14b, console (user side) (#<n>, PR #<n>):** My grants, Account.
- **Task 15, console (admin side) (#<n>, PR #<n>):** the user drawer's sign-in controls, entitlements, sessions and sign-ins; Team member access; the Settings page and mail queue.
- **Task 16, documentation (#<n>):** "Signing in and self-service", the remaining API reference, the README and the spec's "What shipped differently".

## Changed

- `/api/v1` accepts a console session (with `X-OKF-CSRF` on writes) beside bearer credentials; `/mcp` and the archive routes stay bearer-only.
- `whoami` answers for a session (`kind: "session"`).
- OAuth consent signs the person in first and caps the grant at their ceiling; sign-in codes still work, uncapped.
- The console's pasted-key card is one of two ways in.
```
